With various musical instruments resounding, surrounded by a flood of troops, filling the four directions with praise and auspicious songs,

197.

197.

Sādhukāra ninādeti, celukkhepasatehi ca;

Mahatā chaṇapujāya, kasanto bhūmipo agā.

The sound of approval resounded, with hundreds of cloths being tossed aloft; with great festivity and reverence, the lord of the land went along plowing.

198.

198.

Vihārañca purañceva, kurumāno padakkhiṇaṃ;

Sīmāya gamanaṭhānaṃ, nadiṃ patvā samāpayi.

Making a circumambulation of the monastery and the city, he completed the course of the boundary upon reaching the river.

199.

199.

Kenakena nimittena, sīmā ettha gatāti ce;

Evaṃ sīmāgataṭhānaṃ, icchamānā nibodhatha.

Should it be asked, 'By what mark has the boundary here been established?'—those wishing to know the site of the boundary should understand it thus:

200.

200.

Najjāpāsāṇatitthamhi[M 0.0094], pāsāṇe kuḍḍavāṭakaṃ;

Tato kumbalavāṭaṃ taṃ, mahānipaṃ tato agā.

From the ford at the Stone River, to a stone enclosure, then to that Kumbala enclosure, then it went to the Great Nipa tree.

201.

201.

Tato kukudhapāḷiṅgo, mahāaṅgaṇago tato;

Tato khujjamadhulañca, maruttapokkharaṇiṃtato.

Then the Kukudha palisade, then to the great courtyard; then the crooked Madhula tree, and then to the Marutta pond.

202.

202.

Vijayārāma uyyāne, uttaradvārakoṭṭha go;

Gajakumbhaka pāsāṇaṃ, thusavaṭṭhika majjhago.

In Vijayārāma Park, to the northern gate tower; the elephant-forehead stone, through the middle of the Thūsavaṭṭhi.

203.

203.

Abhaye balākapāsāṇaṃ, mahāsusāna majjhago;

Dīghapāsāṇakaṃ gantvā, kammāradeva gāmato.

To the Balāka stone at Abhaya, through the middle of the great cemetery; having gone to the long stone, from the village of Kammāradeva.

204.

204.

Nigrodha maṅgaṇaṃ gantvā, hiyagallasamīpake;

Diyāvasabrāhmaṇassa, devokaṃ pubbadakkhiṇaṃ.

Having gone to Nigrodhamaṅgaṇa, near Hiyagalla, to the southeastern corner of the Brahmin Diyāvasa's dwelling.

205.

205.

Tato telumapāliṅgo,

Tato tālacatukkago;

Assamaṇḍalavāmena,

Dve kadambā ajāyisuṃ.

Then to the Teluma palisade, then to the Tāla square; to the left of the horse circle, two Kadamba trees had grown.

206.

206.

Tato marumbatittaṅgo, tato uddhaṃ nidiṃ agā;

Paṭhama cetiya pācine, dve kadambā ajāyisuṃ.

Then to the Marumba ford, then it went upwards to the river; to the east of the first cetiya, two Kadamba trees had grown.

207.

207.

Senindaguttarajjamhi, damiḷā dakasuddhikā;

Nadiṃ dūranti bandhitvā, nagarāsannamakaṃsu taṃ.

During the reign of Sena and Gutta, the Damiḷas, skilled in waterworks, having dammed the river far away, brought it near to the city.

208.

208.

Jīva mānakadambañca, antosīmagataṃ ahu;

Mataka dambatīrena, sīmāuddakadambagā.

The Jīvamānaka-kadamba tree was within the boundary; by the bank of the Mataka-damba, the boundary went to the Uddaka-damba.

209.

209.

Sīhasinā natitthena, uggantvā tīrato vajaṃ;

Pāsāṇatitthaṃ gantvāna, nimittaṃ ghaṭṭayi isi.

The sage, having gone up from the bank at the Sīhasināna ford, proceeded to the Pāsāṇa ford and struck the mark.

210.

210.

Nimittetu pane’tasmiṃ, ghaṭṭite devamānusā;

Sādhukāraṃ pavattesuṃ, sāsanaṃ suppatiṭṭhitaṃ.

When this mark was struck, gods and humans raised a shout of approval: 'The Dispensation is well-established!'

211.

211.

Rañño dinnāya sītāya, nimitte parikittayi;

Dvattiṃsamāḷakatthañca, thūpārāmatthameva ca.

On the boundary-line given by the king, he proclaimed the marks for the thirty-two māḷakas and for the Thūpārāma as well.

212.

212.

Nimitte kittayitvāna, mahāthero mahāmati;

Sīmantaranimitte ca, kittayitvā yathāvidhiṃ.

Having proclaimed the marks, the great elder of great wisdom also proclaimed the inner boundary marks according to rule.

213.

213.

Abandhī [M 0.0095] sabbā sīmāyo, tasmiṃyeva dinevasī;

Mahāmahī akampittha, sīmābandhe samāpite.

The powerful one established all the boundaries on that very day. The great earth trembled when the binding of the boundary was completed.

214.

214.

Pañcame divase thero, rañño gehamhi bhuñjiya;

Nisajja nandanavane, suttantaṃ khajjanīyakaṃ.

On the fifth day, the elder, having dined in the king’s house and sat in the Nandana Grove, expounded the Khajjanīya Sutta.

215.

215.

Mahājanassa desetvā, sahassaṃ mānuse tahiṃ;

Pāyetvā amataṃ pānaṃ, mahāmeghavane vasī.

Having taught the great assembly and caused a thousand people there to drink the deathless drink, he dwelt in the Mahāmeghavana.

216.

216.

Chaṭṭhepi divase thero, raññogehamhi bhuñjiya;

Nisajja nandanavane, sutta gomaya piṇḍikaṃ.

On the sixth day also, the elder, having dined in the king's house and sat in the Nandana Grove, expounded the Gomayapiṇḍika Sutta.

217.

217.

Desayitvā desanaññū, mahassaṃyeva mānuse;

Pāpayitvā’bhisamayaṃ, mahā meghavane vasī.

The knower of the teaching, having taught a great multitude of people and caused them to attain realization, dwelt in the Mahāmeghavana.

218.

218.

Sattamepi dine thero, rājagehamhi bhuñjiya;

Nisajja nandanavane, dhammacakkappavattanaṃ.

On the seventh day also, the Elder, having dined in the king's house and sat in the Nandana Grove, expounded the Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta.

219.

219.

Suttantaṃ desayitvāna, sahassaṃyeva mānuse;

Pāpayitvā’bhisamayaṃ, mahā meghavane vasi.

Having taught the Suttanta, he caused a thousand people to attain realization, and dwelt in the Mahāmeghavana.

220.

220.

Evañhi aṭṭha navama-sahassāni jutindharo;

Kārayitvā’bhisamayaṃ, divaseheva sattati.

Thus indeed, the radiant one caused eight or nine thousand people to attain realization in just seven days.

221.

221.

Taṃ mahānandanavanaṃ, vuccate tena tādinā;

Sāsanajotitaṭṭhāna-mīti jotivanaṃ iti.

Therefore, that great Nandana Grove is called 'Jotivana' by him, the Such-a-one, meaning, 'the place illuminated by the Dispensation'.

222.

222.

Tissarāmamhi kāresi,

Rājā therassa ādito;

Pāsādaṃ sīghamukkāya,

Sukkhā petvāna mattikā.

At the Tissārāma, the king first had a palace built for the Elder, having quickly brought earth and caused it to be dried.

223.

223.

Pāsādo kāḷakābhāso,

Āsi so tena taṃ tahiṃ;

Kāḷapāsāda pariveṇa-mīti saṅkhamupāgataṃ.

That palace was dark in appearance; therefore, it came to be known there as the 'Kāḷapāsāda-pariveṇa' (Black Palace Residence).

224.

224.

Tato mahābodhigharaṃ, lohapāsāda meva ca;

Salākaggañca kāresi, bhattasālañca sādhukaṃ.

Then he had the Mahābodhi-ghara built, and also the Lohapāsāda, the Salākagga, and a fine refectory.

225.

225.

Bahūni [M 0.0096] pariveṇāni, sādhu pokkharaṇīpi ca;

Rattiṭhāna divāṭhāna-pabhutīni ca kārayi.

He had many residences made, and fine ponds, and places for night and day, and so forth.

226.

226.

Tassa nahānapāpassa, nhānapokkharaṇītaṭe;

Sunahātapariveṇanti, pariveṇaṃ pavuccati.

On the bank of the bathing pond, for his bathing, the residence is called the 'Sunahāta-pariveṇa' (Well-bathed Residence).

227.

227.

Tassa caṅkamitaṭhāne, dīpa dīpassa sādhuno;

Vuccate pariveṇaṃ taṃ, dīghacaṅkamanaṃ iti.

In the place where that virtuous one, the Lamp of the Island, used to walk, that residence is called the 'Dīghacaṅkamana' (Long Promenade).

228.

228.

Aggaphalasamāpattiṃ, samāpajja yahiṃ tuso;

Phalagga pariveṇanti, etaṃ tena pavuccati.

Where he entered into the attainment of the highest fruit and was content, for that reason this is called the 'Phalagga-pariveṇa' (Residence of the Highest Fruition).

229.

229.

Apassiya apassenaṃ, thero tattha nisīdiso;

Therā passaya pariveṇaṃ, etaṃ tena pavuccati.

The elder sat there without leaning on a support; therefore, it is called the Therāpassaya Pariveṇa.

230.

230.

Bahū marugaṇā yattha, upāsiṃsu upaccataṃ;

Teneva taṃ marugaṇa-pariveṇanti vuccati.

Where many groups of gods dwelt, for that very reason it is called the Marugaṇa Pariveṇa.

231.

231.

Senāpatitassa rañño, therassa dīghasandako;

Kāresi cūḷapāsādaṃ, mahāthambhehi aṭṭhahi.

The king's general, Dīghasandaka, had a small palace built for the elder, with eight great pillars.

232.

232.

Dīghasanda senāpati-pariveṇanti taṃ tahiṃ;

Vuccate pariveṇaṃ taṃ, pamukhaṃ pamukhākaraṃ.

There, that dwelling is called the Dīghasanda Senāpati Pariveṇa; it is foremost, a source of leaders.

233.

233.

Devānaṃpiyavacano’paguḷanāmo,

Laṃkāyaṃ paṭhamamimaṃ mahāvihāraṃ;

Rājā so sumatimahāmahindatheraṃ,

Āgammā malamatimetthakārayitthāti.

That king, whose name was concealed by the epithet 'Beloved of the Gods,' having approached the wise Great Elder Mahinda, first caused this Great Monastery to be built in Laṅkā, and had the impurities removed here.

Sujanappasāda saṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Mahāvaṃsa, composed for the serene joy and spiritual urgency of the good.

Mahāvihārapaṭiggahako nāma

Named 'The Acceptance of the Great Monastery'

Pannarasamo paricchedo.

The Fifteenth Chapter.

Soḷasama pariccheda

The Sixteenth Chapter.

Cetiyapabbatavihāra paṭiggahako

The Acceptance of the Cetiyapabbata Monastery.

1.

1.

Pure [M 0.0097] caritvā piṇḍāya, karitvā janasaṅgahaṃ;

Rājagehamhi bhuñjanto, kārento rājasaṅgahaṃ.

Wandering for alms in the morning, ministering to the people; eating in the royal palace, ministering to the king.

2.

2.

Chabbasadivase thero, mahāmeghavane vasī;

Āsaḷhasukkapakkhassa, terase divase pana.

For twenty-six days the elder dwelt in the Mahāmeghavana; but on the thirteenth day of the bright fortnight of Āsāḷha,

3.

3.

Rājagehamhi bhuñjitvā, mahārañño mahāmati;

Mahā’ppamādasuttantaṃ, desayitvā tato ca so.

The greatly wise one, having eaten in the royal palace and having taught the Great Discourse on Heedfulness to the great king, thereupon...

4.

4.

Vihārakaraṇaṃ icchaṃ, tattha cetiyapabbate;

Nikkhamma purimadvārā, agā cetiyapabbataṃ.

Wishing to make a monastery there on Cetiyapabbata, he went out through the eastern gate and proceeded to Cetiyapabbata.

5.

5.

Theraṃ tattha gataṃ sutvā, rathaṃ āruyha bhūpati;

Deviyo dve ca ādāya, therassānupadaṃ akā.

Hearing that the elder had gone there, the king mounted his chariot, and taking his two queens, he followed in the elder's footsteps.

6.

6.

Therā nāgacatukkamhi, nahātvā rahade tahiṃ;

Pabbatārohaṇatthāya, aṭṭhaṃsu paṭipāṭiyā.

The elders, having bathed there in the lake at Nāgacatukka, stood in order for the purpose of ascending the mountain.

7.

7.

Rājā rathā tado’ruyha, sabbe there’bhivādayi;

Uṇhe kilante kiṃrāja, āgatosī’ti ahute.

Then the king, alighting from his chariot, paid homage to all the elders. They asked him, saying: 'Why have you come, O king, weary in the heat?'

8.

8.

Tumhākaṃ gamanāsaṅkī, āgatomhī’ti bhāsite;

Idheva vassaṃ vasituṃ, āgatamhā’ti bhāsiya.

When the king said, 'Fearing your departure, I have come,' the elder replied, saying: 'We have come to spend the rains-retreat right here.'

9.

9.

Tassūpanāyikaṃ thero, khandhakaṃ khandhakovido;

Kathesi rañño taṃ sutvā, bhāgineyyo ca rājino.

The elder, skilled in the Khandhakas, taught the king a discourse from the Khandhaka suitable for the occasion. Hearing this, the king's nephew...

10.

10.

Mahāriṭṭho mahāmacco, pañcapaññāsabhātuhi;

Saddhiṃ jeṭṭhakaniṭṭhehi, rājānamabhito ṭhito.

The great minister Mahāriṭṭha, together with his fifty-five elder and younger brothers, stood near the king.

11.

11.

Yācitvā tadahu ceva, pabbajuṃ therasantike;

Pattārahattaṃ sabbepi, te khuragge mahāmatī.

Having made their request on that very day, they went forth in the presence of the elder; all of those greatly wise ones attained arahantship at the razor's edge.

12.

12.

Kantakacetiyaṭhāne, parito tadaheva so;

Kammāni ārabhāpetvā, leṇāni aṭṭhasaṭṭhiyo.

Then, at the site of the Kaṇṭaka Cetiya, he at once had work begun all around and had sixty-eight rock-caves completed.

13.

13.

Agamāsi [M 0.0098] puraṃ rājā, therā tattheva te vasuṃ;

Kāle piṇḍāya nagaraṃ, pavisantā’nukampakā.

The king went to the city; those elders remained right there. At the proper time, being compassionate, they would enter the city for alms.

14.

14.

Niṭṭhite leṇakammamhi, āsaḷhipuṇṇamāsiyaṃ;

Gantvā adāsi therānaṃ, rājā vihāradakkhiṇaṃ.

When the work on the caves was finished, on the full-moon day of the month of Āsāḷha, the king went and gave the gift of the monastery to the elders.

15.

15.

Dvattiṃsamāḷakānañca, vihārassa ca tassa kho;

Sīmaṃ sīmātigo thero, bandhitvā tadaheva so.

Then, on that very day, the elder, who had transcended all boundaries, established the boundary for the thirty-two pavilions and for that monastery.

16.

16.

Tesaṃ pabbajjāpekkhānaṃ, akāsi upasampadaṃ;

Sabbesaṃ sabbapaṭhamaṃ, baddhe tumbarumāḷake.

He conferred the higher ordination on all those who were seeking it, first of all within the bounded Tumbaru Pavilion.

17.

17.

Ete dvāsaṭṭhi arahanto, sabbe cetiyapabbate;

Tattha vassaṃ upagantvā, akaṃsu rājasaṅgahaṃ.

These sixty-two arahants, all of them, having entered upon the rains-residence there on Cetiyapabbata, ministered to the king.

18.

18.

Devamanussagaṇagaṇitaṃ taṃ,

Tañca gaṇaṃ guṇavitthatakittiṃ;

Yānamupacca ca mānayamānā,

Puññacayaṃ vipulaṃ akariṃsūti.

That assembly, esteemed among the hosts of gods and humans, that community whose fame was spread wide by its virtue—by approaching and honoring it, and the Vehicle, they made an abundant accumulation of merit.

Sujanapasādasaṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Mahāvaṃsa, composed for the serene joy and spiritual urgency of the good.

Cetiyapabbatavihārapaṭiggahako nāma

Named 'The Acceptance of the Cetiyapabbata Monastery'.

Soḷasamo paricchedo.

The Sixteenth Chapter.

Sattarasama pariccheda

The Seventeenth Chapter.

Dhātuāgamano

The Arrival of the Relics.

1.

1.

Vutthavasso pavāretvā, kattikapuṇṇamāsiyaṃ;

Avoce’daṃ mahārājaṃ, mahāthero mahāmati.

The great elder Mahāmati, having completed the rains retreat and performed the Pavāraṇā ceremony on the full-moon day of Kattika, addressed the great king thus:

2.

2.

Ciradiṭṭho hi sambuddho, satthā no manujādhipa;

Anāthavāsaṃ avasimha, natthi no pūjiyaṃ idha.

“For long have we not seen the Buddha, our Teacher, O lord of men. We have lived without a protector; there is none here worthy of our worship.”

3.

3.

“Bhāsittha nanu bhanteme, sambuddho nibbuto” iti;

Āha dhātūsu diṭṭhesu, diṭṭho hoti jino” iti.

“Did you not say, venerable sirs, that the Fully Enlightened One has attained Nibbāna?” The elder replied, “When the relics are seen, the Conqueror is seen.”

4.

4.

Vidito [M 0.0099] vo adhippāyo, thūpassa kāraṇe mayā;

Kāressāmi ahaṃ thūpaṃ, tumhe jānātha dhātuyo.

“Your intention regarding the building of the stupa is known to me. I will have the stupa built; you should ascertain where the relics are.”

5.

5.

Mantehi sumanenāti, thero rājānamabravi;

Rājā’ha sāmaṇeraṃ taṃ, kuto lacchāma dhātuyo.

“Consult with Sumana,” the elder said to the king. The king then said to the novice, “From where shall we obtain the relics?”

6.

6.

Vibhūsayitvā nagaraṃ, maggañca manujādhipa;

Uposathī sapariso, hatthiṃ āruyha maṅgalaṃ.

“Having adorned the city and the road, O lord of men, observing the Uposatha day with your retinue, mount the auspicious elephant.”

7.

7.

Setacchattaṃ dhārayanto, tālāvacarasaṃhito;

Mahānāgavanuyyānaṃ, sāyanhasamaye vaja.

“Holding a white parasol, accompanied by attendants with palmyra fans, go to the Mahānāgavana park in the evening.”

8.

8.

Dhātubhedaññuno rāja, dhātuyo tattha lacchasi;

Icchāha sāmaṇero so, sumano taṃ sumānasaṃ.

“O king, you who know the distribution of the relics, there you shall obtain the relics.” Thus spoke the novice Sumana to him of joyful mind.

9.

9.

Thero’tha rājakulato, gantvā cetiyapabbataṃ;

Āmantiya sāmaṇeraṃ, sumanaṃ sumano gatiṃ.

Then the elder, having gone from the royal palace to Cetiyapabbata, addressed the novice Sumana, who was of good destiny:

10.

10.

Ehi tvaṃ bhadra sumana, gantvā pupphapuraṃ varaṃ;

Ayyakaṃ te mahārājaṃ, evaṃ no vacanaṃ vada.

“Come, good Sumana, go to the excellent city of Pupphapura and speak these words of ours to your grandfather, the great king.”

11.

11.

Sahāyo te mahārāja, mahārājā maruppiyo;

Pasanno buddhasamaye, thūpaṃ kāretumicchati.

“O great king, your friend, the great king dear to the gods, being devoted to the Buddha’s Dispensation, wishes to have a stupa built.”

12.

12.

Munino dhātuyo dehi, pattaṃ bhuttañca satthunā;

Sarīradhātuyo santi, bahavo hi tavantike.

“Give the relics of the Sage and the bowl used by the Teacher, for many bodily relics are in your possession.”

13.

13.

Pattapūrā gahetvā tā, gantvā devapuraṃ varaṃ;

Sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ taṃ, evaṃ no vacanaṃ vada.

“Having taken them, filling the bowl, go to the excellent city of the gods and speak these words of ours to Sakka, the lord of the gods.”

14.

14.

Tilokadakkhiṇeyyassa, dāṭhādhātu ca dakkhiṇā;

Tavantikamhi devinda, dakkhiṇakkhakadhātu ca.

“O lord of the gods, the right tooth relic and the right collarbone relic of him who is worthy of offerings in the three worlds are in your possession.”

15.

15.

Dāṭhaṃ tvameva pūjehi, akkhakaṃ dehi satthuno;

Laṃkādīpassa kiccesu, māpamajja surādhipa.

“You yourself should venerate the tooth relic; give the Teacher's collarbone relic. In the affairs of the Isle of Laṅkā, be not negligent, O lord of the gods.”

16.

16.

“Evaṃ bhante”ti vatvā so, sāmaṇero mahiddhiko;

Taṅkhaṇaṃyeva agamā, dhammāsokassa santikaṃ.

“So be it, venerable sir,” said that novice of great psychic power, and at that very moment, he went to the presence of Dhammāsoka.

17.

17.

Sālamūlamhi ṭhapitaṃ, mahābodhiṃ tahiṃ sutaṃ;

Kattikacchaṇapūjāhi, pūjiyaṃ tañca addasa.

There he saw the renowned Great Bodhi tree, established at the foot of a Sāla tree, being venerated with the offerings of the Kattika festival.

18.

18.

Therassa [M 0.0100] vacanaṃ vatvā, rājato laddhadhātuyo;

Pattapūraṃ gahetvāna, himavantamupāgami.

Having spoken the elder's words and received the relics from the king, he took the bowl filled with them and went to the Himālaya.

19.

19.

Himavante ṭhapetvāna, sadhātuṃ pattamuttamaṃ;

Devindasantikaṃ gantvā, therassa vacanaṃ bhaṇi.

Having placed the supreme bowl with the relics in the Himālaya, he went to the presence of the lord of the gods and spoke the elder’s words.

20.

20.

Cūḷāmaṇi cetiyamhā, gahetvā dakkhiṇakkhakaṃ;

Sāmaṇerassa pādāsi, sakko devānamissaro.

Taking the right collarbone relic from the Cūḷāmaṇi Cetiya, Sakka, the lord of the gods, gave it to the novice.

21.

21.

Taṃ dhātuṃ dhātupattañca, ādāya sumano tato;

Āgamma cetiyagiriṃ, therassa’dāsi taṃ yati.

Taking that relic and the bowl of relics, the ascetic Sumana then returned to Cetiyagiri and gave them to the elder.

22.

22.

Mahānāgavanuyyānaṃ, vuttenā vidhinā’gamā;

Sāyanhāsamaye rājā, rājasenā purakkhato.

The king, preceded by the royal army, went to the Mahānāgavana park in the evening, following the prescribed method.

23.

23.

Ṭhapesi dhātuyo sabbā, thero tattheva pabbate;

Missakaṃ pabbataṃ tasmā, āhu cetiya pabbataṃ.

The elder placed all the relics there on that very mountain. Therefore, they call Missaka mountain Cetiya mountain.

24.

24.

Ṭhapetvā dhātupattaṃ taṃ, thero cetiyapabbate;

Gahetvā akkhakaṃ dhātuṃ, saṅketaṃ sagaṇo’gamā.

Having placed that bowl of relics on Cetiyapabbata, the elder, taking the collarbone relic, went with his retinue to the appointed place.

25.

25.

Sacāyaṃ munino dhātu, chattaṃ namatu me sayaṃ;

Jaṇṇukehi karīdhātu, dhātucaṅkoṭako ayaṃ.

“If this is indeed a relic of the Sage, may the parasol bow to me of its own accord, may the elephant kneel, and may this relic casket…”

26.

26.

Sirasmiṃ me patiṭṭhātu, āgamma saha dhātuko;

Iti rājā vicintesi, cintitaṃ taṃ tathā ahu.

“…coming, be established upon my head with the relic.” Thus the king reflected, and it came to pass just as he had thought.

27.

27.

Amatenā’bhisittova, ahu haṭṭho’ti bhūpati;

Sīsato taṃ gahetvāna, hatthikkhandhe ṭhapesitaṃ.

The king was as delighted as if sprinkled with ambrosia. Taking the relic from his head, he had it placed on the elephant's back.

28.

28.

Haṭṭho hattī kuñcanādaṃ, akā kampittha medinī;

Tato nāgo nivattitvā, sathera balavāhano.

The delighted elephant trumpeted, and the earth trembled. Then the elephant, the powerful carrier, turned back with the Elder.

29.

29.

Puratthimena dvārena, pavisitvā puraṃ subhaṃ;

Dakkhiṇena ca dvārena, nikkhamitvā tato puna.

Entering the splendid city through the eastern gate, he then exited again through the southern gate.

30.

30.

Thūpārāme cetiyassa, ṭhānato pacchato kataṃ;

Pamojavatthuṃ gantvāna, bodhiṭhāne nivattiya.

Having gone to the Pamojavatthu, which was made to the west of the site of the Thūpārāma cetiya, he turned back at the Bodhi-site.

31.

31.

Puratthāvadano aṭhā, thūpaṭhānaṃ tadā hitaṃ;

Kadambapupphaādāri-vallīhi citakaṃ ahu.

Facing east, he stood at what was then a suitable site for a stūpa; the pyre was adorned with Kadamba flowers and creepers.

32.

32.

Manussadevo [M 0.0101] devehi, taṃ ṭhānaṃ rakkhitaṃ suciṃ;

Sodhāpetvā bhūsayitvā, taṅkhaṇaṃyeva sādhukaṃ.

The god among men had that pure place, which was guarded by devas, well cleansed and adorned at that very moment.

33.

33.

Dhātuṃ oropanatthāya, ārabhī hatthikkhandhato;

Nāgo na icchitaṃ rājā, theraṃ pucchittha taṃ manaṃ.

To lower the relic, he began from the elephant’s back. The elephant did not wish it, so the king asked the Elder about its intention.

34.

34.

Attano khandhasamake, ṭhāne ṭhapanamicchati;

Dhātuoropanaṃ tena, na iṭṭhamī’ti so bravi.

It desires to place it on a level with its own shoulder. Thus, lowering the relic was not to its liking, so he said.

35.

35.

Āṇāpetvā khaṇaṃyeva,

Sukkhāto’bhayavāpito;

Sukkhakaddama khaṇḍehi,

Citā petvāna taṃ samaṃ.

Having commanded, in an instant, the Abhaya tank was dried up; with pieces of dried mud, he had it piled up to the same level.

36.

36.

Alaṅkaritvāna bahudhā, rājā taṃ ṭhānamuttamaṃ;

Oropetvā hatthikkhandhā, dhātuṃ tattha ṭhapesitaṃ.

Having adorned that excellent place in many ways, the king, lowering the relic from the elephant's shoulder, had it enshrined there.

37.

37.

Dhātārakkhaṃ saṃvidhāya, ṭhapetvā tattha hatthinaṃ;

Dhātuthūpassa karaṇe, rājā turitamānaso.

Having arranged for the protection of the relic and stationed the elephant there, the king, with an eager mind, proceeded to build the relic stūpa.

38.

38.

Bahū manusse yojetvā, itthikākaraṇe lahuṃ;

Dhātukiccaṃ vicintento, sāmacco pāvisī puraṃ.

Having swiftly engaged many people for the brickwork, and pondering the ceremony for the relic, the king entered the city with his ministers.

39.

39.

Mahāmahindatthero tu, mahā meghavanaṃ subhaṃ;

Sagaṇo abhigantvāna, tattha vāsamakappayi.

The great Elder Mahinda, with his retinue, approached the delightful Mahāmegha Grove and established his residence there.

40.

40.

Rattiṃ nāgo’nupariyāti, taṃ ṭhānaṃ so sadhātu kaṃ;

Bodhiṭhānamhi sālāya, divāṭhāti sadhātuko.

By night the elephant patrols that place containing the relic; by day he stands with the relic in the hall at the Bodhi-site.

41.

41.

Vatthussa tasso’parito, thūpaṃ theramatānu go;

Jaṅghāmattaṃ citāpetvā, katipāhena bhūpati.

The king, following the Elder's advice, had a stūpa built over that site, piling it up to the height of a shin in a few days.

42.

42.

Tattha dhātupatiṭṭhānaṃ, ghosāpetvā upāgami;

Tato tato samanto ca, samāgami mahājano.

There, having announced the establishment of the relic, he approached; from here and there, and all around, a great multitude gathered.

43.

43.

Tasmiṃ samāgame dhātu, hatthikkhandhā nagāggatā;

Sattatālappamāṇamhi, dissanti nabhasiṭṭhitā.

In that assembly, the relic rose up from the elephant's shoulder; it was seen standing in the sky at a height of seven palmyra trees.

44.

44.

Vimhāpayanti janataṃ, yamakaṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ;

Kaṇṇambamūle buddho’va, akari lomahaṃsanaṃ.

Astonishing the people, it performed the twin miracle, a hair-raising wonder, just as the Buddha did at the foot of the mango tree.

45.

45.

Tato [M 0.0102] nikkhantajālāhi, jaladhārāhi cā’sakiṃ;

Ayaṃ obhāsitā’sittā, sabbālaṃkāmahī mahu.

Then, with flames issuing forth and streams of water simultaneously, this whole adorned earth was illuminated and bathed.

46.

46.

Parinibbānamañcamhi, nipannena jinena hi;

Kataṃ mahāadhiṭṭhāna-pañcakaṃ pañcacakkhunā.

Indeed, the five great resolutions were made by the Victor, the One with Five Eyes, as he was lying on his Parinibbāna couch.

47.

47.

Gayhamānā mahābodhi sākhāsokena dakkhiṇā;

Chijjitvāna sayaṃyeva, patiṭṭhātu kaṭāhake.

May the great Bodhi tree's southern branch, when being taken by Asoka, break off by itself and be established in the pot.

48.

48.

Patiṭṭhahitvā sā sākhā, chabbaṇṇarasmiyo subhā;

Rañjayantī disā sabbā, phalapattehi muccatu.

Having been established, may that branch, illuminating all directions with beautiful six-colored rays, be endowed with fruits and leaves.

49.

49.

Sasuvaṇṇakaṭāhā sā, uggantvāna manoramā;

Adissamānā sattāhaṃ, himagabbhamhi tiṭṭhatu.

May it, with the golden pot, having risen up delightfully, remain unseen for seven days in a snow-chamber.

50.

50.

Thūpārāme patiṭṭhantaṃ, mama dakkhiṇaakkhakaṃ;

Karotu nabhamuggantvā, yamayaṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ.

When my right collar-bone is established in the Thūpārāma, may it rise into the sky and perform the twin miracle.

51.

51.

Laṅkā laṅkārabhūtamhi, hemamālikacetiye;

Patiṭṭhahantiyo dhātu, doṇamattā pamāṇato.

May the relics, a doṇa in measure, when being established in the Hemamālika Cetiya, the ornament of Laṅkā,

52.

52.

Buddhavesadharā hutvā, uggantvā nabhasiṭṭhitā;

Patiṭṭhaṃ tu karitvāna, yamakaṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ.

having taken on the form of the Buddha, rise up and stand in the sky, and having established themselves firmly, perform the Twin Miracle.

53.

53.

Adhiṭṭhānāni pañce’va, adhiṭṭhāsi tathāgato;

Akāsi tasmā sā dhātu, tadā taṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ.

The Tathāgata made these five resolutions; therefore that relic then performed that miracle.

54.

54.

Ākāsā otaritvā sā, aṭṭhābhūpassa muddhani;

Atīvahaṭṭho taṃ rājā, patiṭṭhāpesi cetiye.

Having descended from the sky, it alighted on the head of the king. Greatly overjoyed, that king enshrined it in the cetiya.

55.

55.

Patiṭṭhitāya tassā ca, dhātuyā cetiye tadā;

Ahu mahābhūmicālo, abbhuto lomahaṃsano.

And when that relic was enshrined in the cetiya, there was a great earthquake, wondrous and hair-raising.

56.

56.

Evaṃ acintiyā buddhā, buddhadhammā acintiyā;

Acintiye pasannānaṃ, vipāko hoti acintiyo.

Thus, inconceivable are the Buddhas, inconceivable are the qualities of a Buddha; for those with faith in the inconceivable, the result is inconceivable.

57.

57.

Taṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ disvā, pasīdiṃsu jane janā;

Mattābhayo rājaputto, kaniṭṭho rājino pana.

Seeing that miracle, many people gained faith, as did Prince Mattābhaya, the king's youngest brother.

58.

58.

Munissare pasīditvā, yācitvāna narissaraṃ;

Purisānaṃ sahassena, saha pabbajisāsane.

Having gained faith in the Lord of Sages, he requested permission from the lord of men and went forth into the Dispensation together with a thousand men.

59.

59.

Cetārigāmato [M 0.0103] cāpi, dvāramaṇḍalatopi ca;

Vihīrabījato cāpi, tathā gallakapiṭṭhito.

Also from the village of Cetāri, and from Dvāramaṇḍala, and from Vihīrabīja, and likewise from Gallakapiṭṭhi.

60.

60.

Tatho’patissagāmā ca, pañca pañca satāni ca;

Pabbajuṃ dārakā haṭṭhā, jātasaddhā tathāgate.

Then from the village of Upatissa also, five hundred youths from each of the five villages, joyful and with faith arisen in the Tathāgata, went forth.

61.

61.

Evaṃ purā bāhirā ca, sabbe pabbajitā tadā;

Tiṃsa bhikkhusahassāni, ahesuṃ jinasāsane.

Thus, all those from the city and from outside went forth then. There were thirty thousand bhikkhus in the Dispensation of the Conqueror.

62.

62.

Thūpārāme thūpavaraṃ, niṭṭhāpetvā mahīpati;

Ratanādīhi’nekehi, sadā pūjamakārayi.

The lord of the earth, having completed the excellent thūpa in the Thūpārāma, always had it venerated with many kinds of jewels and other gifts.

63.

63.

Rājorodhā khattiyā ca, amaccā nāgarā tathā;

Sabbe janapadā ceva, pujā’kaṃsu visuṃ visuṃ.

The royal women, the nobles, the ministers, and the townspeople, and all the people of the countryside, each made offerings separately.

64.

64.

Thūpapubbaṅgamaṃ rājā, vihāraṃ tattha kārayi;

Thūpārāmoti tene’sa, vihāro vissuto ahu.

The king had a monastery built there, which was preceded by the thūpa; for that reason this monastery became renowned as the Thūpārāma.

65.

65.

Sakadhātusarīrakena ce’vaṃ,

Parinibbānagatopi lokanātho;

Janakāyahitaṃ sukhañca sammā,

Bahudhā’kāsi ṭhite jine kathāvakāti.

Thus the Lord of the World, though he has passed into Parinibbāna, has in many ways rightly worked for the welfare and happiness of the host of people by means of his own relic-body. While the Conqueror thus remains, what more is there to say?

Sujanappasādasaṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Mahāvaṃsa, composed for the faith and spiritual urgency of good people.

Dhātuagamano nāma

Named 'The Arrival of the Relic'.

Sattarasamo paricchedo.

The Seventeenth Chapter.

Aṭṭhārasama pariccheda

The Eighteenth Chapter.

Mahābodhiggahaṇo

The Reception of the Great Bodhi Tree.

1.

1.

Mahābodhiñca theriñca, āṇāpetuṃ mahīpati;

Therena vuttavacanaṃ, saramāno sake ghare.

The lord of the earth, remembering in his own house the words spoken by the Thera, resolved to send for the Great Bodhi tree and the Therī.

2.

2.

Antovasse’ka divasaṃ, nisinno therasantike;

Sahā’maccehi mantetvā, bhāgineyyaṃ sayaṃ sakaṃ.

One day during the rains-retreat, while sitting near the Thera, he consulted with his ministers concerning his own nephew.

3.

3.

Ariṭṭhanāmakā’maccaṃ[M 0.0104], tasmiṃ kamme niyojituṃ;

Mantvā āmantayitvāna, idaṃ vacanamabravi.

Having decided to appoint the minister named Ariṭṭha to that task, he summoned him and spoke this word:

4.

4.

Tā sakkhissasi…, dhammāsokassa santikā;

Mahābodhiṃ saṅghamittaṃ, theriṃ ānayituṃ idha.

Friend, will you be able to go to the presence of Dhammāsoka and bring here the Great Bodhi tree and the Therī Saṅghamittā?

5.

5.

Sakkhissāmi ahaṃ deva, ānetuṃ taṃ duve tato;

Idhā’gato pabbajituṃ, sace lacchāmi mānada.

I will be able, O king, to bring them both from there, O giver of honor, if I am permitted to go forth upon my return here.

6.

6.

Evaṃ hotūti vatvāna, rājā taṃ tattha pesayi;

So therassa ca rañño ca, sāsanaṃ gayha vandiya.

Having said, 'So be it,' the king dispatched him. He took the message of the Thera and the king, and after paying homage, departed.

7.

7.

Assayujasukkapakkhe, nikkhanto dutiye’hani;

Sānuyutto jambukole, nāvamāruyha paṭṭane.

He set out on the second day of the bright fortnight of Assayuja, and with his retinue boarded a ship at the port of Jambukola.

8.

8.

Mahodamiṃ karitvāna, therādhiṭṭhānayogato;

Nikkhantadivaseyeva, rammaṃ pupphapuraṃ agā.

Through the power of the Thera's resolution, he crossed the great ocean and on the very day of his departure arrived at the delightful city of Pupphapura.

9.

9.

Tadā tu anulādevī, pañcakaññāsatehi ca;

Antepurikaitthīnaṃ, saddhiṃ pañcasatehi ca.

At that time Queen Anulā, together with five hundred maidens and five hundred women of the royal harem,

10.

10.

Dasasīlaṃ samādāya, kāsāya vasanā suci;

Pabbajjāpekkhi nisekhā, pekkhanti theriyā’gamaṃ.

having undertaken the ten precepts and clad in ochre robes, pure and desiring to go forth, were all awaiting the arrival of the Therī.

11.

11.

Nagarasse’kadesamhi, ramme bhikkhunupassaye;

Kārāpite narindena, vāsaṃ kappesi subbatā.

The virtuous lady took up residence in a delightful nunnery built by the king in a certain part of the city.

12.

12.

Upāsikāhi tāhe’sa, vutto bhikkhunupassayo;

Upāsikā vihāroti, tena laṃkāya vissuto.

Because this nunnery was occupied by those laywomen, it became famous in Laṅkā as the 'Vihāra of the Laywomen'.

13.

13.

Bhāgineyyo mahā’riṭṭho, dhammāsokassa rājino;

Appetvā rājasandesaṃ, therasandesa’mabravi.

The great Ariṭṭha, the nephew, delivered the king's message to King Dhammāsoka and then spoke the message of the Thera.

14.

14.

Bhātujayā sahāyassa, rañño te rājakuñjara;

Ākaṅkhamānā pabbajjaṃ, niccaṃ vasati saññatā.

O elephant among kings, the sister-in-law of your friend the king, desiring to go forth, lives always in restraint.

15.

15.

Saṅghamittaṃ bhikkhuniṃ taṃ, pabbājetuṃ visajjaya;

Tāya saddhiṃ mahābodhi-dakkhiṇasākhameva ca.

Send the bhikkhunī Saṅghamittā to give her the going-forth, and with her also a southern branch of the Great Bodhi tree.

16.

16.

Theriyā ca tamevatthaṃ, abravi therabhāsitaṃ;

Gantvā pitusamīpaṃ sā, therī theramataṃ bravī.

He also told the Therī that same matter as spoken by the Thera. Going to her father's presence, that Therī conveyed the Thera's opinion.

17.

17.

Āha [M 0.0105] rājā tuvaṃ amma, apassanto kathaṃ ahaṃ;

Sokaṃ vinodayissāmi, puttanattaviyogajaṃ.

The king said: 'My dear, not seeing you, how shall I dispel the sorrow born of separation from my son and grandson?'

18.

18.

Āha sā me mahārāja, bhātuno vacanaṃ garu;

Pabbājanīyā ca bahū, gantabbaṃ tattha tena me.

She said: 'O great king, my brother's word is weighty. Many are to be ordained, and for that reason I must go there.'

19.

19.

“Satthaghātamanārahā, mahābodhimahīruhā;

Kathannu sākhaṃ gaṇissaṃ”, iti rājā vicintayī.

'The great Bodhi-tree is not to be harmed by any weapon; how then shall I get a branch from it?' Thus the king pondered.

20.

20.

Amaccassa mahādeva-nāmakassa matena so;

Bhikkhusaṅghaṃ nimantetvā, bhojetvā pucchi bhūpatiṃ.

Following the counsel of the minister named Mahādeva, the king invited the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, and having fed them, he asked a question.

21.

21.

Bhante laṃkaṃ mahābodhi, pesetabbā nu kho iti;

Thero moggaliputto so, pesetabbāti bhāsiya.

'Venerable sirs, should the Great Bodhi be sent to Laṅkā?' The Thera Moggaliputta replied, 'It should be sent.'

22.

22.

Kataṃ mahāadhiṭṭhāna-pañcakaṃ pañcacakkhunā;

Ābhāsi rañño taṃ sutvā, tussitvā dharaṇīpati.

He told the king that the five great resolutions had been made by the one with the five eyes. Hearing this, the lord of the earth was pleased.

23.

23.

Sattayojanikaṃ maggaṃ, so mahābodhigāminaṃ;

Sodhāpetvāna sakkaccaṃ, bhūsāpeti anekadhā.

He had the seven-yojana road leading to the Great Bodhi tree carefully cleared and had it adorned in many ways.

24.

24.

Suvaṇṇaṃ nīharāpesi, kaṭāhakaraṇāya ca;

Vissakammo ca āgantvā, satulādhārarūpavā.

He had gold brought out for the making of a pot. Then Vissakamma came, in the guise of a goldsmith.

25.

25.

“Kaṭāhaṃ kiṃ pamāṇaṃ nu, karomī’ti apucchitaṃ;

“Ñatvā pamāṇaṃ tvaṃyeva, karohi” iti bhāsiya.

When he asked, 'What size pot shall I make?' the king replied, 'You yourself know the measure; make it accordingly.'

26.

26.

Suvaṇṇā gahetvāna, hatthena parimajjiya;

Kaṭāhaṃ taṅkhaṇaṃyeva, nimminitvāna pakkami.

Taking the gold and molding it with his hand, he fashioned the pot in that very instant and then departed.

27.

27.

Navahatthaparikkhepaṃ, pañcahatthaṃ gabhīrato;

Tihatthavikkhambhayutaṃ, aṭṭhaṅgulaghanaṃ subhaṃ.

It was beautiful, nine cubits in circumference, five cubits deep, three cubits in diameter, and eight finger-breadths thick.

28.

28.

Yuvassa hatthino soṇḍa-pamāṇamukhavaṭṭikaṃ;

Gāhā petvāna taṃ rājā, bālasurasamappakaṃ.

Its rim was the size of a young elephant's trunk. The king had it brought, and it was as radiant as the morning sun.

29.

29.

Sattayojanadīghāya, vitthatāyati yojanaṃ;

Senāya caturaṅginyā, mahābhikkhugaṇena ca.

With the fourfold army, seven yojanas long and a yojana wide, and with a great assembly of bhikkhus,

30.

30.

Upagamma mahābodhiṃ, nānālaṅkārabhūsitaṃ;

Nānāratanacittaṃ taṃ, vividhaddhajamāliniṃ.

he approached the Great Bodhi tree, which was adorned with various ornaments, variegated with many kinds of jewels, and decked with diverse banners and garlands.

31.

31.

Nānākusumasaṃkiṇṇaṃ[M 0.0106], nānāturiyaghositaṃ;

Senāya parivāretvā, parikkhipiya sāṇiyā.

It was strewn with various flowers and filled with the sounds of various musical instruments. He surrounded it with the army and enclosed it with a curtain.

32.

32.

Mahātherasahassena, pamukhena mahāgaṇe;

Raññaṃ pattābhisekānaṃ, sahassenā’dhikena ca.

with a thousand great theras at the head of the great assembly, and with more than a thousand consecrated kings,

33.

33.

Attānaṃ parivāretvā, mahābodhiñca sādhukaṃ;

Olokesi mahābodhiṃ, paggahetvāna añjaliṃ.

Having thus surrounded himself and the Great Bodhi tree, he gazed upon the Great Bodhi tree with his hands raised in reverence.

34.

34.

Tassā dakkhiṇasākhāya, catuhatthapamāṇakaṃ;

Ṭhānaṃ khandhañca vajjetvā, sākhā antaradhāyisuṃ.

The other branches of the tree became invisible, leaving only the southern branch and a four-cubit section of the trunk.

35.

35.

Taṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ disvā, patīto puthavīpati;

“Pūjema’haṃ mahābodhiṃ, rajjenā’hi udīriya.

Seeing this miracle, the lord of the earth was pleased and declared: 'I shall honor the Great Bodhi tree with my kingdom!'

36.

36.

Abhisiñci mahābodhīṃ, mahārajje mahīpati;

Pupphādīhi mahābodhiṃ, pūjetvāna padakkhiṇaṃ.

The lord of the earth consecrated the Great Bodhi tree with the great kingship. Having venerated the Great Bodhi tree with flowers and other offerings, he circumambulated it.

37.

37.

Katvā aṭṭhasu ṭhānesu, vanditvāna katañjalī;

Suvaṇṇakhacite pīṭhe, nānāratanamaṇḍite.

Having paid homage with clasped hands at eight places, he stood on a golden stool adorned with various gems.

38.

38.

Svārohe yāva sāucce, taṃ suvaṇṇakaṭāhakaṃ;

Ṭhapāpetvāna āruyha, gahetuṃ sākhamuttamaṃ.

Having had the golden pot placed at a height he could reach, he climbed up to take the excellent branch.

39.

39.

Ādiyitvāna sovaṇṇa tulikāya manosilaṃ;

Lekhaṃ datvāna sākhāya, saccakriyamakā iti.

Taking red arsenic with a golden brush, he drew a line on the branch and made this solemn declaration of truth:

40.

40.

“Laṃkādīpaṃ yadi ito, gantabbaṃ urubodhiyā;

Nibbematiko buddhassa, sāsanamhi sace ahaṃ.

'If it is destined for this Great Bodhi branch to go from here to the island of Laṅkā, and if I am unshakable in my faith in the Buddha's Dispensation,

41.

41.

Sayaṃyeva mahābodhi-sākhāyaṃ dakkhiṇā subhā;

Chijjitvāna patiṭṭhātu, idha hemakaṭāhake.

then may this auspicious southern branch of the Great Bodhi tree sever itself and become established here in this golden pot.'

42.

42.

Lekhaṭhāne mahābodhi, chijjitvā sayameva sā;

Gandhakaddamapūrassa, kaṭāhasso’pariṭṭhitā.

At the place where the line was drawn, the Great Bodhi branch severed itself and stood poised over the pot filled with fragrant clay.

43.

43.

Mūlalekhāya upari, tiyaṅgulatiyaṅgule;

Dadaṃ manosilā lekhā, parikkhipi narissaro.

Above the main line, the lord of men drew encircling lines with red arsenic at intervals of three finger-breadths.

44.

44.

Ādiyā thūlamūlāni, khuddakāni’tarāhi tu;

Nikkhamitvā dasa dasa, jālībhūtā niotaruṃ.

From the main line, ten large roots emerged, and from the other lines, ten smaller roots each; they descended, forming a net.

45.

45.

Taṃ [M 0.0107] pāṭihāriyaṃ disvā, rājā’tīva pamodito;

Tatthevā’kāsi ukkuṭṭhiṃ, samantā parisāpi ca.

Seeing this miracle, the king was exceedingly joyful. He raised a shout of acclamation on the spot, and so did the entire assembly around him.

46.

46.

Bhikkhusaṅgho sādhukāraṃ, tuṭṭhacitto pamodayi;

Celukkhepasahassāni, pavattiṃsu samantato.

The Saṅgha of bhikkhus, with delighted minds, acclaimed it with cries of 'Sādhu!' Thousands of cloths were waved on all sides.

47.

47.

Evaṃ satena mūlānaṃ, tattha sā gandhakaddame;

Patiṭṭhāsi mahābodhi, pasādentī mahājanaṃ.

Thus with a hundred roots the Great Bodhi branch established itself in the fragrant clay, inspiring faith in the great multitude.

48.

48.

Tassā khandho dasahattho, pañcasākhā manoramā;

Catuhatthā catuhatthā, dasaḍḍhaphalamaṇḍitā.

Its trunk was ten cubits, and it had five beautiful branches, each four cubits long, adorned with five fruits.

49.

49.

Sahassantu pasākhānaṃ, sākhānaṃ tāsamāsi ca;

Evaṃ āsi mahābodhi, manoharasiridharā.

From those main branches grew a thousand smaller branches. Thus was the Great Bodhi, endowed with captivating splendour.

50.

50.

Kaṭāhamhi mahābodhi-patiṭṭhitakkhaṇe mahī;

Akampi pāṭihīrāni, ahesuṃ vividhāni ca.

At the moment the Great Bodhi was established in the pot, the earth quaked, and various miracles occurred.

51.

51.

Sayaṃ nādehi tūriyānaṃ, devesu mānusesu ca;

Sādhukāraninādeti, devabrahmagaṇassa ca.

Musical instruments among devas and humans sounded by themselves, and the hosts of devas and brahmās resounded with cries of 'Sādhu!'

52.

52.

Meghānaṃ migapakkhinaṃ, yakkhādīnaṃ ravehi ca;

Ravehicamahīkampe, ekakolāhalaṃ ahu.

With the sounds of the clouds, of beasts and birds, of yakkhas and others, and with the quaking of the earth, there arose a single great uproar.

53.

53.

Bodhiyā phalapattehi, chabbaṇṇarasmiyo subhā;

Nikkhamitvā cakkavāḷaṃ, sakalā sobhayiṃsu ca.

Beautiful six-colored rays, issuing forth from the fruits and leaves of the Bodhi tree, illuminated the entire world-sphere.

54.

54.

Sakaṭāhā mahābodhi, uggantvāna tato nabhaṃ;

Aṭṭhāsi himagabbhamhi, sattāhāni adassanā.

The Great Bodhi, together with its pot, rising from there into the sky, stood amidst a mass of clouds, unseen for seven days.

55.

55.

Rājā oruyha pīṭhamhā, taṃ sattāhaṃ tahiṃ vasaṃ;

Niccaṃ mahābodhipūjaṃ, akāsi ca anekadhā.

The king, descending from his dais, dwelt there for those seven days, constantly performing worship to the Great Bodhi in many ways.

56.

56.

Atīte tamhi sattāhe, sabbe himavalāvakā;

Pavisiṃsu mahābodhiṃ, sabbākā raṃsiyopi ca.

When that week had passed, all the masses of clouds and all the rays entered back into the Great Bodhi.

57.

57.

Suddhenakadisissittha, sākaṭāhe pattiṭṭhitā;

Mahājanassa sabbassa, mahābodhi manoramā.

The delightful Great Bodhi, established together with its pot, was clearly visible to the entire great populace.

58.

58.

Pavattamhi mahābodhi, vividhe pāṭihāriye;

Vimhāpayanti janataṃ, pathavītalamoruhi.

While various miracles were occurring, the Great Bodhi, astonishing the populace, descended to the surface of the earth.

59.

59.

Pāṭihirehi’nekehi[M 0.0108], tehi so pīṇito puna;

Mahārājā mahābodhiṃ, mahārajjena pūjayi.

Pleased again by those many miracles, the great king worshipped the Great Bodhi with his great kingdom.

60.

60.

Mahābodhiṃ mahārajje-nābhisiñciya pūjayaṃ;

Nānāpūjāhi sattāhaṃ, puna tattheva so vasi.

Having consecrated the Great Bodhi with his great kingdom and worshipping it with various offerings, he again dwelt right there for seven days.

61.

61.

Assayujasukkapakkhe, pannarasauposathe;

Aggahesi mahābodhiṃ, dvisattāhamaccaye tato.

Then, after two weeks had passed, on the fifteenth uposatha day of the bright fortnight of Assayuja, he took up the Great Bodhi.

62.

62.

Assayujakāḷapakkhe, catuddasauposathe;

Rathe subhe ṭhapetvāna, mahābodhiṃ rathesabho.

On the fourteenth uposatha day of the dark fortnight of Assayuja, the lord of chariots placed the Great Bodhi on a beautiful chariot.

63.

63.

Pūjento taṃ dinaṃyeva, upanetvā sakaṃ puraṃ;

Alaṅkaritvā bahudhā, kāretvā maṇḍapaṃ subhaṃ.

Worshipping it on that very day, he brought it to his own city and, having adorned the city in many ways, had a beautiful pavilion made.

64.

64.

Kattikasukkapakkhassa, dine pāṭipade tahiṃ;

Mahābodhiṃ mahāsāla-mūle pācinate subhe.

On the first day of the bright fortnight of Kattika, he placed the Great Bodhi there at the foot of a great, auspicious, east-facing Sāla tree.

65.

65.

Ṭhapāpetvāna kāresi, pūjā’nekā dine dine;

Gāhato sattarasame, vivase tu navaṅkirā.

Having had it placed there, he performed many acts of worship day by day. Then, on the seventeenth day from its reception, nine shoots appeared.

66.

66.

Sakiṃ yevaajāyiṃsu, tassā’nekanarādhipo;

Tuṭṭhacitto mahābodhiṃ, puna rajjena pūjayi.

They arose from it at once. The lord of many men, with a delighted heart, again worshipped the Great Bodhi with his kingdom.

67.

67.

Mahārajje’bhi siñcitvā, mahābodhiṃ mahissaro;

Kāresi ca mahābodhi-pūjā nānappakārakaṃ.

Having consecrated the Great Bodhi with his great kingdom, the great lord performed various kinds of worship for the Great Bodhi.

68.

68.

Iti kusumapure saresaraṃsā,

Bahuvidhacārudhajākulāvisālā;

Surucirapavaroru bodhipūjā,

Marunaracittavikāsinī ahosīti.

Thus in Kusumapura, a city resonant with its lakes, vast and filled with many kinds of beautiful banners, the great, excellent, and most brilliant worship of the Bodhi took place, causing the minds of gods and men to blossom.

Sujanappasādasaṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Mahāvaṃsa, made for the serene joy and spiritual urgency of good people.

Mahābodhiggahaṇo nāma

Named 'The Reception of the Great Bodhi'.

Aṭṭhārasamo paricchedo.

The Eighteenth Chapter.

Ekūnavīsatima pariccheda

The Nineteenth Chapter.

Bodhi āgamano

The Arrival of the Bodhi Tree.

1.

1.

Mahābodhirakkhaṇatthaṃ[M 0.0109], aṭṭhārasa rathe sabho;

Devakulāni datvāna, aṭṭhāmaccā kulāni ca.

For the protection of the Great Bodhi, the lord of chariots gave eighteen guardian families and eight families of ministers.

2.

2.

Aṭṭha brāhmaṇakulāni, aṭṭha vassakulāni ca;

Gopakānaṃ taracchānaṃ, kuliṅgānaṃ kulāni ca.

Eight brahmin families, eight merchant families, and also families of cowherds, Taracchas, and Kuliṅgas.

3.

3.

Tatheva pesakārānaṃ, kumbhakārānameva ca;

Sabbe sañcāpi senīnaṃ, nāgayakkhānameva ca.

Likewise, families of weavers and potters, and from all the guilds, and also of the nāgas and yakkhas.

4.

4.

Hemasajjughaṭeceva, datvā aṭṭhaṭṭha mānado;

Āropetvā mahābodhiṃ, nāvaṃ gaṅgāya bhūsitaṃ.

The giver of honor, having given eight of each kind of new golden pitcher, placed the Great Bodhi on a ship adorned for the Ganges.

5.

5.

Saṅghamitta mahātherī, sahe kadasa bhikkhuniṃ;

Tathevā’ropayitvāna, ariṭṭhapamukhepi ca.

He likewise embarked the great Theri Saṅghamittā with eleven bhikkhunīs, and also those headed by Ariṭṭha.

6.

6.

Nagarā nikkhamitvāna, viñjāṭavimaticcaso;

Tāmalitthiṃ anuppatto, sattāhene’va bhūpati.

Having departed from the city and crossed the Vindhya forest, the king reached Tāmalitti in just seven days.

7.

7.

Accuḷā rāhi pūjāyi, devānāgānarāpi ca;

Mahābodhiṃ pūjayantā, sattāhena’vupāgamuṃ.

Devas, nāgas, and humans, worshipping the great Bodhi tree with magnificent offerings, arrived in seven days.

8.

8.

Mahāsamuddatīramhi, mahābodhiṃ mahīpati;

Ṭhapāpetvāna pūjesi, mahārajjena so puna.

On the shore of the great ocean, the lord of the earth had the great Bodhi tree set down and worshipped it again with his great kingdom.

9.

9.

Mahābodhiṃ mahārajje, abhisiñcīyakāmado;

Aggasira sukkapakkhe, dine pāṭipade tato.

Then, on the first day of the bright fortnight of the month Māgasira, the king, the granter of wishes, consecrated the great Bodhi tree with his great kingdom.

10.

10.

Uccāretuṃ mahābodhiṃ, tehiyeva’ṭṭha aṭṭhahi;

Sālamūlamhi dinnehi, dhātuggatakulehi so.

He had the great Bodhi tree lifted up by those very eight times eight families who had been appointed.

11.

11.

Ukkhipitvā mahābodhiṃ, galamattaṃ jalaṃ tahiṃ;

Ogāhetvā sanāvāya, patiṭṭhāpayi sādhukaṃ.

Having entered the water up to his neck, he took up the great Bodhi tree and established it securely upon the ship.

12.

12.

Nāvaṃ [M 0.0110] āropayitvā taṃ, mahātheriṃ satherikaṃ;

Mahāriṭṭhaṃ mahāmaccaṃ, idaṃ vacanamabravi.

Having embarked the great Theri and her companions on the ship, he spoke these words to the great minister Mahāriṭṭha.

13.

13.

“Ahaṃ rajjena tikkhattuṃ, mahābodhimapūjayiṃ;

Eva mevā’bhi pūjetu, rājā rajjena me sakhā”.

“I have worshipped the great Bodhi tree three times with my kingdom. In this same way, may the king my friend also worship it with his kingdom.”

14.

14.

Idaṃ vatvā mahārājā, tīre pañjaliko ṭhito;

Gacchamānaṃ mahābodhiṃ, passaṃ assūnivattayi.

Having said this, the great king stood on the shore with his hands raised in reverence and, watching the great Bodhi tree departing, he shed tears.

15.

15.

Mahābodhi viyogena,

Dhammā soko sasokavā;

Kannitvā paridevitvā,

Agamāsi sakaṃ puraṃ.

Sorrowful because of his separation from the great Bodhi tree, Dhammāsoka wept and lamented, and then returned to his own city.

16.

16.

Mahābodhi samāruḷhā, nāvāpakkhandhī toyadhiṃ;

Samantā yojane vicī, sannisīdi mahaṇṇave.

The ship with the great Bodhi tree on board plunged into the sea, and for a yojana all around, the waves in the great ocean grew still.

17.

17.

Pupphiṃsu pañcavaṇṇāni, padumāni samantato;

Antalikkhe pavajjiṃsu, aneka tūriyāni ca.

Five-colored lotuses bloomed all around, and in the sky countless musical instruments played.

18.

18.

Devatāhi anekāhi, pūjā’nekā pavattitā;

Gahetuñca mahābodhi, nāgā’kāsuṃ vikubbanaṃ.

Many devatās performed various kinds of worship. And in order to seize the great Bodhi tree, the nāgas created a magical display.

19.

19.

Saṅghamittā mahātheri, abhiññābalapāragā;

Supaṇṇarūpā hutvāna, te tāsesi mahorage.

The great Theri Saṅghamittā, who had perfected the power of the higher knowledges, assumed the form of a Supaṇṇa and terrified those great serpents.

20.

20.

Te tāsitā mahātheriṃ, yācitvāna mahoragā;

Nayitvāna mahābemadhiṃ, bhujaṅgabhavanaṃ tato.

Terrified, the great serpents begged the great Theri and then led the great Bodhi tree to their serpent abode.

21.

21.

Sattāhaṃ nāgarajjena, pūjāhi vividhāhi ca;

Pūjayitvāna ānetvā, nāvāyaṃ ṭhapayiṃsu te.

Having worshipped it for seven days with the honors of the nāga kingdom and with various offerings, they brought it back and placed it on the ship.

22.

22.

Tadaheva mahābodhi, jambukolamidhagamā;

Devānaṃpiyatisso tu, rājā lokahite rato.

On that very day the great Bodhi tree arrived here at Jambukola. King Devānaṃpiyatissa, who was devoted to the welfare of the world,

23.

23.

Sumanā sāmaṇeramhā, pubbe sutatadāgamo;

Maggasirādidinagho, pabhuti vacasādaro.

having previously heard of its arrival from the novice Sumana, from the first day of the month Māgasira onwards, was awaiting it with anticipation.

24.

24.

Uttaradvārato [M 0.0111] yāva, jambukolaṃ mahāpathaṃ;

Vibhūsayitvā sakalaṃ, mahābodhigatāsayo.

With his mind intent upon the great Bodhi tree, he had the entire great road from the north gate to Jambukola adorned.

25.

25.

Samuddāsanasālāya, ṭhāne ṭhatvā mahaṇṇave;

Āgacchantaṃ mahābodhiṃ, mahātheriddhiyā’ddasa.

Standing at the site of the Ocean-Viewing Hall and looking out at the great ocean, he saw the great Bodhi tree approaching by means of the great Thera's psychic power.

26.

26.

Tasmiṃṭhāne katā sālā, pakā setuṃ tamabbhutaṃ;

Samuddāsanasālāti, nāmenā‘si’dha pākaṭā.

The hall built at that place to proclaim that marvel became famous here by the name Samuddāsana-sālā, the Ocean-Viewing Hall.

27.

27.

Mahātherānubhāvena, saddhiṃ therehi tehi ca;

Tadaheva’gamā rājā, jambukolaṃ sa senako.

By the spiritual power of the great Thera, the king, together with those theras and his army, went to Jambukola on that very day.

28.

28.

Mahābodhā gamepīti-vegenu’nno udānayaṃ;

Galappamāṇaṃ salilaṃ, vigāhetvā suviggaho.

Uplifted by a surge of joy at the arrival of the great Bodhi tree, the king, handsome in form, uttered an inspired utterance and plunged into the water up to his neck.

29.

29.

Mahābodhiṃ soḷasahi, kulehi saha muddhanā;

Ādāyo’ropayitvāna, velāyaṃ maṇḍape subhe.

He took the great Bodhi tree upon his head and, together with the sixteen families, brought it ashore and placed it in a beautiful pavilion.

30.

30.

Ṭhapayitvāna laṃkindo, laṃkārajjena pūjayi;

Soḷasannaṃ samappetvā, kulānaṃ rajjamattano.

Having established it, the Lord of Laṅkā worshipped it with the kingdom of Laṅkā, entrusting his own kingdom to the sixteen families.

31.

31.

Sayaṃ dovārikaṭhāne, ṭhatvāna divase tayo;

Tattheva pūjaṃ kāresi, vividhaṃ manujādhipo.

Standing himself in the position of a gatekeeper for three days, the lord of men had various acts of worship performed right there.

32.

32.

Mahābodhiṃ dasamiyaṃ, āropetvā rathesubhe;

Ānayanto manussindo, dumindaṃ taṃ ṭhapāpayi.

On the tenth day, the lord of men placed the great Bodhi tree on a splendid chariot and, bringing that lord of trees along, had it set down

33.

33.

Pācinassa vihārassa, ṭhāne ṭhānavicakkhaṇo;

Pātarāsaṃ pavattesi, sasaṅghassa janassa so.

at the site of the eastern monastery. Discerning the proper place, he provided the morning meal there for the Sangha and the people.

34.

34.

Mahāmahindathere’ttha, kataṃ dasabalena taṃ;

Kathesi nāgadamanaṃ, rañño tassa asesato.

There, the great Thera Mahinda recounted fully to the king the Taming of the Nāga, which was accomplished by the one with Ten Powers.

35.

35.

Therassa sutvā kāretvā, saññāṇāni tahiṃ tahiṃ;

Paribhuttesu ṭhānesu, nisajjādīhi satthunā.

Hearing the Elder, the king had markers made here and there in the places used by the Teacher for sitting and so on.

36.

36.

Tivakkassa brāhmaṇassa, gāmadvāre ca bhūpati;

Ṭhapāpetvā mahābodhiṃ, ṭhānesu tesu tesu ca.

The king had the great Bodhi tree set down at the village gate of the brahmin Tivakka and at those various other places.

37.

37.

Suddhavāluka santhāre, nānāpupphasamākule;

Paggahitadhaje magge, pupphagghikavibhūsite.

Along the path, spread with pure sand, strewn with various flowers, with banners raised and adorned with floral arches,

38.

38.

Mahābodhiṃ [M 0.0112] pūjayanto, rattindiva matandito;

Ānayitvā cuddasiyaṃ, anurādha purantikaṃ.

he worshipped the great Bodhi tree tirelessly day and night, and on the fourteenth day brought it to the vicinity of Anurādhapura.

39.

39.

Vaḍḍhamānakacchāyāya, puraṃ sādhu vibhūsitaṃ;

Uttarena ca dvārena, pūjayanto pavesiya.

Making offerings, he had it enter the beautifully adorned city through the northern gate and brought it to the shade of the Vaḍḍhamāna tree.

40.

40.

Dakkhiṇena ca dvārena, nikkhamitvā pavesiya;

Mahā meghavanārāmaṃ, catubuddhanisevitaṃ.

Exiting through the southern gate, he had it enter the great Mahāmeghavana park, a place frequented by the four Buddhas.

41.

41.

Sumanasseva vacasā, padesaṃ sādhusaṅkhataṃ;

Pubbabodhiṭhitaṭṭhānaṃ, upanetvā manoramaṃ.

Following the words of Sumana, he brought it to the delightful and well-prepared place where the previous Bodhi trees had stood.

42.

42.

Kulehi so soḷasahi, rājā laṅkāradhārihi;

Oropetvā mahābodhiṃ, patiṭṭhā petu mossajji.

The king, guardian of Laṅkā, together with the sixteen families, lowered the great Bodhi tree and released it to establish itself.

43.

43.

Hatthato muttamattasā, asītiratanaṃ nabhaṃ;

Uggantvāna ṭhitā muñci, chabbaṇṇā rasmiyo subhā.

As soon as it was released from their hands, it rose eighty cubits into the sky and, standing there, emitted beautiful six-colored rays.

44.

44.

Dīpe patthariyā’hacca, brahmalokaṃ ṭhitā ahu;

Sūriyatthaṅgamanāyāva, rasmiyo tā manoramā.

Spreading over the island and reaching up to the Brahmā world, those delightful rays remained until sunset.

45.

45.

Purisā dasasahassāni, pasannā pāṭihāriye;

Vipassitvānā’rahatthaṃ, patvāna idha pabbajuṃ.

Ten thousand men, their hearts inspired by the miracle, developed insight, attained arahantship, and went forth into homelessness right there.

46.

46.

Orohitvā mahābodhi, sūriyatthaṅgame tato;

Rohiṇiyā patiṭṭhāsi, mahiyaṃ kampi medinī.

At sunset, the great Bodhi tree descended and established itself on the earth under the constellation Rohiṇī, and the earth quaked.

47.

47.

Mūlāni tāni uggantvā, kaṭāhamukhavaṭṭito;

Vinandhantā kaṭāhaṃ taṃ, otariṃsu mahītalaṃ.

Its roots, springing up from the rim of the pot and enveloping it, descended into the earth.

48.

48.

Patiṭṭhitaṃ mahābodhiṃ, janā sabbe samagatā;

Gandhamālādi pūjāhi, pūjayiṃsu samantato.

When the great Bodhi tree was established, all the people gathered and worshipped it from all sides with perfumes, garlands, and other offerings.

49.

49.

Mahāmegho pavassittha, himagabbhā samantato;

Mahābodhiṃ chādayiṃsu, sītalāni ghanāni ca.

A great cloud poured rain, and from all sides cool, dense mists enveloped the great Bodhi tree.

50.

50.

Sattāhāni mahābodhiṃ, tahiṃyeva adassanā;

Himagabbhe sannisīdi, pasādajananī jane.

For seven days the great Bodhi tree remained there, unseen within the mass of mist, inspiring faith in the people.

51.

51.

Sattāhā tikkame meghā, sabbe apagamiṃsu te;

Mahābodhi ca dissittha, chabbaṇṇā raṃsiyopi ca.

When seven days had passed, all those clouds dispersed, and the great Bodhi tree became visible, along with its six-colored rays.

52.

52.

Mahāmahindattheroca, saṅghamittā ca bhikkhunī;

Tatthā’gañchuṃsaparisā, rājā saparisopi ca.

The Elder Mahāmahinda and the bhikkhunī Saṅghamittā, with their retinues, and the king also with his retinue, came there.

53.

53.

Khattiyā [M 0.0113] kājaraggāme, candanaggāma khattiyā;

Tivakka brāhmaṇo ceva, dīpavāsī janāpi ca.

The khattiyas of Kājaraggāma, the khattiyas of Candanaggāma, Tivakka the brāhmaṇa, and also the inhabitants of the island,

54.

54.

Devānubhāvenā’gañchuṃ, mahābodhi mahussukkā;

Mahāsamāgame tasmiṃ, pāṭihāriyavimhite.

By the power of the devas, they came with great zeal to the Great Bodhi. In that great assembly, they were astonished by the miracle.

55.

55.

Pakkaṃ pācinasākhāya, pekkhataṃ pakka’makkhataṃ;

Thero patantamādāya, ropetuṃ rājino adā.

A ripe, unblemished fruit from the eastern branch fell while all were watching. The Elder, taking it as it fell, gave it to the king to plant.

56.

56.

Paṃsūnaṃ gandhamissānaṃ, puṇṇe soṇṇa kaṭāhake;

Mahāsanassa ṭhāne taṃ, ṭhapitaṃ ropa’yissaro.

The lord planted it in a golden vessel filled with fragrant, mixed soil, in the place of the great assembly.

57.

57.

Pekkhataṃyeva sabbesaṃ, uggantvā aṭṭha aṅkurā;

Jāyiṃsu bodhitaruṇā, aṭṭhaṃsu catuhatthakā.

While all were watching, eight shoots sprouted forth; eight young Bodhi trees arose, four cubits high.

58.

58.

Rājā te bodhitaruṇe, disvā vimhitamānaso;

Setacchattena pūjesi, abhisekamadāsi ca.

Seeing those young Bodhi trees, the king, with his mind full of wonder, honored them with a white parasol and also bestowed the consecration.

59.

59.

Patiṭṭhāpesi aṭṭhannaṃ, jambukolamhi paṭṭane;

Mahābodhi ṭhita ṭhāne, nāvāyo rohane tadā.

He then planted one of the eight at the port of Jambukola, at the place where the Great Bodhi tree had stood upon being disembarked from the ship.

60.

60.

Tivakkabrāhmaṇagāme, thūpārāme tatheva ca;

Issarasamaṇārāme, paṭhame cetiyaṅgaṇe.

In the village of the brāhmaṇa Tivakka, likewise at the Thūpārāma, at the Issarasamaṇārāma, and in the courtyard of the First Cetiya.

61.

61.

Cetiya pabbatā rāme, tathā kājaragāmake;

Candanagāmake cāti, ekekaṃ bodhilaṭṭhikaṃ.

At the monastery of the Cetiya mountain, likewise in Kājaragāma, and in Candanagāma, he planted one Bodhi-sapling in each.

62.

62.

Sesā catupakkajātā, dvattiṃsa bodhilaṭṭhiyo;

Samantā yojanaṭhāne, vihāresu tahiṃ tahiṃ.

The remaining thirty-two Bodhi-saplings, which sprang from four fruits, were planted in various monasteries here and there, at a distance of one yojana all around.

63.

63.

Dīpāvāsī janasseva, hitatthāya patiṭṭhite;

Mahābodhi dumindamhi, sammāsambuddha tejasā.

For the welfare of the inhabitants of the island they were established. By the majesty of the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, the Great Bodhi, the king of trees, stands there.

64.

64.

Anulāsāsa parisā, saṅghamittāya theriyā;

Santike pabbajitvāna, arahattamapāpuṇi.

Anulā and her retinue went forth in the presence of the Elder Saṅghamittā and attained Arahantship.

65.

65.

Ariṭṭho so pañcasata-parivāro ca khattiyo;

Therantike pabbajitvā, arahattamapāpuṇi.

The khattiya Ariṭṭha, together with his retinue of five hundred, went forth in the presence of the Elder and attained Arahantship.

66.

66.

Yāni seṭṭhikulāna’ṭṭha-mahābodhimidhāharuṃ;

Bodhāharakulānīti, tāni tena pavuccare.

The eight chief families that brought the Great Bodhi here were for that reason called the 'Bodhi-bringer families'.

67.

67.

Upāsikā vihāroti, ñāte bhikkhunupassaye;

Sasaṅghā saṅghamittā sā, mahātherī tahiṃ vasi.

In the nunnery known as the Upāsikā-vihāra, the Great Elder Saṅghamittā dwelt together with her Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs.

68.

68.

Agārattayapāmokkhe[M 0.0114], agāre tattha kārayi;

Dvādasa tesu ekasmiṃ, mahāgāre ṭhapāpayi.

She had twelve dwellings built there, with three being pre-eminent. In one of these great dwellings she had the mast of the ship placed.

69.

69.

Mahābodhisametāya, nāvāya kūpayaṭṭhikaṃ;

Ekasmiṃ piya mekasmiṃ, arittaṃ tehi teviduṃ.

The mast of the ship that came with the Great Bodhi was placed in one building, the rudder in another, and the oar in a third; so the wise have related.

70.

70.

Jāte aññanikāyepi, agārā dvādasāpi te;

Hatthāḷaka bhikkhunīhi, vaḷañjayiṃsu sabbadā.

Even when other sects arose, those twelve dwellings were always used by the bhikkhunīs of the Hatthāḷhaka convent.

71.

71.

Rañño maṅgalahatthi so, vicaranto yathāsukhaṃ;

Purassa ekapassamhi, kandarantamhi sītale.

The king's state elephant, wandering about as it pleased on one side of the city, in a cool grotto,

72.

72.

Kadambapupphagumbante, aṭṭhāsi gocaraṃ caraṃ;

Hatthiṃ tattharataṃ ñatvā, akaṃsu tattha āḷhakaṃ.

stood near a thicket of Kadamba flowers, seeking its pasture. Knowing the elephant was delighted there, they built a stable for it on that spot.

73.

73.

Atheka divasaṃ hatthī, nagaṇhi kabaḷāni so;

Dīpappasādakaṃ theraṃ, rājā so pucchitaṃ mataṃ.

Then one day that elephant would not take its food. The king asked the opinion of the Elder, the illuminator of the island.

74.

74.

Kadambapupphagumbasmiṃ, thūpassa karaṇaṃ karī;

Icchatīti mahāthero, mahārājassa abravi.

The Great Elder told the great king: 'The elephant wishes for a thūpa to be built at the thicket of Kadamba flowers.'

75.

75.

Sadhātukaṃ tattha thūpaṃ, thūpassa gharameva ca;

Khippaṃ rājā akāresi, niccaṃ janahiterato.

The king, who was always intent on the welfare of the people, quickly had a thūpa containing relics built there, and also a house for the thūpa.

76.

76.

Saṅghamittā mahātherī, suññāgārābhilāsinī;

Ākiṇṇattā vihārassa, vussamānassa tassa sā.

The Great Elder Saṅghamittā, desiring a solitary dwelling, since that monastery where she was living was crowded,

77.

77.

Vuddhatthinī sāsanassa, bhikkhunīnaṃ hitāya ca;

Bhikkhunupassayaṃ aññaṃ, icchamānā vicakkhaṇā.

and since she, the wise one, desiring the growth of the Dispensation and the welfare of the bhikkhunīs, wished for another nunnery,

78.

78.

Gantvā cetiyagehaṃ taṃ, pavivekasukhaṃ bhusaṃ;

Divāvihāraṃ kappesi, vihārakusalā’malā.

she, the pure one skilled in the practice of dwelling, went to that cetiya-house and made it her day-abode, enjoying the great bliss of seclusion.

79.

79.

Theriyā vandanatthāya, rājā bhikkhunupassayaṃ;

Gantvā tattha gataṃ sutvā, gantvāna tattha vandiya.

The king went to the nunnery to pay homage to the Elder. Hearing she had gone there, he went to that place and paid homage to her.

80.

80.

Sammoditvā tāya saddhiṃ, tatthāgamanakāraṇaṃ;

Tassā ñatvā adhippāyaṃ, adhippāya vidū vidū.

Having exchanged friendly greetings with her, the wise king, an expert in discerning intentions, understood her purpose in coming there.

81.

81.

Samantā thūpagehassa, rammaṃ bhikkhunupassayaṃ;

Devānaṃpiyatisso so, mahārājā akārayi.

That great king, Devānaṃpiyatissa, had a delightful nunnery built all around the thūpa-house.

82.

82.

Hatthāḷhakasamīpamhi[M 0.0115], kato bhikkhunupassayo;

Hatthāḷhakavihāroti, vissuto āsi tena so.

Because the nunnery was built near the elephant stable (hatthāḷhaka), it became known as the Hatthāḷhaka-vihāra.

83.

83.

Sumittā saṅghamittā sā, mahātherī mahāmatī;

Tasmiñhi vāsaṃ kappesi, ramme bhikkhunupassaye.

That good friend, the Great Elder Saṅghamittā, the greatly wise one, took up her residence in that delightful nunnery.

84.

84.

Evaṃ laṃkā lokahitaṃ sāsanavuddhiṃ;

Saṃsodhento esa mahābodhi dumindo;

Laṃkādīpe ramme mahāmeghavanasmiṃ,

Aṭṭhā sīghaṃ kālamanekabbhūtayuttoti.

Thus this Great Bodhi, the king of trees, stood for a long time in the delightful Mahāmeghavana on the isle of Laṅkā, purifying the island, promoting the welfare of the world and the growth of the Dispensation, and endowed with many wonders.

Sujanappasādasaṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Mahāvaṃsa, compiled for the serene joy and emotion of good people,

Bodhiāgamano nāma

Named 'The Arrival of the Bodhi Tree',

Ekūnavīsatimo paricchedo.

The Nineteenth Chapter.

Vīsatima pariccheda

The Twentieth Chapter

Theraparinibbānaṃ

The Final Nibbāna of the Elders

1.

1.

Aṭṭhārasamhi vassamhi, dhammāsokassa rājino;

Mahāmeghavanārāme, mahābodhi patiṭṭhati.

In the eighteenth year of King Dhammāsoka, the great Bodhi tree was established in the Mahāmeghavana Park.

2.

2.

Tato dvādasame vasse, mahesī tassa rājino;

Piyā asandhīmittā sā, matā sambuddhamāmakā.

Then, twelve years later, the chief queen of that king, his beloved Asandhimittā, a devotee of the Sambuddha, died.

3.

3.

Tato catutthe vassamhi, dhammāsoko mahīpati;

Tissarakkha mahesitte, ṭhapesi visamāsayaṃ.

Then, four years after that, the lord of the earth Dhammāsoka raised the wicked-minded Tissarakkhā to the rank of chief queen.

4.

4.

Tato tu tatiye vasse, sābālā rūpamāninī;

“Mayāpi ca ayaṃ rājā, mahābodhiṃ ma māyati”.

Then, three years after that, that foolish woman, proud of her beauty, thought: ‘This king cherishes the great Bodhi tree, but not me.’

5.

5.

Iti kodhavasaṃ gantvā, attano’nattha kārikā;

Maṇḍukaṇṭakayogena, mahābodhi maghā tayi.

Thus, falling prey to anger, the author of her own ruin, she had the great Bodhi tree injured by means of a maṇḍu-thorn.

6.

6.

Tato [M 0.0116] ca tutthevassamhi, dhammā soko mahāyaso;

Anicca tāva saṃpatto, sattatiṃsasamā ime.

And in the fourth year after that, Dhammāsoka of great fame came to his end. These were his thirty-seven years of reign.

7.

7.

Devānaṃ piyatisso tu, rājā dhammaguṇe rato;

Mahāvihāre navakammaṃ, tathā cetiyapabbate.

King Devānampiyatissa, delighting in the qualities of the Dhamma, undertook new construction work at the Mahāvihāra and likewise at Cetiyapabbata.

8.

8.

Thūpārāme navakammaṃ, niṭṭhāpetvā yathārahaṃ;

Dīpappasādakaṃ theraṃ, pucchi pucchitakovidaṃ.

Having fittingly completed the new work at the Thūpārāma, he questioned the Elder, the Illuminator of the Island, who was skilled in answering questions.

9.

9.

Kārāpessamahaṃ bhante, vihāresu bahū idha;

Patiṭṭhāpetuṃ thūpesu, kathaṃ lacchāma dhātuyo.

‘Venerable sir, I will have many monasteries built here. How shall we obtain relics to enshrine in the stūpas?’

10.

10.

Sambuddhapattaṃ pūretvā, sumanenā’haṭā idha;

Cetiyapabbate rāja, ṭhapitā atthi dhātuyo.

‘The relics that were brought here by the novice Sumana, filling the Sambuddha’s bowl, have been placed on Cetiyapabbata, O king.’

11.

11.

Hatthikkhandhe ṭhapetvā tā, dhātuyo idha āhara;

Iti vutto satherena, tathā āhari dhātuyo.

‘Having placed those relics on the back of an elephant, bring them here.’ Thus addressed by the Elder, the king brought the relics accordingly.

12.

12.

Vihāre kārayitvāna, ṭhāne yojanayojane;

Dhātuyo tattha thūpesu, nidhāpesi yathārahaṃ.

Having had monasteries built at intervals of a yojana, he had the relics fittingly enshrined in the stūpas there.

13.

13.

Sambuddhabhuttapattaṃ tu, rājavatthughare subhe;

Ṭhapayitvāna pūjesi, nānāpūjāhi sabbadā.

He placed the bowl used by the Sambuddha in a beautiful royal building and always venerated it with various kinds of offerings.

14.

14.

Pañcasatehi’ssareti, mahātherassa santike;

Pabbajjavasitaṭhāne, issarasamaṇako ahu.

Because five hundred nobles went forth into homelessness in the presence of the great Elder, the place where they dwelt after ordination became the Issarasamaṇaka Vihāra.

15.

15.

Pañcasatehi vassehi, mahātherassa santike;

Pabbajjavasitaṭhāne, tathā vassagiri ahu.

Likewise, because five hundred people of the merchant class went forth in the presence of the great Elder, the place where they dwelt after ordination became the Vassagiri Vihāra.

16.

16.

Yā yā mahāmahindena, therena vasitā guhā;

Sapabbatavihāresu, sā mahindaguhā ahu.

Whichever cave in any of the mountain monasteries was inhabited by the great Elder Mahinda, that came to be known as Mahinda’s Cave.

17.

17.

Mahāvihāraṃ paṭhamaṃ, dutiyaṃ cetiyavhayaṃ;

Thūpārāmaṃ tu tatiyaṃ, thūpapubbaṅgamaṃ subhaṃ.

The Mahāvihāra was the first, the Cetiyavihāra the second, and the beautiful Thūpārāma, distinguished by its stūpa, was the third.

18.

18.

Catutthaṃ tu mahābodhi-patiṭṭhāpanameva ca;

Thūpaṭhānīyabhūtassa, pañcamaṃ pana sādhukaṃ.

The fourth was the establishment of the great Bodhi tree itself; and the fifth was the proper establishment at the place that was to be the site of the Great Stūpa:

19.

19.

Mahācetiyaṭhānamhi, silāthūpassa cāruno;

Sambuddhagīvādhātussa, patiṭṭhāpanameva ca.

namely, the enshrinement of the Sambuddha’s collar-bone relic in the beautiful stone stūpa at the site of the Great Cetiya.

20.

20.

Issarasamaṇaṃ [M 0.0117] chaṭṭhaṃ, tissavāpintusattamaṃ;

Aṭṭhamaṃ paṭhamaṃ thūpaṃ, navamaṃ vassagirivhayaṃ.

The Issarasamaṇa Vihāra was the sixth, the Tissavāpi the seventh, the Paṭhama-thūpa the eighth, and the one named Vassagiri the ninth.

21.

21.

Upāsikāvhayaṃ rammaṃ, tathā hatthāḷhakavhayaṃ;

Bhikkhunupassake dve’me, bhikkhunī phāsukāraṇā.

For the comfort of the bhikkhunīs, he built these two nunneries: the delightful one named Upāsikā Vihāra and the one named Hatthāḷhaka Vihāra.

22.

22.

Hatthāḷhake osaritvā, bhikkhunīnaṃ upassaye;

Gantvāna bhikkhusaṅghena, bhattaggahaṇakāraṇā.

For the purpose of the Saṅgha of bhikkhus receiving their meal, a path was made for going to the nunnery, descending at the Hatthāḷhaka Vihāra.

23.

23.

Hattasālaṃ sūpahāraṃ, mahāpāḷikanāmakaṃ;

Sabbupakaraṇūpetaṃ, sampattaparicārikaṃ.

He also built the great refectory named Mahāpāḷi, which provided curry, was endowed with all necessary equipment, and was supplied with attendants.

24.

24.

Tathā bhikkhusahassassa, saparikkhāramuttamaṃ;

Pavāraṇāya dānañca, anuvassakameva ca.

Likewise, he established an annual gift for the Pavāraṇā ceremony for a thousand bhikkhus, providing them with the best of requisites.

25.

25.

Nāgadīpe jambukola-vihāraṃ ta mhipaṭṭane;

Tissamahāvihārañca, pācīnārāma meva ca.

He built the Jambukola Vihāra at the seaport of that name in Nāgadīpa, and also the Tissamahāvihāra and the Pācīnārāma.

26.

26.

Iti etāni kammāni, laṃkājanahitatthiko;

Devānaṃpiyatisso so, laṃkindo puññapaññavā.

Thus that lord of Laṅkā, Devānampiyatissa, who possessed merit and wisdom and sought the welfare of the people of Laṅkā, performed these works.

27.

27.

Paṭhameyeva vassamhi, kārāpesi guṇappiyo;

Yāva jīvantunekāni, puññakammāni ācini.

This lover of virtue had these built in the very first year of his reign, and for as long as he lived he accumulated numerous meritorious deeds.

28.

28.

Ayaṃ dīpo ahu ṭhito, vijite tassa rājino;

Vassāni cattālīsaṃ so, rājā rajjamakārayi.

This island was secure in the dominion of that king. For forty years that king reigned over the kingdom.

29.

29.

Tassa’cca ye taṃ kaniṭṭho, uttiyo iti vissuto;

Rājaputto aputtaṃ taṃ, rajjaṃ kāresi sādhukaṃ.

After his death, since he was without a son, his younger brother, the prince known as Uttiya, ruled the kingdom well.

30.

30.

Mahāmahindatthero tu, jinasāsanamuttamaṃ;

Pariyattiṃ paṭipattiṃ, paṭivedhañca sādhukaṃ.

The great Elder Mahinda, having well established the supreme Dispensation of the Victor in Laṅkā—its scriptural learning, its practice, and its penetration—

31.

31.

Laṃkādīpamhi dīpetvā, laṃkādīpo mahāgaṇi;

Laṃkāyaso satthu kappo, katvā laṃkāhitaṃ bahuṃ.

that Lamp of Laṅkā, that great teacher, the glory of Laṅkā, like the Teacher himself, having brought much welfare to Laṅkā,

32.

32.

Tassa uttiyarājassa, jayavassamhi aṭṭhame;

Antovassaṃ saṭṭhivasso, cetiyapabbate vasaṃ.

in the eighth year of the reign of King Uttiya, while dwelling on Cetiyapabbata during the rains-retreat at the age of sixty,

33.

33.

Assayujassa māsassa, sukkapakkhaṭhame dine;

Parinibbāyite netaṃ, dinaṃ tannāmakaṃ ahu.

that leader attained Parinibbāna on the eighth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Assayuja. That day became known by his name.

34.

34.

[Nibbutassa [M 0.0118] mahindassa, aṭṭhamiyaṃ dine pana,

Tena taṃ divasaṃ nāma, aṭṭhamiyāti sammataṃ.]

[Since the great Mahinda passed away on the eighth day, that day is known as ‘the eighth.’]

35.

35.

Taṃ sutvā uttiyo rājā, sokasallasamappito;

Gantvāna theraṃ vanditvā kanditvā bahudhā bahuṃ.

When King Uttiya heard this, he was struck by the arrow of grief. He went and paid homage to the Elder’s body and wept long and in many ways.

36.

36.

Āsittagandhatelāya, bahuṃ sovaṇṇadoṇiyā;

Theradebhaṃ khipāpetvā, taṃ doṇiṃ sādhuphussitaṃ.

He had the Elder’s body placed in a golden coffin filled with fragrant oil, and had the coffin well closed.

37.

37.

Sovaṇṇakūṭāgāramhi, ṭhapāpetvā alaṅkate;

Kūṭāgāraṃ gāhayitvā, kārento sādhukīḷitaṃ.

He had the coffin placed on an adorned golden bier, and taking up the bier, he ordered solemn funeral ceremonies to be held.

38.

38.

Mahatā ca janoghena, āgatenatato tato;

Mahatā ca baloghena, kārento pūjanāvidhiṃ.

With a great flood of people who had come from here and there, and with a great host of his army, he had the rites of veneration performed.

39.

39.

Alaṅkatena maggena, bahudhā’laṅkataṃ puraṃ;

Ānayitvāna nagare, cāretvā rājavīthiyo.

He had the bier brought into the city, which was adorned in many ways, along a decorated road, and had it paraded through the royal streets.

40.

40.

Mahāvihāraṃ ānetvā, ettha pañhambamāḷake;

Kuṭāgāraṃ ṭhapāpetvā, sattāhaṃ so mahīpati.

Having brought it to the Mahāvihāra, that lord of the earth had the bier placed on the Pañhamba terrace, and for seven days

41.

41.

Toraṇaddhajapupphehi, gandhapuṇṇaghaṭehi ca;

Vihārañca samantā ca, maṇḍihaṃ yojanattayaṃ.

he had the monastery and the area for three yojanas around it adorned with arches, banners, flowers, and pots full of incense.

42.

42.

Ahu rājānubhāvena, dīpantu sakalaṃ pana;

Ānubhāvena devānaṃ, tathevā’laṅkataṃ ahu.

By the king’s power the entire island was adorned, and likewise it was adorned by the power of the devas.

43.

43.

Nānāpūjaṃ kārayitvā, sattāhaṃ so mahīpati;

Puratthimadisābhāge, therānaṃ baddhamāḷake.

Having had various offerings made for seven days, that lord of the earth, in the eastern direction, on the terrace built for the Elders,

44.

44.

Kāretvā gandhacitakaṃ, mahāthūpaṃ padakkhiṇaṃ;

Karonto tattha netvā taṃ, kūṭāgāraṃ manoramaṃ.

had a pyre of fragrant wood made. Then, circumambulating the Great Stūpa, he brought the delightful bier there.

45.

45.

Citakamhi ṭhapāpetvā, sakkāraṃ antimaṃ akā;

Cetiyañcettha kāresi, gāhā petvāna dhātuyo.

Having had the body placed on the pyre, he performed the last honors. And he had a cetiya built there after collecting the relics.

46.

46.

Upaḍḍhadhātuṃ [M 0.0119] gāhetvā, cetiye pabbatepi ca;

Sabbesu ca vihāresu, thūpe kāresi khattiyo.

Taking half of the relics, the khattiya king had stūpas built on Cetiyapabbata and in all the monasteries.

47.

47.

Isino dehanikkhepa-kataṭhānañhi tassa taṃ;

Vuccate bahumānena, isibhūmaṅganaṃ iti.

The place where the sage’s body was cremated is called, out of great reverence, Isibhūmaṅgana.

48.

48.

Tato pabhutya’riyānaṃ, samantā yojanattaye;

Sarīraṃ āharitvāna, tamhi desamhi ḍayhati.

From that time onwards, when noble ones pass away within a three-yojana radius, their bodies are brought and cremated in that place.

49.

49.

Saṅghamittā mahātherī, mahā’bhiññā mahāmatī;

Katvā sāsanakiccāni, tathā lokahitaṃ bahuṃ.

The great Therī Saṅghamittā, of great direct knowledge and great wisdom, having fulfilled the duties of the Dispensation and done much for the welfare of the world,

50.

50.

Ekūnasaṭṭhivassā sā, uttiyasse’va rājino;

Vassamhi navame kheme, hatthāḷhakaupassaye.

being fifty-nine years of age, in the ninth year of King Uttiya’s reign, while dwelling in the secure Hatthāḷhaka nunnery,

51.

51.

Vasantī parinibbāyī, rājā tassāpi kārayi;

Therassa viya sattāhaṃ, pūjāsakkāra muttamaṃ.

dwelling there, she attained Parinibbāna. The king also arranged for her the highest honors and veneration for seven days, just as he had for the Elder.

52.

52.

Sabbā alaṅkatā laṃkā, therassa viya āsi ca;

Kūṭāgāragataṃ theri-dehaṃ sattadinaccaye.

All of Laṅkā was adorned as it had been for the Elder. After seven days had passed, the Therī’s body, placed on a bier,

53.

53.

Nikkhāmetvāna nagaraṃ, thūparāma puratthato;

Cittasālā samīpamhi, mahābodhipa dassaye.

was brought out of the city to a place east of the Thūpārāma, near the Cittasālā, in sight of the great Bodhi tree.

54.

54.

Theriyā vuṭṭhaṭhānamhi, aggikicca makārayi;

Thūpañca tattha kāresi, uttiyo so mahīpati.

At the very spot where the Therī had been ordained, that lord of the earth, Uttiya, had the cremation ceremony performed, and he also had a stūpa built there.

55.

55.

Pañcāpi te mahātherā, therāriṭṭhādayopi ca;

Tathā’neka sahassāni, bhikkhu khīṇāsavāpi ca.

Those five great Elders, and the other Elders headed by Ariṭṭha, and likewise many thousands of bhikkhus who were destroyers of the corruptions,

56.

56.

Saṅghamittā pabhutiyo, tā ca dvādasatheriyo;

Khīṇāsavā bhikkhuniyo, sahassāni bahūni ca.

the twelve Therīs, led by Saṅghamittā, and many thousands of bhikkhunīs who were destroyers of the corruptions,

57.

57.

Bahussutā mahāpaññā, vinayādijānāgamaṃ;

Jotayitvāna kālena, payātā’niccatāvasaṃ.

all of them of great learning and great wisdom, knowing the Vinaya and the other scriptures, having illuminated the Dispensation in due time, have passed away, subject to impermanence.

58.

58.

Dasavassāni so rājā, rajjaṃ kāresi uttiyo;

Evaṃ aniccatā esā, sabbalokavināsinī.

That King Uttiya reigned for ten years. Such is this impermanence, the destroyer of the entire world.

59.

59.

Taṃ [M 0.0120] etaṃ atisāhasaṃ atibalaṃ na vāriyaṃ naro;

Jānantopi aniccataṃ bhavagate nibbindateneva ca;

Nibbindo viratiṃ ratiṃ na kurute pāpehi puññehi ca;

Tasse’sāatimohajālabalatājānampi sammuyhatīti.

This impermanence is so rash, so powerful, it cannot be checked by any person. Even while knowing the impermanence inherent in existence, one does not become disenchanted. Not being disenchanted, one does not abstain from evil nor delight in meritorious deeds. Such is the power of the net of great delusion that it confounds even one who knows.

Sujanappasādasaṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Mahāvaṃsa, compiled for the serene joy and spiritual urgency of good people.

Theraparinibbānaṃ nāma

Entitled: The Final Nibbāna of the Elder.

Vīsatimo paricchedo.

The Twentieth Chapter.

Ekavīsatima pariccheda

The Twenty-First Chapter

Vañca rājako

The Five Kings

1.

1.

Uttiyassa [M 0.0120] kaniṭṭho tu, mahāsivo tadaccaye;

Dasa vassāni kāresi, rajjaṃ sujana sevako.

After his (Uttiya's) passing, his younger brother Mahāsiva, a servant of the virtuous, ruled the kingdom for ten years.

2.

2.

Bhaddasālamhi so there, pasīditvā manoramaṃ;

Kāresi purimāyantu, vihāraṃ nagaraṅgaṇaṃ.

Pleased with the thera Bhaddasāla, he had a delightful monastery built in the eastern court of the city.

3.

3.

Mahāsivakaniṭṭho tu, suratisso tadaccaye;

Dasavassāni kāresi, rajjaṃ puññesu sādaro.

After his passing, his younger brother Sūratissa, who was devoted to merit, ruled the kingdom for ten years.

4.

4.

Dakkhiṇāya disāyaṃ so, vihāraṃ nagaraṃ gaṇaṃ;
