“These things were acquired by me for the family’s attendant elder, and this pair of cloths for my son; I give all of them to you.”

41.

41.

Iti vatvāna datvā te, gahetvā gacchato pana;

Vanditvā rājavacasā, rañño sandesamāha so.

Having spoken thus and given those things, as the elder accepted them and was departing, he paid homage with the king’s words and delivered the king’s message.

42.

42.

Mahāthūpe kayiramāne, satiyākammakārakā;

Anekasaṅkhāhi janā, pasannā sugatiṃ gatā.

While the Great Stūpa was being built, the workers were mindful; countless faithful people went to a good destination.

43.

43.

Cittappasādamattena, sugate gatiuttamā;

Labbhatīti viditvāna, thūpapūjaṃ kare budho.

Knowing that by mere serenity of mind towards the Sugata a supreme destination is attained, the wise one should perform worship of the stūpa.

44.

44.

Ettheva bhatiyā kammaṃ, karitvā itthiyo duve;

Tāvatiṃsamhi nibbattā, mahāthūpamhi niṭṭhite.

Right here, two women, having done work for wages, were reborn in Tāvatiṃsa when the Great Stūpa was completed.

45.

45.

Āvajjitvā pubbakammaṃ, diṭṭhakammaphalā ubho;

Gandhamālā’diyitvāna, thūpaṃ pūjetumāgatā.

Having reflected on their past deeds, both seeing the fruit of their actions, they took perfumes and garlands and came to worship the stūpa.

46.

46.

Gandhamālāhi pūjetvā, cetiyaṃ abhivandisuṃ;

Tasmiṃ khaṇe bhātivaṅka-vāsī thero mahāsivo.

Having worshipped with perfumes and garlands, they paid homage to the cetiya. At that moment, the Elder Mahāsiva, a resident of Bhātivaṅka,

47.

47.

Rattibhāge mahāthūpaṃ, vandissāmīti āgato;

Tādisvāna mahāsatta-paṇṇirukkhama passito.

came during the night, intending, “I will worship the Great Stūpa.” He saw them, who were like great beings, resplendent as a great paṇṇi tree.

48.

48.

Adassayitvā attānaṃ, passaṃ sampattimabbhutaṃ;

Ṭhatvā tāsaṃ vandanāya, pariyosāne apucchitaṃ.

Not revealing himself, seeing their wondrous splendor, he stood by, and at the conclusion of their worship, he asked them:

49.

49.

“Bhāsate sakalo dīpo,

Dehobhāsena vo idha;

Kinnukammaṃ karitvāna,

Devalokaṃ ito gatā.

“The whole island shines here with the radiance of your bodies. Having done what deed have you gone from here to the world of the devas?”

50.

50.

Mahāthūpe kataṃ kammaṃ, tassa āhaṃsu devatā;

Evaṃ tathāgate heva, pasādo hi mahapphalo.

The devatās told him of the work done at the Great Stūpa. Thus, indeed, faith in the Tathāgata is of great fruit.

51.

51.

Pupphadhānattayaṃ thūpe, iṭṭhikāhi citaṃ citaṃ;

Samaṃ pathaviyā katvā, iddhimanto’va sīdayuṃ.

The three flower-altars at the stūpa, built up again and again with bricks, were made to sink level with the ground as if by those with psychic power.

52.

52.

Nava vāre citaṃ sabbaṃ, evaṃ osīdayiṃsu te;

Atha rājā bhikkhusaṅgha-sannipāta makārayi.

Nine times was it all built up, and thus did they cause it to sink. Then the king had an assembly of the Bhikkhu Saṅgha convened.

53.

53.

Tatthāsītisahassāni[M 0.0172], sannipātamhi bhikkhavo;

Rājā saṅghamupāgamma, pūjetvā abhivandiya.

There, in the assembly, were eighty thousand bhikkhus. The king, approaching the Saṅgha, honored and paid homage to them.

54.

54.

Iṭṭhakosidanehetuṃ, pucchi saṅgho viyākari;

“No sīdanatthaṃ thūpassa, iddhimantehi bhikkhūhi.

He asked the reason for the sinking of the bricks. The Saṅgha explained: “Not for the sinking of the stūpa was this done by the bhikkhus with psychic power.

55.

55.

Kataṃ etaṃ mahārāja, na idāni karissate;

Aññathattamakatvā taṃ, mahāthūpaṃ samāpaya.

“This was done, O great king, and it will not be done now. Without making any alteration, complete the Great Stūpa.”

56.

56.

Taṃ sutvā sumano rājā, thūpakammamakārayi;

Pupphādhānesu dasasu, iṭṭhikā dasakoṭiyo.

Hearing this, the king, being pleased, had the work on the stūpa carried out. For the ten flower-altars, ten crores of bricks were used.

57.

57.

Bhikkhusaṅgho sāmaṇere, uttaraṃ sumanampi ca;

“Cebhiya dhātugabbhatthaṃ, pāsāṇe meghavaṇṇake.

The Bhikkhu Saṅgha appointed the novices Uttara and Sumana, saying: “For the relic-chamber of the cetiya, bring cloud-colored stones.”

58.

58.

Āharathā”ti yojesi, te gantvā uttaraṃ kuruṃ;

Asīti ratanāyāma, vitthāre ravibhāsure.

Thus he appointed them. They went to Uttarakuru and brought slabs eighty ratanas in length, broad in width, and shining like the sun.

59.

59.

Aṭṭhaṅgulāni bahale, gaṇṭhipupphanibhe subhe;

Chameghavaṇṇapāsāṇe, āhariṃsu khaṇetato.

Eight fingers thick, beautiful, and like clustered flowers, they dug up and brought from there cloud-colored stone slabs.

60.

60.

Pupphadhānassa upari, majjhe ekaṃ nipātiya;

Catupassamhi caturo, mañjūsaṃ viya yojiya.

Above the flower-receptacle, they placed one in the middle and joined four on the four sides, like a casket.

61.

61.

Ekaṃ pidhānakatthāya, disābhāge puratthime;

Adassanaṃ karitvā te, ṭhapayiṃsu mahiddhikā.

For the lid, the ones of great power placed one slab in the eastern direction, having made it invisible.

62.

62.

Majjhamhi dhātugabbhassa, tassa rājā akārayi;

Ratanamayaṃ bodhirukkhaṃ, sabbākāramanoramaṃ.

In the middle of that relic chamber, the king had a Bodhi-tree of gems made, beautiful in every way.

63.

63.

Aṭṭhārasa rataniko, khandho sākhāssa pañca ca;

Pavālamayamūlo so, indanīle patiṭṭhito.

Its trunk was eighteen cubits high, and it had five branches; its roots were of coral, established on lapis lazuli.

64.

64.

Susuddharajatakkhandho, maṇipattehi sobhito;

Hemamayapaṇḍupatta, phalo pavāḷaaṅkuro.

Its trunk was of pure silver, adorned with leaves of gems; it had yellow leaves made of gold, and its fruits and shoots were of coral.

65.

65.

Atha maṅgalikā tassa, khandhe pupphalatāpi ca;

Catuppadānaṃ pantīdha, haṃsapanti ca sobhanā.

Then, on its trunk, there were auspicious flower creepers; here, rows of quadrupeds and beautiful rows of swans.

66.

66.

Uddhaṃ cāruvitānante, muttā kiṃ kiṇijālakā;

Suvaṇṇa ghaṇṭāpantīdha, dāmāni ca tahiṃ tahiṃ.

Above, at the edge of the beautiful canopy, hung nets of pearls and tinkling bells; here too were rows of golden bells, and garlands here and there.

67.

67.

Vitāna [M 0.0173] catukoṇamhi, muttādāmakalāpako;

Navasata sahassaggho, eke ko asilambito.

At the four corners of the canopy was a cluster of pearl strings; each one was worth nine hundred thousand, and from each hung a sword.

68.

68.

Ravicandatāra rūpāni, nānāpadumakāni ca;

Ratanehi katāneva, dhitāne appitāna’yuṃ.

Images of the sun, moon, and stars, and various lotuses, made of gems, were affixed to the canopy.

69.

69.

Aṭṭhuttarasahassāni, vattāni vividhāni ca;

Mahagghanānāraṅgāni, vitāne lambitāna’yuṃ.

One thousand and eight various cloths, of great price and diverse colors, were hung from the canopy.

70.

70.

Bodhiṃ parikkhipitvāna, nānāratanavedikā;

Mahāmalaka muttāhi, santhāretu tadantare.

Having encircled the Bodhi tree with a railing of various gems, he had large Malaka pearls scattered within that space.

71.

71.

Nānāratana pupphānaṃ, catugandhūdakassa ca;

Puṇṇā puṇṇaghaṭapanti, bodhimūle katāna’yuṃ.

Rows of full vessels, filled with various gem-like flowers and four kinds of fragrant water, were arranged at the foot of the Bodhi tree.

72.

72.

Bodhi pācina paññatte, pallaṅkekoṭiagghake;

Sovaṇṇa buddhapaṭimaṃ, nisīdāpesi bhāsuraṃ.

To the east of the Bodhi tree, on a prepared throne worth a koṭi, he had a radiant, golden Buddha image seated.

73.

73.

Sarīrāvayavātassā, paṭimāya yathārahaṃ;

Nānāvaṇṇehi ratanehi, katā surucirā ahuṃ.

The various limbs of that image were beautifully wrought in due proportion with gems of diverse colors.

74.

74.

Mahābrahmā ṭhito tattha, rājatacchatta dhārako;

Vijayuttarasaṅkhena, sakko ca abhisekado.

Great Brahmā stood there, holding a royal parasol; and Sakka, with the conch shell Vijayuttara, performed the consecration.

75.

75.

Viṇāhattho pañcasikho, kāḷanāgo sanāṭiko;

Sahassahattho māro ca, sahattīsaha kiṃkaro.

Pañcasikha with a lute in hand; Kāḷanāga with his troupe of dancers; and Māra with a thousand arms, together with his elephant and attendants.

76.

76.

Pācinapallaṅkanibhā, tīsu sesadisāsu ca;

Koṭikoṭidhanagghā ca, pallaṅkā atthatā ahuṃ.

In the three remaining directions, thrones resembling the eastern throne, worth a koṭi of koṭis, were spread out.

77.

77.

Bodhiṃ ussisake katvā, nānāratanamaṇḍitaṃ;

Koṭi dhanagghakaṃyeva, paññattaṃ sayanaṃ ahu.

Having made the Bodhi tree a headrest, a bed adorned with various gems and worth a koṭi of wealth was prepared.

78.

78.

Sattasattāha ṭhānesu, tattha tattha yathārahaṃ;

Adhikāre akāresi, brahmayācanameva ca.

In the places of the seven weeks, in each place as was appropriate, he had depictions made of the events, including the request of Brahmā.

79.

79.

Dhammacakkappavattañca, yasapabbajanampi ca;

Bhaddavaggiya pabbajjaṃ, jaṭilānaṃ damanampi ca.

The turning of the Wheel of Dhamma, the going forth of Yasa, the ordination of the Bhaddavaggiyas, and the taming of the Jaṭilas.

80.

80.

Bimbisārāgamañcāpi[M 0.0174], rājagehappavesanaṃ;

Veḷuvanassagahanaṃ, asītisāvake tathā.

Bimbisāra’s arrival and entry into the royal palace, the acceptance of the Veḷuvana grove, and likewise the eighty disciples.

81.

81.

Kapila vatthugamanaṃ, tathā ratana caṅkamaṃ;

Rāhulānandapabbajjaṃ, gahaṇaṃ jetavanassa ca.

The journey to Kapilavatthu, likewise the Jeweled Promenade, the ordination of Rāhula and Nanda, and the acceptance of Jetavana.

82.

82.

Ambamūle pāṭihīraṃ, tāvatiṃsamhi desanaṃ;

Devorohaṇapāṭihīraṃ, therapañhasamāgamaṃ.

The miracle at the foot of the mango tree, the teaching in Tāvatiṃsa, the miracle of the descent from the deva world, and the assembly for the elder's question.

83.

83.

Mahāsamaya suttantaṃ, rāhulovādamevaca;

Mahāmaṅgalasuttañca, dhanapālasamāgamaṃ.

The Mahāsamaya Sutta, the Rāhulovāda, the Mahāmaṅgala Sutta, and the encounter with Dhanapāla.

84.

84.

Āḷavakaṅgulimāla, apalāladamanampi ca;

Pārāyanakasamitiṃ, āyuvossajjanaṃ tathā.

The subduing of Āḷavaka and Aṅgulimāla, and the taming of Apalāla; the Pārāyana assembly, and likewise the relinquishing of the life-span.

85.

85.

Sūkaramaddavaggāhaṃ, siṅgīvaṇṇayugassa ca;

Pasannodakapānañca, parinibbāna meva ca.

The acceptance of sūkaramaddava, the pair of golden-colored robes, the drinking of clear water, and the final Parinibbāna itself.

86.

86.

Devamanussa paridevaṃ, therena pādavandanaṃ;

Dahanaṃ agginibbānaṃ, tattha sakkāra meva ca.

The lamentation of devas and humans, the elder's homage at the feet, the cremation, the extinguishing of the fire, and the honors there.

87.

87.

Dhātuvitaṅga doṇena, pasādajanakāni ca;

Yebhuyyena akāresi, jātakāni sujātimā.

The distribution of relics by Doṇa, and other acts inspiring faith; the king, of noble birth, mostly had the Jātakas depicted.

88.

88.

Vessantara jātakantu, vitthārena akārayi;

Kusināpurato yāva, bodhimanti tatheva ca.

The Vessantara Jātaka he had depicted in detail; and likewise, scenes from Kusinārā up to the Bodhi-maṇḍa.

89.

89.

Catuddisaṃ te cattāro, mahārājā ṭhitā ahuṃ;

Tettiṃsadeva puttā ca, bāttiṃsa ca kumāriyo.

In the four directions, the four great kings stood; and the thirty-three sons of devas, and thirty-two maidens.

90.

90.

Yakkhasenāpatiaṭṭha, vīsati ca tato pari;

Añjalīpaggahādevā, pupphapuṇṇaghaṭā tato.

Eight commanders of the yakkha hosts, and twenty more besides; then devas holding their hands in reverence, and devas with pots filled with flowers.

91.

91.

Naccakā devatāceva, tūriyavādaka devatā;

Ādāsagāhakā devā, pupphasākhā dharā tathā.

Dancing devas, devas playing musical instruments, devas holding mirrors, and likewise those holding branches of flowers.

92.

92.

Padumādigāhakā devā, aññe devā ca nekadhā;

Ratanagghiya panti ca, dhammacakkāna meva ca.

Devas holding lotuses and other offerings, and other devas in various ways; also rows of precious offerings, and indeed Wheels of Dhamma.

93.

93.

Khaggadharādevapanti, devāpātidharā tathā;

Tesaṃ sīse pañcahatthā, gandhatelassa pūritā.

Rows of devas carrying swords, and likewise devas bearing shields; on their heads, vessels five hands high were filled with fragrant oil.

94.

94.

Dukūlavaṭṭikā [M 0.0175] panti, sadāpañjalitā ahu;

Phalikagghiye catukkaṇṇe, ekeko ca mahāmaṇi.

A row of linen wicks was always burning brightly; and in each of the four corners of the crystal casket, a great gem.

95.

95.

Suvaṇṇamaṇi muttānaṃ, rāsiyo vajirassa ca;

Catukkaṇṇesu cattāro, kathā’hesuṃ pabhassarā.

Heaps of gold, gems, pearls, and diamonds; in the four corners, four radiant ones were made.

96.

96.

Medavaṇṇakapāsāṇa, bhittiyaṃyeva ujjalā;

Vijjātā appitā āsuṃ, dhātugabbhevibhūsitā.

Bright upon the wall itself were cloud-colored stones; expertly affixed, they were shining, adorning the relic chamber.

97.

97.

Rūpakānettasabbāni, dhātugabbhe manorame;

Ghanakoṭṭi mahemassa, kārāpesi mahīpati.

In the delightful relic-chamber, the king had all manner of images made, and a solid chamber for the Great Sage.

98.

98.

Kammādhiṭṭhāyako ettha, sabbaṃ saṃvidahi imaṃ;

Indagutto mahāthero, chaḷabhiñño mahāmatī.

Here, the superintendent of the work, the great Elder Indagutta, of great wisdom and with the six higher knowledges, arranged all this.

99.

99.

Sabbaṃ rājiddhiyā etaṃ, devatānañca iddhiyā;

Iddhiyā ariyānañca, asambādhaṃ patiṭṭhitaṃ.

All this was established without obstruction by the power of the king, by the power of deities, and by the power of the noble ones.

100.

100.

Niṭṭhantaṃ sugatañca pūjiyatamaṃ lokuttamaṃ nittamaṃ;

Dhātu tassa vicuṇṇitaṃ janahitaṃ āsiṃsatā pūjiya;

Puññaṃ taṃ samamicca’cecca matimā saddhāguṇalaṅkato;

Tiṭṭhantaṃ sugataṃ viya’ssa munino dhātu ca sambūjaye.

The wise one, adorned with the quality of faith, having well considered that merit, and having venerated his powdered relics while wishing for the welfare of the people, should venerate the relics of this Sage as if the Well-Gone One himself were present—he who is perfected, most worthy of veneration, supreme in the world, and unsurpassed.

Sujanappasādasaṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Great Chronicle, composed for the purpose of serene joy and spiritual urgency of the virtuous.

Dhātugabbharacano nāma

Named the Construction of the Relic-Chamber

Tiṃsatimo paricchedo.

The Thirtieth Chapter.

Ekatiṃsatima pariccheda

The Thirty-First Chapter

Dhātunidhānaṃ

The Enshrining of the Relics

1.

1.

Dhātugabbhamhi [M 0.0176] kammāni, niṭṭhāpetvā arindamo;

Sannipātaṃ kārayitvā, saṅghassa idhamabravi.

Having completed the works in the relic-chamber, the tamer of foes convened an assembly of the Sangha and spoke thus.

2.

2.

Dhātugabbhamhi kammāni, mayā niṭṭhāpi tāni hi;

Suve dhātuṃ nidhessāmi, bhante jānātha dhātuyo”.

“Indeed, the works in the relic-chamber have been completed by me. Tomorrow I shall enshrine the relics. Venerable sirs, be informed of the relics.”

3.

3.

Idaṃ vatvā mahārājā, nagaraṃ pāvisī tato;

Dhātu āharakaṃ bhikkhuṃ, bhikkhusaṅgho vicintiya.

Having said this, the great king then entered the city. The Sangha of monks, having considered a monk to bring the relics,

4.

4.

Soṇuttaraṃ nāmayatiṃ, pūjāpariveṇavāsi kaṃ;

Dhātāharaṇa kammamhi, chaḷabhiññaṃ niyojayi.

assigned the ascetic named Soṇuttara, who resided in the Pūjāpariveṇa and possessed the six higher knowledges, to the task of bringing the relics.

5.

5.

Cārikaṃ caramānamhi, nāthe lokahitāyahi;

Nanduttaro’ti nāmena, gaṅgātīramhi māṇavo.

While the Protector was wandering on his journey for the welfare of the world, there was a youth named Nanduttara on the bank of the Ganges.

6.

6.

Nimantetvā’bhisambuddhaṃ, saha saṅghaṃ abhojayi;

Satthāpayogapaṭṭhāne, sasaṅghonāvamāruhi.

Having invited the Fully Enlightened One, he fed him together with the Sangha. At the Payoga landing place, the Teacher, together with the Sangha, boarded the ship.

7.

7.

Tattha bhaddajithero tu, chaḷabhiñño mahiddhiko;

Jalapakkhalitaṭṭhānaṃ, disvā bhikkhū idaṃ vadī.

There, the Elder Bhaddaji, who possessed the six higher knowledges and great psychic power, seeing the place where the water was stirred up, spoke thus to the monks.

8.

8.

“Mahā panādabhūtena, mayā vutto suvaṇṇayo;

Pāsādo patito ettha, pañcavīsatiyojako.

“A palace, twenty-five leagues in size, fell here with a great sound, as was spoken by me, the golden-hued one.”

9.

9.

Taṃ pāpuṇitvā gaṅgāya, jalaṃ pakkhili taṃ idha;

Bhikkhū asaddahantā taṃ, satthuno taṃ nivedayuṃ.

When it reached the Ganges, the water here became muddy; the monks, disbelieving it, reported it to the Teacher.

10.

10.

Satthā’ha “kaṅkhaṃ bhikkhunaṃ, vinodehī”tisotato;

Ñāpetuṃ brahmaloke’pi, vasavattisamattha taṃ.

The Teacher said, “Dispel the monks' doubt.” He was capable of making that known even in the Brahma realm, like Vasavatti.

11.

11.

Iddhiyā nabhamuggantvā, sattatālasame ṭhito;

Dūssathūpaṃ brahmaloke, ṭhapetvā vaḍḍhite kare.

Rising into the sky by psychic power, he stood at the height of seven palm trees and, extending his hands, took the cloth stupa from the Brahma realm.

12.

12.

Idhā’netvā [M 0.0177] dassayitvā, janassa puna taṃ tahiṃ;

Ṭhapayitvā yathāṭhāne, iddhiyā gaṅgāmāgato.

Bringing it here and showing it to the people, then placing it back there in its original place, he came to the Ganges by psychic power.

13.

13.

Pādaṅguṭṭhena pāsādaṃ, gahetvā thupikāyaso;

Ussāpetvāna dassetvā, janassa khipi taṃ tahiṃ.

Taking the palace by its iron pinnacle with his big toe, raising it up and showing it to the people, he threw it down there.

14.

14.

Nanduttaro māṇavako, disvā taṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ;

Parāyattamahaṃ dhātuṃ, pahuānayituṃ siyaṃ.

The young man Nanduttara, seeing that miracle, thought: “I am able to bring the relic that is dependent on another.”

15.

15.

Iti patthayi tenetaṃ, saṅgho soṇuttaraṃ yatiṃ;

Tasmiṃ kamme niyojesi, soḷasavassikaṃ api.

Thus he aspired, and so the Sangha assigned the ascetic Soṇuttara to that task, even though he was only sixteen years of age.

16.

16.

“Āharāmi kuto dhātuṃ”, iti saṅghamapucchiso;

Kathesi saṅgho therassa, tassa tā dhātuyo iti.

“From where shall I bring the relic?” he thus asked the Sangha. The Sangha then spoke to him thus concerning those relics:

17.

17.

“Parinibbāna mañcamhi, nipanno loka nāyako;

Dhātūhipilokahi taṃ, kātuṃ devinda mabruvi.

Lying on the couch of Parinibbāna, the Leader of the World told the Lord of the Devas to bring about the welfare of the world by means of the relics.

18.

18.

Devinda’ṭṭhasu doṇesu, mama sāriradhāthusu;

Ekaṃ doṇaṃ rāmagāme, koḷiyehi ca sakkataṃ.

“Lord of Devas, among the eight measures of my bodily relics, one measure is in Rāmagāma, revered by the Koliyans.

19.

19.

Nāgalokaṃ tato nitaṃ, tato nāgehi sakkataṃ;

Laṃkādipe mahāthūpe, nidhānāya bhavissati.

Taken thence to the Nāga world, and there honored by the Nāgas, it is destined for enshrinement in the great stupa on the Isle of Laṅkā.”

20.

20.

Mahākassapattheropi, dīghadassī mahāyati;

Dhammāsoka narindena, dhātuvitthārakārako.

The great Elder Mahākassapa, far-seeing and a great ascetic, and King Dhammāsoka were promoters of the relics' distribution.

21.

21.

Rājagahassa sāmante, raññā ajātasattunā;

Kārāpento mahādhātuṃ, nidhānaṃ sādhu saṅkhataṃ.

In the vicinity of Rājagaha, King Ajātasattu caused a great, well-prepared relic deposit to be made.

22.

22.

Satta doṇāni dhātūnaṃ, āharitvāna kārayi;

Rāmagāmamhi doṇantu, sattucittaññuna’ggahi.

Having brought seven measures of relics, he caused it to be done. But the measure in Rāmagāma he did not take, knowing the mind of the Master.

23.

23.

Mahādhātunidhānaṃ taṃ, dhammāsokopi bhūpati;

Passitvā aṭṭhamaṃ doṇaṃ, āṇāpetuṃmakiṃ akā.

King Dhammāsoka also, having seen that great relic deposit, resolved to give an order concerning the eighth measure.

24.

24.

Mahāthūpe nidhānatthaṃ, vihitaṃ taṃ jineni’ti;

Dhammāsokaṃ nivāresuṃ, tattha khiṇāsavāyati.

“That was set aside by the Conqueror for enshrinement in the Great Stupa,” they said; thus, the arahant ascetics restrained Dhammāsoka there.

25.

25.

Rāmagāmamhi thūpotu, gaṅgātīre kato tato;

Bhijjigaṅgāya oghena, sotu dhātu karaṇḍako.

But the stupa at Rāmagāma, built there on the bank of the Ganges, was broken by the river's flood, and that relic casket was carried into the current.

26.

26.

Samuddaṃ [M 0.0178] pavisitvāna, dvidhā bhinne jale tahiṃ;

Nānāratanapiṭṭhamhi, aṭṭhārasmiṃ samākulo.

Entering the ocean, it came to rest there upon a heap of various gems where the water was split in two, causing a great stir in the eighteenth realm.

27.

27.

Nāgā disvā karaṇḍaṃ taṃ, kāḷanāgassa rājino;

Mañjerikanāgabhavanaṃ, upagamma nivedayuṃ.

The Nāgas, seeing that casket, went to the Mañjerika Nāga-palace of King Kāḷanāga and informed him.

28.

28.

Dasakoṭisahassehi, gantvā nāgehi so tahiṃ;

Dhātū tā abhipūjento, netvāna bhavanaṃ sakaṃ.

He went there with ten thousand crores of Nāgas and, honoring those relics, took them to his own abode.

29.

29.

Sabbaratanamayaṃ thūpaṃ, tassoparigharaṃ tathā;

Māpetvā saha nāgehi, sadā pūjesi sādaro.

Having caused a stupa made of all jewels to be built, and likewise a shrine-house over it, he, together with the Nāgas, always worshipped it with reverence.

30.

30.

Ārakkhāmahatī tattha, gantvā dhātuidhānaya;

Suve dhātunidhānañhi, bhūmipālo karissati”.

“Great is the protection there. Go and bring the relic here, for tomorrow the ruler of the land will perform the enshrinement of the relics.”

31.

31.

Iccevaṃ saṅghavacanaṃ, sutvā sādhūti so pana;

Pattabbakālaṃ pekkhanto, pariveṇa magāsakaṃ.

Thus, having heard the Sangha's words, he responded, “It is well.” Then, awaiting the proper time, he went to his own monastic cell.

32.

32.

Bhavissati suve dhātu, nidhānanti mahīpati;

Cāresi nagare bheriṃ, sabba kiccaṃ vidhāya taṃ.

“Tomorrow the enshrinement of the relics will take place,” declared the great king. Having arranged all that was needful, he had a drum beaten throughout the city.

33.

33.

Nagaraṃ sakalañceva, idhāgāmiñca añjasaṃ;

Alaṅkārayi sakkaccaṃ, nagare ca vibhūsayi.

He carefully adorned the entire city and the direct road leading to it, and further embellished the city.

34.

34.

Sakko devānamindo ca, laṃkādīpamasesakaṃ;

Āmantetvā vissakammaṃ, alaṅkārayinekadhā.

Sakka, the king of the gods, summoned Vissakamma and had him adorn the whole of the island of Laṅkā in a uniform manner.

35.

35.

Nagarassa catudvāre, vattabhattaṃhi nekadhā;

Mahājanopabhogatthaṃ, ṭhapāpesi narādhipo.

At the four gates of the city, the king had provisions of food established in many ways for the benefit of the great multitude.

36.

36.

Uposathe pannarase, aparanhe sumānaso;

On the fifteenth Uposatha day, in the afternoon, the king, wise in royal duties and adorned with all ornaments, was of joyful mind.

37.

37.

Sabbāhi nāṭakatthīhi, yodhehi sāyudhehi ca;

38.

38.

Nānāvidhavibhūsehi, sabbato parivārito;

Surrounded on all sides by various splendors, he mounted and stood upon a superb white chariot drawn by excellent Sindh horses.

39.

39.

Bhūsitaṃ kaṇḍūlaṃ hatthiṃ, kāretvā puratosubhaṃ;

40.

40.

Aṭṭhuttara [M 0.0179] sahassāni, nāgaranāriyo subhā;

One thousand and eight beautiful women of the city, adorned and bearing full water pots, surrounded that chariot.

41.

41.

Nānāpupphasamuggāni, tatheva daṇḍadīpikā;

Likewise, the same number of women were there, holding caskets of various flowers and torches on poles.

42.

42.

Aṭṭhuttara sahassāni, dārakā samalaṅkatā;

One thousand and eight well-adorned boys, holding beautiful banners of various colors, formed a retinue.

43.

43.

Nānātūriyaghosehi, anekehi tahiṃ tahiṃ;

Hatthasarathasaddehi, bhijjante viya bhūtale.

With the sounds of many various musical instruments here and there, and with the noises of elephants, horses, and chariots, it was as if the surface of the earth were splitting.

44.

44.

Yanto mahāmeghavanaṃ, siriyā so mahāyaso;

The glorious one, greatly renowned, went to the Mahāmeghavana, shining forth like the king of gods going to the Nandana Grove.

45.

45.

Rañño niggamanārambhe, mahātūriya ravaṃpure;

46.

46.

Nimujjitvā puthuviyā, gantvāna nāgamandiraṃ;

47.

47.

Vuṭṭhāya abhivādetvā, pallaṅke taṃ nivesīla;

48.

48.

Tasmiṃ vutte athopucchi, therāgamanakāraṇaṃ;

Patvā’dhikāraṃ sabbaṃ so, saṅgha sandesa mabruvi.

49.

49.

Mahāthūpe nidhānatthaṃ, buddhena vihitā idha;

Tava hatthagatā dhātu, dehitā kira me tuvaṃ.

50.

50.

Taṃ sutvā nāgarājāso, atīva domanassi to;

“Pahū ayañhi samaṇo, balakkārena gaṇhituṃ.

Hearing this, that Nāga king became deeply distressed, thinking, ‘This ascetic is indeed powerful enough to take them by force.’

51.

51.

Tasmā aññattha netabbā, dhātuyo”iti cintiya;

Tattha ṭhitaṃ bhāgineyyaṃ, ākārena nivedayi.

Thinking, “Therefore, the relics must be taken elsewhere,” he communicated this by a sign to his nephew who was standing there.

52.

52.

Nāmena vāsuladatto, jānitvā tassa iṅgitaṃ;

Gantvā taṃ cetiyagharaṃ, gilitvāna karaṇḍakaṃ.

Vāsuladatta by name, having understood his hint, went to that shrine chamber and swallowed the casket.

53.

53.

Sinerupādaṃ [M 0.0180] gantvāna, kuṇḍalāvaṭṭakosayi;

Tiyojanasataṃ dīgho, bhogoyojanavaṭṭavā.

Having gone to the foot of Mount Sineru, he lay in a circular coil, three hundred yojanas in length, with a body a yojana in circumference.

54.

54.

Anekāni sahassāni, māpetvāna phaṇāni ca;

Dhūpāyati pajjalati, sayitvā so mahiddhiko.

Having created many thousands of hoods, that one of great psychic power lay there, emitting smoke and blazing.

55.

55.

Anekāni sahassāni, attanā sadise ahi;

Māpayitvā sayāpesi, samantā parivārite.

Creating many thousands of snakes similar to himself, he had them lie down all around in a circle.

56.

56.

Bahū devā ca nāgā ca, osariṃsu tahiṃ tadā;

Many gods and nāgas gathered there then, thinking, “We shall witness the battle between the two great beings.”

57.

57.

Mātulo bhāgineyyena, haṭātā dhātuyo iti;

The uncle, knowing that the relics had been taken by his nephew, said to that elder, “I do not have the relics with me.”

58.

58.

Āditoppabhutithero, tāsaṃ dhātūnamāgamaṃ;

Vatvāna nāgarājaṃ taṃ, “dehi dhātū”ti abruvi.

The elder, relating from the very beginning the origin of those relics, spoke to that nāga king, saying, “Give the relics.”

59.

59.

Aññathā saññāpetuṃ taṃ, theraṃ so uragādhipo;

To distract the elder, that serpent lord took him to the shrine chamber and described it to him.

60.

60.

Anekadhā anekehi, ratanehi susaṅkhataṃ;

61.

Laṃkādīpamhi sakale, sabbāni ratanānipi;

62.

63.

“Saccābhisamayo nāma, tumhākaṃ hīna vijjati;

64.

64.

“Saṃsāra dukkha mokkhāya, uppajjanti tathāgatā;

65.

65.

Dhātunidhānaṃ ajje’va, so hi rājā karissati;

Tasmā papañcamakaritvā, lahuṃ me dehi dhātuyo”.

That king will indeed perform the enshrinement of the relics this very day. Therefore, without making complications, give me the relics quickly.”

66.

66.

Nāgoāhasace bhante, tuvaṃ passasi dhātuyo;

67.

67.

Sukhumaṃ [M 0.0181] karaṃ māpayitvā, thero tatraṭhito’vaso;

68.

68.

69.

70.

71.

72.

72.

Bhikkhu nāgassa vijaye, tuṭṭhā devā samāgatā;

73.

73.

74.

75.

76.

77.

77.

Mātukaraṇḍamādāya, tassa therassa hatthato;

78.

79.

79.

Cattāro tu mahārājā, aṭṭhaṃsu khaggapāṇino;

80.

80.

Pāricchattaka pupphehi, pūjayantā tahiṃṭhitā;

81.

81.

Palāpetvā [M 0.0182] duṭṭhayakkhe, yakkhasenāpati pana;

82.

82.

83.

84.

85.

86.

87.

88.

88.

89.

89.

Dibbacchattādikānettha, dibbagandhādikāni ca;

90.

90.

Apassitvā brahmadevo, tuṭṭho acchariyabbhuto;

Dhātuchattena pūjesi, laṃkārajje’bhisiñci ca.

Not seeing the god Brahmā, the king was delighted and amazed; he worshipped with the parasol of the relics and consecrated the kingdom of Laṅkā.

91.

91.

“Dibbacchattaṃ mānusañca, vimutticchattameva ca;

Iti ticchittadhārissa, lokanāthassa satthuno.

92.

93.

93.

Pūjayanto dhātuyotā, devehi mānusehi ca;

94.

94.

95.

95.

Arahanto channavuti-koṭiyo thūpamuttamaṃ;

Samantā parivāretvā, aṭṭhaṃsu katapañjalī.

Ninety-six crores of Arahants, having surrounded the supreme thūpa on all sides, stood with their hands clasped in reverence.

96.

96.

Otaritvā [M 0.0183] dhātugabbhaṃ, mahagghe sayanesubhe;

97.

97.

Sadhātu dhātucaṅkoṭo, uggantvā tassa sīsato;

98.

98.

Sayaṃ karaṇḍo vivari, uggantvā dhātuyo tato;

Buddhavesaṃ gahetvāna, lakkhaṇebyañjanujjalaṃ.

99.

99.

Gaṇḍambamūle buddho’va, yamakaṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ;

100.

100.

Taṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ disvā, pasannekaggamānasā;

Devāmanussā arahattaṃ, pattā dvādasa koṭiyo.

Having seen that miracle, twelve crores of devas and humans, with serene and one-pointed minds, attained Arahantship.

101.

101.

Sesā phalattayaṃ pattā, atītā gaṇanāpathaṃ;

Hitvā’tha buddhavesaṃ tā, karaṇḍamhi patiṭṭhayuṃ.

The rest, beyond reckoning, attained the three lower fruits. Then, abandoning that Buddha-form, they settled in the reliquary.

102.

102.

Tato oruyha caṅkoṭo, rañño sīse patiṭṭhahi;

Sahindaguttatherena, nāṭakīhi ca so pana.

103.

103.

Dhātugabbhaṃpariharaṃ, patvāna sayanaṃ subhaṃ;

Circumambulating within the relic chamber and reaching the beautiful couch, the glorious king, having placed the casket on the jeweled throne...

104.

104.

Dhovitvāna punohatthe, gandhavāsita vārinā;

Catujjātiyagandhena, ubbatetvā sagāravo.

Having washed his hands again with perfumed water, he respectfully anointed them with the four kinds of perfume.

105.

105.

Karaṇḍaṃ vivaritvāna, tāgahetvāna dhātuyo;

Iti cintayi bhūmindo, mahājanahitatthiko.

106.

106.

Anākulaṃ kehicipi, yadi hessanti dhātuyo;

107.

in the manner the Teacher lay down on the couch of final Nibbāna, may they lie down on this well-prepared, magnificent resting place.”

108.

108.

109.

109.

110.

111.

112.

112.

113.

114.

115.

116.

116.

may they, at that very moment, come and worship the relics here, and then return to their own homes.’ It happened just as he had resolved.

117.

118.

119.

120.

“Mālettha mā milāyantu, gandhāsussantumā ime;

121.

122.

123.

124.

125.

In the Mahāvaṃsa, composed for the serene joy and spiritual urgency of good people.

1.

2.

3.

4.

5.

7.

8.

9.

10.

13.

39.

48.

Taṃ sutvā abhayo thero, taṃ dānadvayameva so;

49.

50.

in the Kalyāṇika Monastery, having shared it among ten thousand five hundred monks, he caused them to partake of it.
