Saṅghassa tāta kiccesu, mā pamajjittha sabbadā”;

Itaṃ taṃ anusāsitvā, tuṇhī āsi mahīpati.

In the affairs of the Sangha, dear one, never be negligent.’ Having thus instructed him, the great king became silent.

63.

63.

Taṅkhaṇaṃ [M 0.0190] gaṇasajjhāyaṃ, bhikkhusaṅgho akāsi ca;

Devatā cha rathe ceva, chahi devehi ānayuṃ.

At that moment, the community of bhikkhus began a group recitation; and deities brought six chariots with six gods.

64.

64.

Yācuṃ visuṃ visuṃ devā, rājānaṃ te rathe ṭhitā;

“Amhākaṃ devalokaṃ tvaṃ, ehi rājamanoramaṃ”.

The deities, standing in their chariots, each separately entreated the king: 'Come, O king, to our delightful heavenly realm!'

65.

65.

Rājā tesaṃ vaco sutvā, “yāva dhammaṃ suṇomahaṃ;

Adhivāsetha tāvā”ti, hatthākārena vārayi.

Having heard their words, the king said, 'Wait while I hear the Dhamma; please wait until then,' and he stopped them with a gesture of his hand.

66.

66.

Vāreti gaṇasajjhāya, mībhi mantvāna bhikkhavo;

Sajjhāyaṃ ṭhapayuṃ rājā, pucchitaṃ ṭhānakāraṇaṃ.

The bhikkhus, thinking he was preventing the group recitation, stopped the recitation. The king, being asked, stated the reason for the stopping.

67.

67.

“Āgamethā”ti saññāya, dinnattā’ti vadiṃsu te;

Rājā “netaṃ tathā bhante”, iti vatvāna taṃ vadi.

They said, '[We stopped] because a sign was given, meaning "Approach."' The king, saying, 'Venerable sirs, it is not so,' spoke thus.

68.

68.

Taṃ sutvāna janā keci, “bhīto maccubhayā ayaṃ;

Lālappatī”ti maññiṃsu, tesaṃ kaṅkhāvinodanaṃ.

Hearing this, some people thought, 'This one is afraid, from fear of death; he is babbling.' To dispel their doubt,

69.

69.

Kāretuṃ abhayatthero, rājānaṃ evamāha so;

“Jānāpetuṃ kathaṃ sakkā, ānītā te rathā”iti.

the Elder Abhaya said this to the king: 'How can it be made known that these chariots were brought for you?'

70.

70.

Pupphadānaṃ khipāpesi, rāja nabhasi paṇḍito;

Tāni laggāni lambiṃsu, rathīsāsu visuṃ visuṃ.

The wise king had a shower of flowers thrown into the sky; they attached themselves and hung down, each separately on a chariot pole.

71.

71.

Ākāse lambamānāni, tāni disvā mahājano;

Kaṅkhaṃ paṭivinodesi, rājā theramabhāsitaṃ.

Seeing them hanging in the sky, the great crowd dispelled their doubt. The king then spoke to the Elder.

72.

72.

“Katamo devaloko hi,

Rammo bhante”ti so bruvi;

“Tusinānaṃ puraṃ rāja,

Rammaṃ”iti sataṃ mataṃ.

'Which heavenly realm, venerable sir, is delightful?' he asked. 'The city of the Tusitas, O King, is delightful,' this is the view of the virtuous.

73.

73.

Buddhabhāvāya samayaṃ, olokento mahādayo;

Metteyyo bodhisatto hi, vasate tusite pure.

The greatly compassionate Bodhisatta Metteyya, awaiting the time for Buddhahood, indeed dwells in the city of Tusita.

74.

74.

Therassa vacanaṃ sutvā, mahārājā mahāmatī;

Olokento mahāthūpaṃ, nipannova nimīlayi.

Hearing the words of the Elder, the great king of great wisdom, while looking at the Great Stupa, closed his eyes as he lay there.

75.

75.

Cavitvā taṃkhaṇaṃyeva, tusitā ahaṭe rathe;

Nibbattitvā ṭhitoyeva, dibbadeho adissatha.

Passing away at that very moment, he was reborn, and standing on a chariot brought from the Tusita realm, his divine body became visible.

76.

76.

Katassa [M 0.0191] puññakammassa, phalaṃ dassetumattano;

Mahājanassa dassento, attānaṃ samalaṅkataṃ.

To show the fruit of the meritorious deeds he had performed, he displayed his well-adorned self to the great multitude.

77.

77.

Rathaṭṭhoyeva tikkhattuṃ, mahāthūpaṃ padakkhiṇaṃ;

Katvāna thūpaṃ saṅghañca, vanditvā tusitaṃ agā.

While still standing on the chariot, he circumambulated the Great Stupa three times; and having paid homage to the Stupa and the Sangha, he went to the Tusita realm.

78.

78.

Nāṭakiyo idhāgantvā, makuṭaṃ yattha mocayuṃ;

“Makuṭamuttasālā”ti, ettha sālā katā ahu.

A hall was built at the place where the dancers came and removed their crowns; it was called the 'Hall of the Removed Crown'.

79.

79.

Citake ṭhapite raññe, sarīramhi mahājano;

Yatthāravi “rāvavaṭṭi-sālā”nāma tahiṃ ahu.

At the place where the great crowd lamented when the king's body was placed on the pyre, there was a hall named 'Rāvavaṭṭi-sālā'.

80.

80.

Rañño sarīraṃ jhāpesuṃ, yasmiṃ nissīmamāḷake;

So eva māḷako ettha, vuccate “rāja māḷako”.

In the boundary-less pavilion where they cremated the king's body, that very pavilion is here called the 'King's Pavilion'.

81.

81.

Duṭṭhagāmaṇirājā so, rājā nāmāraho mahā;

Metteyyassa bhagavato, hessati aggasāvako.

That King Duṭṭhagāmaṇi, a great king worthy of the name, will be the chief disciple of the Blessed One Metteyya.

82.

82.

Rañño pitā pitā tassa,

Mātā mātā bhavissati;

Saddhātisso kaniṭṭho tu,

Dutiyo hessati sāvako.

The king's father will be his father, and his mother will be his mother; Saddhātissa, his younger brother, will be the second disciple.

83.

83.

Sālirājakumāro yo,

Tassa rañño suto tuso;

Metteyyassa bhagavato,

Puttoyeva bhavissati.

Prince Sāli, who was the son of that king, will indeed become the son of the Blessed One Metteyya.

84.

84.

Evaṃ yo kusalaparo karoti puññaṃ,

Chādento aniyatapāpakaṃ bahumpi;

So saggaṃ sakale rami vo payāti tasmā,

Sappañño sa tatarato bhaveyya puññeti.

Thus, whoever is intent on good and performs merit, thereby overcoming even much uncertain evil, goes to heaven, delighting in every way. Therefore, a person of wisdom should be ever intent on merit.

Sujanappasādasaṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Mahāvaṃsa, composed for the serene faith and spiritual urgency of the virtuous.

Tusitapuragamanaṃ nāma

Named 'The Journey to the Tusita City'.

Dvattiṃsatimo paricchedo

The Thirty-second Chapter.

Tettiṃsatima pariccheda

The Thirty-third Chapter.

Dasarājako

The Ten Kings.

1.

1.

Duṭṭhagāmaṇirañño [M 0.0192] tu, rajjeṭhitā janā ahū;

Sālirājakumāroti, hassāsi vissuto suto.

As for King Duṭṭhagāmaṇi, he had a renowned and famous son known as Prince Sāli.

2.

2.

Atīva dhañño so āsi, puññakammarato sadā;

Atīva cārurupāya, satto caṇḍāliyā ahu.

He was exceedingly meritorious, always delighting in deeds of merit. He became attached to an outcaste woman who was of exceedingly charming beauty.

3.

3.

Asokamālādeviṃtaṃ, sambandhaṃ pubbajātiyā;

Rūpenā’ti piyāyanto, so rajjaṃ nevakāmayi.

Loving that Asokamālādevī exceedingly for her beauty, with whom he was connected from a previous birth, he did not desire the kingdom.

4.

4.

Duṭṭhagāmaṇibhātā’so, saddhātisso tadacchaye;

Rajjaṃ kāressā’bhisitto, aṭṭhārassa samā’samo.

After his demise, Duṭṭhagāmaṇi's brother, Saddhātissa, was anointed and ruled the kingdom for eighteen years.

5.

5.

Chakkakammaṃ sudhākammaṃ, hatthipākārameva ca;

Mahāthūpassa kāresi, so saddhākatanāmako.

He had the wheel-work, the plaster-work, and the elephant rampart for the Great Stupa made; he was named Saddhākata ('Done-by-Faith').

6.

6.

Dīpena lohapāsādo, uḍḍiyhittha susaṅkhato;

Kāresi lohapāsādaṃ, puna so sattabhūmakaṃ.

The well-constructed Lohapāsāda was burnt down by a lamp; he had the Lohapāsāda built again, seven stories high.

7.

7.

Navutisatasahassaggho, pāsādo āsi so tadā;

Dakkhiṇagīrivihāraṃ, kallakaleṇa meva ca.

At that time, that palace was worth ninety hundred thousand. He also built the Dakkhiṇagiri monastery and the Kallaka cave.

8.

8.

Kuḷumbālavihārañca, tathāpettaṅga vālikaṃ;

Velaṅgavaṭṭikañceva, dubbalavāpitissataṃ.

He also built the Kuḷumbāla monastery, and likewise Pettaṅgavālika, Velaṅgavaṭṭika, and the Dubbalavāpi-Tissa monastery.

9.

9.

Duratissakavāpiñca, tathāmātuvihārakaṃ;

Kāresi ādīghavāpiṃ, vihāraṃyojana yojane.

He built the Duratissaka tank and likewise the Mātuvihāra; he had the Dīghavāpi constructed, and a monastery at every yojana.

10.

10.

Dīghavāpivihārañca, kāresi sahacetiyaṃ;

Nānāratanakacchannaṃ, tattha kāresi cetiye.

He also had the Dīghavāpi monastery built, together with its cetiya. There, on the cetiya, he had a covering of various jewels made.

11.

11.

Sandhiyaṃ sandhiyaṃ tattha, rathacakkappamāṇakaṃ;

Sovaṇṇamālaṃ kāretvā, laggāpesi manoramaṃ.

There, at every joint, having had a beautiful golden garland made, the size of a chariot wheel, he had it attached.

12.

12.

Caturāsītisahassānaṃ[M 0.0193], dhammakkhandhānamissaro;

Caturāsītisahassāni, pūjācāpi akārayi.

He, the lord of the land, had eighty-four thousand offerings made for the eighty-four thousand sections of the Dhamma.

13.

13.

Evaṃ puññāni katvā so, anekāni mahīpati;

Kāyassabhedā devesu, tusitesu’papajjatha.

Having thus performed many meritorious deeds, that great king, after the breakup of the body, was reborn among the Tusita gods.

14.

14.

Saddhātissapakārāje, vasante dīghavāpiyaṃ;

Lajjītisso jeṭṭhasuto, girikumbhimanāmakaṃ.

While King Saddhātissa was residing at Dīghavāpi, his eldest son, Lajjītissa, built the delightful monastery named Girikumbhila.

15.

15.

Vihāraṃ kārayi rammaṃ, taṃkaniṭṭhasuto pana;

Thullatthano akāresi, vihāraṃ kandaravhayaṃ.

His youngest son, however, Thullatthana, built the monastery called Kandara.

16.

16.

Pitarā thullatthanako, bhātusantikamāyatā;

Sahevā’ha vihārassa, saṅghabhogatthamattano.

Thullatthana, having come to his brother's presence with his father, said, 'For the monastery, I too have a right to the Sangha's revenue for my own use.'

17.

17.

Saddhātisseuparate, sabbe’maccā samāgatā;

Thūpārāme bhikkhusaṅghaṃ, sakalaṃ sannipātiya.

After Saddhātissa's passing, all the ministers assembled, having gathered the entire Sangha at the Thūpārāma.

18.

18.

Saṅghānuññāyaraṭṭhassa, rakkhaṇatthaṃ kumārakaṃ;

Abhisiñcuṃ thullatthanaṃ, taṃ sutvā lajjītissato.

With the Sangha's permission, for the protection of the kingdom, they anointed the prince Thullatthana. Hearing this, Lajjītissa came here.

19.

19.

Idhāgantvā gahetvā taṃ, sayaṃ rajjamakārayi;

Māsañceva dasāhañca, rājā thullatthano pana.

Having come here and seized him, he himself took the throne. King Thullatthana, however, had reigned for one month and ten days.

20.

20.

Tissosamaṃ lajjītisso, saṅgho hutvā anādaro;

“Na jāniṃsu yathāvuḍḍhaṃ” mīti taṃ paribhāsayi.

Lajjītissa became disrespectful towards the Sangha. 'They did not recognize seniority,' thus he reviled them.

21.

21.

Pacchā saṅghaṃ khamāpetvā, daṇḍakammatthamissaro;

Tīṇi satasahassāni, datvāna urucetiye.

Later, having asked the Sangha for forgiveness, the lord, as a penalty, gave three hundred thousand at the great cetiya.

22.

22.

Silāmayāni kāresi, pupphayānāni tīṇiso;

Atho satasahassena, citāpesi ca antarā.

He had three stone flower-altars made. Then, with a hundred thousand, he also had a mound constructed in between.

23.

23.

Mahāthūpathūpārāmānaṃ, bhūmiṃbhūmissaro samaṃ;

Thūpārāme ca thūpassa, silākañcuka muttamaṃ.

The lord of the earth made the ground of the Mahāthūpa and the Thūpārāma level. And at the Thūpārāma, he made an excellent stone casing for the thūpa.

24.

24.

Thūpārāmassa purato, silāthūpakameva ca;

Lajjīkāsanasālañca, bhikkhusaṅghassa kārayi.

In front of the Thūpārāma, he also built a stone thūpa, and a Lajjika-seat hall for the Sangha of monks.

25.

25.

Kañcukaṃ [M 0.0194] kaṇṭake thūpe, kārāpesi silāmayaṃ;

Datvāna satasahassaṃ, vihāre cetiyavhaye.

He had a stone casing made for the Kaṇṭaka Thūpa, and gave a hundred thousand to the Cetiyagiri monastery.

26.

26.

Girikumbhilanāmassa, vihārassa mahamhi so;

Saṭṭhibhikkhusahassānaṃ, ticīvaramadāpayi.

At the great festival of the monastery named Girikumbhila, he provided the three robes for sixty thousand monks.

27.

27.

Ariṭṭhavihāraṃ kāresi, tathākandarahinakaṃ;

Gāmikānañca bhikkhūnaṃ, bhesajjāni adāpayi.

He had the Ariṭṭha monastery built, and likewise the Kandarahinaka. And he provided medicines for the village monks.

28.

28.

Kimicchakaṃ taṇḍulañca, bhikkhunīnamadāpayi;

Samānava’ṭhamāsañca, rajjaṃ so kārayī idha.

He had rice and whatever else they wished for given to the nuns. And he ruled the kingdom here for nine years and eight months.

29.

29.

Mate lajjikatissamhi, kaniṭṭho tassa kārayi;

Rajjaṃ chaḷeva vassāni, khallāṭanāganāmako.

When Lajjitissa died, his younger brother, named Khallāṭanāga, ruled for six years.

30.

30.

Lohapāsādaparivāre, pāsāde’ti manorame;

Lohapāsādasobhatthaṃ, eso dvattiṃsakārayi.

For the splendor of the Lohapāsāda, he had thirty-two very delightful small palaces built as an enclosure for the Lohapāsāda.

31.

31.

Mahāthūpassa parito, cāruno hemamālino;

Vālikaṅgaṇamariyādaṃ, pākārañca akārayi.

Around the beautiful Great Thūpa with its golden garlands, he had the boundary of the sand courtyard and a surrounding wall made.

32.

32.

Sovakurundapāsakaṃ, vihārañca akārayi;

Puññakammānicaññāni, kārāpesi mahīpati.

He constructed the Kurundapāsaka monastery. The great king also had other meritorious deeds performed.

33.

33.

Taṃ mahārattatonāma, senāpati mahīpatiṃ;

Khallāṭanāgarājānaṃ, nagareyeva aggahi.

A commander named Mahāratta seized that king, King Khallāṭanāga, right in the city.

34.

34.

Tassa rañño kaniṭṭhotu, vaṭṭagāmaṇināmako;

Taṃ duṭṭhasenāpatikaṃ, hantvā rajjamakārayi.

But that king's younger brother, named Vaṭṭagāmaṇi, having killed that wicked commander, took the throne.

35.

35.

Khallāṭanāgaraññoso, puttakaṃ sakabhātuno;

Mahācūlikanāmānaṃ, puttaṭhāne ṭhapesi ca.

He placed his nephew, Mahācūlika by name, the son of his brother King Khallāṭanāga, in the position of a son.

36.

36.

Tammātaraṃ nuḷādeviṃ, mahesiñca akāsiso;

Pītiṭhāne ṭhitatā’ssa, pītirājāti abravuṃ.

He also made his mother, Queen Anulā, his chief queen. Because he stood in the place of a father, they called him Piturāja.

37.

37.

Evaṃ rajje’bhisittassa, tassa māsamhi pañcame;

Rohaṇe nakulanagare, eko brāhmaṇaceṭato.

Thus, in the fifth month after his consecration to the kingship, in the city of Nakula in Rohaṇa, a certain brahmin servant...

38.

38.

Tiyo [M 0.0195] nāma brāhmaṇassa, vaco sutvā apaṇḍito;

Coro asu mahātassa, parivāro ahosi ca.

A foolish brahmin named Tissa, upon hearing a certain word, became a great rebel, and his following was large.

39.

39.

Sagaṇāsattadamiḷā, mahātitthamhi otaruṃ;

Tadā brāhmaṇatiyo ca, te sattadamiḷāpica.

Seven Damilas with their troops landed at Mahātittha. Then the brahmin Tissa and those seven Damilas...

40.

40.

Chakkatthāya visajjesuṃ, lekhaṃ bhūpatisantikaṃ;

Rājā brāhmaṇatiyassa, lekhaṃ pesesi nītimā.

They sent a letter to the king for the sake of the royal umbrella. The wise king sent a letter to the brahmin Tissa.

41.

41.

“Rajjaṃ tava idāneva, gaṇha tvaṃ damiḷe” iti;

Sādhūti so damiḷehi, yujjhi gaṇhiṃsu te tu taṃ.

“The kingdom is now yours; you may seize the Damilas.” “Good,” said he, and fought with the Damilas; but they captured him.

42.

42.

Tato te damiḷā yuddhaṃ, raññā saha pavattayuṃ;

Koḷambālakasāmantā, yuddhe rājā parājito.

Then those Damilas waged war with the king. Near Koḷambālaka, the king was defeated in battle.

43.

43.

Titthārāmaduvārena, rathāruḷho palāyati;

Paṇḍukābhayarājena, titthārāmohi kārito;

Vāsito ca tadā āsi, ekavīsati rājusū.

Mounted on a chariot, he fled through the gate of the Titthārāma. The Titthārāma had been built by King Paṇḍukābhaya, and at that time, it was inhabited by twenty-one princes.

44.

44.

Taṃ disvā palāyantaṃ, nigaṇṭhogirināmako;

“Palāyati mahākāḷa-sīhaḷo”ti bhusaṃ ravi.

Seeing him fleeing, a Nigaṇṭha named Giri shouted loudly, “The great black Sinhalese is fleeing!”

45.

45.

Taṃ sutvāna mahārājā, “siddhe mama manorathe;

Vihāraṃ ettha kāressaṃ”, iccevaṃ cintayī tadā.

Hearing this, the great king then thought, “When my wish is fulfilled, I shall have a monastery built here.”

46.

46.

Sagabbhaṃ anulādeviṃ, aggahī rakkhiyā iti;

Mahācūḷa mahānāga-kumārecāpī rakkhiye.

He took with him for protection the pregnant Queen Anulā, and also the princes Mahācūḷa and Mahānāga.

47.

47.

Rathassa lahubhāvatthaṃ, ḍatvā cūḷāmaṇiṃsubhaṃ;

Otāresi somadeviṃ, tassa’nuññāya bhūpati.

To lighten the chariot, the king, having given her the splendid crest-jewel, had Somadevī dismount with her permission.

48.

48.

Yuddhāyagamaneyeva, puttake dve ca deviyo;

Gāhayitvāna nikkhanto, saṅkito so parājaye.

Indeed, when going to the battle, he had set out taking with him his two sons and the queens, for he was apprehensive of defeat.

49.

49.

Asakkuṇitvā gāhetuṃ, pattaṃ bhuttaṃ jinena taṃ;

Palāyitvā vessagīri-vane abhiniyiyiso.

Unable to take with him the bowl used by the Victor, he fled and hid himself in the Vessagiri forest.

50.

50.

Kutthikkulamahātissa-thero disvā tahaṃ tu taṃ;

Bhattaṃ pādā anāmaṭṭhaṃ, piṇḍadānaṃ vivajjiya.

The elder Kutthikkula Mahātissa, seeing him there, avoided the alms-gift which the king offered from his own untouched food.

51.

51.

Atha [M 0.0196] ketakipattamhi, likhitvā haṭṭhamānaso;

Saṅghabhogaṃ vihārassa, tassa pādāmahīpati.

Then, with a joyful mind, the king wrote on a ketaki leaf and gave to him the monastery's revenue.

52.

52.

Tato gantvā silāsobbha-kaṇḍakamhi vasī tato;

Gantvāna mātuvelaṅge, sālagalasamīpago.

Then, going to Silāsobbha-kaṇḍaka, he dwelt there. From there, going to Mātuvelaṅga, he came near to Sālagala.

53.

53.

Tatthaddasa diṭṭhapubbaṃ, theraṃ thero mahīpatiṃ;

Upaṭṭhākassa appesi, tanasivassa sādhukaṃ.

There he saw the elder whom he had seen before. The elder duly entrusted the king to his attendant, Tanasiva.

54.

54.

Tassa so tanasivassa, raṭṭhikassa’ntike tahiṃ;

Rājā cuddasavassāni, vasī tena upaṭṭhito.

The king lived there for fourteen years in the vicinity of the regional chief Tanasiva, attended by him.

55.

55.

Sattasu damīḷesve’ko, somādeviṃ madāvahaṃ;

Rāgaratto gahetvāna, paratīramagālahuṃ.

One among the seven Damilas, inflamed with passion, seized the enchanting Somādevī and quickly went to the other shore.

56.

56.

Ekopattaṃ dasabalassa, anurādhapure ṭhitaṃ;

Ādāya tena santuṭṭho, paratīramagālahuṃ.

Another, taking the bowl of the Ten-Powered One that was in Anurādhapura, was content with it and quickly went to the other shore.

57.

57.

Puḷahattho tu damiḷo, tīṇivassāni kārayi;

Rajjaṃ senāpatiṃ katvā, damiḷaṃ bāhiyavhayaṃ.

The Damila Puḷahattha ruled for three years, having made the Damila named Bāhiya his general.

58.

58.

Puḷahatthaṃ gahetvā taṃ, dūre vassāni bāhīyo;

Rajjaṃ kāresi tassā’si, paṇayamāro camūpati.

Having seized that Puḷahattha, Bāhiya ruled the kingdom for two years. Paṇayamāra was his army commander.

59.

59.

Bāhīyaṃ taṃ gahetvāna, rājā’si paṇayamārako;

Sattavassāni tassā’si, piḷayamāro camūpati.

Having seized that Bāhiya, Paṇayamāra became king. For seven years, Piḷayamāra was his army commander.

60.

60.

Paṇayamāraṃ gahetvā so, rājāsi pīḷayamārako;

Sattamāsāni tassāsi, dāṭhiyo tu camūpati.

Having seized Paṇayamāra, Piḷayamāra became king. For seven months, Dāṭhiya was his army commander.

61.

61.

Pīḷayamāraṃ gahetvā so, dāṭhiyo damiḷo pana;

Rajjaṃ’nurādhanagare, duve vassāni kārayi.

Having seized Piḷayamāra, that Damila Dāṭhiya then ruled the kingdom in the city of Anurādhapura for two years.

62.

62.

Evaṃ damiḷarājūnaṃ, tesaṃ pañcannamevahi;

Honti cuddasavassānī, sattamāsā ca uttariṃ.

Thus, for those five Damila kings, there were fourteen years and seven months besides.

63.

63.

Gatāya tu nivāsatthaṃ, malaye’nuladeviyā;

Bhariyākanasivassa, pādāpahari pacchiyaṃ.

When Anulādevī, the wife of Kanasiva, had gone to a dwelling in Malaya, she struck his foot from behind.

64.

64.

Kujjhitvā rodamānāsā, rājānaṃ upasakimi;

Taṃ sutvā tanasivoso, manumādāya nikkhami.

Angered and weeping, she approached the king. Hearing this, that Tanasiva took Manu and departed.

65.

65.

Deviyā [M 0.0197] vacanaṃ sutvā, tassa āgamanā purā;

Dviputtaṃ devimādāya, tato rājā’pi nikkhami.

Hearing the queen's words, before his arrival, the king also departed, taking the queen with her two sons.

66.

66.

Dhanuṃ sandhāya āyantaṃ, sīvaṃ vijjhi mahāsīvo;

Rājā nāmaṃ bhāvayitvā, akāsi jinasaṅgahaṃ.

Drawing his bow, Mahāsīva pierced Sīva as he approached. The king, reflecting on the name, made an offering to the Conqueror.

67.

67.

Alattha aṭṭhāmacceca, mahante yodhasammate;

Parivāro mahāāsī, parihāro ca rājino.

He gained eight ministers, great and esteemed warriors. The king's retinue was vast, and so were his resources.

68.

68.

Kumbhīlakamahātissa-thera disvā mahāyaso;

Acchagallavihāramhi, buddhapūjamakārayi.

The glorious one, seeing the elder Kumbhīlaka Mahātissa at the Acchagalla monastery, had an offering to the Buddha performed.

69.

69.

Vatthuṃ sodhetumāruḷho, akāsacetiyaṅgaṇaṃ;

Kavisīse amaccamhi, orohantomahīpati.

Having ascended the terrace of the Ākāsa Cetiya to cleanse the site, the king was descending while the minister Kavisīsa was there.

70.

70.

Ārohanto sadeviko, disvā magge nisinnakaṃ;

“Na nipanno”ti kujjhitvā, kavisīsaṃ aghātayi.

Ascending with his queen, and seeing him seated on the path, the king became enraged, thinking, 'He is not prostrate,' and killed Kavisīsa.

71.

71.

Sesā sattaamaccāvi, nibbinnā tena rājinā;

Tassa’ntikā palāyitvā, pakkamantā yathāruci.

The remaining seven ministers, disgusted with that king, fled from his presence, departing as they pleased.

72.

72.

Magge viluttā corehi, vihāraṃ hambugallakaṃ;

Pavisitvāna addakkhuṃ, tissattheraṃ bahussutaṃ.

Robbed by thieves on the road, they entered the Hambugallaka monastery and saw the very learned elder Tissa.

73.

73.

Catunekāyiko thero, yathāladdhāni dāpayi;

Vatthaphāṇitatelāni, taṇḍulā pāhuṇā tathā.

The elder, master of the four Nikāyas, gave what he had received: cloth, molasses, oil, rice, and likewise provisions.

74.

74.

Assatthakāle thero so,

“Kuhiṃyātā”ti pucchite;

Attānaṃ āvīkatvā te,

Taṃ pavattiṃ nivedayuṃ.

At a time of ease, when asked by that elder, 'Whence have you come?' they revealed themselves and recounted that event.

75.

75.

“Kāretuṃ kehi sakkā nu, jinasāsanapaggahaṃ;

Damiḷehi vā’tha raññā, iti puṭṭhā tu te pana.

But when they were asked, 'By whom is it possible to bring about the upholding of the Conqueror's Dispensation, by the Damiḷas or by the king?'

76.

76.

“Rañño sakkā”ti āhaṃsu, saññāpetvāna te iti;

Ubho tissa mahātissa-therā ādāya te tato.

'It is possible for the king,' they said. Having thus persuaded them, both elders, Tissa and Mahātissa, then took them from there.

77.

77.

Rājino santikaṃ netvā, aññamaññaṃ khamāpayuṃ;

Rājā ca te amaccā ca, thero eva mayācayuṃ.

Having led them to the king's presence, they made them forgive each other. Both the king and those ministers then entreated the elders.

78.

78.

Siddhe [M 0.0198] kamme pesiteno, gantabbaṃ santikaṃ iti;

Therā datvā paṭiññaṃ te, yathāṭhānamagañchisuṃ.

'When the task is accomplished and we send for you, you must come to our presence.' The elders, having given their promise to them, departed to their own places.

79.

79.

Anurādhapuraṃ rājā, āgantvāna mahāyaso;

Dāṭhikaṃ damiḷaṃ hantvā, sayaṃ rajjamakārayi.

The glorious king, having come to Anurādhapura, slew Dāṭhika the Damiḷa and himself ruled the kingdom.

80.

80.

Tato nigaṇṭhārāmaṃ taṃ, viddhaṃsetvā mahīpati;

Vihāraṃ kārayi tattha, dvādasa pariveṇakaṃ.

Then the king, having destroyed that monastery of the Nigaṇṭhas, built a vihāra there with twelve cells.

81.

81.

Mahāvihārapaṭṭhānā, dvīsu vassasa tesu ca;

Sattarasasu vassesu, dasamāsā’mikesu ca.

Two hundred and seventeen years and ten additional months having passed since the founding of the Mahāvihāra,

82.

82.

Tathā dinesu dasasu, atikkantesu sādaro;

Abhayagiri vihāraṃso, patiṭṭhāpesi bhūpati.

and when ten days had likewise passed, the king reverently established the Abhayagiri Vihāra.

83.

83.

Akkosiyitvā te there, tesu pubbupakārino;

Taṃ mahātissa therassa, vihāraṃ mānado adā.

Having reviled those elders who were his former benefactors, the giver of honor gave that monastery to the elder Mahātissa.

84.

84.

Girissa yasmā gārāme, rājā kāresi sobhayo;

Tasmā’bhaya giritveva, vihāro nāmako ahu.

Because the king built the splendid monastery in the grove of Giri, therefore the monastery came to be named Abhayagiri.

85.

85.

Āṇāpetvā somādeviṃ,

Yathā ṭhāne ṭhapesiso;

Tassātannāmakaṃ katvā,

Somārāma makārayi.

Having summoned Queen Somā, he established her in a suitable place. Naming it after her, he had the Somārāma built.

86.

86.

Rathā oropitā sā hi, tasmiṃṭhāne varaṅganā;

Kaddambapuppha gumbamhi, nilinā tattha addasa.

For that noble lady had been made to descend from her chariot at that place; there she saw one hiding in a thicket of Kadamba flowers.

87.

87.

Muttayantaṃ sāmaṇeraṃ, maggaṃ hatthena chādiya;

Rājā tassa vaco sutvā, vihāraṃ tattha kārayi.

The king, hearing the words of a novice who was urinating while covering the path with his hand, had a monastery built there.

88.

88.

Mahāthūpassuttarato,

Cetiyaṃ uccavatthukaṃ;

Silā sobhakaṇḍakaṃ nāma,

Rājā soyeva kārayi.

To the north of the Great Thūpa, that same king had a cetiya with a high foundation built, named Silāsobhakaṇḍaka.

89.

89.

Tesu sattasu yodhesu, uttiyo nāma kārayi;

Nagaramhā dakkhiṇato, vihāraṃ dakkhiṇavhayaṃ.

Among those seven warriors, the one named Uttiya had a monastery called Dakkhiṇa built, south of the city.

90.

90.

Tatteva [M 0.0199] mūlavokāsa, vīhāraṃ mūlanāmako;

Amacco kārayī tena, sopi taṃnāmako ahu.

There indeed, at the root-site, a minister had a monastery named Mūla built; for that reason, he too became known by that name.

91.

91.

Kāresi sāliyārāmaṃ, amacco sāliyavhayo;

Kāresi pabbatārāmaṃ, amacco pabbatavhayo.

The minister named Sāliya had the Sāliyārāma built. The minister named Pabbata had the Pabbatārāma built.

92.

92.

Uttaratissarāmantu, tissāmacco akārayi;

Vihāre niṭṭhite ramme, tissathera mupaccate.

The minister Tissa had the Uttaratissārāma built. When the delightful monastery was completed, he approached the elder Tissa.

93.

93.

“Tumhākaṃ paṭisanthāra, vasena’mhehi kārite;

Vihāre dema tumhākaṃ, iti vatvā adaṃsu ca.

‘We have caused these monasteries to be built on account of your hospitality; we give them to you,’ so saying, they gave them.

94.

94.

Thero sabbatthavāsesi, te te bhikkhū yathā rahaṃ;

Amaccā’daṃsu saṅghassa, vividhe samaṇārahe.

The elder had those various monks take up residence everywhere, as was fitting. The ministers gave to the Saṅgha various requisites suitable for ascetics.

95.

95.

Rājā sakavihāramhi, vasante samupaṭṭhahi;

Paccayehi anunehi, tena te bahavo ahuṃ.

The king attended upon him while he was dwelling in his own monastery; through requisites and kindness, on that account, they became numerous.

96.

96.

Theraṃ kulehī saṃsaṭṭhaṃ, mahātissoti vissutaṃ;

Kulasaṃsaṭṭha dosena, saṅgho taṃ nīhari ito.

The Saṅgha expelled from here that elder, known as Mahātissa, who associated with families, due to the fault of associating with families.

97.

97.

Tassa sisso bahalamassu-

Tissattheroti pissuto;

Kuddho’bhayagiriṃ gantvā,

Vasi pakkhaṃ vahaṃ tahiṃ.

His disciple, the Elder Tissa, known as Bahalamassu-Tissa, went to Abhayagiri in anger and dwelt there, supporting a faction.

98.

98.

Tatoppabhuti te bhikkhū, mahāvihāranāgamuṃ;

Evaṃ te’bhayagirikā, niggatā theravādato.

From that time onward, those monks did not go to the Mahāvihāra. Thus, those of Abhayagiri departed from the Theravāda.

99.

99.

Pabhinnā’bhayagirikehi, dakkhiṇavihārikāyati;

Evaṃ te theravādīhi, pabhinnā bhikkhavo dvidhā.

The residents of the Dakkhiṇavihāra split from the residents of Abhayagiri; thus those monks were split in two from the Theravādins.

100.

100.

Mahā abhayabhikkhū te, vaḍḍhetuṃ dīpavāsino;

Vaṭṭagāmaṇibhūmindo, pattiṃ nāma adāsi so.

In order to support those great monks of Abhayagiri, dwellers on the island, that ruler of the land, Vaṭṭagāmaṇi, gave a village named Patti.

101.

101.

Vihārapariveṇāni, ghaṭābaddhe akārayi;

“Paṭisaṅkharaṇaṃ evaṃ, hessatīti vicintiya.

He had monasteries and cells built, bound with water pots, thinking, ‘Thus will there be restoration.’

102.

102.

Piṭakattayapāḷiñca, tassa aṭṭhakathampi ca;

Mukhapāṭhena ānesuṃ, pubbe bhikkhū mahāmati.

Formerly, the monks of great wisdom handed down the Pāḷi of the Three Piṭakas and its commentary by oral recitation.

103.

103.

Hāniṃ [M 0.0200] disvāna sattānaṃ, tadā bhikkhū samāgatā;

Ciraṭṭhitatthaṃ dhammassa, potthakesu likhāpayuṃ.

Seeing the decline of beings, the monks then assembled; for the long-lasting stability of the Dhamma, they had it written in books.

104.

104.

Vaṭṭagāmaṇi abhayo, rājā rajjamakārayi;

Iti dvādasavassāni, pañcamāsesu ādito.

King Vaṭṭagāmaṇi Abhaya reigned. Thus, from the beginning, for twelve years and five months.

105.

105.

Itī parahita mattano hitañca,

Paṭilabhiyissariyaṃ karoti pañño;

Vipulamapi kubuddhiladdhabhovaṃ,

Ubhayahitaṃ na karoti bhogaluddho’ti.

Thus, a wise person, having obtained sovereignty, acts for the welfare of others and for his own welfare. But one with wrong understanding, greedy for wealth, though he has obtained vast possessions, does not act for the welfare of both.

Sujanappasādasaṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Mahāvaṃsa, composed for the serene joy and spiritual urgency of the virtuous.

Dasarājako nāma

The Ten Kings.

Tettiṃsatimo paricchedo.

The Thirty-third Chapter.

Catuttiṃsatima pariccheda

The Thirty-fourth Chapter.

Ekādasarājadīpano

The Elucidation of the Eleven Kings.

1.

1.

Tadaccaye mahācūlī-mahātisso akārayi;

Rajjaṃ cuddasavassāni, dhammena ca samena ca.

After his passing, Mahācūḷī-Mahātissa reigned; he ruled the kingdom for fourteen years, righteously and justly.

2.

2.

Sahatthena kataṃ dānaṃ, so sutvāna mahapphalaṃ;

Paṭhameyeva vassamhi, gantvā aññātavesavā.

Hearing that a gift given with one's own hand bears great fruit, in the very first year, he went in disguise.

3.

3.

Katvāna sālilavanaṃ, laddhāya bhatiyā tato;

Piṇḍapātaṃ mahāsumma-therassā’dā mahīpati.

Having worked at reaping rice, and then having obtained wages from that, the lord of the earth gave almsfood to the Elder Mahāsumma.

4.

4.

Soṇṇagirimhi puna so, tīṇivassāni khattiyo;

Guḷayantamhi katvāna, bhatiṃladdhā guḷe tato.

Again, in Soṇṇagiri, that khattiya for three years, having worked at a sugar mill, then obtained wages in sugar.

5.

5.

Te guḷe āharāpetvā, puraṃ āgamma bhūpati;

Bhikkhusaṅghassa pādāsi, mahādānaṃ mahīpati.

Having had those sugar balls brought, the lord of the earth came to the city; the ruler of the land gave a great alms-offering to the community of monks.

6.

6.

Tiṃsabhikkhusahassassa, adā acchādanāni ca;

Dvādasannaṃ sahassānaṃ, bhikkhūnīnaṃ tatheva ca.

He gave robes to thirty thousand monks, and likewise to twelve thousand nuns.

7.

7.

Kārayitvā [M 0.0201] mahīpālo, vihāraṃ suppatiṭṭhitaṃ;

Saṭṭhibhikkhu sahassassa, ticīvaramadāpayi.

The protector of the earth, having had a well-established monastery built, caused the triple robe to be given to sixty thousand monks.

8.

8.

Tiṃsa sahassa saṅkhānaṃ, bhikkhunīnañca dāpayi;

Maṇḍavāpi vihāraṃ so, tathā abhayagallakaṃ.

He also caused robes to be given to thirty thousand nuns; he built the Maṇḍavāpi monastery, as well as the Abhayagallaka.

9.

9.

Vaṅgupaṭṭaṅgagallañca, dīghabāhukagallakaṃ;

Vālagāma vihārañca, rājā soyeva kārayi.

That same king also had Vaṅgupaṭṭaṅgagalla, Dīghabāhukagallaka, and the Vālagāma monastery built.

10.

10.

Evaṃ saddhāya so rājā, katvā puññāninekadhā;

Catuddasannaṃ vassānaṃ, accayena divaṃ agā.

Thus, that king, with faith, having performed meritorious deeds of many kinds, after the passing of fourteen years, went to heaven.

11.

11.

Vaṭṭagāmaṇino putto, coranāgoti vissuto;

Mahācūḷissarajjamhi, coro hutvā caritadā.

The son of Vaṭṭagāmaṇi, known as Coranāga, having become a robber, wandered about during the reign of Mahācūḷi.

12.

12.

Mahācūḷe uparate, rajjaṃ kārayi āgato;

Attano corakāle so, nivāsaṃ yesunālabhi.

When Mahācūḷi passed away, he came and ruled the kingdom. During his time as a robber, there were those from whom he did not obtain shelter.

13.

13.

Aṭṭharasavihāre te, viddhaṃsāpesi dummati;

Rajjaṃ dvādasavassāni, coranāgo akārayi.

That evil-minded one caused those eighteen monasteries to be destroyed; Coranāga ruled the kingdom for twelve years.

14.

14.

Lokantarika nirayaṃ, pāposoupapajjatha;

Tadaccaye mahācūḷhi-rañño putto akārayi.

That evil one was reborn in the Lokantarika hell; after his passing, the son of King Mahācūḷi reigned.

15.

15.

Rajjaṃ tīṇeva vassāni, rājātisso’ti vissuto;

Coranāgassa devītu, vīsamaṃ vīsamānulā.

Renowned as King Tissa, he ruled the kingdom for just three years. But the wicked Anulā, queen of Coranāga, gave him poison.

16.

16.

Vīsaṃ datvāna māresi, balattherattamānasā;

Tasmiṃyevabalatthesā, anulārattamānasā.

Having given poison, she killed him, her mind being infatuated with a palace guard. In that very palace guard was Anulā's mind infatuated.

17.

17.

Tissaṃ vīsenaghātetvā, tassa rajjamadāsisā;

Sīvo nāma balatthoso, jeṭṭhadovāriko tahiṃ.

Having killed Tissa with poison, she gave the kingdom to him. He was a palace guard named Sīva, the chief doorkeeper there.

18.

18.

Katvā mahesiṃ anulaṃ, vassaṃ māsadvayā’cikaṃ;

Rajjaṃ kāresi nagare, vaṭuke damiḷe’nulā.

Having made Anulā his chief queen, he ruled the kingdom in the city for a year and two months. Anulā became infatuated with Vaṭuka the Damiḷa.

19.

19.

Rattā vīsena taṃ hantvā, vaṭuke rajjamappayi;

Vaṭuko damiḷo so hi, pure nagaravaḍḍhakī.

Being infatuated, she killed him with poison and gave the kingdom to Vaṭuka. For that Vaṭuka the Damiḷa was formerly a city carpenter.

20.

20.

Mahesiṃ anulaṃ katvā, vassaṃ māsadvayādhikaṃ;

Rajjaṃ kāresi nagare, anulā tattha āgataṃ.

Having made Anulā his chief queen, he ruled the kingdom in the city for a year and two months. Anulā then saw one who had come there.

21.

21.

Passitvā dārubhatikaṃ, tasmiṃ sārattamānasā;

Hantvā visena vaṭukaṃ, tassa rajjaṃ samappayi.

Seeing the wood-carrier, she became infatuated with him; having killed Vaṭuka with poison, she handed the kingdom over to him.

22.

22.

Dārubhatikatisso [M 0.0202] so, mahesiṃ kariyānulaṃ;

Ekamāsādhikaṃ vassaṃ, pure rajjamakārayi.

That Tissa the wood-carrier, having made Anulā his chief queen, ruled the kingdom in the city for a year and one month.

23.

23.

Kāresi so pokkharaṇiṃ, mahāmeghavane lahuṃ;

Nilīye nāma damiḷe, sā purohitabrāhmaṇe.

He quickly had a pond made in the Mahāmeghavana. She became infatuated with a Damiḷa named Niliya, a purohita-brahmin.

24.

24.

Rāgena rattā anulā, tena saṃvāsakāminī;

Dārubhatikatissaṃtaṃ, vīsaṃ datvāna ghātiya.

Anulā, impassioned with lust and desiring intercourse with him, killed that Tissa the wood-carrier by giving him poison.

25.

25.

Nilīyassa adā rajjaṃ, sopi nilīyabrāhmaṇo;

Taṃ mahesiṃ karitvāna, niccaṃ tāya upaṭṭhito.

She gave the kingdom to Niliya, and that brahmin Niliya, having made her his chief queen, was constantly attended by her.

26.

26.

Rajjaṃ kāresi chammāsaṃ, anurādhapure idha;

Dvattiṃsāya balatthehi, vatthukāmā yathāruciṃ.

He ruled the kingdom for six months here in Anurādhapura, while she, indulging her desires, consorted with thirty-two palace guards as she pleased.

27.

27.

Vīsena taṃ ghātayitvā, nilīyaṃ khattiyānulā;

Rajjaṃ sā anulādevī, catumāsamakārayi.

Having had that Niliya killed with poison, the Khattiyā Anulā, that Queen Anulā, herself ruled the kingdom for four months.

28.

28.

Mahācūḷikarājassa, putto dutiyako pana;

Kūṭakaṇṇatisso nāma, bhīto so’nuladeviyā.

Now, the second son of King Mahācūḷika, named Kūṭakaṇṇatissa, was afraid of Queen Anulā.

29.

29.

Palāyitvā pabbajitvā, kāle pattabalo idha;

Āgantvā ghātayitvā, taṃ anulaṃ duṭṭhamānasaṃ.

Having fled and gone forth, in time he gained a force here; returning, he killed that wicked-minded Anulā.

30.

30.

Rajjaṃ kāresi dvāvīsaṃ, vassāni manujādhipo;

Mahāuposathāgāraṃ, akā cetiyapabbate.

The lord of men ruled the kingdom for twenty-two years; he built the great Uposatha hall on Cetiyapabbata.

31.

31.

Gharassa tassa purato, silāthūpamakārayi;

Bodhiṃ ropesi tattheva, sova cetiyepabbate.

In front of that house, he had a stone thūpa made; he also planted a Bodhi tree right there on Cetiyapabbata.

32.

32.

Pelagāmavihārañca, antaragaṅgāya kārayi;

Tattheva vaṇṇakaṃ nāma, mahāmātikameva ca.

He had the Pelagāmavihāra built by the Antaragaṅgā, and right there also the one named Vaṇṇaka and the Mahāmātika.

33.

33.

Ambaduggamahāvāpiṃ, bhayoluppalameva ca;

Sattahatthuccapākāraṃ, purassa parikhaṃ tathā.

He also had made the Ambadugga great tank and the Bhayoluppala tank, likewise a rampart seven cubits high and a moat for the city.

34.

34.

Mahāvatthumhi anulaṃ, jhāpayitvā asaññataṃ;

Apanīya tato thokaṃ, mahāvatthumakārayi.

Having had the unrestrained Anulā burned on a pyre, and having removed a little of the earth from there, he had a palace built on that site.

35.

35.

Padumassaravanuyyānaṃ, nagareyeva kārayi;

Matā’ssa dante dhovitvā, pabbaji jinasāsane.

He had the Padumassara pleasure garden made in the city itself; his mother, having cleaned her teeth, went forth into the Dispensation of the Conqueror.

36.

36.

Kulasantake [M 0.0203] gharaṭṭhāne, mātubhikkhunupassayaṃ;

Kāresi dantagehanti, vissato āsi tena so.

On the site of the family house, he had a nunnery built for his mother; for that reason, he became known as Dantageha.

37.

37.

Tadaccaye tassa putto, nāmako bhātikābhayo;

Aṭṭhavīsativassāni, rajjaṃ kāresi khattiyo.

After his passing, his son, the Khattiya named Bhātikābhaya, ruled the kingdom for twenty-eight years.

38.

38.

Mahādāṭṭhikarājassa, bhātikattāmahīpati;

Dīpe “bhātikarājā”ti, pākaṭo āsi dhammiko.

Because he was the brother of King Mahādāṭhika, this righteous king became known on the island as ‘King Bhātika’.

39.

39.

Kāresi lohapāsāde, paṭisaṅkhārametthaso;

Mahāthūpe vedikā dve, thūpavhe’posathavhayaṃ.

He had restoration work done on the Lohapāsāda here, and at the Mahāthūpa he had two railings made, named the Thūpa railing and the Uposatha railing.

40.

40.

Attano balimujjhitvā, nagarassa samantato;

Ropāpetvā yojanamhi, sumanāna’jjukāni ca.

Having given up his own revenue, he had rows of jasmine planted for a yojana all around the city.

41.

41.

Pādavecikato yāva, dhuracchattānarādhipo;

Caturaṅgalabahalena, gandhena urucetiyaṃ.

The lord of men had the great cetiya, from its base railing up to the parasol shaft, plastered with fragrant paste four finger-breadths thick.

42.

42.

Limpāpetvāna pupphāni, vaṇṭehi tattha sādhukaṃ;

Nivesitvāna koresi, thūpaṃ mālāgulopamaṃ.

And having had it plastered, he then had flowers carefully fixed there by their stalks, making the thūpa resemble a ball of garlands.

43.

43.

Punadvaṅgulabahalāya, manosilāya cetiyaṃ;

Limpāpetvāna kāresi, tatheva kusumācitaṃ.

Again, having had the cetiya plastered with realgar two finger-breadths thick, he then had it covered with flowers in the same way.

44.

44.

Puna sopānato yāva, dhuracchattāva cetiyaṃ;

Pupphehi okirāpetvā, chādesi puppharāsino.

Again, having had the cetiya strewn with flowers from the staircase up to the parasol shaft, he covered it with heaps of blossoms.

45.

45.

Uṭṭhāpetvāna yantehi, jalaṃ abhayavāpito;

Jalehi thūpaṃ sevanto, balapūjamakārayi.

Having drawn water with machines from the Abhaya Tank, he honored the stupa with water and made a great offering.

46.

46.

Sakaṭasatena muttānaṃ, saddhiṃ telena sādhukaṃ;

Maddāpetvā sudhāpiṇḍaṃ, sudhākammamakārayi.

With a hundred cartloads of pearls, together with well-prepared oil, having had a plaster compound kneaded, he had the plasterwork done.

47.

47.

Pavālajālaṃ kāretvā, taṃ khipāpiya cetiye;

Sovaṇṇāni padumāni, cakkamattāni sandhisu.

Having had a net of coral made, he had it cast over the cetiya; in its intersections, he had golden lotuses, the size of wheels, placed.

48.

48.

Laggāpetvā tato muttā-kalāpe yāva heṭṭhimā;

Padumā’lambayitvāna, mahāthūpamapūjayi.

Then, having had clusters of pearls fastened all the way to the bottom and having hung lotuses, he paid homage to the great stupa.

49.

49.

Gaṇasajjhāyasaddaṃ [M 0.0204] so, dhātugabbhamhitādini;

Sutvā “adisvā taṃnā’haṃ, vuṭṭhahissanti nicchito.

Having heard the sound of group recitation in the relic chamber and so forth, he, being determined, resolved: 'Without seeing that, I shall not rise.'

50.

50.

Pācinādikamūlamhi, anāhāro nipajjatha;

Therā dvāraṃ māpayitvā, dhātugabbhaṃ nayiṃsu taṃ.

At the eastern base, he lay down without food; the elders, having had a door created, led him into the relic chamber.

51.

51.

Dhātugabbhavibhūtiṃso, sabbaṃ disvā mahīpati;

Nikkhanto tādiseheva, pottharūpehi pūjayi.

Having seen all the splendor of the relic chamber, the great king, upon emerging, offered worship with models of that very same kind.

52.

52.

Madhugandhehi gandhehi, ghaṭehi sarasehi ca;

Añjanaharitālehi, tathāmanosilāhi ca.

With honey-scented perfumes, and with jars filled with juices; with collyrium and orpiment, and likewise with realgar.

53.

53.

Manosilāsu vassena, bhassitvā cetiyaṅgaṇe;

Ṭhitāsu gopphamattāsu, racite pu’ppalehi ca.

When realgar, washed down by rain, lay ankle-deep in the cetiya courtyard, he had it strewn with flowers.

54.

54.

Thūpaṅgaṇamhi sakale, purite gandhakaddame;

Cittakilañjachiddesu, racite pu’ppalehi ca.

The entire courtyard of the stupa was filled with fragrant paste, and in the openings of the painted lattice, flowers were arranged.

55.

55.

Vārayitvā vārimaggaṃ, tatheva purite ghaṭe;

Dīpavaṭṭihi nekāni, katavaṭṭisikhāhi ca.

Having dammed the water-course, and likewise with filled jars; with numerous lamp-wicks, and with flames from well-made wicks.

56.

56.

Madhukatelamhi tathā, tilatele tatheva ca;

Tatheva paṭṭavaṭṭīnaṃ, su bahūhi sikhāhi ca.

Likewise with honey-oil and sesame oil, and also with very many flames from cloth wicks.

57.

57.

Yathāvuttehi etehi, mahāthūpassa khattiyo;

Sattakkhattuṃ sattakkhattuṃ, pūjā’kāsi visuṃ visuṃ.

With these aforementioned things, the warrior king performed worship for the great stupa, seven times for each, separately.

58.

58.

Anuvassañca niyataṃ, sudhāmaṅgalamuttamaṃ;

Bodhisinānapūjā ca, tatheva urubodhiyā.

And annually, he regularly held the excellent plastering ceremony, and the bathing ceremony of the Bodhi tree, and likewise of the great Bodhi tree.

59.

59.

Mahāvesākha pūjā ca, uḷārā aṭṭhavīsati;

Caturāsīti sahassāni, pūjā ca anuḷārikā.

The great Vesākha festival, twenty-eight magnificent offerings, and eighty-four thousand minor offerings.

60.

60.

Vividhaṃ naṭanaccañca, nānātūriyavāditaṃ;

Mahāthūpe mahāpūjaṃ, saddhānunno akārayi.

Impelled by faith, he sponsored various dramas and dances, and the playing of diverse musical instruments as a great offering at the great stupa.

61.

61.

Divasassa ca tikkhattuṃ, buddhuppaṭṭhānamāgamā;

Dvikkhattuṃ, pupphabheriñca, niyataṃ so akārayi.

Three times a day he went to attend upon the Buddha's shrine, and twice a day he regularly had the flower-drum sounded.

62.

62.

Niyatañcanadānañca, pavāraṇādānameva ca;

Telaphāṇitavatthādi-parikkhāraṃ samaṇārahaṃ.

And regular alms-giving, and the Pavāraṇā offering; oil, molasses, cloth, and other requisites suitable for ascetics.

63.

63.

Bahuṃ [M 0.0205] pādāsi saṅghassa, cetiyakhettameva ca;

Cetiye parikammatthaṃ, adāsi tattha khattiyo.

He gave much to the Saṅgha, and also land for the cetiya; the warrior king gave it for the maintenance of the cetiya.

64.

64.

Sadā bhikkhusahassassa, vihāre cetiyapabbate;

Salākavattabhattañca, so dāpesi ca bhūpati.

That ruler also had a regular ticket-food offering provided for a thousand bhikkhus at the monastery on Cetiya Mountain.

65.

65.

Cintāmaṇimucelavhe, upaṭṭhānattaye ca so;

Tathā padumaghare chatta-pāsāde ca manorame.

In the Cintāmaṇi and Mucalinda halls, and in the three attendance halls; likewise in the Lotus House and in the delightful Parasol Palace.

66.

66.

Bhojento pañcaṭhānamhi, bhikkhūganthadhure yute;

Paccayehi upaṭṭhāsi, sadā dhamme sagāravo.

In these five places, he fed bhikkhus dedicated to the study of the scriptures and attended to them with requisites, always with reverence for the Dhamma.

67.

67.

Porāṇarājaniyātaṃ, yaṃkiñci sāsanassitaṃ;

Akāsi puññakammaṃso, sabbaṃ bhātikabhūpati.

Whatever meritorious deeds connected with the Dispensation were established by ancient royal custom, King Bhātika performed them all.

68.

68.

Tassa bhābhakarājassa, accaye taṃ kaniṭṭhako;

Mahādāṭhimahānāga-nāmo rajjamakārayi.

Upon the passing of that radiant king, his younger brother, named Mahādāṭhika Mahānāga, ruled the kingdom.

69.

69.

Dvādasaṃyeva vassāni, nānāpuññaparāyano;

Mahāthūpamhi kiñjakkha- pāsāṇe attharāpayi.

For twelve years, devoted to various meritorious deeds, he had the courtyard of the Great Stupa paved with kiñjakkha stones.

70.

70.

Vālikāmariyādañca, kāresi vitthataṅgaṇaṃ;

Dīpe sabbavihāresu, dhammāsanamadāpayi.

He also made a sand-boundary and extended the courtyard. In all the monasteries on the island, he had preaching seats provided.

71.

71.

Ambatthala mahāthūpaṃ, kārāpesi mahīpati;

Ca yeaniṭṭhamānamhi, saritvā munino guṇaṃ.

The great king had the Ambatthala Mahāthūpa constructed; when the building of the mound was not being completed, he reflected on the virtues of the Sage.

72.

72.

Cajitvāna sakaṃ pāṇaṃ, nipajjitvā sayaṃ tahiṃ;

Ṭhapayitvā cayaṃ tassa, niṭṭhāpetvāna cetiyaṃ.

Having renounced his own life and lying down there himself, he had its mound established and the cetiya completed.

73.

73.

Catudvāre ṭhapāpesi, caturo ratanagghike;

Susippikehi suvibhatte, nānāratanajotite.

At the four gateways, he had four jeweled arches erected, well-proportioned by skilled artisans and gleaming with various precious stones.

74.

74.

Cetiye paṭimocetvā, nānāratanakañcukaṃ;

Kañcana bubbulañcettha, muttolambañca dāpayi.

Having draped the cetiya with a covering of various jewels, he also offered golden bosses and pearl pendants there.

75.

75.

Cetiya pabbatāvaṭṭe, alaṅkariya yojanaṃ;

Yojāpetvā catudvāraṃ, samantā cāruvīthikaṃ.

Around the Cetiya mountain, having adorned a yojana, and having erected four gateways, he made delightful streets all around.

76.

76.

Vīthiyā ubhato passe, āpaṇāni pasāriya;

Dhajagghika to raṇāni, maṇḍayitvā tahiṃ tahiṃ.

On both sides of the street, having set up shops, he had them decorated here and there with banners and arches.

77.

77.

Dīpamālā [M 0.0206] samujjotaṃ, kārayitvā samantato;

Naṭanaccāni gītāni, vāditāni ca kārayi.

He had rows of lamps lit all around, and he arranged for dancing, singing, and music to be performed.

78.

78.

Magge kadambanadito, yāvacetiya pabbatā;

Gantuṃ dhotehi pādehi, kārayi’ttharaṇatthataṃ.

From the Kadamba river to the Cetiya mountain, he had the path spread with coverings, so that one could walk with washed feet.

79.

79.

Sanaccagītavādehi, samajjamakaruṃ tahiṃ;

Nagarassa catudvāre, mahā dānañca dāpayi.

With dancing, singing, and instrumental music, he held festivals there. At the four gates of the city, he also had great alms given.

80.

80.

Akāsi sakale dīpe, dīpamālānirantaraṃ;

Salilepi samuddassa, samantā yojanantare.

Throughout the entire island, he made continuous rows of lamps, and even in the waters of the ocean for a yojana all around.

81.

81.

Cetiyassa mahetena, pūjā sā kāritā subhā;

Giribhaṇḍā mahāpūjā, uḷārā vuccate idha.

By the majesty of the cetiya, that splendid offering was made; here it is called the great, magnificent Giribhaṇḍa offering.

82.

82.

Samāgatānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, tasmiṃ pūjā samāgame;

Dānaṃ aṭṭhasu ṭhānesu, ṭhapāpetvā mahīpati.

For the assembled bhikkhus at that festival of offerings, the king had alms established in eight places.

83.

83.

Tāḷayitvāna tatraṭṭhā, aṭṭhasovaṇṇabheriyo;

Catuvīsasahassānaṃ, mahādānaṃ pavattayi.

Having sounded the eight golden drums there, he instituted a great alms-giving for twenty-four thousand bhikkhus.

84.

84.

Chacīvarāni pādāsi, bandhamokkhañca kārayi;

Catudvārenvāpitehi, sadā kammamakārayi.

He gave six kinds of robes and arranged for the release of prisoners. He continually had meritorious deeds performed at the four gates and at the wells.

85.

85.

Pubbarājūhi ṭhapitaṃ, bhātaraṃ ṭhapitaṃ tathā;

Puññakammaṃ ahāpetvā, sabbaṃ kārayibhūpati.

The meritorious work that had been established by previous kings, and likewise that established by his brother, the king had all of it done without diminution.

86.

86.

Attānaṃ deviṃputte dve, hatthiṃ assañca maṅgalaṃ;

Vāriyanto’pi saṅghena, saṅghassā’dāsi bhūpati.

The king gave himself, the queen, his two sons, the state elephant, and the state horse to the Saṅgha, even though he was being prevented by the Saṅgha.

87.

87.

Chasata sahassagghakaṃ, bhikkhusaṅghassa so adā;

Satasahassagghanakaṃ, bhikkhūnīnaṃ gaṇassa tu.

He gave that which was worth six hundred thousand to the community of bhikkhus, and that which was worth a hundred thousand to the community of bhikkhunīs.

88.

88.

Datvāna kappiyaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ, vividhaṃ vidhikovido;

Attānañca’va sese ca, saṅghato abhinīhari.

The king, skilled in procedure, having given various suitable goods, redeemed himself and the others from the Saṅgha.

89.

89.

Kālāyana kaṇṇikamhi, maṇināga pabbatavhayaṃ;

Vihārañca kaḷavhayaṃ, kāresi manujādhipo.

In Kālāyana-kaṇṇikā, the ruler of men had the Maṇināga-pabbata monastery and the monastery named Kaḷa built.

90.

90.

Kubu [M 0.0207] bandhanadītīre, samuddavihārameva ca;

Huvāvakaṇṇike cūḷa, nagapabbatasavhayaṃ.

He also built the Samudda-vihāra on the bank of the Kububandhana river, and the monastery named Cūḷa-Nagapabbata at Huvāvakaṇṇika.

91.

91.

Pāsāṇadīpakavhamhi, vihāre kārite sayaṃ;

Pāniyaṃ upanitassa, sāmaṇerassa khattiyo.

At the Pāsāṇadīpaka monastery, which he himself had built, a novice offered water to the khattiya king.

92.

92.

Upacāre pasīditvā, samantā aṭṭhayojanaṃ;

Saṅghabhogamadātassa, vihārassa mahīpati.

Being pleased with the novice's conduct, the great king gave to that monastery an endowment for the Saṅgha from the land for eight yojanas all around.

93.

93.

Maṇḍavāpi vihāre ca, sāmaṇerassa khattiyo;

Tuṭṭho vihāraṃ dāpesi, saṅghe bhogaṃ tatheva so.

And at the Maṇḍavāpi monastery, the king, pleased with a novice, had a monastery given to him, and likewise an endowment for the Saṅgha.

94.

94.

Iti vibhavamanappaṃ sādhupaññā labhitvā,

Vigatamadapamādācatta kāmapasaṅgā;
