Vipulavividhapuññaṃ suppannākarontīti.

Thus, the good and wise, having obtained abundant wealth, with pride and negligence gone, having abandoned attachment to sensual pleasures, not causing sorrow to people, delighting in meritorious deeds, perform abundant and various merit.

Sujanappasādasaṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Mahāvaṃsa, made for the faith and spiritual emotion of good people.

Ekādasarājadīpano nāma

Named the Elucidation of the Eleven Kings.

Catuttiṃsatimo paricchedo.

The Thirty-fourth Chapter.

Pañcatiṃsatimapariccheda

The Thirty-fifth Chapter.

Dvādasarājako

The Twelve Kings.

1.

1.

Āmaṇḍagāmaṇyabhayo, mahādāṭhikaaccaye;

Navavassanaṭṭhamāse, rajjaṃ kāresi taṃ suto.

Upon the death of Mahādāṭhika, his son Āmaṇḍagāmaṇi Abhaya ruled the kingdom for nine years and eight months.

2.

2.

Chattāti chattaṃ kāresi, mahāthūpe manorame;

Tatheva pādavediñca, muddhavediñca kārayi.

He had a parasol placed over the parasol on the great, delightful thūpa; likewise, he had the base railing and the top railing constructed.

3.

3.

Tatheva lohapāsāda, thūpavhe posathavhaye;

Kāresi kucchiājiraṃ, kucchiāḷindameva ca.

Likewise, at the Uposatha house of the Thūpārāma and at the Lohapāsāda, he had the Kucchi-ājira and also the Kucchi-āḷinda made.

4.

4.

Ubhayatthāpi [M 0.0208] kāresi, cāruṃ ratanapaṇḍapaṃ;

Rajataleṇa vihārañca, kārāpesi narādhipe.

In both of those places he had a beautiful jeweled pavilion built; and the lord of men also had the Rajatalena-vihāra built.

5.

5.

Mahāgāmeṇḍavāpiṃso, passe kāriya dakkhiṇe;

Dakkhiṇassa vihārassa, adāsi puññadakkhiṇo.

That meritorious king, having built the Mahāgāmeṇḍa tank on the south side, gave it to the Dakkhiṇa-vihāra.

6.

6.

Māghātaṃ sakale dīpe, kāresi manujādhipo;

Valliphalāni sabbāni, ropāpetvā tahiṃ tahiṃ.

The ruler of men proclaimed a prohibition of killing throughout the entire island, having caused all kinds of vine fruits to be planted here and there.

7.

7.

Maṃ sakubhaṇḍakaṃ nāma, āmaṇḍiya mahīpati;

Pattaṃ pūrāpayitvāna, kāretvā vatthacumbaṭaṃ.

The king, Āmaṇḍa, having had a dish named Maṃsakubhaṇḍaka prepared, and having caused the bowl to be filled and a cloth-ring to be made,

8.

8.

Dāpesi sabbasaṅghassa, vippasannena cetasā;

Patte pūrāpayitvā so, āmaṇḍa gāmaṇividū.

With a very clear mind, that wise village headman Āmaṇḍa had it given to the entire Sangha, having caused the bowls to be filled.

9.

9.

Taṅkaniṭṭhokaṇirājā-tisso ghātiya tātaraṃ;

Tīṇi vassāni nagare, rajjaṃ kāresi khattiyo.

The khattiya, King Kaṇirājātissa, having killed his father, ruled the kingdom in the city for three years.

10.

10.

Uposathagharaṭṭaṃ esā, nicchini cekiyavhaye;

Rājāparādhakammamhi, putte saṭṭhitu bhikkhavo.

He determined the site for the Uposatha hall at the place called Cetiya. For the king's offense, the monks placed sixty sons there.

11.

11.

Sahoḍḍe gāhayitvāna, rājā cetiya pabbate;

Khipāpesi kaṇiravhe, pabbhāramhi asīlake.

Having had them seized red-handed, the king on Cetiya mountain had the immoral ones thrown into a ravine called Kaṇi.

12.

12.

Kaṇirājā accayena, āmaṇḍagāmaṇi suto;

Cūḷābhayo vassamekaṃ, rajjaṃ kāresi khattiyo.

After the passing of King Kaṇirājātissa, Cūḷābhaya, son of Āmaṇḍagāmaṇi, ruled the kingdom for one year as a khattiya.

13.

13.

So goṇakanadītīre, purapassamhi dakkhiṇe;

Kārāpesi mahīpālo, vihāre cūḷagallakaṃ.

On the bank of the Goṇaka River, on the southern side of the city, that protector of the earth had the Cūḷagallaka monastery built.

14.

14.

Cūḷābhayassa’cca yena, sīvali taṃ kaniṭṭhikā;

Āmaṇḍadhītā caturo, māse rajjamakārayi.

After Cūḷābhaya's passing, his younger sister Sīvalī, daughter of Āmaṇḍa, ruled the kingdom for four months.

15.

15.

Āmaṇḍa bhāgineyyā tu, sīvaliṃ apanīyataṃ;

Iḷanāgoti nāmena, chattaṃ ussāpayi pure.

But Āmaṇḍa's nephew, having removed Sīvalī, raised the parasol in the city under the name Iḷanāga.

16.

16.

Tissavāpiṃ gate tasmiṃ, ādivasse narādhipe;

Taṃ hitvā puramāgañchuṃ, bahavolambakaṇṇakā.

When that ruler of men had gone to Tissavāpi in the first year, many Lambakaṇṇas, abandoning him, came to the city.

17.

17.

Tahiṃ adisvā te rājā, kuddho tehi akārayi;

Maddayaṃ vāpiyā passe, mahāthūpañjasaṃsayaṃ.

Not seeing them there, the king, angered, had them trample the path to the great stupa near the tank, without a doubt.

18.

18.

Tesaṃ [M 0.0209] vicārake katvā, caṇḍāle ca ṭhapāpayi;

Tena kuddhālambakaṇṇā, sabbe hutvāna ekato.

Having appointed caṇḍālas as their overseers, all the Lambakaṇṇas, angered by this, united.

19.

19.

Rājānaṃ taṃ gahetvāna, rundhitvāna sake ghare;

Sayaṃ rajjaṃ vicāresuṃ, rañño devī tadā sakaṃ.

Seizing that king and confining him in their own house, they themselves administered the kingdom. Then the king's own queen...

20.

20.

Puttaṃ candamukhasivaṃ, maṇḍayitvā kumārakaṃ;

Datvāna hatthe dhātīnaṃ, maṅgalahatthi santike.

...having adorned her son, the young prince Candamukhasiva, and having given him into the hands of the nurses near the state elephant,

21.

21.

Pesesi vatvā sandesaṃ, netvā taṃ dhātiyo tahiṃ;

Vadiṃsu devisandesaṃ, sabbaṃ maṅgala hatthino.

She sent them with a message, and the nurses, taking him there, delivered the queen’s entire message to the state elephant.

22.

22.

“Ayaṃ te sādhino putto,

Sāmiko cārake ṭhito;

Arihi ghātato seso,

Tayā ghāto imassa tu.

‘This is the son of your master. The master is confined in prison. He is what remains from the slaughter by enemies. His killing is now by you.

23.

23.

Tvamenaṃ kira ghātehi, idaṃ devivaco”iti;

Vatvā tu sayāpesuṃ, pādamūlamhi hatthino.

You, indeed, kill him! This is the queen's word.’ Having spoken thus, they laid him down at the foot of the elephant.

24.

24.

Dukkhito so ruditvāna, nāgo bhetvāna āḷakaṃ;

Pavisitvā mahāvatthuṃ, dvāraṃ pātiya thāmasā.

Distressed and weeping, the elephant broke its tethering post, entered the great stable, and struck the gate with force.

25.

25.

Rañño nisinnaṅgaṇamhi, ugghāṭetvā kavāṭakaṃ;

Nisīdāpiya taṃ khandhe, mahātitthamupāgami.

Having opened the door in the king's sitting-courtyard and placed him on its back, it went to the great ford.

26.

26.

Nāvaṃ āro payitvāna, rājānaṃ tattha kuñjaro;

Pacchimo dadhitīrena, sayaṃ malaya māruhī.

Having caused the king to board a boat there, the elephant itself ascended Malaya by the western ocean shore.

27.

27.

Paratīre vasitvā so, tīṇivassāni khattiyo;

Balakāyaṃ gahetvāna, āgā nāvāti rohaṇaṃ.

That khattiya, having lived on the farther shore for three years and gathered an army, came to Rohaṇa, the landing place for boats.

28.

28.

Titthe sakkharasobbhamhi, otaritvāna bhūpati;

Akāsi rohaṇe tattha, mahantaṃ balasaṅgahaṃ.

Disembarking at the Sakkhara-sobbha ford, the lord of the earth assembled a great army there in Rohaṇa.

29.

29.

Rañño maṅgalahatthiso, dakkhiṇaṃ malayaṃ tato;

Rohaṇaṃye’vupāgañchi, tassa kammāni kātave.

The king's state elephant then went to southern Malaya and approached Rohaṇa itself, in order to perform his tasks.

30.

30.

Mahāpadumanāmassa, tattha jātakabhāṇino;

Tulādhāravhavāsissa, mahātherassa santike.

There, in the presence of the great elder named Mahāpaduma, the reciter of the Jātaka, who resided at Tulādhāra,

31.

31.

Kapijātakaṃ [M 0.0210] sutvāna, bodhisatte pasādavā;

Nāgamahāvihāraṃ so, jiyāmuttadhanussataṃ.

Having heard the Kapi Jātaka, and filled with faith in the Bodhisatta, he founded the Nāgamahāvihāra, which had a hundred bows with pearl strings.

32.

32.

Katvā kāresi thūpañca, vaḍḍhāpesi yathāṭhitaṃ;

Tissavāpiñca kāresi, tathā duravhavāpikaṃ.

Having done so, he also had a stupa built and enlarged it as it stood; he also had the Tissavāpi tank and likewise the Duravāpika tank constructed.

33.

33.

So gahetvā balaṃ rājā, yuddhāya abhinikkhami;

Taṃ sutvā lambakaṇṇā ca, yuddhāya abhisaṃyutā.

That king, taking his army, marched out to battle. Hearing this, the Lambakaṇṇas also prepared themselves for war.

34.

34.

Papallakkhandhadvāramhi, khette hiṅkaravāpike;

Yuddhaṃ ubhinnaṃ vattittha, aññamaññavihesanaṃ.

At the Papallakkhandha gate, in the Hiṅkaravāpika field, a battle that caused mutual harm occurred between the two.

35.

35.

Nāvākilantadehattā, posā sīdanti rājino;

Rājā nāmaṃ sāvayitvā, sayaṃ pāvisi tena so.

As their bodies were weary from the sea voyage, the king's men were faltering. The king, having announced his name, then entered the battle himself.

36.

36.

Tena bhītālambakaṇṇā, sayiṃsu udarena so;

Tesaṃ sīsāni chinditvā, ratanābhisamaṃkari.

Terrified by that, the Lambakaṇṇas lay on their bellies. Having cut off their heads, he made a heap like jewels.

37.

37.

Tikkhattumevantukate, karuṇāya mahīpati;

“Amāretvā’va gaṇhātha, jīvaggāha’nti abruvi.

When this had been done three times, the compassionate lord of the earth commanded: 'Seize them without killing them, take them alive!'

38.

38.

Tato vijitasaṅgāmo, puraṃ āgamma bhūpati;

Chattaṃ ussāpayitvāna tissavāpi chaṇaṃ agā.

Then, victorious in battle, the king returned to the city. Having raised his parasol, he went to the Tissavāpi festival.

39.

39.

Jalakīḷāya uggantvā, sumaṇḍitapasādhito;

Attano sirisampattiṃ, disvā tassantarāyike.

After rising from water-play, well-adorned and decorated, and seeing his own royal splendor, he recalled those who were a danger to it.

40.

40.

Lambakaṇṇe saritvāna, kuddho so yojayīrathe;

Yugaparamparā tesaṃ, purato pāvisī puraṃ.

Remembering the Lambakaṇṇas, enraged, he had chariots yoked. A continuous line of their yokes entered the city before him.

41.

41.

Mahāvatthussa ummāre, ṭhatvā rājāṇapesi so;

“Imesaṃ sīsamummāre, asmiṃ chindatha bho”iti.

Standing at the threshold of the great place, the king commanded: 'Sirs, cut off their heads on this very threshold!'

42.

42.

Goṇā eterathe yuttā, tava honti rathesabha;

Siṅgaṃkhurañca etesaṃ, chedāpayata bho”iti.

“O lord of chariots, these are oxen yoked to the chariot; have their horns and hooves cut off, sirs!”

43.

43.

Mātuyā atha saññatto, sīsacchedaṃ nivāriya;

Nāsañca pādaṅguṭṭhañca, tesaṃ rājā achedayi.

Then, instructed by his mother, he stopped the beheadings; the king cut off their noses and big toes instead.

44.

44.

Hatthivutthaṃ janapadaṃ, adā hatthissa khattiyo;

Hatthibhogo janapado, iti tenāsi nāmato.

The khattiya gave the elephant-abounding country to the elephant. Therefore, the country became known by the name Hatthibhoga.

45.

45.

Evaṃ anurādhapure, iḷānāgo mahīpati;

Chabbassāni anunāni, rajjaṃ kāresi khattiyo.

Thus in Anurādhapura, the khattiya King Iḷānāga, the great ruler, reigned for nearly six years.

46.

46.

Iḷanāgaccaye [M 0.0211] tassa, putto candamukhosivo;

Aṭṭhavassaṃ sattamāsaṃ, rājā rajjamakārayi.

After Iḷanāga's demise, his son Candamukhasiva, the king, ruled the kingdom for eight years and seven months.

47.

47.

Maṇikāragāme vāpi, kārāpetvā mahīpati;

Issarasamaṇavhassa, vihārassa adāsi so.

The great ruler, having had a tank built in Maṇikāragāma, gave it to the monastery named Issarasamaṇa.

48.

48.

Tassa rañño mahesī ca, saṅgāme pattimattano;

Tassevā’dā vihārassa, damiḷadevīti vissutā.

His chief queen, known as Damiḷadevī, also gave her own share from the battle to that same monastery.

49.

49.

Taṃ tissavāpī kīḷāya, hantvā candamukhaṃ sivaṃ;

Yasaḷālakatisso’ti, vissuto taṅkaniṭṭhako.

His younger brother, having killed Candamukhasiva during the water-sports at Tissavāpi, became known as Yasaḷālakatissa.

50.

50.

Anurādhapure ramme, laṅkābhuvadane subhe;

Sattavassānaṭṭhamāse, rājā rajjamakārayi.

In delightful Anurādhapura, the beautiful face of Laṅkā, the king reigned for seven years and eight months.

51.

51.

Dovirikassa dattassa, puttho dovāriko sayaṃ;

Rañño sadisarūpena, ahosi subhanāmavā.

A doorkeeper named Subha, son of the doorkeeper Datta, was of similar appearance to the king.

52.

52.

Subhaṃ balatthaṃ taṃ rājā, rājabhūsāya bhūsiya;

Nisidāpiya pallaṅke, hāsatthaṃ yasaḷālako.

For amusement, King Yasaḷālaka adorned that guard Subha with royal ornaments, had him seated on the throne, and laughed.

53.

53.

Sīsacoḷaṃ balatthassa, sasīse paṭimuñciya;

Yaṭṭhiṃ gahetvā hatthena, dvāramūle ṭhito sayaṃ.

Having bound the guard's head-cloth on his own head and taking a staff in hand, he himself stood at the gate.

54.

54.

Vandantesu amaccesu, nisinnaṃ āsanamhi taṃ;

Rājā hasati evaṃ so, kurute antarantarā.

While the ministers were bowing to him who was seated on the throne, the king would laugh; this he did from time to time.

55.

55.

“Balattho ekadivasaṃ, rājānaṃ hasamānakaṃ;

Ayaṃ balattho kasmā me, sammukhāhasatī”ti so.

One day, as the king was laughing, that guard thought: 'Why does this guard laugh in my presence?'

56.

56.

Mārāpayitvā rājānaṃ, balattho so subho idha;

Rajjaṃ kāresi chabbassaṃ, subharājāti vissuto.

Having had the king killed, that guard Subha ruled the kingdom here for six years, and was known as King Subha.

57.

57.

Dvisu mahāvihāresu, subharājā manoramaṃ;

Pariveṇapantiṃ subha-nāmakaṃyeva kārayi.

In the two great monasteries, King Subha had a beautiful row of cells built, which was named Subha.

58.

58.

Uruvelasamīpamhi, tathā vellivihārakaṃ;

Puratthime ekadvāraṃ, gaṅgante nandigāmakaṃ.

Likewise, he built the Vellivihāra near Uruvela, the Ekadvāra Vihāra in the east, and the Nandigāmaka Vihāra on the bank of the river.

59.

59.

Lambakaṇṇasuto [M 0.0212] eko, uttarapassavāsiko;

Senāpatimupaṭṭhāsi, vasabho nāma mātulaṃ.

A certain son of a Lambakaṇṇa named Vasabha, who dwelt in the northern region, attended upon his maternal uncle, the general.

60.

60.

Hessati vasabho nāma, rājā’ti sutiyāsadā;

Ghāteti rājādīpamhi, sabbe vasabhanāmake.

From a prophecy it was heard, 'One named Vasabha will become king'; therefore, the king had all those on the island named Vasabha slain.

61.

61.

“Rañño dassāma vasataṃ, ima”nti bhariyāya so;

Senāpatimantayitvā, pāto rājakulaṃ agā.

Having consulted with his wife, that general said, 'We shall give this Vasabha to the king,' and at dawn he went to the royal palace.

62.

62.

Gacchato tena sahasā, tambulaṃ cuṇṇavajjitaṃ;

Hatthamhi vasabhassā’dā, taṃ sādhu parirakkhituṃ.

As he was going with him, she gave into Vasabha's hand a betel leaf without powder, for him to keep carefully.

63.

63.

Rājagehassa dvāramhi, tambulaṃ cuṇṇavajjitaṃ;

Senāpati udikkhitvā, taṃ cuṇṇatthaṃ visajjayi.

At the gate of the royal palace, the general, having noticed the betel leaf without powder, sent him for powder.

64.

64.

Senāpatissa bhariyā, cuṇṇatthaṃ vasabhaṃ gataṃ;

Vatvā rahassaṃ datvā ca, sahassaṃ taṃ palāpayi.

The general's wife, seeing Vasabha who had gone for powder, told him the secret, gave him a thousand coins, and made him flee.

65.

65.

Mahāvihāraṭhānaṃ so, gantvāna vasabho pana;

Tattha therehi khiranna-vatthehi katasaṅgaho.

Then that Vasabha went to the site of the Great Monastery; there, he was supported by the elders with milk-rice and robes.

66.

66.

Tato paraṃ kuṭṭhino ca, rājabhāvāya nicchitaṃ;

Sutvāna vacanaṃhaṭṭho, “coro hessa”nti nicchito.

Thereafter, having heard the words of the leper confirming his kingship, he was delighted and resolved, 'I shall become a robber.'

67.

67.

Laddhasamatthapurise, gāmaghātaṃ tato paraṃ;

Karonto rohaṇaṃ gantvā, kapallapuvopadesato.

Having gained capable men, he then raided villages; going to Rohaṇa, he acted upon the advice of Kapallapūva.

68.

68.

Kamena raṭṭhaṃ kaṇhantho, sampattabalavāhano;

So rājā dvīhi vassehi, āgamma purasantikaṃ.

Gradually seizing the kingdom, with an army possessing accumulated power, that king, in two years, came to the vicinity of the city.

69.

69.

Subharājaṃ raṇe hantvā, vasabho so mahabbalo;

Ussāpayi purebhattaṃ, mātulo’pi raṇe pati.

Slaying King Subha in battle, that mighty Vasabha raised the standard of sovereignty before the morning meal; his maternal uncle also fell in battle.

70.

70.

Taṃ mātulassa sariraṃ, pubbabhūtopakārikaṃ;

Akāsi vasabho rājā, mahesiṃ mettanāmikaṃ.

King Vasabha performed rites for the body of his uncle, who had previously been his benefactor, and made the lady named Mettā his chief queen.

71.

71.

Sohorapāṭhakaṃ pucchi, āyuppamāṇamattano;

“Āha dvādasavassāni”, rahoyevassa sopi ca.

He asked the astrologer about the measure of his own lifespan. 'Twelve years,' he said, and that to him in secret.

72.

72.

Rahassaṃ rakkhaṇatthāya, sahassaṃ tassā dāpiya;

Saṅghaṃ so sannipātetvā, vanditvā pucchi bhūpati.

To keep the secret, he had a thousand given to him; then, having assembled the Sangha, the lord of the earth bowed and asked:

73.

73.

“Siyānu [M 0.0213] bhante āyussa, vaḍḍhanakāraṇaṃ”iti;

“Atthī”ti saṅgho ācikkhi, antarāyavimocanaṃ.

'Venerable sirs, might there be a cause for increasing one's lifespan?' The Sangha replied, 'There is: the removal of dangers.'

74.

74.

Parissāvanadānañca, āvāsadāna meva ca;

Gilānavattadānañca, dātabbaṃ manujādhipa.

'The gift of water-strainers, the gift of dwellings, and the gift of care for the sick should be given, O lord of men.'

75.

75.

“Kātabbaṃ jiṇṇakāvāsa-paṭisaṅkharaṇaṃ tathā;

Pañcasīlasamādānaṃ, katvā taṃ sādhurakkhiyaṃ.

'The restoration of dilapidated dwellings should also be done; the five precepts should be undertaken and carefully guarded.'

76.

76.

Uposathūpavāso ca, kattabbo’ posathe”iti;

Rājā sādhūti gantvāna, tathā sabbaṃ makāsi so.

'And the Uposatha observance should be undertaken on the Uposatha day.' The king, saying 'Good!', went and did everything accordingly.

77.

77.

Tiṇṇaṃ tiṇṇañca vassānaṃ, accayena mahīpati;

Dīpamhi sabbasaṅghassa, ticīvaramadāpayi.

At the end of every three years, the great ruler had the three robes given to the entire Sangha on the island.

78.

78.

Anāgatānaṃ therānaṃ, pesayitvāna dāpayi;

Dvattiṃsāyahi ṭhānesu, dāpesi madhupāyasaṃ.

For the elders who had not come, he sent and had gifts given; in thirty-two places, he had honey-rice porridge distributed.

79.

79.

Catusaṭṭhiyā ca ṭhānesu, mahādānaṃtu missakaṃ;

Sahassavaṭṭi catusu, ṭhānesu ca jalāpayi.

In sixty-four places, he gave a great mixed alms-gift; and in four places, he had a thousand lamps lit.

80.

80.

Cetiyapabbate ceva, thūpārāme ca cetiye;

Mahāthūpe mahābodhi-ghare iti imesu hi.

These were at Cetiyapabbata, at the cetiya in Thūpārāma, at the Great Thūpa, and at the house of the Mahābodhi.

81.

81.

Cittalakūṭe kāresi, dasathūpe manorame;

Dīpe’khilamhi āvāse, jiṇṇe ca paṭisaṅkhari.

He had ten delightful thūpas built at Cittalakūṭa. Throughout the entire island, he also restored dilapidated dwellings.

82.

82.

Valliyeravihāre ca, therassa so pasīdiya;

Mahāvalligottaṃ nāma, vihārañca akārayi.

Being pleased with the elder at the Valliyera monastery, he had a monastery built named Mahāvalligotta.

83.

83.

Kāresi anurārāmaṃ, mahāgāmassa santike;

Heḷigāmaṭṭhakarisa, sahassaṃ tassa dāpayi.

He had the Anurārāma built near Mahāgāma; for it, he had a thousand karīsas of land at Heḷigāma given.

84.

84.

Mucelavihāraṃ kāretvā, so tissavaḍḍhamānake;

Āḷisārodakabhāgaṃ, vihārassa adāpayi.

Having had the Mucela monastery built at Tissavaḍḍhamānaka, he had the water-revenue from Āḷisāra given to the monastery.

85.

85.

Kalambatitthe thūpamhi, kāresiṭṭhikakañcukaṃ;

Kāresuposathā gāraṃ, vaṭṭitelattha massatu.

At Kalambatittha, he had a brick mantle made for the thūpa. He had an Uposatha hall built and plastered.

86.

86.

Sahassakarīsavāpiṃso[M 0.0214], kārāpetvā adāsi ca;

Kāresuposathāgāraṃ, vihāre kumbhigallake.

Having had a reservoir of a thousand karīsas made, he also gave it. He had an Uposatha hall built at the Kumbhigallaka monastery.

87.

87.

Soye’vu posathāgāraṃ, issarasamaṇake idha;

Thūpārāmethūpagharaṃ, kārāpesi mahīpati.

That same king had an Uposatha hall built here at Issarasamaṇaka; the great ruler also had a thūpa-house built at Thūpārāma.

88.

88.

Mahāvihāre pariveṇa, pantiṃ pacchimapekkhiniṃ;

Kāresi ca catusālañca, jiṇṇakaṃ paṭisaṅkhari.

In the Mahāvihāra, he had a west-facing row of cells built, and he restored the dilapidated four-sided hall.

89.

89.

Catubuddhapaṭimārammaṃ, paṭimānaṃgharaṃtathā;

Mahābodhiṅgaṇe ramme, rājā soyeva kārayi.

Likewise, that same king had an image house for the four Buddha images built in the delightful Mahābodhi courtyard.

90.

90.

Tassa rañño mahesī sā, vuttanāmā manoramaṃ;

Thūpaṃ thūpagharañceva, rammaṃ tatheva kārayi.

The aforesaid chief queen of that king likewise had a delightful thūpa and a charming thūpa-house built there.

91.

91.

Thūpārāme thūpagharaṃ, niṭṭhāpetvā mahīpati;

Tassa niṭṭhāpitamahe, mahādānamadāsi ca.

Having had the thūpa-house at Thūpārāma completed, the great ruler gave a great donation at the festival of its completion.

92.

92.

Yuttānaṃ buddhavacane, bhikkhūnaṃ paccayampi ca;

Bhikkhūnaṃ dhammakathikānaṃ, sappiphāṇitameva ca.

He also gave requisites to the monks devoted to the Buddha's word, and ghee and molasses to the monks who were preachers of the Dhamma.

93.

93.

Nagarassa catudvāre, kapaṇavaṭṭañca dāpayi;

Gilānānañca bhikkhūnaṃ, gilānavaṭṭameva ca.

At the four gates of the city, he had a regular provision for the needy established, and also a regular provision for sick monks.

94.

94.

Mayettiṃ rājuppalavāpiṃ, vahakolambagāmakaṃ;

Mahānika vittavāpiṃ, mahārāmotti meva ca.

He built the Mayetti tank, the Rājuppala tank, the Vahakolambagāmaka tank, the Mahānika tank, the Vittavāpi tank, and also the Mahārāma tank.

95.

95.

Kehālaṃ kāḷivāpiñca, cambuṭṭhiṃ vātamaṅganaṃ;

Abhivaḍḍhamānakañca, iccekādasa vāpiyo.

Kehāla, Kāḷivāpi, Cambuṭṭhi, Vātamaṅgana, and Abhivaḍḍhamānaka—thus, eleven reservoirs in all.

96.

96.

Dvādasa mātikā ceva, subhikkhatthamakārayi;

Guttattha purapākāraṃ, ceva muccamakārayi.

He had twelve main canals constructed to ensure abundant food; for protection, he had the city rampart and a moat made.

97.

97.

Gopurañca catudvāre, mahāvatthuñca kārayi;

Saraṃ kāresi uyyāne, haṃsetatthavisajjayi.

He had gateway towers built at the four gates and a great edifice constructed. He had a pond made in the park and released geese into it.

98.

98.

Pure bahū pokkharaṇī, kārāpetvā tahiṃ tahiṃ;

Ummaggena jalaṃ tattha, pavesesi mahīpati.

The king had many lotus ponds constructed here and there in the city and brought water into them through a tunnel.

99.

99.

Evaṃ [M 0.0215] nānāvidhaṃ puññaṃ, katvā vasabhabhūpati;

Hatantarāyo so hutvā, puññakamme sadādaro.

Having performed such various meritorious deeds, King Vasabha, freed from obstacles, remained ever devoted to meritorious actions.

100.

100.

Catuttāsīsavassāni, pure rajjamakārayi;

Catuttālīsavesākha, pūjā yo ca akārayi.

For forty-four years he reigned in the city, and forty-four times he sponsored the Vesākha festival.

101.

101.

Subharājā dharanto so, attano ekadhītaraṃ;

Vasabhena bhayāsaṃkī, appesi’ṭhika vaḍḍhakiṃ.

King Subha, while reigning, being fearful and apprehensive of Vasabha, entrusted his only daughter to a brick-mason.

102.

102.

Attano kambalañceva, rājā bhaṇḍāni ca’ppayi;

Vasabhena hate tasmiṃ, tamādāsiṭṭhavaḍḍhakī.

The king gave his own blanket and also royal articles. When that king was slain by Vasabha, the brick-mason took her in.

103.

103.

Dhītiṭhāne ṭhapetvāna, vaḍḍheti attano ghare;

Sakammaṃ karato tassa, bhattaṃ āhari dārikā.

Having established her in the position of a daughter, he raised her in his own home. While he was at his work, the girl brought him his meal.

104.

104.

Sā nirodhasamāpannaṃ, tadambapuppha gumbake;

Sattame divase disvā, bhattaṃ medhāvīnī adā.

The wise maiden, having seen on the seventh day one who had attained cessation in a thicket of mango flowers, gave him food.

105.

105.

Puna bhattaṃ randhayitvā, pituno bhattamāhari;

Papañcakāraṇaṃ puṭṭhā, tamatthaṃ pituno vadi.

Again, having cooked food, she brought the meal to her father. When asked the reason for the delay, she told the matter to her father.

106.

106.

Tuṭṭho punappunañce’so, bhattaṃ therassa dāpayi;

Vissattho’nāgataṃ disvā, thero āha kumārikaṃ.

Pleased, he again and again had food given to the Elder. The Elder, confident, seeing the future, spoke to the maiden.

107.

107.

“Tavaissariyejāte, imaṃ ṭhānaṃ kumārike;

Sareyyāsī’ti thero tu, tadā ca parinibbuto.

‘When sovereignty comes to you, O maiden, you should remember this place.’ The Elder then attained Parinibbāna.

108.

108.

Sake so vasabho rājā, vayappattamhi puttake;

Vaṅkanāsikatissamhi, kaññaṃtassānurūpikaṃ.

When his son Vaṅkanāsika Tissa came of age, that King Vasabha sought a suitable maiden for him.

109.

109.

Gavesāpesi purisā, taṃ disvāna kumārikaṃ;

Iṭṭhakavaḍḍhakīgāme, itthilakkhaṇa kovidā.

The men he sent to search, who were skilled in the marks of women, saw that maiden in the village of the brick-mason.

110.

110.

Rañño nivedayuṃ rājā, tamāṇāpetumārabhi;

Tassāha rājadhītattaṃ, iṭṭhakavaḍḍhakī tadā.

They reported to the king, and the king began to summon him. Then the brick-mason declared her status as a king's daughter.

111.

111.

Subharañño tu dhītattaṃ, kambalādīhi ñāpayi;

Rājā tuṭṭho sutassā’dā, taṃ sādhu katamaṅgalaṃ.

He proved she was King Subha's daughter with the blanket and other articles. The king, pleased, gave her to his son after performing the auspicious ceremony.

112.

112.

Vasabhassaccaye putto, vaṅkanāsika tissako;

Anurādhapure rajjaṃ, tīṇi vassāni kārayi.

After the passing of Vasabha, his son, Vaṅkanāsika Tissa, reigned in Anurādhapura for three years.

113.

113.

So [M 0.0216] goṇanadiyā tīre, mahāmaṅgalanāmakaṃ;

Vihāraṃ kārayi rājā, vaṅkanāsikatissako.

That King Vaṅkanāsika Tissa had a monastery named Mahāmaṅgala built on the bank of the Goṇa river.

114.

114.

Mahāmattā tu devī sā, sarantī therabhāsitaṃ;

Vihārakāraṇatthāya, akāsi dhanasañcayaṃ.

That queen, remembering the words of the Elder, accumulated wealth for the purpose of building a monastery.

115.

115.

Vaṅkanāsikatissassa, accaye kārayī suto;

Rajjaṃ bāvīsavassāni, gajjabāhukagāmaṇi.

After the passing of Vaṅkanāsika Tissa, his son, Gajabāhuka Gāmaṇi, reigned for twenty-two years.

116.

116.

Sutvā so mātuvacanaṃ, mātudatthāya kārayi;

Kadambapupphaṭhānamhi, rājamātuvihārakaṃ.

Having heard his mother's word, for his mother's benefit he had the Rājamātuvihāraka built at the place of the Kadamba flowers.

117.

117.

Mātā satasahassaṃ sā, bhūmiatthoya paṇḍitā;

Adā mahāvihārassa, vihārañca akāra yi.

That wise mother gave a hundred thousand for the price of the land to the Mahāvihāra, and she also had a monastery built.

118.

118.

Sayameva akāresi, tattha thūpaṃ silāmayaṃ;

Saṅghabhogañca pādāsi, kiṇitvāna tato tato.

He himself had a stone thūpa built there, and having purchased them from various places, he provided possessions for the Saṅgha.

119.

119.

Abhayuttara mahāthūpaṃ, vaḍḍhāpetvā citāpayi;

Catudvāre ca tattheva, ādimukhamakārayi.

He had the great Abhayuttara thūpa enlarged, and at its four gates he had frontispieces made.

120.

120.

Gāmaṇitissavāpiṃ so, kārāpetvā mahīpati;

Abhayagiri vihārassa, pākavaṭṭāya’dāsi ca.

That ruler, having had the Gāmaṇitissa tank built, gave it to the Abhayagiri Monastery for the provision of food.

121.

121.

Maricavaṭṭikathūpamhi, kañcukañca akārayi;

Kiṇitvā satasahassena, saṅghabhogamadāsi ca.

He had a mantle made for the Maricavaṭṭi thūpa, and he also gave possessions for the Saṅgha, having purchased them for a hundred thousand.

122.

122.

Kāresi pacchime vasse, vihāraṃ rāmakavhayaṃ;

Mahejasanasālañca, nagaramhi akārayi.

In his last year, he had a monastery called Rāmaka built, and he also had a great hall for offerings made in the city.

123.

123.

Gajabāhussaccayena, sasuro tassa rājino;

Rajjaṃ mahallako nāgo, chabbassāni akārayi.

After the passing of Gajabāhu, his father-in-law, Mahallaka Nāga, reigned for six years.

124.

124.

Puratthime pejalakaṃ, dakkhiṇe koṭi pabbataṃ;

Pacchime dakapāsāṇe, nāgadīpe sālipabbataṃ.

In the east, the Pejalaka; in the south, the Koṭipabbata; in the west, the Dakapāsāṇa; on Nāgadīpa, the Sālipabbata.

125.

125.

Bījagāme tanaveḷiṃ, rohaṇe janapade pana;

Tobbalanāgapabbatañca, antoṭṭhe girihālikaṃ.

In Bījagāma, the Tanaveḷi; and in the country of Rohaṇa, the Tobbalanāgapabbata; and in Antoṭṭha, the Girihālika.

126.

126.

Ete [M 0.0217] satta vihāre so, mahallanāgabhūpati;

Parittenapi kālena, kārāpesi mahāmatī.

These seven monasteries, that greatly wise King Mahallanāga had built in a short time.

127.

127.

Evaṃ asārehi dhanehi sāraṃ,

Puññāni katvāna bahūni paññā;

Ādenti bālā pana kāma hetu,

Bahūni pāpāni karontā mohā’ti.

Thus the wise, having performed many meritorious deeds, take the essence from worthless riches; but the foolish, for the sake of sensual pleasures, commit many evil deeds out of delusion.

Sujanappasādasaṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Great Chronicle, composed for the faith and spiritual urgency of the virtuous.

Dvādasa rājako nāma

The Chapter of the Twelve Kings.

Pañcatiṃsatimo paricchedo.

The thirty-fifth chapter.

Chattiṃsatima pariccheda

The Thirty-sixth Chapter

Tayodasa rājako

The Thirteen Kings

1.

1.

Mahallanāgaccayena[M 0.0217], putto bhātikatissako;

Catuvīsativassāni, laṃkārajjamakārayi.

After the passing of Mahallanāga, his son Bhātikatissa ruled the kingdom of Laṅkā for twenty-four years.

2.

2.

Mahāvihāre pākāraṃ, kārāpesi samantato;

Gavaratissavihāraṃ, so kārayitvā mahīpati.

That lord of the earth had a wall built all around the Mahāvihāra; and having had the Gavaratissavihāra built,

3.

3.

Mahāgāmaṇikaṃ vāpiṃ, vihārassa’ssa’dāsi ca;

Vihārañca akāresi, bhātiyatissa nāmakaṃ.

he also gave the Mahāgāmaṇika reservoir to this monastery; and he had a monastery built named Bhātiyatissa.

4.

4.

Kāresuposathāgāraṃ, thūpārāme manorame;

Randhakaṇḍakavāpiñca, kārāpesi mahīpati.

He had an Uposatha hall built in the delightful Thūpārāma; the king also had the Randhakaṇḍaka tank constructed.

5.

5.

Sattesu muducittoso, saṅghamhi tibbagāravo;

Ubhatosaṅghe mahīpālo, mahādānaṃ pavattayi.

With a gentle heart towards beings and with intense reverence for the Saṅgha, the king instituted a great offering to both Saṅghas.

6.

6.

Bhātikatissaccayena, tassa kaniṭṭhatissako;

Aṭṭhavīsasamārajjaṃ, laṃkādīpe akārayi.

After the passing of Bhātikatissa, his younger brother Kaṇiṭṭhatissa ruled in the island of Laṅkā for twenty-eight years.

7.

7.

Bhūtārāma [M 0.0218] mahānāga, therasmiṃ so pasīdiya;

Kāresi ratanapāsādaṃ, abhayagirimhi sādhukaṃ.

Being pleased with the elder Mahānāga of Bhūtārāma, he had a jeweled palace built excellently at Abhayagiri.

8.

8.

Abhayagirimhi pākāraṃ, mahāpariveṇameva ca;

Kāresi maṇisomavhe, mahāpariveṇameva ca.

At Abhayagiri he had a rampart and also a great monastic college built; and likewise at Maṇisoma, a great monastic college.

9.

9.

Tattheva cetiyagharaṃ, ambatthale tatheva ca;

Kāresi paṭisaṅkhāraṃ, nāgadīpe ghare pana.

He had repairs made to the shrine-house there, and likewise at Ambatthala; and further, to the house in Nāgadīpa.

10.

10.

Mahāvihārasīmaṃso, madditvā tattha kārayi;

Kukkuṭagiri pariveṇa, pantiṃ sakkacca bhūpati.

Having encroached upon the boundary of the Mahāvihāra, the king carefully had a row of monastic dwellings built there at Kukkuṭagiri.

11.

11.

Mahāvihāre kāresi, dvādasa manujādhipo;

Mahācaturassapāsāde, dassaneyyemanorame.

The ruler of men had twelve great, four-sided palaces, sightly and delightful, built at the Mahāvihāra.

12.

12.

Dakkhiṇavihāra thūpamhi, kañcukañca akārayi;

Bhattasālaṃ mahāmegha, vanāsimañca maddiya.

At the stupa of the Dakkhiṇavihāra, he also had a casing made; and having encroached upon the boundary of the Mahāmeghavana, he built a refectory.

13.

13.

Mahāvihārapākāraṃ, passato apanīyaso;

Maggaṃ dakkhiṇavihāra, gāmiñcāpi akārayi.

Having removed a side-section of the Mahāvihāra wall, he also had the road leading to the Dakkhiṇavihāra made.

14.

14.

Bhūtārāma vihārañca, rāmagoṇakameva ca;

Tatheva nandatissassa, ārāmañca akārayi.

He had the Bhūtārāma monastery built, and also the Rāmagoṇaka; likewise, he had the park of Nandatissa made.

15.

15.

Pācinato anuḷātissa, pabbataṃ gaṅgarājiyaṃ;

Niyelatissārāmañca, piḷa piṭṭhi vihārakaṃ.

He established the Pācinatissapabbata monastery, the Gaṅgarājiya monastery, the Niyelatissārāma, and the Piḷapiṭṭhi monastery.

16.

16.

Rājamahāvihārañca, kāresi manujādhipo;

Soyeva tīsu ṭhānesu, kāresu’posathālayaṃ.

The ruler of men also had the Rājamahāvihāra built; he himself had Uposatha halls constructed in three places:

17.

17.

Kalyāṇīka vihāre ca, maṇḍalagirike tathā;

Dubbalavāpitissavhe, vihāresu imesu hi.

At the Kalyāṇīka monastery, likewise at Maṇḍalagiri, and at the monastery called Dubbalavāpitissa—indeed, in these monasteries.

18.

18.

Kaniṭṭhatissaccayena, tassa putto akārayi;

Rajjaṃ dveyeva vassāni, cūḷanāgoti vissuto.

After the passing of Kaṇiṭṭhatissa, his son, known as Cūḷanāga, ruled the kingdom for only two years.

19.

19.

Cūḷanāgakaniṭṭhotu, rājāghātiya bhātikaṃ;

Ekavassaṃ kuḍḍanāgo, rajjaṃ laṃkāya kārayi.

But Cūḷanāga's younger brother, Kuḍḍanāga, having slain his brother the king, ruled the kingdom of Laṅkā for one year.

20.

20.

Mahāpeḷañca vaḍḍhesi, ekanāḷikachātake;

Bhikkhusatānaṃ pañcannaṃ, abbhocchinnaṃ mahīpati.

The king increased the Mahāpeḷa alms and the Ekanāḷikachātaka grant, providing uninterruptedly for five hundred monks.

21.

21.

Kuḍḍanāgassa [M 0.0219] rañño tu, devīyā bhātuko tadā;

Senāpati sirināgo, coro hutvāna rājino.

Then the brother of King Kuḍḍanāga's queen, the general Sirināga, having become a rebel against the king,

22.

22.

Balavāhana sampanno, āgamma nagarantikaṃ;

Rājabalena yujjhanto, kuḍḍanāgaṃ mahīpatiṃ.

endowed with an army and vehicles, approached the city and, fighting with the king's army, engaged King Kuḍḍanāga.

23.

23.

Palāpetvā laddhajayo, anurādha pure vare;

Laṃkārajjamakāresi, vassānekūnavīsati.

Having put him to flight and gained the victory, he ruled the kingdom of Laṅkā in the noble city of Anurādhapura for nineteen years.

24.

24.

Mahāthūpavare chattaṃ, kārāpetvāna bhūpati;

Suvaṇṇakammaṃ kāresi, dassaneyyaṃ manoramaṃ.

The lord of the earth, having had a parasol made for the excellent Great Stūpa, had beautiful and delightful gold work done upon it.

25.

25.

Kāresi lohapāsādaṃ, saṃkhittaṃ pañcabhūmakaṃ;

Mahābodhi catudvāre, sopānaṃ punakārayi.

He built the Lohapāsāda, a condensed five-storied structure. At the four gateways of the Great Bodhi tree, he again had stairways made.

26.

26.

Kāretvā chattapāsādaṃ, mahe pūjamakārayi;

Kulambaṇañca dīpasmiṃ, vissajjesi dayāparo.

Having had the Chattapāsāda built, he caused a great offering to be made. Being compassionate, he remitted the Kulambaṇa tax on the island.

27.

27.

Sirināgaccaye tassa, putto tisso akārayi;

Rajjaṃ dvāvīsavassāni, dhammavohāra kovido.

Upon the passing of Sirināga, his son Tissa, who was skilled in lawful administration, ruled the kingdom for twenty-two years.

28.

28.

Ṭhapesi so hi vohāraṃ, hiṃsā muttaṃ yatoidha;

Vohāraka tissarājā, iti nāmaṃ tato ahu.

Because he established here a legal procedure free from violence, he thenceforth became known by the name Vohārika Tissarāja.

29.

29.

Kambugāmakavāsissa, devattherassa santike;

Dhammaṃ sutvā paṭikammaṃ, pañcāvāse akārayi.

Having heard the Dhamma in the presence of the Elder Deva, a resident of Kambugāmaka, he had renovation work done in five monasteries.

30.

30.

Mahātissassa therassa, anurā rāmavāsino;

Pasanno mucelapaṭṭane, dāna vaṭṭamakārayi.

Pleased with the Elder Mahātissa, a resident of the Anurā-ārāma, he established a continuous giving of alms in Mucelapaṭṭana.

31.

31.

Tissarāja maṇḍapañca, mahāvihāradvayepi so;

Mahābodhighare pāci, loharūpaddhayampi ca.

He built the Tissarāja pavilion in both of the great monasteries, and to the east of the Mahābodhi House, he also placed two bronze images.

32.

32.

Sattapaṇṇikapāsādaṃ, kāretvā sukhavāsakaṃ;

Māse māse sahassaṃ so, mahāvihārassa dāpayi.

Having had the Sattapaṇṇika Palace built, a pleasant dwelling, he caused a thousand pieces of money to be given each month to the Mahāvihāra.

33.

33.

Abhayagirivihāre, dakkhiṇamūlasavhaye;

Maricavaṭṭi vihāramhi, kulālitissasavhaye.

At the Abhayagiri Monastery, at the monastery called Dakkhiṇamūla, at the Maricavaṭṭi Monastery, and at the monastery called Kulālitissa;

34.

34.

Mahiyaṅgaṇa vihāramhi, mahāgāmakasavhaye;

Mahānāgatissavhamhi, tathā kalyāṇīkavhaye.

At the Mahiyaṅgaṇa Monastery, at the monastery called Mahāgāmaka, at the one called Mahānāgatissa, and likewise at the one called Kalyāṇī.

35.

35.

Iti [M 0.0220] aṭṭhasu thūpesu, chattakammamakārayi;

Mūkanāgasenāpati, vihāre dakkhiṇe tathā.

Thus, at these eight stūpas, he had umbrella-work done. Likewise, the general Mūkanāga did so at the Southern Monastery.

36.

36.

Marica vaṭṭi vihāramhi, puttabhāgavhaye tathā;

Issarasamaṇavhamhi, tissavhe nāgadīpake.

At the Maricavaṭṭi Monastery, and likewise at the one called Puttabhāga; at the one called Issarasamaṇa, and at the one called Tissa in Nāgadīpa.

37.

37.

Iti chasu vihāresu, pākārañca akārayi;

Kāresu’ posathāgāraṃ, anurārāmasavhaye.

Thus, at six monasteries, he also had enclosure walls built. He built an Uposatha hall at the monastery called Anurārāma.

38.

38.

Ariyavaṃsakathāṭhāne, laṃkādīpekhilepi ca;

Dāna vaṭṭaṃ ṭhapāpesi, saddhamme gāravena so.

Out of reverence for the True Dhamma, he caused a regular giving of alms to be established at the places where the Ariyavaṃsa discourse was held, and throughout the entire island of Laṅkā.

39.

39.

Tiṇī satasahassāni, datvāna manujādhipo;

Iṇato sayike bhikkhū, mocesi sāsanappiyo.

The lord of men, who was devoted to the Dispensation, gave three hundred thousand and freed the monks of his realm from debt.

40.

40.

Mahā vesākha pūjaṃ so, kāretvā dīpavāsinaṃ;

Sabbe saṃyeva bhikkhūnaṃ, ticīvaramadāpayi.

Having held the great Vesākha festival for the inhabitants of the island, he caused the triple robe to be given to all the monks without exception.

41.

41.

Vetullavādaṃ madditvā, kāretvā pāpaniggahaṃ;

Kapilena amaccena, sāsanaṃ jotayīca so.

Having suppressed the Vetulla heresy and having carried out an inquiry into this evil, he, with his minister Kapila, made the Dispensation shine forth.

42.

42.

Vissuto’bhayanāgo’ti, kaniṭṭho tassarājino;

Deviyā tassa saṃsaṭṭho, ñāto bhīto sabhātarā.

That king's younger brother, known as Abhayanāga, had an illicit affair with the queen. Having been found out by his brother, he became afraid.

43.

43.

Palāyitvā hallatitthaṃ, gantvāna sahasevako;

Kuddho viya mātulassa, hatthapādañca chedayi.

Fleeing, he went to Bhallatittha with his followers. There, pretending to be angry with his maternal uncle, he had his hands and feet cut off.

44.

44.

Rājino raṭṭhatedatthaṃ, ṭhapetvāna idheva taṃ;

Sunakhopamaṃ dassayitvā, gahetvā’ti siniddhake.

For the king's purpose in the kingdom, having placed him there and having shown the simile of the dog, he thus won over the affectionate ones.

45.

45.

Tattheva nāvaṃ āruyha, paratīramagāsayaṃ;

Subhavo mātulo tu, upagamma mahīpati.

Boarding a ship right there, he went to the opposite shore. His maternal uncle, Subha, however, approached the great king.

46.

46.

Suhado viya hutvāna, tasmiṃ raṭṭhamabhindiso;

Abhayo taṃ jānanatthaṃ, dūtaṃ idha visajjayi.

Pretending to be a friend, he created division in the kingdom. Abhaya, in order to learn of this, sent a messenger here.

47.

47.

Taṃ disvā pūgarukkhaṃ so, samantā kuntanāḷiyā;

Paribbhamanto madditvā, katvā dubbalamūlakaṃ.

He, seeing an areca-nut tree surrounded on all sides by kundaṭī-grass, walked around it, crushing the grass and weakening the tree's roots.

48.

48.

Bāhunāyeva pātetvā, tajjetvā taṃ palāpayi;

Dūto gantvā abhayassa, taṃ pavattiṃ pavedayi.

Then, having felled it with his bare arm, he threatened the messenger and made him flee. The messenger went to Abhaya and reported these events.

49.

49.

Ñatvā’bhayo [M 0.0221] taṃ damiḷe, ādāya basuke tato;

Nagarantikamāgañchi, bhātarā saha yujjhituṃ.

Understanding this, Abhaya then took many Damiḷa soldiers and came near the city to fight with his brother.

50.

50.

Taṃ ñatvāna palāyitvā, assamāruyhadeviyā;

Malayaṃ āgamā rājā, taṃkaniṭṭho’nu bandhiya.

Learning of this, the king fled. Mounting a horse with the queen, he went to the Malaya region, pursued by his younger brother.

51.

51.

Rājānaṃ malaye hantvā, devīmādāya āgato;

Kāresi nagare rajjaṃ, aṭṭhavassāni bhūpati.

Having killed the king in the Malaya region, he returned, taking the queen. This sovereign then ruled the kingdom in the city for eight years.

52.

52.

Pāsāṇavediṃ kāresi, mahābodhisamantato;

Lohapāsādaṅgaṇamhi, rājā maṇḍapameva ca.

He had a stone terrace made all around the Great Bodhi tree, and the king also had a pavilion made in the courtyard of the Lohapāsāda.

53.

53.

Dvihi satasahassehi, nekavatthāni bhāgiya;

Dīpamhi bhikkhusaṅghassa, vatthadānamadāsi so.

Spending two hundred thousand, he gave a gift of various cloths to the community of monks on the island.

54.

54.

Abhayassa’ccaye bhātu, tassassa tassa atrajo;

Dvevassāni sirināgo, laṃkārajja makārayi.

Upon the death of Abhaya, his brother's son, Sirināga, ruled the kingdom of Laṅkā for two years.

55.

55.

Paṭisaṅkhariya pākāraṃ, mahābodhisamantato;

Mahābodhigharasseva, soyeva vālikātale.

He repaired the enclosure wall all around the Great Bodhi Tree, and likewise the Great Bodhi Shrine on the sand-terrace.

56.

56.

Mūcelarukkhaparato, haṃsavaṭṭaṃ manoramaṃ;

Mahantaṃ maṇḍapañceva, kārāpesi mahīpati.

Beyond the Mūcela tree, the lord of the earth caused a beautiful swan-balustrade and a great pavilion to be built.

57.

57.

Vijayakumārako nāma, sirināgassa atrajo;

Pituno accaye rajjaṃ, ekavassamakārayi.

Vijayakumāraka, Sirināga's son, upon his father's death, ruled the kingdom for one year.

58.

58.

Lambakaṇṇā tayo āsuṃ, sahātā mahiyaṅgaṇe;

Saṅghatisso saṅghabodhi, tatiyo goṭṭhakābhayo.

There were three Lambakaṇṇas together in Mahiyaṅgaṇa: Saṅghatissa, Saṅghabodhi, and the third, Goṭṭhakābhaya.

59.

59.

Te tissavāpimariyāda-gato andho vicakkhaṇo;

Rājupaṭṭhānamāyante, padasaddena abravi.

As they were approaching the king's presence, a blind, wise man who had gone to the bank of the Tissa tank spoke upon hearing the sound of their footsteps:

60.

60.

“Pathavīsāmino ete, tayo vahatibhū’iti;

Taṃ sutvā abhayo pacchā, yanto pucchi punāhaso.

"These three are lords of the earth, bearers of the land." Having heard that, Abhaya went later and asked him again.

61.

61.

Tassa vaṃso ṭhassatīti,

Puna pucchitameva so;

“Pacchimassā”ti so āha,

Taṃ sutvā dvīhisoagā.

When he was asked again, "Whose lineage will endure?" he replied, "The last one's." Having heard this, the other two departed.

62.

62.

Te [M 0.0222] puraṃ pavisitvāna, tayo rañño’ti vallabho;

Rājakiccāni sādhentā, vasantā rājasantike.

Those three, having entered the city, became favorites of the king; performing royal duties, they dwelt near the king.

63.

63.

Hantvā vijayarājānaṃ, rājagehamhi ekato;

Senāpatiṃsaṅghatissaṃ, duverajje’bhisecayuṃ.

Having together killed King Vijayarāja in the royal palace, the two consecrated the commander, Saṅghatissa, to the kingship.

64.

64.

Evaṃ so abhisittova, anurādhapuruttame;

Rajjaṃ cattāri vassāni, saṅghatisso akārayi.

Thus consecrated, Saṅghatissa ruled the kingdom in the excellent city of Anurādhapura for four years.

65.

65.

Mahāthūpamhi chattañca, hemakammañca kārayi;

Visuṃ satasahassagghe, caturo ca mahāmaṇi.

He had a parasol and golden work made for the Great Stupa, and also four great gems, each worth a hundred thousand.

66.

66.

Majjhe catunnaṃ sūriyānaṃ, ṭhapāpesi mahīpati;

Thūpassa muddhani tathā-nagghavajiracumbaṭaṃ.

The lord of the earth had these placed in the midst of the four sun-symbols, and likewise on the crest of the stupa, a priceless diamond ring.

67.

67.

So chattamahapūjāya, saṅghassa manujādhipo;

Cattālīsasahassassa, cha cīvaramadāpayi.

For the great festival of the parasol, the ruler of men caused six robes to be given to the Sangha of forty thousand.

68.

68.

Taṃ mahādevatherena, dāmagallaka vāsino;

Desitaṃ khandhake suttaṃ, yāgānisaṃsa dīpanaṃ.

That was the Sutta expounded in the Khandhaka by the great elder Mahādeva, a resident of Dāmagallaka, which illuminates the benefits of gruel.

69.

69.

Sutvā pasanno saṅghassa, yāgudānamadāpayi;

Nagarassa catudvāre, sakkaccañceva sādhu ca.

Having heard it and being pleased, he caused an offering of gruel to be given to the Sangha, carefully and well, at the four gates of the city.

70.

70.

So antarantare rājā, jambupakkāni khādituṃ;

Sahorodho sahāmacco, agāpācina dīpakaṃ.

From time to time, that king, together with his harem and ministers, went to the eastern district to eat ripe jambu fruits.

71.

71.

Upaddutaṃ’ssa gamane, manussā pāci vāsino;

Visaṃ phalesu yo jesuṃ, rājabhojjāya jambuyā.

Troubled by his going, the people residing in the eastern district put poison in the jambu fruits intended for the king’s meal.

72.

72.

Khāditvā jambupakkāni, tāni tattheva so mato;

Senāpati saṅghadhabādhīṃ-bhayo rajje’bhisecayi.

Having eaten those ripe jambu fruits, he died on that very spot. Goṭṭhakābhaya then consecrated the commander Saṅghabodhi to the kingship.

73.

73.

Rājāsiri saṅgha bodhi, vissuto pañcasīlavā;

Anurādhapure rajjaṃ, duve vassāni kārayi.

King Sirisaṅghabodhi, renowned and observant of the five precepts, ruled the kingdom in Anurādhapura for two years.

74.

74.

Mahāvihāre kāresi, salākaggaṃ manoramaṃ;

Tadādīpe manusseso, ñatvā dubbuṭṭhupaddute.

He had a beautiful ticket-hall built at the Mahāvihāra. Then, the lord of men learned that the people of the island were afflicted by drought.

75.

75.

Karuṇāya kampitamano, mahāthūpaṅgaṇe sayaṃ;

Nipajji bhūmiyaṃ rājā, katvāna iti nicchayaṃ.

With a heart trembling with compassion, the king himself lay down on the ground in the courtyard of the Great Stupa, having made this resolution:

76.

76.

“Pavassitvāna [M 0.0223] devena, jalenupalāvite mayi;

Naheva vuṭṭhahissāmi, maramānopahaṃ idha”.

"Though the god should rain until I am inundated with water, I will not rise from here, even if I am to die."

77.

77.

Evaṃ nipanne bhūminde, devo pāvassi tāvade;

Laṃkādīpamhi sakale, piṇayanto mahāmahiṃ.

As the lord of the earth lay thus, the god rained at once over the entire island of Laṅkā, gladdening the great earth.

78.

78.

Tathāpi nuṭṭhahatiso, apilāpanato jale;

Āvariṃsu tato’maccā, jalaniggamanāḷiyo.

Yet he did not rise, because the water was not yet making him float. Then the ministers blocked the water outlets.

79.

79.

Tato jalamhi pilavaṃ, rājā vuṭṭhāsi dhammiko;

Karuṇāyanudi evaṃ, dīpe dubbuṭṭhikābhayaṃ.

Then, floating upon the water, the righteous king arose; thus, through his compassion, he dispelled the fear of drought on the island.

80.

80.

Corātahiṃ tahiṃ jātā, iti sutvāna bhūpati;

Core āṇāpayitvāna, rahassena palāpīya.

Hearing that thieves had arisen here and there, the king, having secretly summoned the thieves, had them sent away.

81.

81.

Āṇāpetvā rahassena, matānaṃ so kalevaraṃ;

Aggīhi uttāsetvāna, hanitaṃ corupaddavaṃ.

Having secretly given orders, he made a terrifying example with the bodies of the dead and with fires, thus eliminating the menace of thieves.

82.

82.

Eko yakkho idhāgamma, rattakkho iti vissuto;

Karoti rattāna’kkhīti, manussānaṃ tahiṃ tahiṃ.

A certain yakkha came here, known as Rattakkhi, the Red-eyed; he made people's eyes red here and there.

83.

83.

Aññamaññamapekkhitvā, bhāyitvā rattanettataṃ;

Narāmaranti te yakkho, sobhakkhesi asaṅkito.

Looking at one another and fearing the redness of eyes, people died; that yakkha, unafraid, devoured them.

84.

84.

Rājā upaddavaṃ tesaṃ, sutvā santattamānaso;

Eko’pavāsa gabbhamhi, hutvā aṭṭhaṅguposathi.

Hearing of their distress, the king, with an afflicted mind, entered a solitary chamber and observed the eight-factored Uposatha.

85.

85.

“Apassitvāna taṃ yakkhaṃ, na cuṭṭhāmī”ti so sayi;

Tassa so dhammatejena, agā yakkho tadantikaṃ.

‘Unless I see that yakkha, I will not rise,’ thus he lay down. By the power of his virtue, that yakkha went into his presence.

86.

86.

Tena “kosī”ti puṭṭho ca, so “aha”nti pavedayi;

“Kasmā pajaṃ me bhakkhesi, mā khāda”iti sobravi.

Asked by him, ‘Who are you?’ he made it known, saying, ‘It is I.’ ‘Why do you devour my people? Do not eat them,’ he said.

87.

87.

“Ekasmiṃ me janapade, nare dehī”ti sobravi;

“Na sakkā iti vutte so, kamenekaṃti abravi.

He said, ‘Give me one person from the country.’ When it was said, ‘That is not possible,’ he replied, ‘Then one at a time.’

88.

88.

“Aññaṃ na sakkā dātuṃ me, maṃ khāda” iti sobravi;

“Na sakkā”iti taṃ yāci, gāme gāme baliñca so.

‘I cannot give another; eat me,’ he said. ‘That is not possible,’ the yakkha replied, and begged him instead for an offering in every village.

89.

89.

Sādhūti vatvā bhūmindo, dipampi sakalepi ca;

Gāmavare nivesetvā, baliṃtassa adāpayi.

Saying, ‘So be it,’ the lord of the earth had offerings given to him, establishing them in choice villages throughout the entire island.

90.

90.

Mahāsattena [M 0.0224] teneva, sabbabhūtānukampinā;

Mahārogabhayaṃ jātaṃ, dīpadīpena nāsitaṃ.

Thus by that great being, compassionate to all beings, by that Lamp of the Island, the great fear of disease that had arisen was destroyed.

91.

91.

So bhaṇḍāgāriko rañño,

Amacco goṭṭhatābhayo;

Cero hutvā uttarato,

Nagaraṃ samupāgami.

That treasurer of the king, the minister Goṭhābhaya, having become a rebel, approached the city from the north.

92.

92.

Parissāvanamādāya, rājā dakkhiṇadvārato;

Parahiṃsamarocento, ekakova palāyi so.

Taking a water strainer, the king departed from the southern gate; not delighting in harm to others, he fled all alone.

93.

93.

Puṭabhattaṃ gahetvāna, gacchanto purito pathi;

Bhattabhogāyarājānaṃ, nibandhittha punappunaṃ.

A man, taking food in a leaf-packet and walking ahead on the path, repeatedly urged the king to partake of the meal.

94.

94.

Jalaṃ parissāvayitvā, bhuñjitvāna dayāluko;

Tassevaṃ’nuggahaṃ kātuṃ, idaṃ vacanamabruvi.

Having strained the water and eaten, the compassionate one, wishing to do him a favor, spoke these words.

95.

95.

“Saṅghabodhi ahaṃ rājā, gahetvā mamabho sīraṃ;

Goṭṭhābhayassa dassehi, bahuṃ dassati te dhanaṃ.

‘I am King Saṅghabodhi. Sir, take my head and show it to Goṭhābhaya; he will give you much wealth.’

96.

96.

Na icchito tathākātuṃ, tassatthāya mahīpati;

Nisinnoyeva amari, so sīsaṃ tassa ādiya.

As the man did not wish to do so, the lord of the earth, for that man's sake, died while still seated. Then the man took his head.

97.

97.

Goṭṭhābhayassa dassesi, sotu vimhitamānaso;

Datvā tassa dhanaṃ rañño, sakkāraṃ sādhukārayi.

He showed it to Goṭhābhaya, who was struck with wonder. Having given wealth to the man, he caused due honor to be paid to the king.

98.

98.

Evaṃ goṭṭhābhayo eso, meghavaṇṇābhayo’ti ca;

Vissuto terasa samā, laṃkārajjamakārayi.

Thus this Goṭhābhaya, also renowned as Meghavaṇṇābhaya, ruled the kingdom of Laṅkā for thirteen years.

99.

99.

Mahāvatthuṃ kārayitvā, vatthudvāramhi maṇḍapaṃ;

Kārayitvā maṇḍayitvā, so bhikkhu tattha saṅghato.

Having had a great precinct built, and at its entrance a pavilion made and adorned, he dedicated it to the community of monks.

100.

100.

Aṭṭhuttarasahassāni, nisīdetvā dine dine;

Yāgukhajjaka bhojjehi, sādūhi vividhehi ca.

Day by day, having seated one thousand and eight monks, he served them with rice gruel, hard and soft foods, and various delicacies.

101.

101.

Sacīvarehi kappetvā, mahādānaṃ pavattayi;

Ekavīsadinā nevaṃ, nibaddhañcassa kārayi.

Having provided them with robes, he initiated a great almsgiving; for twenty-one days he had this carried on without interruption.

102.

102.

Mahāvihāre kāresi, silāmaṇḍapa muttamaṃ;

Lohapāsādathambhe ca, parivattiya ṭhāpayi.

He had an excellent stone pavilion built in the Mahāvihāra, and he had the pillars of the Lohapāsāda replaced and set up.

103.

103.

Mahābodhi [M 0.0225] silāvediṃ, uttaradvāratoraṇaṃ;

Patiṭṭhāpesi thambhe ca, cakukaṇṇe sacakkake.

He established the stone terrace for the great Bodhi tree, the arch at the northern gate, and pillars fitted with sockets and wheels.

104.

104.

Tisso sīlāpaṭimāyo, tīsu dvāresu kārayi;

Ṭhapāpesi ca pallaṅkaṃ, dakkhiṇamhi silāmayaṃ.

He had three stone images made for the three gates, and on the southern side, he had a stone throne set up.

105.

105.

Padhānabhūmiṃ kāresi, mahāvihārapacchato;

Dīpamhi jiṇṇakāvāsaṃ, sabbañca paṭisaṅkhari.

He had a meditation ground made behind the Mahāvihāra, and he repaired all the dilapidated monastic dwellings on the island.

106.

106.

Thūpārāme thūpagharaṃ, therambatthalake tathā;

Ārāme maṇisomavhe, paṭisaṅkhārayi ca so.

He repaired the thūpa-house in the Thūpārāma, likewise in the Therambatthalaka monastery, and also in the monastery named Maṇisoma.

107.

107.

Thūpārāme maṇisomā-rāme maricavaṭṭake;

Dakkhiṇavha vihāre ca, uposathagharāni ca.

He also restored the Uposatha halls in the Thūpārāma, the Maṇisomārāma, the Maricavaṭṭika monastery, and the Dakkhiṇa-vihāra.

108.

108.

Meghavaṇṇābhayavhañca, navavihāramakārayi;

Vihāramahapūjāyaṃ, piṇḍetvā dīpavāsīnaṃ.

He also had a new monastery built, named Meghavaṇṇābhaya. For the great festival of the monastery, he assembled the inhabitants of the island.

109.

109.

Tiṃsabhikkhusahassānaṃ, chacīvaramadāsi ca;

Mahāvesākhapūjañca, tadā evaṃ akārayi.

He gave six robes to each of thirty thousand monks, and at that time he also instituted the great Vesākha festival.

110.

110.

Anuvassañca saṅghassa, chacīvaramadāmayi;

Pāpakānaṃ niggahena, sodhento sāsanaṃ tu so.

Year after year, he had six robes given to the Sangha; and by suppressing the wicked, he purified the Dispensation.

111.

111.

Vetullavādino bhikkhū, abhayagirinivāsino;

Gāhayitvāsaṭṭhimatte, jinasāsanakaṇṭake.

He seized about sixty monks dwelling in the Abhayagiri monastery, adherents of the Vetulla doctrine whom he considered thorns in the Dispensation of the Victor.

112.

112.

Katvāna niggahaṃ tesaṃ, paratire khipāpayi;

Tattha khittassa therassa, nissito bhikkhucoḷiko.

Having suppressed them, he had them banished to the opposite shore. A monk from the Coḷa country was a disciple of an elder who had been banished there.

113.

113.

Saṅghamitto’tināmena, bhūtivijjādikovido;

Mahāvihāre bhikkhunaṃ, kujjhitvāna idhagamā.

Named Saṅghamitta, he was an expert in exorcism and related arts; having become angry with the monks of the Mahāvihāra, he came here.

114.

114.

Thūpārāme sannipātaṃ, pavisitvā asaññato;

Saṅghapālassa pariveṇa, vāsittherassa tattha so.

Having entered the assembly at the Thūpārāma unrestrained, he was there in the residence of the elder Saṅghapāla.

115.

115.

Goṭṭhāsayassa therassa, mātulassa’ssa rājino;

Rañño nāmenā“lapanto, vacanaṃ paṭibāhiya.

Defying the words of the elder Goṭṭhāsaya, the king's maternal uncle, he addressed him in the king's name.

116.

116.

Rañño kulūpago āsi, rājā tasmiṃ pasīdiya;

Jeṭṭhaputtaṃ jeṭṭhatissaṃ, mahāsenaṃ kaniṭṭhakaṃ.

He became a retainer of the king, and the king was pleased with him. The eldest son was Jeṭṭhatissa, the youngest was Mahāsena.

117.

117.

Appesi [M 0.0226] tassa bhikkhussa, so saṅgaṇhi dutiyakaṃ;

Upanandhi tasmiṃ bhikkhusmiṃ, jeṭṭhatisso kumārako.

He entrusted them to that monk; he took to the second son, but Prince Jeṭṭhatissa bore a grudge against that monk.

118.

118.

Pituno accaye jeṭṭha, sisso rājāahosiso;

Pitu sārīra sakkāre, niggantuṃ nicchamānake.

Upon the father's passing, the eldest son became king. He wished to go forth to perform the funeral rites for his father's body.

119.

119.

Duṭṭhāmacce niggahetuṃ, sayaṃ nikkhamma bhūpati;

Kaniṭṭhaṃ purato katvā, pitukāyaṃ anantaraṃ.

To restrain the wicked ministers, the king himself went forth, placing the youngest son in front and his father's body immediately after.

120.

120.

Tato amacce katvāna, sayaṃ hutvāna pacchato;

Kaniṭṭhe pitukāye ca, nikkhante tadanantaraṃ.

Then, having placed the ministers, he himself followed behind. And immediately after the youngest and the father's body had departed,

121.

121.

Dvāraṃ saṃvarayitvāna, duṭṭhamacce nighātiya;

Sūle appesi pituno, citakāyasamantato.

Having closed the gate and slain the wicked ministers, he impaled them on stakes all around his father's funeral pyre.

122.

122.

Tena’ssa kammunā nāmaṃ, kakkhalopapadaṃahu;

Saṅghamittotu so bhikkhu, bhīto tasmiṃ narādhipā.

By that deed, his name acquired the epithet 'the Harsh.' That monk Saṅghamitta, however, became fearful of that lord of men.

123.

123.

Tassābhisekasamakālaṃ, mahāsenena mantiya;

Tassābhisekaṃ pekkhanto, paratīraṃ gato ito.

At the very time of his consecration, having consulted with Mahāsena and anticipating that consecration, he went from here to the other shore.

124.

124.

Pitarā so vippakataṃ, lohapāsāda muttamaṃ;

Koṭidhanaṃ agghanakaṃ, kāresi sattabhūmakaṃ.

He had the excellent Lohapāsāda, which his father had left unfinished and which was worth ten million, built with seven stories.

125.

125.

Saṭṭhisatasahassagghaṃ, pūjayitvā maṇiṃtahiṃ;

Kāresi jeṭṭhatissotaṃ, maṇipāsādanāmakaṃ.

Having offered there a jewel worth six million, Jeṭṭhatissa had it named the Maṇipāsāda, the Jewel Palace.

126.

126.

Maṇi duve mahagghe ca, mahāthūpe apūjayi;

Mahābodhighare tīṇi, toraṇāni ca kārayi.

He offered two jewels of great value at the Great Stūpa, and he had three gateways made at the shrine of the Great Bodhi-tree.

127.

127.

Kārayitvā vihāraṃ so, pācinatissa pabbataṃ;

Pañcavāsesu saṅghassa, adāsi puthuvī pati.

That lord of the earth had the Pācinatissapabbata monastery built and gave it to the Sangha of the five residences.

128.

128.

Devānaṃpiyatissena, so patiṭṭhāpitaṃ purā;

Thūpārāme urusilā, paṭimaṃ cārudassanaṃ.

The great stone image of beautiful appearance, established long ago by Devānaṃpiyatissa in the Thūpārāma,

129.

129.

Netvāna thūpārāmavhaṃ, jeṭṭhatisso mahīpahi;

Patiṭṭhāpesi ārāme, pācinatissa pabbate.

King Jeṭṭhatissa, the lord of the earth, brought from the Thūpārāma and established in the Pācinatissapabbata monastery.

130.

130.

Kāḷamattikavāpiṃso, adācetiya pabbate;

Vihāra pāsāda mahaṃ, mahāvesākhameva ca.

He gave the Kāḷamattika reservoir to the Cetiyapabbata; he also held a great festival for the vihāra and the palace, as well as the great Vesākha festival.

131.

131.

Katvā [M 0.0227] tiṃsa sahassassa, saṅghassa’dā chacīvaraṃ;

Āḷambagāmavāpiṃso, jeṭṭhatisso akārayi.

He gave six robes each to thirty thousand members of the Sangha. Jeṭṭhatissa also had the Āḷambagāma reservoir built.

132.

132.

Evaṃ so vividhaṃ puññaṃ, pāsādakaraṇādikaṃ;

Kārento dasavassāni, rājā rajjamakārayi.

Thus, performing various meritorious deeds such as the construction of palaces, the king ruled the kingdom for ten years.

133.

133.

Iti bahuvidha puñña hetu bhūtā,

Narapatitā bahupāpahetu cāti;

Madhuramiva visenamissamannaṃ,

Sujanamano bhajate na taṃ kadāpi.

Thus, though kingship is a cause of manifold merit, it is also a cause of much evil. Like sweet food mixed with poison, the mind of a virtuous person never resorts to it.

Sujanappasāda saṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Mahāvaṃsa, composed for the serene joy and spiritual emotion of the virtuous.

Tayodasarājakonāma

Named The Thirteen Kings

Chattiṃsatimo paricchedo.

The Thirty-sixth Chapter.

Sattatiṃsatima pariccheda

The Thirty-seventh Chapter

Pañcarājako

The Five Kings

1.

1.

Jeṭṭhatissaccaye tassa, mahāseno kaniṭṭhako;

Sattavīsativassāni, rājā rajjamakārayi.

Upon the passing of Jeṭṭhatissa, his younger brother Mahāsena ruled the kingdom for twenty-seven years.

2.

2.

Tassa rajjābhisekaṃ taṃ,

Kāretuṃ paratīrato;

So saṅghamittatthero tu,

Kālaṃ ñatvā idhāgato.

To perform his royal consecration, the elder Saṅghamitta, knowing the right time, came here from the other shore.

3.

3.

Tassābhisekaṃ kāretvā, aññaṃ kiccañcanekadhā;

Mahāvihāra viddhaṃsaṃ, kātukāmo asaññato.

Having performed his consecration and various other duties, that unrestrained one desired to bring about the destruction of the Mahāvihāra.

4.

4.

Avinayavādino ete, mahāvihāravāsino;

Vinayavādī mayaṃ rāja, iti gāhiya bhūpabhiṃ.

"These residents of the Mahāvihāra are proponents of non-Discipline; we, O king, are proponents of the Discipline." Thus he won over the king.

5.

5.

Mahāvihāravāsissa[M 0.0228], āhāraṃ deti bhikkhuno;

Yo so sataṃ daṇḍiyo’ti, raññā daṇḍaṃ ṭhapāpayi.

He had the king impose a penalty: "Whoever gives food to a monk dwelling in the Mahāvihāra is liable to a fine of one hundred."

6.

6.

Upaddutā tehi bhikkhū, mahāvihāravāsino;

Mahāvihāraṃ chaḍḍetvā, malayaṃ rohaṇaṃ aguṃ.

Harassed by those monks, the monks dwelling in the Great Monastery, abandoning the Great Monastery, went to Malaya and Rohaṇa.

7.

7.

Tena mahāvihāro’yaṃ, navavassāni chaḍḍito;

Mahāvihāravāsīhi, bhikkhūhi āsi suññako.

Thus, this Great Monastery was abandoned for nine years by the monks dwelling in the Great Monastery, and was empty.

8.

8.

“Hoti assāmikaṃ vatthu, putuvisāmino”iti;

Rājānaṃ saññāpetvā so, thero dummati dummatiṃ.

“Ownerless property belongs to the king”; having thus persuaded the king, that evil-minded elder led the foolish one astray.

9.

9.

Mahāvihāraṃ nāsetuṃ, laddhānumati rājato;

Tathā kātuṃ manusse so, yojesi duṭṭhamānaso.

Having obtained permission from the king to destroy the Great Monastery, that wicked-minded one engaged men to do so.

10.

10.

Saṅghamittassa therassa, sevako rājavallabho;

Soṇāmacco dāraṇo ca, bhikkhavo ca alajjino.

The minister Soṇa, an attendant of the elder Saṅghamitta and a favorite of the king, and Dāraṇa, and shameless monks were among them.

11.

11.

Bhinditvā lohapāsādaṃ, sattabhūmaka muttamaṃ;

Ghare nānappakāre ca, ito’bhayagiriṃ nayuṃ.

Having broken up the excellent seven-storied Lohapāsāda and various kinds of dwellings, they took them from there to Abhayagiri.

12.

12.

Mahāvihārā nītehi, pāsādehi bahūhi ca;

Abhayagirivihāroyaṃ, bahupāsādako ahu.

With the many palatial buildings brought from the Great Monastery, this Abhayagiri Monastery became endowed with many such buildings.

13.

13.

Saṅghamittaṃ pāpamittaṃ, theraṃ soṇañca sevakaṃ;

Āgamma subahuṃ pāpaṃ, akāsi so mahīpati.

Relying on the elder Saṅghamitta, an evil friend, and Soṇa the attendant, that king committed much evil.

14.

14.

Mahāsilāpaṭimaṃ so, pācinatissapabbatā;

Ānetvā’bhayagirimhi, patiṭṭhāpesi bhūpati.

Having brought the great stone image from the Pācīnatissapabbata, the king enshrined it at Abhayagiri.

15.

15.

Paṭimāgharaṃ bodhigharaṃ, dhātusālaṃ manoramaṃ;

Catusālañca kāresī, saṅkharī kukkuṭavhayaṃ.

He had an image house, a Bodhi-tree shrine, a delightful relic hall, and a four-halled building constructed, and he also built the monastery named Kukkuṭa.

16.

16.

Saṅghamittena therena, tena dāruṇakammunā;

20.

Uttamo vata’yaṃ satto, rājā hessati nicchayaṃ;

Rakkhitabbo’ti ādāya, taṃ vihāramupāgato.

'Truly, this being is supreme; he will surely become a king. He must be protected!' Thinking thus, he took him and went to the monastery.

21.

21.

Goṇisādi vihāre’yaṃ, kattabbo nītimā iti;

Sikkhāpesi kumāraṃ taṃ, paṇḍuko taṃ vijāniya.

Thinking, 'He should be made an expert in statecraft,' he instructed the boy. But Paṇḍuka, having learned of this, sent men to seize him.

22.

22.

Gaṇhathetantipesesi, sevake tassārattiyaṃ;

Disvāna supinaṃ thero, nīharittha kumārakaṃ.

He sent his servants, saying, 'Seize him!' But that night, the Elder, having seen a dream, took the boy away.

23.

23.

Tasmiṃ nikkhantamattamhi, sevakaṃ parivāriya;

Pariveṇe na passiṃsu, tato nikkhamma te ubho.

As soon as he had departed, the servants, having surrounded the monastic cell, did not see him. Then those two departed from there.

24.

24.

Dakkhiṇasmiṃ disābhāge, goṇa nāmaṃ mahānadiṃ;

Patvā sampuṇṇamaṭṭhaṃsu, gantukāmāpi vegasā.

Having reached the great river named Goṇa in the southern region, they stood before it in its fullness, eager to proceed swiftly.

25.

25.

Yathā nadiyaṃ vāreti, amhe taṃ tvampi vāraya;

Vāpiṃgahetvā etthe’ti, vatvā thero tadā nadiṃ.

'Just as this river obstructs us, you too obstruct it, making it a reservoir here!' Having spoken thus, the Elder then addressed the river.

26.

26.

Otaritthakumārena, saddhiṃ disvāna te ubho;

Nāgarājā tadā eko, piṭṭhiṃ pādāsi tena so.

Seeing the two of them descending with the boy, a certain Nāga king then offered his back to him.

27.

27.

Uttaritvā kumāraṃ taṃ, netvā paccantamāvasaṃ;

Laddhā khīrodanaṃ sutvā, sesaṃ pattena tassa’dā.

Having crossed over, he led that boy to a borderland dwelling. Having obtained milk-rice and having heard a sound, he gave the remainder in his bowl to him.

28.

28.

Cittakārena [M 0.0248] theramhi, bhattaṃ pakkhippa bhūmiyaṃ;

Bhuñji theropi taṃ jāni, bhuñja te yaṃ mahiṃ iti.

He ate, having deliberately thrown the meal for the Elder on the ground. The Elder, knowing this, said: 'Eat what is on the ground for you.'

29.

29.

Paṇḍurājāpi katvāna, rajjaṃ vassamhi pañcame;

Cuto putto pipārindo, tatiyo tassa bhātuko.

King Paṇḍu, having ruled the kingdom for five years, passed away. His son was Pārinda, and the third was his brother.

30.

30.

Kaṇiṭṭho khuddapārindo, kubbaṃ rajjaṃ mahāmahiṃ;

Dhātusenānuge sabbe, viheṭhesi mahājane.

The youngest, Khuddapārinda, while ruling the great kingdom, oppressed all the followers of Dhātusena and the great populace.

31.

31.

Saṅgahetvā jane sādhu-seno yujjittha rājinā;

So soḷasahi vassehi, puññapāpakaromato.

Sādhu-sena, having gathered the people, fought with the king. For sixteen years, he performed acts of merit and demerit.

32.

32.

Niritaro tato āsi, rājāmāsadvayena taṃ;

Dhātuseno vināsesi, tena katvā mahāhavaṃ.

Then there was Niritara, who was king for two months. Dhātusena destroyed him, having waged a great battle.

33.

33.

Hate tasmiṃ mahīpāle, dāṭhiyo damiḷo tato;

Rājā vassattha ye hutvā, dhātusenahatotato.

When that king was slain, the Damiḷa Dāṭhiya then became king. Having been so for three years, he was then slain by Dhātusena.

34.

34.

Piṭṭhiyo damiḷo satta-māsena nidhanaṃ gato;

Dhātusenena yujjhitvā, vaṃso pacchijji dāmiḷo.

Piṭṭhiya the Damiḷa went to his destruction in seven months. Having fought with Dhātusena, the Damiḷa lineage was cut off.

35.

35.

Athā’si rājālaṅkāyaṃ, dhātuseno irādhipo;

Bhātarā saha dīpamhi, damiḷe dīpaghātake.

Then Dhātusena became king in Laṅkā, lord of the earth. With his brother, he destroyed the Damiḷas, the destroyers of the island, upon the island.

36.

36.

Upāyehi anekeyi, ekavīsappamāṇake;

Khandhavāre nivesetvā, katvā yuddhamasesato.

By means of many strategies, having established camps against some twenty-one chieftains, he waged war to the end.

37.

37.

Sodhetvā mediniṃ sādhu, katvā ca sukhitaṃjanaṃ;

Sāsanañca yathāṭhāne, ṭhapesi paranāsitaṃ.

Having well cleansed the earth and made the people happy, he established in its proper place the Dispensation, which had been destroyed by enemies.

38.

38.

Damiḷe ye’nuvattiṃsu, kulīnā kulagāmavā;

Te maṃ vā sāsanaṃ vā no, rakkhiṃsū’ti pakuppiya.

He became angry with the noble families and villagers who had followed the Damiḷas, thinking: 'These did not protect me nor the Dispensation!'

39.

39.

Tesaṃ gāme gahetvāna, gāme svākāsirakkhake;

Rohaṇā’gamma te sabbe, kulīnā tamupaṭṭhahuṃ.

Having seized their villages, he placed his own guards in those villages. All the nobles, having come from Rohaṇa, attended upon him.

40.

40.

Tesaṃ sakkārasammānaṃ, yathāyogamakāsi so;

Amacce attano dukkha-sahāyecā’bhi tosayi.

To them, he gave honor and respect as was fitting. He also greatly pleased his own ministers and companions in hardship.

41.

41.

Bandhāpetvā mahāgaṅgaṃ, kedāre’kā thirodake;

Mahāpāḷamhi bhikkhūnaṃ, sālibhattañca dāpayi.

Having caused the Mahāgaṅgā to be dammed, he made the rice fields have stable water. He also caused rice meals to be given to the monks at the Mahāpāḷi alms hall.

42.

42.

Paṅgurogā turaṭṭānaṃ, sālāyokāsi buddhimā;

Kāḷavāpiṃca gaṇhitvā, bandhi goṇaṃ mahānadiṃ.

The wise one made halls for the crippled and the sick who were afflicted. And having constructed the Kāḷavāpi tank, he dammed the great Goṇa river.

43.

43.

Mahāvihāraṃ [M 0.0249] katvāna, pantiyuttamanākulaṃ;

Tathā bodhigharañceva, dassaneyya makārayi.

Having made restorations to the Mahāvihāra, making it well-arranged, excellent, and orderly, and likewise a Bodhi-tree shrine, he caused them to be made splendid to behold.

44.

44.

Bhikkhavo paritosetvā, paccayehi catūhipi;

Dhammāsoko’va sokāsi, saṅgahaṃ piṭakattaye.

Having satisfied the monks with the four requisites, he, like Dhammāsoka, sponsored a compilation of the three Piṭakas.

45.

45.

Aṭṭhārasavihāre ca, theriyāna makārayi;

Sampannabhoge dīpamhi, aṭṭhārasa ca vāpiyo.

He also caused eighteen monasteries to be made for the Therīs, and on the island endowed with abundant resources, he made eighteen reservoirs.

46.

46.

Kāḷavāpī vihāro ca, koṭipassāvanāmako;

Dakkhiṇa girināmo ca, vihāro vaḍḍhamānako.

The Kāḷavāpī monastery, the one named Koṭipassāva, the monastery named Dakkhiṇagiri, and the Vaḍḍhamānaka monastery.

47.

47.

Paṇṇavallakabhūto ca, bhallātakasanāmako;

Pāsāṇasinne desamhi, dhātuseno ca pabbato.

The Paṇṇavallaka, the one named Bhallātaka, one in the region of Pāsāṇasinna, and the Dhātusena-pabbata.

48.

48.

Maṃ gano thūpaviṭṭhi ca, dhātusenopi uttare;

Pācina kambaviṭṭhi ca, tathā antarame giri.

The Maṅgaṇa, the Thūpaviṭṭhi, the Dhātusena in the north, the Pācīna-kambaviṭṭhi, and likewise the Antaragiri.

49.

49.

Antāḷi dhātuseno ca, kassapiṭṭhika pubbako;

Rohaṇedāyagāmo ca, sālavāṇo vibhīsano.

The Antāḷi-dhātusena, the former Kassapiṭṭhika, the one in the village of Rohaṇedāya, the Sālavāṇa, and the Vibhīsana.

50.

50.

Vihāro bhallivāṇo ca, aṭṭhārasanaruttamo;

Pādūlakaṃ hambalaṭṭhi, mahādatthādivāpi yo.

The Bhallivāṇa monastery—these are the eighteen. The foremost of men also built the Pādūlaka, Hambalaṭṭhi, and Mahādatthādi reservoirs.

51.

51.

Khuddake ca vihāreso, aṭṭhārasanaruttamo;

Vāpīyo ca tathākatvā, tesameva tu dāpayi.

That foremost of men also built eighteen small monasteries; and having likewise made reservoirs, he had them given to those same monasteries.

52.

52.

Pañcavīsati hatthañca, mayūrapariveṇakaṃ;

Haritvā’kāsipāsāda-mekavīsati hatthakaṃ.

The Mayūrapariveṇa was twenty-five cubits. Having dismantled a palace, he made it twenty-one cubits.

53.

53.

Kumārasenassa’petvā, pubbabhogaṃ visodhayi;

Kāḷavāpimmibhāgaddhaṃ, khettānañca satadvayaṃ.

Having removed Kumārasena, he cleared the former property: a half share of the Kāḷavāpi tank and two hundred fields.

54.

54.

Loha pāsadake jiṇṇe, navakammamakārayi;

Mahāthūpesu chattāni, tīsu jiṇṇāni kārayi.

He had renovation work done on the dilapidated Lohapāsāda; and on the great stūpas, he had the three dilapidated canopies repaired.

55.

55.

Devānaṃpiyatissena, kataṃ bodhimahaṃ viya;

Sinhānapūjaṃ bodhissa, varabodhissa kārayi.

Like the great Bodhi festival held by Devānampiyatissa, he had a bathing ceremony performed for the excellent Bodhi tree.

56.

56.

Dhāvanā lobhanāvāyo, tattha pūjesi soḷasa;

Alaṅkāraṃ munindassa, abhisekañca kārayi.

There he made sixteen offerings of ablutions and 'boats of gain'; he also had an adornment for the Lord of Sages and a consecration performed.

57.

57.

Mahābodhi patiṭṭhānā, oraṃ laṅkāya bhūmipā;

Yāva dvādasamaṃ vassaṃ, bodhipūjamakārayuṃ.

From the time of the establishment of the Mahābodhi, the kings of Laṅkā performed Bodhi offerings up to the twelfth year.

58.

58.

Mahāmahindattherassa[M 0.0250], kāretvā paṭibimbakaṃ;

Therassā’lāhanaṃ netvā, kātuṃ pūjaṃ mahārahaṃ.

Having had an image of the great Elder Mahinda made, and having brought it to the Elder's cremation ground to perform a great and worthy offering,

59.

59.

Datvā sahassaṃ dīpetuṃ, dīpavaṃsaṃ samādisi;

Ṭhitānaṃ tattha bhikkhūnaṃ, dātuñcāṇāpayiguḷaṃ.

Having given a thousand to illuminate it, he ordered the Dīpavaṃsa to be expounded; and he commanded that sweets be given to the monks present there.

60.

60.

Bhikkhussa attano sīse, saṅkārokiraṇaṃ saraṃ;

Lābhaṃ nādāsi vutthassa, pariveṇassa attano.

Remembering the scattering of rubbish by a monk upon his own head, he did not give income to his own pariveṇa where that monk had dwelt.

61.

61.

Phātikammaṃ bahuṃ’kāsi, vihāre abhayuttare;

Silāsatthussa kāresi, mandirañca samaṇḍapaṃ.

He performed much repair work in the Abhayuttara monastery; for the Stone Teacher, he had a shrine and a pavilion built.

62.

62.

Buddha dāsakatenette, naṭṭhe’nagghamaṇi dvayaṃ;

Akāsi nettaṃ satthussa, raṃsi cūḷāmaṇiṃtathā.

The two priceless gem-eyes made by Buddhadāsa having been lost, he made new eyes for the Teacher, and likewise a radiant crest-gem.

63.

63.

Maṇihi ghananīlehi, kesā vattaṃ sumuttamaṃ;

Hemapaṭṭaṃ tathevuṇṇa-lomaṃ sovaṇṇa cīvaraṃ.

He made a most excellent hair-whorl with deep blue gems, a golden headband, likewise the uṇṇa-hair, and a golden robe.

64.

64.

Pādajālaṃ suvaṇṇassa, padumaṃ dīpamuttamaṃ;

Nānārāgambaraṃ tattha, pūjayittha asaṃkhiyaṃ.

He made a golden foot-netting and a supreme lotus lamp; and there he worshipped immeasurably with garments of various colors.

65.

65.

Akāsi paṭimā gehe, bahumaṅgalacetiye;

Bodhisatte tathā’kāsi, kāḷaselassa satthuno.

He made images in the image-house at the Bahumaṅgala-cetiya; likewise, he made images of Bodhisattas and of the teacher Kāḷasela.

66.

66.

Upasumbhavhayassāpi, lokanāthassa kārayi;

Raṃsīcūḷāmaṇiñceva, abhisekavhayassa ca.

He also had an image made of the Lord of the World named Upasumbha, as well as a radiant crest-gem, and an image of the one named Abhiseka.

67.

67.

Buddhabimbassa kāresi, pubbe vuttaṃ piḷandhanaṃ;

Vāmapassamhi bodhissa, bodhisattagharaṃ tathā.

He had the previously mentioned adornments made for the Buddha image; and likewise, on the left side of the Bodhi tree, a Bodhisatta house.

68.

68.

Metteyyassa ca kāresi, sabbaṃ rājapiḷandhanaṃ;

Samantā yojane tassa, tadā rakkhañca yojayi.

And for Metteyya, he had all the royal adornments made; he then established protection for him for a yojana all around.

69.

69.

Kārāpesi vihāresu, dhāturājavhapantiyo;

Tathā satasahassena, mahābodhigharaṃ varaṃ.

He had rows of royal reliquaries built in the monasteries; likewise, with a hundred thousand, he built the excellent Mahābodhi-house.

70.

70.

Thūpāramamhi thūpassa, pūjaṃ jiṇṇavisodhanaṃ;

Dāṭhā dhātugharecāpi, jiṇṇassa paṭisaṅkharaṃ.

At the Thūpārāma, he performed worship and renovation of the old stūpa; and in the Tooth Relic House, he also restored what was dilapidated.

71.

71.

Dāṭhādhātukaruṇḍañca, raṃsiñca ghanakoṭṭimaṃ;

Mahagghamanisaṃkiṇṇaṃ, suvaṇṇa padumāni ca.

He made the Tooth Relic casket, a radiant, solid chamber strewn with priceless gems, and golden lotuses.

72.

72.

Dāṭhādhātumhi pūjesi, pūjācākā asaṅkhiyā;

Cīvarādīni dāpesi, bhikkhūnaṃ dīpavāsinaṃ.

He worshipped at the Tooth Relic and made innumerable offerings; he also had robes and other requisites given to the monks dwelling on the island.

73.

73.

Kārāpetvā [M 0.0251] vihāresu, navakammaṃ tahiṃ tahiṃ;

Pākāre ca gharetvā’kā, sudhākammaṃ manoharaṃ.

Having had renovation work done in the monasteries here and there, he also made walls and houses with delightful plasterwork.

74.

74.

Mahācetittaye katvā, sudhākammaṃ mahārahaṃ;

Suvaṇṇachattaṃ kāresi, tathā vajiracumbaṭaṃ.

Having done priceless plasterwork on the three great cetiyas, he had a golden parasol made, and likewise a diamond finial.

75.

75.

Mahāvihāre pāpena, mahāsenena nāsite;

Vasisuṃ dhammarucikā, bhikkhū cetiyapabbate.

When the Mahāvihāra was destroyed by the wicked Mahāsena, the Dhammarucika bhikkhus dwelt on the Cetiyapabbata.

76.

76.

Katvā ambatthalaṃ thera-vādānaṃ dātu kāmako;

Yācito tehi tesaṃ’va, adāsi dharaṇī pati.

Having restored the Ambatthala and desiring to give it to the Theravādins, the lord of the earth, being requested by them, gave it to them.

77.

77.

Dātu paṭhānanāvañca, kāretvā kaṃsalohajaṃ;

Dānavaṭṭaṃ pavattesi, ambaṇebhi dvipañcahi.

Having had a distribution vessel made of bronze and iron, he established a constant giving of alms, with ten ambaṇas.

78.

78.

Anto bahi ca kāretvā, nagarassa jinālaye;

Paṭimāyo ca pūjesi, dhammāsokasamo’samo.

Having had shrines of the Conqueror built inside and outside the city, he also worshipped the images, being equal to Dhammāsoka, yet incomparable.

79.

79.

Tassa puññāni sabbāni, vatthu paṭipadaṃ naro;

Ko hi nāma samatthoti, mukhamattaṃ nidassitaṃ.

Who indeed is able to describe all the merits of that man, their substance and his practice? Only a mere sample has been shown.

80.

80.

Tassa puttaduve āsuṃ, kassapo bhinnamātiko;

Samānamātiko ceva, moggallāno mahabbalo.

He had two sons: Kassapa, of a different mother; and Moggallāna, of the same mother, who was of great strength.

81.

81.

Tathā pāṇasamā ekā, duhitā ca manoramā;

Bhāgineyyassa pādāsi, senāpaccañca tañca so.

Likewise, he had one charming daughter, dear as life; he gave her to his nephew, and he made that nephew the general.

82.

82.

Vinā dosena tāḷesi, kasāyūrusu so’pitaṃ;

Rājā disvāna duhitu-vatthaṃ lohitamakkhitaṃ.

He, for no offense, struck her on the thighs with a whip. The king, seeing his daughter's garment stained with blood,

83.

83.

Ñatvā taṃ mātaraṃ tassa, naggaṃ jhapesi kujjhiya;

Tatoppabhutiso baddha-vero saṅgamma kassapaṃ.

Knowing her to be his mother, he, in his anger, had her burned naked. From then on, that man, bound by enmity, went over to Kassapa.

84.

84.

Rajje netaṃ palobhetvā, bhinditvā pituantare;

Saṅgahetvā janaṃ java-gāhaṃ gāhāpayī patiṃ.

Having lured him with the kingdom and created a rift with his father, he gathered the people and caused the lord to be swiftly seized.

85.

85.

Ussāpesi tato chattaṃ, kassapo pitupakkhiye;

Vināsetvā jane laddha-sabbapāpasahāyako.

Then Kassapa, having destroyed the people on his father's side, raised the umbrella, having gained companions for all evil deeds.

86.

86.

Moggallāno tato tena,

Kātukāmo mahāhavaṃ;

Aladdha balatāya’gā,

Jambudīpa balatthiko.

Then Moggallāna, desiring to wage a great war with him, but being unable to obtain forces, went to Jambudīpa seeking an army.

87.

87.

Mahārajja [M 0.0252] vināsena, viyogena ca sūnuno;

Baddhanāgāravāsena, dukkhitampi durādhipaṃ.

By the destruction of the great kingdom, by separation from his son, and by confinement in a prison-house, the wicked ruler was afflicted.

88.

88.

Dukkhāpetumapaññoso, āha kassaparājakaṃ;

Nidhi rājakulerāja-gutta te pitarā iti.

That foolish one, intending to torment him further, said to King Kassapa: 'O King, the treasure of the royal family is guarded by your father.'

89.

89.

Ne’ti gutte na jānāsi, cittametassa bhūmipa;

Moggallānassa kāpeti, nidhiṃsoti tadabrūvi.

The thought of this king was: 'You do not know what is guarded.' He then said: 'He is keeping the treasure for Moggallāna.'

90.

90.

Sutvā taṃ kupito dūte, pāhesī pitusantikaṃ;

Ācikkhatu nidhiṭhāna-miti vatvā narādhamo.

Hearing this, the wicked man, angered, sent messengers to his father, saying: 'Declare the location of the treasure!'

91.

91.

Māretu amhe pāpassa, tassupāyo’ti cintiya;

Tuṇhī ahosi te gantvā, rājakassa nivedayuṃ.

Thinking, 'This is a device of that wicked one to have me killed,' he remained silent. They went and reported this to the king.

92.

92.

Tato’tīva pakuppitvā, pesayittha punappunaṃ;

Sādhu disvā sahāyamme, nhatvāna kāḷavāpiyaṃ.
