Laṅkādīpamhi sakale, sayameva vicārayī.

He himself administered the provision of medicine for the sick and the performance of auspicious and inauspicious ceremonies throughout the entire island of Laṅkā.

73.

73.

Salākabhattaṃ dāpesi, nikāyattaya vāsinaṃ;

Bhojanaṃ paṃsukūlīnaṃ, attayoggaṃ mahārahaṃ.

He had ticket-food distributed to the residents of the three Nikāyas, and food of great value, suitable for himself, to the wearers of rag-robes.

74.

74.

Evamādīni katvāna, puññāni sasayaṃ vasī;

Cuto’si chahi vassehi, pulatthinagare vasaṃ.

Having performed these and other meritorious deeds, he ruled securely. After six years, he passed away while dwelling in the city of Pulatthinagara.

75.

75.

Tato pubbeva tassāsi, putto so yuvarājako;

Mato kira tato rajjaṃ, aputtaṃ taṃ tadā ahu.

It is said that his son, the crown prince, had died even before this. Therefore, the kingdom was then without an heir.

76.

76.

Putto mahindo nāmā’si, silā meghassa rājino;

Rajjayoggo mahāpuñño, lokasaṅgaṇha nakkhamo.

There was a son of King Silāmegha named Mahinda, who was worthy of kingship, of great merit, and capable of protecting the world.

77.

77.

Tassa jātadineyeva, rājā nakkhattapāṭhake;

Pucchitvā rajjayoggoti, sutvā tehi viyākataṃ.

On the very day of his birth, the king questioned the astrologers, and having heard their declaration that he was worthy of kingship,

78.

78.

Datvā tesaṃ dhanaṃ sādhu, pavattiṃ taṃ nigūhayi;

Atha naṃ so vayappattaṃ, katvā senāpatiṃsakaṃ.

Having given them wealth generously, he concealed the matter. Then, when the boy came of age, he made him his commander of the army.

79.

79.

Rajjaṃ vasseva katvāna, sabbaṃ hatthe sayaṃvasī;

So dhammena vicāresi, rāja kiccaṃ mahāmati.

Having brought the entire kingdom under his own control, that one of great wisdom administered the royal duties in accordance with the Dhamma.

80.

80.

Matepi tasmiṃ tasmā so, aggabodhābhidhānino;

Senāpaccaṃ na gaṇhittha, nayaññū tassa hatthako.

Even after the king died, he, being a knower of policy, did not accept the post of commander of the army from the one named Aggabodhi.

81.

81.

Tadā kenaci gantvā so, karaṇīyena rājino;

Samuddatīre vasati, mahātitthamhi paṭṭane.

Then, having gone on some royal business, he was dwelling on the seashore in the port city of Mahātittha.

82.

82.

Sutvā so cūḷapituno, maraṇaṃ vegasā’gamā;

Corā rajjaṃ gahetvāna, nāseyyuṃ nagaraṃ iti.

Having heard of his paternal uncle's death, he came with speed, thinking, 'Lest thieves seize the kingdom and destroy the city.'

83.

83.

Tato uttaradesamhi, maṇḍalīkā saraṭṭhiyā;

Acchinditvāna taṃ desaṃ, chinnarājakaraṃ karuṃ.

Then in the northern region, the provincial chiefs, having seized that region, stopped paying the royal taxes.

84.

84.

So [M 0.0302] taṃ sutvā mahāseno, gantvā uttaradesakaṃ;

Sabbe nimmathayitvāna, maṇḍalī kesaraṭṭhiye.

Hearing this, he of the great army went to the northern region and crushed all the provincial chiefs there.

85.

85.

Gantvā rañño mataṭhānaṃ, disvā deviṃ parodiya;

Assāsetvā yathākālaṃ, idaṃ vacanamabravi.

Having gone to the place where the king had died and seen the queen, he wept. Then, having consoled her at the proper time, he spoke these words:

86.

86.

Mācintesi mahādevī, mato me sāmiko iti;

Rakkhissāmi ahaṃ dīpaṃ, tumhe rajjaṃ karissatha.

'Great Queen, do not grieve thinking, "My lord is dead." I shall protect the island; you shall rule the kingdom.'

87.

87.

Tuṇhibhūtā’dhivāsetvā, piyasā pāpabuddhikā;

Raho yojayī taṃ hantuṃ, vatthukāmā yathāruciṃ.

She of evil mind, consenting silently, secretly plotted to kill him, desiring sensual pleasures according to her fancy.

88.

88.

Senāpati taṃ ñatvāna, tassā’rakkhaṃ vidhāya so;

Taṃ pakkhiyehi yujjhitvā, palāpesi mahājanaṃ.

The commander, learning of this, arranged protection for her. Then, having fought with her partisans, he routed the great host.

89.

89.

Tato deviṃ sabandhetvā, pakkhipitvāna yānake;

Ādāya taṃ puraṃ gantvā, rajjaṃ gaṇhi sasādhanaṃ.

Then, having bound the queen and placed her in a vehicle, he took her, went to the city, and seized the kingdom with its resources.

90.

90.

Atthi dappuḷa nāmo’pi,

Silā meghassa rājino;

Bhāgineyyo mahāseno,

Ādipādo mahā dhano.

There was also one named Dappuḷa, the nephew of King Silāmegha. He was an Ādipāda of great wealth, with a great army.

91.

91.

So senaṃ sannipātetvā, vasanto kāḷavāpiyaṃ;

Kātuṃ saṅgāma māgañchi, saṅgagāmappadesakaṃ.

Having assembled his army, he was dwelling at Kāḷavāpi. Then he came to the region of Saṅgagāma to wage war.

92.

92.

Senāpati pavattiṃ taṃ, sutvā sampannavāhano;

Deviñca taṃ samādāya, agamā tattha sajjukaṃ.

The commander, hearing that news, took the queen with him and, well-equipped with forces, went there at once.

93.

93.

Tesaṃ tatthasi saṅgāmo, ubhinnaṃ lomahaṃsano;

Ādipādo tadāsenaṃ, ohīyantaṃ samekkhiya.

A hair-raising battle ensued there between the two of them. The Ādipāda, seeing his army then faltering,

94.

94.

Palāyitvā āruhittha, acchaselaṃ savāhano;

Palāpetvāna taṃ tattha, senāpati sukhaṃ vasi.

fled and ascended Acchasela with his mount. Having routed him there, the commander dwelt in comfort.

95.

95.

Suññaṃti nagaraṃ sutvā, maṇḍalīkāpi uttare;

Dese sabbe samāgamma, aggahesuṃ puraṃ tadā.

Hearing that the city was empty, all the provincial chiefs in the northern region assembled and then seized the city.

96.

96.

So hi te paṭibāhesi, sūro dhīraparakkamo;

Athāgamma puraṃ rajjaṃ, vicāresi yathānayaṃ.

But he, a hero wise and brave, repelled them. Then, having returned to the city, he administered the kingdom according to principle.

97.

97.

Bhikkhusaṅghassa lokassa, macchānaṃ migapakkhinaṃ;

Ñātīnaṃ balakāyassa, kattabbaṃ sabbamācari.

For the Sangha of bhikkhus and for the world, for the fish, beasts, and birds, for his relatives and his army—for all these he did everything that ought to be done.

98.

98.

Pacchā [M 0.0303] anu balappatto, dappulo malayaṃ gato;

Bhāgineyyo duve ceva, pakkositvāna rohaṇā.

Afterwards, having regained his strength, Dappuḷa went to Malaya and summoned his two nephews from Rohaṇa.

99.

99.

Raṭṭhe janapade sabbe, ādāya bahuvāhano;

Rattiyaṃ puramāgamma, samuddo viya otthari.

Taking with him all in the kingdom and the country districts, with a great force of troops he came to the city by night and overwhelmed it like the ocean.

100.

100.

Balakāyo puraṃ rundhi, ugghosento samantato;

Hesitena turaṅgānaṃ, koñcanāde nadantinaṃ.

The army besieged the city, shouting on all sides with the neighing of horses and the trumpeting of elephants.

101.

101.

Tāḷāvacara saddānaṃ, kāhaḷānaṃ ravena ca;

Gajjitena bhaṭānañca, ākāsaṃ na tadā phali.

With the sound of percussion, the blare of trumpets, and the roaring of the soldiers, it was a wonder the sky did not split apart.

102.

102.

Tadā senāpati disvā, mahāsenaṃ pamodiya;

Ārocesi avattiṃ taṃ, balakāyassa attano.

Then the commander, seeing the great army, rejoiced and announced the matter to his own host of troops.

103.

103.

Rājaputtā tayo ete, mahantaṃ balamādiya;

Nagaraṃ no’parundhiṃsu, kintu kattabba mettha vo.

'These three princes, having taken a great army, have besieged our city. What, then, should be done by you in this matter?'

104.

104.

Evaṃ vuttā tamāhaṃsu, sūrā tassa raṇatthino;

Devāsevā dineyeva, sevakānaṃ na jīvitaṃ.

Thus addressed, his brave warriors, eager for battle, said to him: 'Our service to our lord is for the day; a servant's life is not his own.'

105.

105.

Evaṃ bhūte sace kāle, ohīnā jīvibhatthino;

Posesi sāmi kiṃ kāla-mettakaṃ no yathā sukhaṃ.

'If, at such a time, we who depend on you for our livelihood were to fail, for what purpose, O lord, have you supported us in comfort for all this time?'

106.

106.

Vutte evaṃ saussāho, balaṃ sajjiya rattiyaṃ;

Uggate aruṇe hatthi-māruyha katakammakaṃ.

Thus inspired, with energy roused, he prepared his force by night; at the rise of dawn, mounting his elephant, he set out to accomplish his task.

107.

107.

Dvārene’kena nikkhamma, patanto asanī viya;

Saddhiṃ yo dhasahassehi, saṅgāmaṃ kāsi dussahaṃ.

Exiting through a single gate, he fell upon them like a thunderbolt; together with ten thousand warriors, he waged a terrible battle.

108.

108.

Balaṃ taṃ ādipādassa, nipphoṭetvā tato tato;

Sannipātiya ekajjhaṃ, niyattiṃ sampavedayi.

Having scattered that force of the Ādipāda here and there, and having assembled his own men together, he announced his command.

109.

109.

Hatāvasese ādāya, ādipādopi dappuḷo;

Pubbaṇheva parājitvā, palāyitvā’ga rohaṇaṃ.

The Ādipāda Dappuḷa, taking the survivors of the slaughter, was defeated in the forenoon and fled to Rohaṇa.

110.

110.

Rājaputte duve ceva, rohaṇamhā tadā gate;

Jīvaggāhaṃ sagāhetvā, te ādāya puraṃ gato.

He also seized alive the two princes who had come from Rohaṇa and, taking them with him, went to the city.

111.

111.

Evaṃ pattajayo sūro, dīpe jāte nirākule;

Pācinadesaṃ sādhetuṃ, pesayittha savāhane.

Thus the heroic victor, when the island had been pacified, sent forth his army and transport to subdue the eastern region.

112.

112.

Tepi gantvāna desaṃ taṃ, uttaraṃ desameva ca;

Sādhayitvā’cireneva, saṅgahesuṃ mahābalaṃ.

They went to that country and to the northern region as well, and having subdued them without delay, they gathered a great army.

113.

113.

Rājāpi [M 0.0304] taṃ mahādeviṃ, bhariyaṃ kāsi attano;

Pariccattuñca māretuṃ, na sakkāyanti cintiya.

The king also took that chief queen as his own wife, thinking, 'It is not possible to abandon or to kill her.'

114.

114.

Tesaṃ saṃvāsamanvāya, gabbho āsi patiṭṭhito;

Puttaṃ vijāyi sādhañña-puññalakkhaṇasaññuttaṃ.

As a result of their cohabitation, a conception took place, and she gave birth to a son endowed with the signs of virtue and merit.

115.

115.

Rañño sā’tipiyā āsi, tato paṭṭhāya sopi kho;

Puttassa tassa pādāsi, oparajjaṃ sabhogiyaṃ.

She became exceedingly dear to the king, and from that time on he bestowed upon that son of his the office of viceroy with all its revenues.

116.

116.

Ṭhitā pācinadesamhi, ādipādā nisammataṃ;

Vinā so’yanti amhākaṃ, ubho hutvāna ekato.

The Ādipādas stationed in the eastern country took counsel together, thinking: 'Without him, we are lost; we two must unite.'

117.

117.

Dvīsu passesu senañca, samādāya mahādhanaṃ;

Sandhiṃbhātaramāhūya, katvārohaṇa desato.

Having raised a force and great wealth on two sides, he summoned his brother from the country of Rohaṇa and made a treaty.

118.

118.

Gaṅgātīramhi vāsaṃ te, kappayiṃsu mahabbalā;

Rājā sabbaṃ nisamme’taṃ, maṇḍalīke tahiṃ tahiṃ.

Those mighty ones established their residence on the bank of the river, and the king, hearing all this, appointed provincial chiefs here and there.

119.

119.

Ārādhetvā gahetvāna, duṭṭhe māriya kecana;

Rakkhaṃ datvāna nagare, kattabbaṃ sādhuyojiya.

Having won some over and seized others, and having executed some of the wicked, he provided protection in the city and properly arranged all that had to be done.

120.

120.

Mahāsenaṅgamādāya, mahesiñca tamādiya;

Khandhāvāraṃ niveseti, mahummāramhi gāmake.

Taking his great army and that chief queen, he set up his camp in the village of Mahummāra.

121.

121.

Tassāgamanamaññāya, ādipādāpi te tayo;

Koviḷāravhaye gāme, mahāyuddhaṃ pavattayuṃ.

Learning of his arrival, those three Ādipādas also commenced a great battle in the village called Koviḷāra.

122.

122.

Atha rājā mahāseno, samugghātesi taṃ balaṃ;

Dappuḷo so palāyittha, ādi pādā duve hatā.

Then the king with his great army annihilated that force. Dappuḷa fled, and the two Ādipādas were slain.

123.

123.

Tatthāpi laddhavijayo, puramāgammabhūmipo;

Rājakiccaṃ vicāresi, mahādānaṃ pavattayi.

Having gained victory there, the king returned to the city, where he administered the affairs of the kingdom and instituted a great almsgiving.

124.

124.

Mahābodhi dumindassa, mahācetittayassa ca;

Dhātūnampi ca sakkaccaṃ, mahāpūjāmakārayī.

He had great offerings made with reverence to the great Bodhi tree, to the three great cetiyas, and also to the relics.

125.

125.

Rohaṇaṃ samupāgamma, dappuḷo so tamāgato;

Balaṃ sampaṭipādesi, yujjhituṃ puna rājinā.

That Dappuḷa, having gone to Rohaṇa, prepared his army there to fight again with the king.

126.

126.

Rājā so puttanattānaṃ, desaṃ kātuṃ nirākulaṃ;

Thūpārāmamhi sabbepi, sannipātiya bhikkhavo.

That king, in order to make the country peaceful for his son and for himself, assembled all the bhikkhus at the Thūpārāma.

127.

127.

Aññepi ca mahāpaññe, yuttā yuttivisārade;

Rājadhammesu sabbesu, nipuṇo nayakovido.

He also assembled other men of great wisdom, skilled in counsel and diplomacy. The king himself was skilled in all royal duties and an expert in policy.

128.

128.

Ārocetvā [M 0.0305] pavattiṃ taṃ, tehi sammā pakāsito;

Caturaṅgamahāseno, sabbūpakaraṇānugo.

Having announced the matter to them and being well advised by them, he, with his great fourfold army, complete with all its equipment,

129.

129.

Dīpe sabbattha yojetvā, kattabbaṃ nagarepi ca;

Nikkhanto na cireneva, agamā mārapabbataṃ.

and having arranged what was to be done everywhere on the island and in the city, set out without delay and went to the Mārapabbata mountain.

130.

130.

Sammadditvāna taṃ desaṃ, khippaṃ pabbatamāruhī;

Taṃ disvā rohaṇe sabbe, bhītā taṃ vasamāgamuṃ.

Having thoroughly subdued that region, he quickly ascended the mountain. Seeing this, all the people of Rohaṇa were terrified and submitted to his authority.

131.

131.

Tato sandhiṃ karitvāna, dappuḷena sadappako;

Hatthī asse ca maṇayo, gahetvā tassa hatthato.

Then he, the proud one, having made a treaty with Dappuḷa, took from his hand elephants, horses, and jewels.

132.

132.

Gāḷhagaṅgañca katvāna, sīmaṃ rohaṇabhoginaṃ;

Oragaṅgaṃ samādāya, rājabhogamakārayi.

He made the Gāḷhagaṅga the boundary for the ruler of Rohaṇa, and taking the land on this side of the river, he made it a royal demesne.

133.

133.

Dīpamevaṃ mahātejo, katvā vigatakaṇṭakaṃ;

Ekātapatto āgamma, puraṃ vasi yathāsukhaṃ.

Thus the one of great majesty, having made the island free from thorns, returned to the city as its sole sovereign and dwelt there in comfort.

134.

134.

Pariveṇaṃ sakāresi, rājā dāmavihārakaṃ;

Tathā sanniratitthañca, pulatthinagare vibhū.

The lordly king had the Dāmavihāraka pariveṇa built in the city of Pulatthinagara, and likewise the Sanniratittha bathing place.

135.

135.

Mahālekhañca kāresi, pariveṇamabhayā cale;

Tathā ratanapāsādaṃ, tatheva sumanoharaṃ.

He had the delightful Mahālekha-pariveṇa built at the Abhayagiri, and likewise the equally delightful Ratanapāsāda.

136.

136.

Anekabhūmaṃ kāretvā, vejayantamivāparaṃ;

Tathā satasahassehi, tīhi ceva mahādhano.

The very wealthy king had this built with many stories, like a second Vejayanta palace, at a cost of three hundred thousand.

137.

137.

Jambonadatuvaṇṇassa, sahassehi ca saṭṭhihi;

Bimbaṃ satthussa kāretvā, nagghaṃ cūḷāmaṇiyutaṃ.

He had an image of the Teacher made from sixty thousand of Jambu-river gold, endowed with a priceless crest-jewel.

138.

138.

Pūjaṃ sabbopahārena, kāretvāna mahārahaṃ;

Pāsādamahane sabbaṃ, rajjaṃ ossajji attano.

Having arranged a magnificent pūjā with all kinds of offerings for the festival of the palace, he offered up his entire kingdom.

139.

139.

Bodhisattañca kāretvā, rājānaṃ sumanoharaṃ;

Saṇṭhapitthasilā meghe, cāruṃ bhikkhūnupassaye.

He also had a delightful image of the Bodhisatta king made and placed it in a beautiful monastery on the Silāmegha rock.

140.

140.

Thūpārāmamhi thupassa, kāsi sovaṇṇakañcukaṃ;

Paṭṭaṃ katvā vicitatthaṃ, rajataṃ antarantarā.

He made a golden casing for the thūpa at the Thūpārāma, fashioning a variegated band with silver inlaid.

141.

141.

Tasmiṃyeva ca pāsādaṃ, parijiṇṇaṃ sakārayi;

Abhidhammaṃ kathāpesi, kārāpetvā mahāmahaṃ.

In that same monastery, he had the dilapidated palace repaired, and arranging a great festival, he had the Abhidhamma recited there.

142.

142.

Mahātherena satimā, hemasālinivāsinā;

Tattha pokkharaṇiñcassa, paribhogāya kārayi.

The mindful king had a pond made there for the use of the Mahāthera who dwelt in Hemasāli.

143.

143.

Jiṇṇe [M 0.0306] devakūle katvā, bahuke tattha tattha so;

Devānaṃ paṭimāyo ca, kārayittha mahārahā.

He repaired many dilapidated shrines of the gods in various places and also had valuable images of the gods made.

144.

144.

Brāhmaṇānañca datvāna, paccagghaṃ rājabhojanaṃ;

Pāyesi khīraṃ sovaṇṇa-taṭṭakehi sasakkharaṃ.

He gave costly royal food to the brahmins and had them drink milk with sugar from golden bowls.

145.

145.

Usabhe paṅgulānañca, jīvikañca sadāpayī;

Damiḷānantu pādāsi, asse goṇe agaṇhataṃ.

He always provided a livelihood for the blind and the crippled. To the Tamils from whom he did not take them, he gave horses and oxen.

146.

146.

Anāthā ye salajjā ca, te ca saṅgaṇhi so raho;

Asaṃgahito dīpamhi, natthi tena yathārahaṃ.

He secretly supported those who were destitute and conscientious, so that there was no one on the island who was not supported by him as was proper.

147.

147.

Dātabboti kathaṃ gunna-mahāro so vicintiya;

Sasse khīragate’dāsi, tesaṃ khettasahassake.

He, who was great in virtue, considering 'What should be given?', gave to them a thousand fields when the crop was in its milky stage.

148.

148.

Kāḷavāpimhi so vāri-sampātaṃ kārayi thiraṃ;

Puññamevaṃ vidhaṃ tassa, appameyyaṃ bahuṃ kira.

At Kāḷavāpi, he had a permanent water channel constructed; his merit of this kind, it is said, was immeasurable and abundant.

149.

149.

Tassa putto tadā āsi, yuvarājā divaṅgato;

Jāto senāpati kāle, aparo atthi dārako.

At that time his son, the crown prince, had passed away. Later a general was born; there was another boy.

150.

150.

Taṃ rājā rājaputtehi, bhīto rājāraho iti;

Māretuṃ taṃ na sakkonti, vaḍḍhapesi yathā tathā.

The king, fearing him on account of the princes and thinking, 'He is worthy of kingship,' was unable to have him killed, so he had him raised in one way or another.

151.

151.

Arīhi nagare ruddhe, pitaraṃ so kirekadā;

Upasaṅkamma yācittha, saṅgamāvacaraṃ gajaṃ.

It is said that once, when the city was besieged by enemies, he approached his father and requested an elephant fit for battle.

152.

152.

So dāpesi mahānāgaṃ, ghoraṃ mārakarūpamaṃ;

Katahatthaṃ balañceva, sabbāyudha visāradaṃ.

He had a great elephant given to him, a fierce one like a form of Māra, skilled and strong, and an expert in all weapons.

153.

153.

Kāloyamīti mantvā so, bandhitvā churikaṃ tadā;

Kuñjaraṃ varamāruyha, nikkhamma nagarā bahi.

Thinking, 'This is the time,' he then fastened on his dagger, mounted the excellent elephant, and went forth out of the city.

154.

154.

Viddhaṃsetvā balaṃ sabbaṃ, dujjayaṃ jayamaggahī;

Rājā disvā pasanno taṃ, senāpaccañca tassa’dā.

Having shattered the entire army, he seized a victory that was hard to win. The king, seeing this and being pleased with him, gave him the rank of general.

155.

155.

Esova kira gantvāna, sabalo desamuttaraṃ;

Palāpesi sasenaṃ taṃ, ādipādañca dappulaṃ.

It is said that this very one, having gone with his army to the northern region, put to flight Ādipāda Dappula along with his army.

156.

156.

Baddhavero tato’hosi, dappuḷo tamhi sādhukaṃ;

Mahāummārayuddhamhi, disvā tamatīkodhavā.

Then Dappula became firmly hostile towards him; seeing him in the great Ummāra battle, he became exceedingly angry.

157.

157.

Sīghaṃ pesesi taṃ hantuṃ, hatthimāruḷhamattanā;

Ovijjhiya palāpesi, tamesa sakadantīnā.

He swiftly sent one mounted on a maddened elephant to kill him. But this one, having attacked with his own tusker, put him to flight.

158.

158.

Disvā [M 0.0307] tamatisantuṭṭho, aññesañca abhāvato;

Rajjayoge adā tassa, uparājattamattano.

Seeing him and being very pleased, and also because there were no others, the king gave him a share in the kingdom: his own rank of viceroy.

159.

159.

Evaṃ vīsati vassāni, dīpametaṃ subhuñjiya;

Vipākaṃ puññakammassa, bhuñjituñca divaṅgato.

Thus, having ruled this island well for twenty years, he passed away to enjoy the fruit of his meritorious deeds.

160.

160.

Evaṃ anekehi nayehi thaddhā;

Janassa dukkhehi virūpakehi;

Bhogā vinassanti khaṇe na sabbe;

Aho tahiṃyeva ramanti bālā.

Thus in many ways, through the manifold sufferings of people, possessions perish in a moment, though not all. Alas, it is in these very things that stubborn fools delight!

Sujanappasādasaṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Mahāvaṃsa, composed for the faith and spiritual urgency of good people.

Cha rājako nāma

The Chapter named 'The Six Kings'.

Chacattālīsatimo paricchedo.

The Forty-sixth Chapter.

Sattacattālīsatima pariccheda

The Forty-seventh Chapter.

Pañcarājako

The Five Kings

1.

1.

Accaye [M 0.0307] pituno rājā, uparājā ahosi so;

Samattho sakkumittānaṃ, kātuṃ niggaha saṃgahe.

Upon the death of his father, that viceroy became king. He was capable of suppressing his enemies and supporting his friends.

2.

2.

Senā nāmasi sappaññā, mahesī tassa rājino;

Khuddaputtā pīyā’tīva, rañño kalyāṇadassanā.

The chief queen of that king was named Senā, and she was wise. The young sons were exceedingly dear to the king and of beautiful appearance.

3.

3.

Adāsi yuvarājattaṃ, jeṭṭhaputtassa attano;

Ādipāde’parekāsi, rājinīpi ca dhītaro.

He gave the rank of viceroy to his own eldest son. He made the other sons Ādipādas, and also honored the queen and his daughters.

4.

4.

Datvā ṭhānantaraṃ rājā, tesaṃ tesaṃ yathārahaṃ;

Janaṃ saṅgahavatthūhi, saṅgahesi catūhipi.

Having given ranks to each of them according to their worth, the king supported the people with the four bases of sympathy.

5.

5.

Atha kenāpi so gantvā, hetunā maṇihīrakaṃ;

Vasanto kira assosi, paccanto kupito iti.

Then, having gone to Maṇihīra for some reason, while he was staying there, it is said, he heard that the border region was in revolt.

6.

6.

Tato senāpatiñceva, jeṭṭhaputtañca attano;

Gantvā sādhetha taṃ desa-mīti pesesi sajjukaṃ.

Then he at once sent the general and his own eldest son, saying, 'Go and subdue that region.'

7.

7.

Tesu tatthopayātesu, pisunā bhedacintakā;

Vatvā yaṃkiñci bhindiṃsu, te ubhopi narādhipe.

When they had gone there, slanderers intent on causing division said whatever they could and created a rift between those two leaders.

8.

8.

Tato [M 0.0308] dve verino hutvā, desaṃ gaṇhitumārabhuṃ;

Rājā sutvā khaṇeneva, duratissa mupāgami.

Then the two became enemies and began to seize the country. The king, hearing of this, went to Duratissa at that very moment.

9.

9.

Te ubho tattha ghātetvā, tesaṃ sabbaṃ samādiya;

Hantvā taṃ pakkhiye sabbe, puḷatthinagaraṃ gami.

Having slain them both there, seized all their possessions, and killed all their partisans, he went to the city of Pulatthinagara.

10.

10.

Tadā rohaṇadesamhi, bhogādhipatino suto;

Dāṭhāsivādipādassa, mahindo nāma khattiyo.

At that time in the country of Rohaṇa, there was a khattiya named Mahinda, the son of Ādipāda Dāṭhāsiva, the lord of Bhoga.

11.

11.

Pituno so’parijjhitvā, rañño santikamāgamā;

Disvā rājāpi santuṭṭho, taṃ saṅgaṇhi yathārahaṃ.

Being dissatisfied with his father, he came into the king’s presence. The king, seeing him, was pleased and received him as was fitting.

12.

12.

Tena mettiṃ thiraṃ kātuṃ, dhītaraṃ deva nāmikaṃ;

Tassa datvāna pāhesi, balaṃ rohaṇamevaso.

To make a firm friendship with him, the king gave him his daughter named Devā and, providing him with an army, sent him to Rohaṇa.

13.

13.

So gantvā rājasenāya, maddāpetvāna rohaṇaṃ;

Jambudīpaṃ palāpetvā, pitaraṃ rohaṇaṃ labhi.

He went with the royal army and crushed Rohaṇa. Having made his father flee to Jambudīpa, he took possession of Rohaṇa.

14.

14.

Mahāvihāre kāresi, salākaggaṃ thiraṃ subhaṃ;

Kholakkhiyamunindassa, parihārāya dāpayi.

He had a firm and beautiful ticket-hall built in the Mahāvihāra and had it given for the use of the Sage of Kholakkhiya.

15.

15.

Mahānāmavhayaṃ gāmaṃ, pūjayitvā yathābalaṃ;

Vaḍḍhamānadumindassa, jiṇṇaṃ gehañca kāriya.

Having honored the village called Mahānāma according to his ability, he also had the dilapidated shrine of the Vaḍḍhamāna tree-spirit rebuilt.

16.

16.

Rukkhaṇatthāya tassā;dā, koṭṭhāgāmaṃ bahudayaṃ;

Nīlārāmassa pādāsi, kāḷussaṃ nāma gāmakaṃ.

For its maintenance, he gave a prosperous granary-village. To the Nīlārāma he gave the village named Kāḷussa.

17.

17.

Loharūpassa pādāsi, ārāmassa ca gāmakaṃ;

Jiṇṇañca paṭisaṅkhāsi, paṭimāyo ca kārayi.

He gave a village to the Loharūpa monastery. He also restored what was dilapidated and had images made.

18.

18.

Pāsāde cetiyo ceva, vihāre ca anappake;

Puḷatthinagare’kāsi, vejjasālaṃ mahādayo.

The very compassionate one built palaces, shrines, and many monasteries, as well as a hospital, in the city of Pulatthinagara.

19.

19.

Tathā paṇḍā viyañceva, bhogagāmasamāyutaṃ;

Piṭṭhasappinamandhānaṃ, sālāyo ca tahiṃ tahiṃ.

Likewise, he built halls here and there for the sick, the crippled, and the blind, endowing them with revenue-villages.

20.

20.

Potthakesu likhāpetvā, aṭṭe sammā vinicchite;

Rājagehe ṭhapāpesi, ukkoṭanabhayena so.

He had the correctly determined meanings written in books and had them placed in the royal palace out of fear of corruption.

21.

21.

Nāgavaḍḍhananāmassa, bhogagāme bahū adā;

Lekhe’pubbe na vāretvā, pāletvā pubbasāsanaṃ.

He gave many revenue-villages to the one named Nāgavaḍḍhana. Without preventing new inscriptions, he maintained the ancient edicts.

22.

22.

Pitarā [M 0.0309] ca mahādānaṃ, puññamaññampi vā kataṃ;

Sabbaṃ tamavināsetvā, niccaṃ so rakkhi sādaro.

Whatever great gift or other meritorious deed was done by his father, he, being ever respectful, protected it all without destroying it.

23.

23.

Mahesī ca mahārañño, puññāni bahukārayi;

Kaṇṭakaṃ cetiyaṃ kāsi, devī cetiyapabbate.

The chief queen of the great king also had many meritorious deeds performed; the queen had the Kaṇṭaka Cetiya built on the Cetiyapabbata.

24.

24.

Kāretvā jayasenañca, pabbataṃ gāmikassadā;

Bhikkhusaṅghassa sā gāmaṃ, mahummārañca tassa dā.

Having had the Jayasena mountain monastery built, she gave it to the Gāmikas. To the Sangha of bhikkhus there, she also gave the village of Mahummāra.

25.

25.

Silāmeghavhayaṃ katvā, bhikkhunīnamupassayaṃ;

Silāmeghavhaye dāsi, bhikkhunīnañca paccaye.

Having built a residence for nuns called Silāmegha, she gave requisites to the nuns in that Silāmegha residence.

26.

26.

Gāmāye’suṃ purākītā, vihāro tattha sādhanaṃ;

Datvā te me cayitvāna, vihārasseva dāpayi.

There were villages formerly purchased for the support of the monastery there. Having consolidated these, she had them given over to the monastery itself.

27.

27.

Chādayitvā mahārukkhe, sabbe cetiyapabbate;

Nānārāge dhaje ceva, paṭākāyo ca pūjayi.

Having covered all the great trees on Cetiyapabbata, she paid homage with banners of various colors and with streamers.

28.

28.

Pubbārāmakabhāgampi, pāsādaṃ paṭisaṅkhari;

Ussānaviṭṭhiṃ dubbhogaṃ, subhogaṃ tassa kārayi.

She also restored the mansion in the Pubbārāma section. She had the Ussānaviṭṭhi, which was difficult to enjoy, made comfortable for him.

29.

29.

Vihāraṃ giribhaṇḍañca, naṭṭhaṃ pākatikaṃ kari;

Bhogagāme ca dāpesi, bhikkhūnaṃ tannivāsinaṃ.

He restored the ruined Giribhaṇḍa monastery to its original condition, and he had revenue villages given to the bhikkhus dwelling there.

30.

30.

Ambuyyānamhi āvāsaṃ, katvā dappuḷapabbataṃ;

Bhikkhūnaṃ tisatassā’dā, sampannacatupaccayaṃ.

Having built the residence named Dappuḷapabbata in the Ambuyyāna park, he gave the four requisites in abundance to three hundred bhikkhus.

31.

31.

Kāretvā nīlagallañca, ārāmaṃ so manoramaṃ;

Dakavāraṃ bahuppādaṃ, tassa dāpesi kāriya.

Having had the delightful Nīlagalla monastery built, he had a highly productive water channel constructed for it.

32.

32.

Arikāri vihāre ca, paṭisaṅkhāsi jiṇṇakaṃ;

Salākaggañca pāsādaṃ, apubbaṃyeva kārayi.

In the Arikāri monastery, he restored what was dilapidated, and he had a ticket-distribution mansion built, a structure like none before.

33.

33.

Vāhadīpe sakāresi, senaggabodhipabbataṃ;

Dhammaṃ tīsu nikāyesu, vācayittha bahussute.

On Vāha island, he had the Senaggabodhipabbata monastery built, and he had the Dhamma of the three Nikāyas recited by the very learned.

34.

34.

Gaṇhāpesi ca bhikkhūnaṃ, ayopattesu gaṇṭhike;

Puññanti vuttaṃ sabbaṃ so, na kiñci parivajjayi.

He had the bhikkhus' iron bowls fitted with rings; he omitted nothing of all that was said to be meritorious.

35.

35.

Kulīnānamanāthānaṃ, itthīnaṃ’dā piḷandhanaṃ;

Bhojanaṃ bhojanatthīnaṃ, bahu so dāsi rattiyaṃ.

To high-born women who were helpless, he gave adornments; and to those in need of food, he gave much food at night.

36.

36.

Gunnaṃ sassāni pādāsi, kākādīnañca bhattakaṃ;

Taṇḍulañca kumārānaṃ, madhuphāṇitasaṃyuttaṃ.

He gave grain to cattle and food to crows and other such creatures; and to children he gave rice mixed with honey and molasses.

37.

37.

Evaṃ [M 0.0310] puññāni katvāna, narindo so sapāriso;

Bhutvā pañcasu vassesu, mediniṃ sampariccaji.

Having thus performed meritorious deeds, that king with his retinue, after having enjoyed the earth for five years, passed away.

38.

38.

Tato tassa suto āsi, sīhaḷānaṃ rathesato;

Sabbarūpaguṇopeto, mahindo nāma khattiyo.

Then his son was the khattiya named Mahinda, a leader among the Sinhalese, endowed with all the qualities of beauty.

39.

39.

So dhammikasīlāmegho, iccāsi dharaṇītale;

Dhammadīpo dhammadhajo, suddhadhammaparāyano.

He was a rain-cloud of righteousness and virtue upon the earth, a lamp of the Dhamma, a banner of the Dhamma, one devoted to the pure Dhamma.

40.

40.

Pubbakehi narindehi, kataṃ dhammapathānugaṃ;

Sabbaṃ kāsi ahāpetvā, adhammaṃ tu vivajjayi.

He carried on all that was done by former kings in accordance with the path of Dhamma, without omitting anything, and he avoided all that was unrighteous.

41.

41.

Rājāratanapāsāde, kātuṃ so navakammakaṃ;

Sabbakālesu dāpesi, geṭṭhumbadakavārakaṃ.

To perform new work on the Ratanapāsāda, he gave the Geṭṭhumba water channel in perpetuity.

42.

42.

Jiṇṇañca paṭisaṅkhāsi, puññakammamakāsi ca;

Rajjaṃ katvāna catūsu, vassesu nidhanaṃ gato.

He restored what was dilapidated and performed meritorious deeds. Having reigned for four years, he passed away.

43.

43.

Aggabodhi tato rājā, chattaṃ ussāpayi pure;

Kārento sabbasattānaṃ, hitaṃ sukhamasesato.

Then King Aggabodhi raised the parasol in the city, working for the welfare and happiness of all beings without exception.

44.

44.

Dhātupūjaṃ sakāresi, satthusabbaguṇārahaṃ;

Pitāmahakatassā’pi, sambuddhassa mahāmahaṃ.

He held a great festival for the Sambuddha, a relic veneration worthy of all the Teacher's qualities, like that performed by his grandfather.

45.

45.

Udayaggādibodhiñca, pariveṇaṃ sakārayi;

Nāmaṃ gahetvā pituno, attano ca narādhipo.

The lord of men had the Udayaggabodhi Pariveṇa built, taking the name from his father and from himself.

46.

46.

Sabhogaṃ pariveṇañca, katvā taṃ bhūtanāmakaṃ;

Sakācariyakassā’dā, bhikkhūnaṃ tisatassa ca.

Having built that pariveṇa named Bhūta, he gave it, together with its revenues, to his own teacher and to three hundred bhikkhus.

47.

47.

Rājasālāya dāpesi, cūḷavāpiyagāmakaṃ;

Gāmadvayañca dāpesi, kāḷūlamallavātake.

He had the village of Cūḷavāpiya given to the Rājasālā, and he also had the two villages of Kāḷūla and Mallavātaka given.

48.

48.

Pavesaṃ vinivāresi, uposathadinesu so;

Macchamaṃsasurādīnaṃ, antonagaramattano.

On Uposatha days, he prohibited the entry of fish, meat, liquor, and the like into his own city.

49.

49.

Bhikkhū vā cetiye vā so, vanditvā nikkhamaṃ tato;

Vālukā hā vinassantu, iti pādesu vodhayī.

After paying homage to the bhikkhus or a cetiya, as he was departing, he would cleanse his feet, saying: 'May the grains of sand perish!'

50.

50.

Yaṃ yaṃ sovaggiyaṃ kammaṃ, kammaṃ nissaraṇavahaṃ;

Vatthuttaye pasanno so, kammaṃ taṃ sabbamācari.

Whatever deed leads to a heavenly birth and whatever deed brings about release, he, with confidence in the Triple Gem, performed them all.

51.

51.

Mātupaṭṭhānanirato, rattindivamahosiso;

Gantvā tassā upaṭṭhānaṃ, pātova kira bhūpati.

He was devoted to attending on his mother day and night. Indeed, the king would go to wait upon her at the very break of dawn.

52.

52.

Sīsaṃ [M 0.0311] telena makkhetvā, ubbaṭṭetvāna jallikaṃ;

Nakhe visuddhe katvāna, nahāpetvāna sādaraṃ.

He would anoint her head with oil, rub away the grime, make her nails clean, and bathe her with reverence.

53.

53.

Acchādetvā navaṃ vatthaṃ, sukhasamphassamattano;

Vatthaṃ chaḍḍitamādāya, pelletvā sayameva taṃ.

Having dressed her in a new garment of his own that was pleasant to the touch, he would take her discarded cloth and wash it himself.

54.

54.

Tassa toyena siñcitvā, sīsaṃ samakuṭaṃ sakaṃ;

Gandhamālāhi taṃ sammā, cetiyaṃ viha pūjiya.

Having sprinkled his own crowned head with the water from that washing, he then duly honored that cloth with perfumes and garlands as if it were a cetiya.

55.

55.

Namassitvāna tikkhattuṃ, katvā taṃ so padakkhiṇaṃ;

Dāpetvā parisāya’ssā, vatthādīni yathāruciṃ.

Having bowed to her three times and circumambulated her, he had robes and other requisites given to her retinue according to their wishes.

56.

56.

Sahattheneva bhojetvā, bhojanaṃ taṃ mahārahaṃ;

Bhutthāvasesaṃ bhuñjitvā, samākiriyamatthake.

Having fed her excellent food with his own hand, and having eaten the leftovers, he then scattered some on his head.

57.

57.

Bhojetvā parisaṃ tassā, rājabhojanamuttamaṃ;

Sajjetvā vāsagehañca, sugandhaparivāsitaṃ.

Having fed her retinue with the finest royal food, he prepared her dwelling, perfuming it with sweet scents.

58.

58.

Sahatthā paññapetvāna, sayanaṃ tattha sādhukaṃ;

Pāde dhoviya makkhetvā, gandhatelena saṇhakaṃ.

With his own hands he prepared a fine bed there, washed her feet, and anointed them gently with fragrant oil.

59.

59.

Sambāhento nisīditvā, katvā niddamupetakaṃ;

Katvā padakkhiṇaṃ mañcaṃ, tikkhattuṃ sādhuvandiya.

Sitting down, he massaged her until she fell asleep. Then, having circumambulated the bed and paid homage three times, he would leave.

60.

60.

Ārakkhake niyojetvā, dāsekammakarepi ca;

Tassā piṭṭhimakatvāna, apakkameva piṭṭhito.

Having appointed guards, servants, and attendants, he would depart by walking backwards, without turning his back to her.

61.

61.

Ṭhatvā adassane ṭhāne, tikkhattuṃ puna vandiya;

Santuṭṭho tena kammena, saranto taṃ punappunaṃ.

Standing in a place where he could not be seen, he paid homage again three times. Content with that deed, he recalled it again and again.

62.

62.

Gehaṃ yāti sajīvantaṃ, evameva upaṭṭhahi;

Ekadā dāsavādena, vanditvā dāsamattano.

While she was alive, he would go home and attend on her in this way. Once, with the words of a slave, he paid homage to her as if he were his own slave.

63.

63.

Tenattano kathāpesi, khamāpetuṃ sayaṃ vaco;

Attānaṃ bhikkhusaṅghassa, dāpayitvāna mātarā.

He himself uttered words to ask for forgiveness, and he had his mother give him to the Sangha of bhikkhus.

64.

64.

Dhanamatthagghanaṃ ñatvā, bhujisso āsi buddhimā;

Evaṃ puññaparo hutvā, katvā dīpassa saṅgahaṃ.

Knowing that wealth is of little worth, the wise one became a freeman. Thus, devoted to merit, he made provision for a lamp.

65.

65.

Ekādasahi vassehi, devalokamupāgami;

Tassānujo dappuḷo’tha, rājā hosi tadaccaye.

After eleven years, he went to the world of the devas. Then, on his passing, his younger brother Dappuḷa became king.

66.

66.

Sabbaṃ pubbakarājūnaṃ, cariyaṃ so samācari;

Tadā mahindanāmassa, puttārohaṇasāmino.

He followed all the conduct of the previous kings. At that time, the sons of Mahinda, the lord of Rohaṇa,

67.

67.

Pitarā [M 0.0312] nihaṭā’gañchuṃ, rājānaṃ mātulaṃ sakaṃ;

So te disvā pavattiṃ taṃ, sutvā datvā mahābalaṃ.

expelled by their father, came to their maternal uncle, the king. He, seeing them and hearing their story, gave them a great army

68.

68.

Pāhesi pitarā yuddhaṃ, kātuṃ bandhu hite rate;

Mahindopi tathābhāvaṃ, viditvā rohaṇādhipo.

and, delighting in the welfare of his kinsmen, sent them to do battle with their father. Mahinda, the lord of Rohaṇa, also knowing that state of affairs,

69.

69.

Yuddhaṃ paṭipadeyeva, tesaṃ’kāsi mahābalo;

Te ubhopi palāyiṃsu, datvā senāya nāyakaṃ.

the mighty one, immediately gave them battle. Both of them fled, having handed over the command of the army.

70.

70.

Punāgantvā mahīpālaṃ, sevamānā idhā’vasuṃ;

Pitāpi tena santuṭṭho, aññena sakabandhunā.

Having returned again to the king, they dwelt there serving him. Their father, too, was pleased with that other kinsman of his.

71.

71.

Yujjhanto maraṇaṃ gañchi, ñātisopi mato kira;

Tadā’dā bhāgineyyassa, rājā kittaggabodhino.

While fighting, he went to his death, and it is said his kinsman also died. Then the king gave Rohaṇa to his nephew, Kittaggabodhi,

72.

72.

Sabbarūpaguṇopetaṃ, dhitaraṃ deva nāmikaṃ;

So dappuḷaṃ ṭhapetvāna, sevatthaṃ tassa rājino.

along with his daughter named Devā, endowed with all beauty and virtue. He, Kittaggabodhi, left Dappuḷa in the service of that king.

73.

73.

Sayaṃ senaṅgamādāya, rohaṇaṃ samupāgami;

Rohaṇādhipati hutvā, sabbākārasamappito.

Taking his army himself, he went to Rohaṇa. Having become the lord of Rohaṇa, he was endowed in every way.

74.

74.

Puttadhītāhi vaḍḍhento, vāsaṃ tattheva kappayi;

Rājākāsi dumindassa, gharaṃ jiṇṇaṃ navaṃ thiraṃ.

Prospering with sons and daughters, he made his dwelling right there. The king made a new and firm house for Duminda, as the old one was dilapidated.

75.

75.

Sovaṇṇakhacitaṃ kammaṃ, maṅgalena ca tassa so;

Attano rājabhāvassa, satthupāramitāya ca.

For that work inlaid with gold, he held a festival, making it worthy of his own royal state and for the perfection of the Teacher.

76.

76.

Sammānucchavikaṃ katvā, mahāpūjaṃ pavattayi;

Jiṇṇaṃ kāresi pāsādaṃ, hatthikucchivihārake.

Making it worthy of honor, he initiated a great pūjā. He had the dilapidated mansion in the Hatthikucchi-vihāra repaired.

77.

77.

Vāhadīpassa ārāmaṃ, lāvarāvañca pabbataṃ;

Vihāre jetanāme ca, katvā sovaṇṇayaṃ muniṃ.

At the Vāhadīpa monastery, on Mount Lāvarāva, and in the vihāra named Jeta, he made a golden image of the Sage.

78.

78.

Vaḍḍhetvā bodhigehamhi, pūjaṃkāsi acintiyaṃ;

Anusaṃvaccharaṃ dīpe, vatthadānaṃ pavattayi.

Having enhanced the Bodhi-tree shrine, he made an inconceivable pūjā. Annually, he instituted the giving of cloth throughout the island.

79.

79.

Mahāpāḷiñca vaḍḍhesi, bhattaggamavalokayī;

Tulābhārañca dāpesi, jiṇṇañca paṭisaṅkhari.

He augmented the Mahāpāli alms hall and supervised the distribution of food. He gave the 'weighing of the body' donation and restored whatever was dilapidated.

80.

80.

Cārittaṃ pubbarājūnaṃ, pālesi manavajjiyaṃ;

Tassā’si vajiro nāma, senāpati mahāpati.

He maintained the blameless conduct of the former kings. He had a general named Vajira, a great lord.

81.

81.

Kacchavālaṃ sakāresi, ārāmaṃ paṃsukūlinaṃ;

Thūpārāmamhi thūpassa, gharaṃ chādesi sādhukaṃ.

He had the Kacchavāla monastery built for the Pāṃsukūlika bhikkhus. At the Thūpārāma, he properly roofed the thūpa-house.

82.

82.

Iṭṭhakāhi [M 0.0313] suvaṇṇāhi, hemadvāre ca kārayi;

Evaṃ soḷasavassāni, katvā rajjaṃ narādhipo.

He had golden doors made with golden bricks. Thus the lord of men, having ruled the kingdom for sixteen years,

83.

83.

Agamā sabbasattānaṃ, gantabbaṃ desameva so;

Tasmiṃ rājini sampatte, devalokaṃ tadā ahu.

went to that very region where all beings must go. When that king had reached the world of the devas,

84.

84.

Aggabodhisanāmo’tha, āṇābheriṃ carāpayi;

Pitā tassa sabhātussa, puttaṃ mahindanāmakaṃ.

then one named Aggabodhi had the drum of command sounded. His father, for the sake of his brother's son named Mahinda,

85.

85.

Rajjatthaṃ sakaputtānaṃ, ādipādaṃ na kārayī;

Ādaraṃ so sabandhūnaṃ, kaniṭṭhānampi kātave.

For the sake of the kingdom, he did not make his own sons heir-apparent. He showed regard for all his kinsmen, even the youngest.

86.

86.

Asahanto palāyittha, paratīraṃ samākulo;

Te samāgamanaṃ sutvā, pesayitvā mahābalaṃ.

Unable to endure this, Mahinda fled in agitation to the further shore. The king, hearing of their assembly, sent a great army,

87.

87.

Kāretvā yuddhametehi, sīsaṃ tesaṃ sagaṇhayi;

Nikāyesu vicāretvā, kattabbaṃ sabbameva so.

and having caused a battle to be fought with them, he seized their heads. Having conducted an investigation among the monastic fraternities, he did everything that ought to be done.

88.

88.

Dīpe’pi sakale kāsi, pāpācāranivāraṇaṃ;

Bhikkhū cūḷavihāresu, yāguṃ gaṇhanti sabbadā.

He effected the prevention of evil conduct in the entire island. The bhikkhus in the lesser vihāras always received rice-gruel.

89.

89.

Mahāvihāre taṃ sutvā, rājā nibbinnamānaso;

Kaṇṭhapiṭṭhimahāgāmaṃ tathā yābālagāmakaṃ.

Hearing that this was not so at the Mahāvihāra, the king was disheartened. The great village of Kaṇṭhapiṭṭhi and likewise the village of Yābālaka,

90.

90.

Telagāmaṃ bahudañca, dakavāraṃ padāpiya;

Yāguṃ gahetuṃ yojesi, vihāresu’pi bhikkhavo.

the village of Telagāma, and Bahuda he gave, along with a water-share, and arranged for the bhikkhus in those vihāras also to receive rice-gruel.

91.

91.

Tato paṭṭhāya taṃ yāguṃ, sabbe gaṇhiṃsu sādarā;

Dīpe bheriṃca rāpetvā, sannipātiya yācake.

From then on, all received that rice-gruel respectfully. And having had a drum beaten on the island and having assembled the beggars,

92.

92.

Suvaṇṇaṃ sopadāpesi, yathicchaṃ divasattayaṃ;

Evamādiṃ sa katvāna, puññavaṃ vassehi tīhi ca.

he had gold given to them according to their wish for three days. Having done these and other meritorious deeds, he, the meritorious one, reigned for three years.

93.

93.

Vatthuttayapasādassa, phalaṃ passitumattano;

Rājā dibbena yānena, gacchanto viya so mari.

That king died as if he were traveling in a celestial vehicle to see for himself the fruit of his faith in the Triple Gem.

94.

94.

Evaṃ aniccā vata sabbadehino;

Sabbaññūnopeva mupeti maccuṃ;

Pahāya tasmā bhavarāgajātaṃ;

Budho subuddhivibhave bhaveyya.

Alas, so impermanent are all embodied beings; even the Omniscient One himself is subject to death. Therefore, having abandoned what is born of craving for existence, the wise one should delight in non-becoming through good wisdom.

Sujanappasādasaṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Mahāvaṃsa, made for the serene joy and spiritual emotion of good people.

Pañcarājako nāma

The Chapter Named the Five Kings

Sattacattālīsatimo paricchedo.

The Forty-Seventh Chapter.

Aṭṭhacattālīsatima pariccheda

The Forty-Eighth Chapter

Ekarājako

The Sole Ruler

1.

1.

Tato [M 0.0314] tassā’nujo seno, chattaṃ ussāpayī pure;

Piyaṃ’va puttaṃ passanto, satte sabbe mahādhano.

Then his younger brother Sena raised the parasol in the city. Greatly wealthy, he looked upon all beings as upon a dear son.

2.

2.

Cariyaṃ pubbarājūnaṃ, samācari yathābhataṃ;

Apubbampi ca vattesi, cariyaṃ dhammasaṃhitaṃ.

He practiced the conduct of former kings as it had been handed down, and he also initiated a new practice consistent with the Dhamma.

3.

3.

Bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhūnīnañca, ñātīnaṃ dīpavāsinaṃ;

Macchānaṃ migapakkhīnaṃ, kattabbaṃ sa samācari.

For the bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs, for his relatives and the inhabitants of the island, for the fish, beasts, and birds, he did what ought to be done.

4.

4.

Mahindaṃ paratīraṃ so, gataṃ yojiyamārayi;

Evaṃ so suvisodhesi, rajjapaccatthike’khile.

He had Mahinda, who had gone to the other shore to prepare for war, slain. Thus he thoroughly eliminated all the enemies of the kingdom.

5.

5.

Mahādānaṃ pavattesi, yācakānaṃ dhanesinaṃ;

Bhikkhūnaṃ brāhmaṇānañca, manuññaṃ rājabhojanaṃ.

He instituted a great donation for supplicants and seekers of wealth, and provided a delightful royal meal for bhikkhus and brahmins.

6.

6.

Ahesuṃ anujātassa, mahindo kassapo tathā;

Udayoti tayo tesu, mahindo yuvarājako.

He had three sons: Mahinda, Kassapa, and Udaya. Of these, Mahinda was the heir-apparent.

7.

7.

Hutvā tassānuvattanto, sakkaccaṃ tamupaṭṭhahi;

Saṅghānāmāsi rājassa, bhariyā tassa rājinī.

The king's wife, his queen, was named Saṅghā. He became her attendant and waited on her respectfully.

8.

8.

Kīḷanatthaṃ samuddassa, gate rājini paṭṭanaṃ;

Udayo ādipādoso, ohīno nagare tadā.

When the queen went to the seaport for recreation, the Ādipāda Udaya was then left behind in the city.

9.

9.

Nālanāmaṃ gahetvāna, dhītaraṃ māṇilāniyā;

Rakkhitaṃ rājarakkhāya, puḷatthinagaraṃ agā.

Taking with him the girl named Nālā, the daughter of Māṇila, who was under the protection of the royal guard, he went to the city of Puḷatthinagara.

10.

10.

Rājā tasmiṃ akujjhitvā, sandhiṃ katvā akuppiyaṃ;

Mahādīpādaṃ pesetvā, tosatvā taṃ idhānayi.

The king, not being angry with him, made an unshakeable pact. He sent the Mahādipāda, who satisfied him and had him brought back here.

11.

11.

Evaṃ samaggā te āsuṃ, tato paṭṭhāya khattiyā;

Rakkhantā sāsanaṃ lokaṃ, vasiṃsu susamāhitā.

Thus, from that time onwards, those nobles were united. Protecting the Dispensation and the world, they lived together well composed.

12.

12.

Tato kenaci kālena, paṇḍurājā mahābalo;

Jambudīpā idhā’gamma, dīpa gaṇhitumārabhi.

Then, after some time, the powerful King Paṇḍu came here from Jambudīpa and began to seize the island.

13.

13.

Rājā [M 0.0315] sutvā mahāsenaṃ, pesuyittha tadantikaṃ;

Amaccānaṃ vivādena, thaddhotāro nārādhipo.

The king, hearing of this, sent a large army to that region. But because of a dispute among the ministers, the invading lord of men became obstinate.

14.

14.

Paṇḍurājā vināsento, sabbaṃ taṃ desamuttaraṃ;

Khandhāvāraṃ nivesesi, mahātālitagāmake.

King Paṇḍu, laying waste to that entire northern region, set up his camp in the village of Mahātālitagāma.

15.

15.

Vasantā damiḷā ettha, bahavo ye tahiṃ tahiṃ;

Sabbe taṃ pakkhiyāhesuṃ, tato so balavā ahu.

The many Tamils dwelling here and there all sided with him, and thus he became powerful.

16.

16.

Tattha gantā mahāsenā, rañño yujjhitumārabhi;

Hatthikkhandhagato paṇḍu-rājāpi samupāvisi.

Having gone there, the great army began to fight with the king. King Paṇḍu also entered the fray, mounted on the back of an elephant.

17.

17.

Ahu damiḷasenāsā, passanti sāmino mukhaṃ;

Sampattabalahussāhā, tadatthe cattajīvitā.

The Tamil army, seeing their master's face, was filled with strength and zeal, and had resolved to give up their lives for his sake.

18.

18.

Dīpasenā tu sāmina-mabhāvena nirussukkā;

Yujjhanti paribhinditvā, palāyittha tato tato.

But the island's army, lacking enthusiasm because of their lord's absence, was broken in battle and fled in all directions.

19.

19.

Otaritthamahāsenā, paṇḍurājāssa taṅkhaṇe;

Mārasenāva gacchanti, vicuṇṇenti mahājanaṃ.

Then the great army of King Paṇḍu descended. Advancing like the army of Māra, they crushed the people.

20.

20.

Rājā senāya bhinnattaṃ, sukkā sabbaṃ samādiya;

Hatthasāraṃ puraṃ hitvā, malayābhimukho gato.

The king, hearing that his army was broken, took all his treasures, abandoned the capital with its choice elephants, and headed towards the Malaya region.

21.

21.

Tato hatthiṃ samāruyha, yuvarājā mahindako;

Yujjhanto sakasenāya, palātattaṃ samekkhiya.

Then the heir apparent Mahinda, mounting an elephant and fighting with his own army, saw that they were fleeing in rout.

22.

22.

Ekename na sakkā ve, sabbe etehi mārituṃ;

Etesaṃ na ca nīcānaṃ, hatthesu maraṇaṃ sukhaṃ.

‘It is impossible for me alone to kill all of these men,’ he thought, ‘and death at the hands of these base fellows would not be a good thing.’

23.

23.

Tasmā varaṃ me maraṇaṃ, mayā eveti cintiya;

Hatthikkhandhagatoyeva, chindi so sīsamattano.

Thinking, ‘Therefore, it is better for me to die by my own hand,’ he cut off his own head while still on the back of the elephant.

24.

24.

Taṃ disvā bahavo sīse, tattha chindiṃsu sevakā;

Taṃ disvā damiḷī senā, haṭṭhatuṭṭhā pamodisā.

Seeing this, many of his retainers also cut off their own heads right there. Seeing that, the Tamil army was joyful, glad, and delighted.

25.

25.

Etaṃ sabbaṃ samekkhitvā, ādāpādo sakassapo;

Turaṅgavaramāruyha, susannaddho mahāyudho.

Having witnessed all this, the Ādipāda Kassapa, a great warrior, mounted a choice steed, fully armed and armored.

26.

26.

Vihāramupasaṅkamma, abhayaṃ ekakova so;

Tādisampi mahāsenaṃ, ogāhetvā vidārayi.

Having approached the monastery, he, all alone and fearless, plunged into that great army and tore it apart.

27.

27.

Supaṇṇo viya gaṇhanto, bhūjagena salilāla ye;

So taṃ sabbaṃ nivattesi, attānañca sugopayi.

Like a Supaṇṇa seizing serpents from the water, he drove them all back and protected himself well.

28.

28.

Asso [M 0.0316] ekova dissittha, turaṅgāvalisannibho;

Attano so janaṃ kañci, apassanto’nugāminaṃ.

His single horse appeared like a whole line of steeds. Seeing none of his own people following him,

29.

29.

Kiṃ me ekena verinaṃ, pūritena manorathaṃ;

Kālantarehaṃ jīvanto, pūressaṃ me manorathaṃ.

‘What is the use of fulfilling my heart's desire on just one enemy? If I live, I shall fulfill my desire at another time.’

30.

30.

Tasmā gantuṃva yuttanti, nimphoṭetvā mahābalaṃ;

Nibbhayova mahāyodho, koṇḍivātamupāgami.

Thinking, ‘Therefore it is proper to leave,’ the fearless great warrior, snapping his fingers at the great army, went to Koṇḍivāta.

31.

31.

Paṇḍurājā mahāsenā, aggahesi tato puraṃ;

Sīsaṃ taṃ yuvarājassa, paṇḍurājassa dassayuṃ.

Then King Paṇḍu with his great army seized the city. They showed the head of the heir apparent to King Paṇḍu.

32.

32.

So taṃ disvā ca jhāpetvā, rājūnaṃ paṇḍudesinaṃ;

Sabbamāḷāhane kiccaṃ, tassa kātuṃ niyojayi.

When he saw it, he had it cremated and ordered that all the funeral rites be performed for him, as is done for the kings of the Pāṇḍyan land.

33.

33.

Sabbaṃ sāraṃ harāpesi, bhaṇḍāgāramhi rājino;

Aggaṇhittha gahetabbaṃ, vihāre nagarepi ca.

He had all the treasures carried away from the king's treasury, and he seized whatever could be taken from the monasteries and the city as well.

34.

34.

Pāsāde ratane sabbe, sovaṇṇaṃsatthubimbakaṃ;

Silāmaya munindassa, cakkhubhūka maṇidvayaṃ.

He took all the gems from the palaces, the golden image of the Teacher, and the pair of jewels that formed the eyes of the stone image of the Lord of Sages.

35.

35.

Tathā sovaṇṇapaṭṭe ca, thūpārāmamhi cetiye;

Suvaṇṇa paṭimāyo ca, vihāresu tahiṃ tahiṃ.

Likewise, he took the golden plaques on the cetiya in the Thūpārāma and the golden images from the various monasteries here and there.

36.

36.

Sabbaṃ gahetvā nissāraṃ, laṅkādīpa makāsi so;

Chaḍḍayittha puraṃ ramma, yakkhabhakkhita rūpakaṃ.

Having taken everything of value, he rendered the island of Laṅkā devoid of substance. He abandoned the beautiful city, leaving it like a place devoured by yakkhas.

37.

37.

Rājā’pi rakkhaṃ datvāna, mahāmagge tahiṃ tahiṃ;

Gaṅgādvaya mukhe vāsaṃ, kappesi parisaṅkito.

The king, for his part, posted guards here and there on the main road and took up his residence at the mouth of the two rivers, full of apprehension.

38.

38.

Paṇḍurājā tato saddhiṃ, kātuṃ sīhaḷasāminā;

Amacce tattha pesesi, disvā te sīhalādhipo.

Then King Paṇḍu, in order to make a treaty with the lord of the Sinhalese, sent ministers there. When the ruler of the Sinhalese saw them...

39.

39.

Suṇitvā sāsanaṃ tesaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ sampaṭicchiya;

Dūtānaṃ kārayitvāna, yathākāmena saṅgahaṃ.

Having heard their message and accepted it in full, he had the envoys honored and provided for them according to their wishes.

40.

40.

Hatthidvayaṃ sadatvāna, sabbamābharaṇampi ca;

Tassa pesesi dūteso, attanopi hitāvahe.

He sent to him by those envoys a pair of elephants and all his ornaments, as well as gifts beneficial to himself.

41.

41.

Paṇḍurājā sitaṃ sabbaṃ, disvā santuṭṭhamānaso;

Niyyātetvāna dūtānaṃ, tadaheva mahāpuraṃ.

King Paṇḍu, seeing all the white gifts, was delighted at heart. Having dismissed the envoys, he departed from the great city on that very day.

42.

42.

Nikkhamitvā purā gantvā, na cireneva paṭṭanaṃ;

Tattha āruyha nāvaṃ so, saka desa mupāgami.

Having departed from the city and gone forth, he soon reached the seaport. There he boarded a ship and went to his own country.

43.

43.

Tato [M 0.0317] āgamma nagaraṃ, sīlāmegho mahīpati;

Yathāṭhāne ṭhapetvāna, dīpaṃ vasi samāhito.

Then King Sīlāmegha, lord of the earth, came to the city. Having established everyone in their proper places, he ruled the island, composed.

44.

44.

Bhātaraṃ dutiyaṃ katvā, udayaṃ nāma khattiyaṃ;

Mahādīpādaṃ tassā’dā, sogatthaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ disaṃ.

Having made his brother, the khattiya named Udaya, his viceroy, he conferred on him the title of Mahādipāda and gave him the southern district for his support.

45.

45.

Sopi kho na cireneva, katvā puññaṃ yathārahaṃ;

Rogenekena samphuṭṭho, paviṭṭho maccuno mukhaṃ.

But he too, before long, having performed meritorious deeds as was fitting, was afflicted by a certain disease and entered the mouth of death.

46.

46.

Kassapo ādipādopi, pulatthinagare vasaṃ;

Yojetvā paṇḍurājena, ahosi kira mārito.

It is said that the Ādipāda Kassapa, while residing in Pulatthinagara, was killed through the contrivance of King Paṇḍu.

47.

47.

Tadā kassapanāmassa, puttā āsuṃ mahārahā;

Ādipādassa cattāro, dhaññalakkhaṇa saññutā.

At that time the Ādipāda Kassapa had four sons of great worth, endowed with the marks of fortune.

48.

48.

Yo senaṃ sabbapaṭhamo, seno nāma kumārako;

Sūro vīro mahussāho, rājabhārakkhamo samo.

The eldest, the prince named Sena, was brave, heroic, and of great energy, capable of bearing the burden of the kingdom like the king himself.

49.

49.

Rājā mahādīpādattaṃ, tassa datvā yathāvidhiṃ;

Bhogatthaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ desaṃ, savāhana mupādisi.

The king duly conferred on him the rank of Mahādipāda and assigned to him the southern district, together with its transport, for his maintenance.

50.

50.

Rohaṇādhipatissā’suṃ, puttā kittaggabodhito;

Cattāro dhītaro tisso, dassaneyyā manoramā.

The ruler of Rohaṇa, Kittaggabodhi, had four sons and three daughters, who were beautiful and charming.

51.

51.

Tadā jeṭṭhasutaṃ tassa, mahindaṃ nāma khattiyaṃ;

Pitucchā mārayitvāna, desaṃ gaṇhi sasādhanaṃ.

At that time, his paternal uncle had the eldest son, the khattiya named Mahinda, killed and seized the country with its resources.

52.

52.

Bhātaro te tayo tasmiṃ,

Saṃruṭṭhā bhātu ghātane;

Ādāya bhagīnī tisso,

Rañño santikamāgamuṃ.

His three brothers, angered at the slaying of their brother, took their three sisters and came into the king’s presence.

53.

53.

Rājāpi disvā tetīva, mamāyanto dayāluko;

Sabbe devakumāreva, sukhaṃ vaḍḍhesi pemavā.

The compassionate king, seeing them and feeling great affection, lovingly raised them all in happiness, as if they were divine princes.

54.

54.

Tato kassapanāmaṃ so, tesaṃ jeṭṭhaṃ narissaro;

Desaṃ taṃ gaṇha yāhīti, datvā balamapesayi.

Then the king, the lord of men, gave an army to the eldest of them, who was named Kassapa, and sent him forth, saying: “Go and take that country!”

55.

55.

So’pi gantvāna taṃ hantvā, rohaṇaṃ kasiṇampi taṃ;

Katvā hatthagataṃ tattha, vasittha nirupaddavo.

He went, and having killed him and brought the whole of Rohaṇa under his control, he dwelt there untroubled.

56.

56.

Atha so bhātaro dve’pi, senañca udayaṃ tathā;

Pakkositvāna, bhājetvā, desaṃ tehi sahāvasi.

Then, having summoned his two brothers, Sena and Udaya, he divided the country and dwelt there together with them.

57.

57.

Rājā [M 0.0318] tā sādhu vaḍḍhetvā, vayapattāsu tīsu so;

Rājakaññāsu dhaññāsu, devaccharasū rūpisu.

The king had raised those three fortunate royal maidens well, and when they, who had forms like celestial nymphs, came of age,

58.

58.

Ṭhapetvā rājini ṭhāne, uparājassa dāpayi;

Saṅghanāmaṃ mahābhogaṃ, datvā rajjasarikkhakaṃ.

Having established one in the rank of queen, he gave the one named Saṅghā to the viceroy, bestowing on her great wealth comparable to a kingdom.

59.

59.

Kaṇiṭṭho uparājassa, mahindo nāma bhātuko;

Atthi sabbaguṇopeto, sabbasatthavisārado.

The viceroy had a younger brother named Mahinda, who was endowed with all virtues and skilled in all the arts and sciences.

60.

60.

Tassā’dāsi duve rājā, rājakaññā manoharā;

Tissavhakitta nāmañca, datvā bhogaṃ yathāruciṃ.

To him the king gave two charming royal maidens, named Tissā and Kittā, bestowing wealth according to his pleasure.

61.

61.

Evaṃ karonto ñātīnaṃ, saṃgahaṃ so yathārahaṃ;

Ārādhento ca dānādi-saṅgahehi mahājanaṃ.

Thus providing fitting support for his relatives and winning over the great populace with gifts and other means of hospitality,

62.

62.

Rājā dasayi rājūnaṃ, dhammehi samupāgato;

Samācaranto puññāni, paribhuñjittha mediniṃ.

the king, endowed with the ten royal virtues, ruled the earth while performing meritorious deeds.

63.

63.

Paṃsukūlika bhikkhūnaṃ, katvā’riṭṭhamhi pabbate;

Mahābhogaṃ adārāmaṃ, nimmitaṃ viya iddhiyā.

On Mount Ariṭṭha, he built for the rag-robe-wearing monks a splendid monastery with great endowments, as if created by psychic power.

64.

64.

Parihārañca tassadā, rājārahamasesato;

Ārāmike ca bahavo, dāse kammakarepi ca.

He also granted it all the privileges worthy of a king, and many monastery attendants, slaves, and workers.

65.

65.

Pāsādaṃ sova kāresi, vihāre jetanāmake;

Anekabhūmiṃ bhūmindo, buddhabhūmigatāsayo.

The lord of the earth, whose mind was set on attaining the stage of a Buddha, had a multi-storied mansion built in the monastery named Jetavana.

66.

66.

Vaḍḍhetvā tattha kāretvā, sabba sovaṇṇayaṃ jinaṃ;

Saṇṭhapetvā mahābhogaṃ, vasāpesi ca bhikkhavo.

Having enlarged the monastery, he had an all-gold image of the Conqueror made and installed there. Establishing great endowments, he also settled monks in residence.

67.

67.

Mahādi pariveṇamhi, kāresi sumanoharaṃ;

Pāsāda maggisandaṃḍḍhaṃ, tasmiṃyeva vihārake.

In that very monastery, in the Mahādipāda-pariveṇa, he had a very charming mansion rebuilt that had been destroyed by fire.

68.

68.

Katvā vīraṅkurārāmaṃ, vihāre abhayuttare;

Mahāsaṅghika bhikkhūnaṃ, theriyānañca dāpayi.

Having built the Vīraṅkurārāma in the Abhayuttara-vihāra, he gave it to the monks of the Mahāsaṅghika and Theravāda fraternities.

69.

69.

Pubbārāmañca kāresi, sampanna catupaccayaṃ;

Saddhiṃ so saṅghanāmāya, deviyāpi ca attano.

He also had the Pubbārāma built, endowed with the four requisites, together with his own queen, Saṅghā.

70.

70.

Mahāvihāretāyeva, saddhiṃ kāresi bhūmipo;

Āvāsaṃ saṅghasenavhaṃ, mahābhogaṃ mahāmati.

The wise lord of the earth, together with her, had a residence named Saṅghasena built in the Mahāvihāra, endowing it with great wealth.

71.

71.

Kāretvā sabbasovaṇṇaṃ, kesadhātu karaṇḍakaṃ;

Mahāpūjaṃ pavattesi, rajjaṃ vissajji uttamo.

Having had an all-gold casket made for the hair-relic, the excellent king held a great festival of offerings, at which he offered up his own kingdom.

72.

72.

Cetiyassa [M 0.0319] gīrissādā, kāṇavāpiṃ bahudayaṃ;

Bhikkhūnaṃ dipavāsīnaṃ, dāpesi ca ticīvaraṃ.

He gave the Kāṇavāpi tank, which had a large revenue, to the Cetiyagiri monastery, and he also had the triple robe distributed to the monks dwelling on the island.

73.

73.

Pulatthi nagare kāsi, vāpiyo thusavāpiyā;

Senaggabodhimāvāsaṃ, gāmārāmika saññutaṃ.

In the city of Pulatthinagara he built the Thusavāpi tank and the Senaggabodhi residence, which was connected with a village monastery.

74.

74.

Tasmiṃyeva ca kāresi, mahāpāḷiṃ subhojanaṃ;

Mahāpāḷiñca sabbesaṃ, mahānettampi pabbate.

In that same city, he also established a great alms-hall providing fine food for all, and he also established the Mahānetta on the mountain.

75.

75.

Vejjasālampi kāresi, nagarassa ca pacchime;

Anāthānaṃ pavattesi, yāgudānaṃ sakhajjakaṃ.

He also had a hospital built to the west of the city, and for the destitute he instituted a regular donation of rice-gruel together with solid food.

76.

76.

Paṃsukūlika bhikkhūnaṃ, paccekañca mahānasaṃ;

Katvā dāpesi sakkaccaṃ, niccaṃ bhojanamuttamo.

For the rag-robe-wearing monks, that excellent one established a great kitchen for each and respectfully caused excellent food to be given constantly.

77.

77.

Hutvā mahādipādo’yaṃ, kappūra pariveṇake;

Uttarāḷhe ca kāresi, paricchede sanāmake.

This one, having become the Mahādipāda, had enclosures named after himself built in the Kappūra-pariveṇa and in Uttarāḷha.

78.

78.

Tulābhārañca pādāsī, tikkhattuṃ so mahādhane;

Puññamaññampi so’kāsi, rājā nānappakārakaṃ.

That king gave the 'weighing-offering' with great wealth three times, and he also performed other meritorious deeds of various kinds.

79.

79.

Saṅghanāmāpi sā devī, uttaramhi vihārake;

Katvā mahindasenavhā-vāsaṃ vāsesi bhikkhavo.

That queen named Saṅghā, having built in the northern monastery a dwelling called Mahindasena, caused monks to dwell there.

80.

80.

Āraddho dappulavhassa, kāle rājassa dhīmabho;

Mahādevena so āsi, rammo dappula pabbato.

The delightful Dappula mountain was begun by Mahādeva in the time of the wise king named Dappula.

81.

81.

Dārukassapanāmena, tathā kassaparājikaṃ;

Ubhopi te vippakate, rājā so vasamāpayi.

Dārukassapa by name, and also Kassaparājika, both of them having gone astray, that king brought under his sway.

82.

82.

Bhaddo senāpati tassa, bhaddasenāpati’vhayaṃ;

Pariveṇampi kāresi, dāsabhogasamāyutaṃ.

His general, Bhadda, also had a pariveṇa built named Bhaddasenāpati, endowed with servants and revenues.

83.

83.

Uttaro ca amacco’kā, vihāre abhayuttare;

Vāsamuttarasenavhaṃ, ramma muttarapaccayaṃ.

And the minister Uttara made in the Abhayuttara monastery a dwelling named Uttarasena, delightful and supported by Uttara.

84.

84.

Vajiro nāma tatthevā-vāsaṃ vajirasenakaṃ;

Kāsi rakkhasanāmocā-vāsaṃ rakkhasanāmakaṃ.

One named Vajira made a dwelling there called Vajirasenaka, and one named Rakkhasa made a dwelling called Rakkhasanāmaka.

85.

85.

Tato vīsati vassesu, pulatthi nagare vasaṃ;

Paṇḍurājakataṃ kāraṃ, saranto saradassano.

Then for twenty years, dwelling in the city of Pulatthi, remembering the deed done by the Paṇḍu king, the clear-sighted one,

86.

86.

Dadanto viya senassa, sūrassāvasarañcaso;

Pahāya dīpaṃ dīpo’va, mahāvāta hato gato.

As if giving an opportunity to the hero Sena, he, having abandoned the island, departed like a lamp extinguished by a great wind.

87.

87.

Bhogo [M 0.0320] aniccā saha jīvitena;

Pageva te bandhujanā sahāyā;

Narādhīpaṃ passatha ekameva;

Samāgataṃ maccumukhaṃ sughoraṃ.

Possessions are impermanent, along with life; how much more so are relatives and friends. Behold the lord of men, all alone, come to the very terrible mouth of death.

Sujanappasādasaṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Mahāvaṃsa, composed for the serene joy and spiritual urgency of the good.

Eka rājako nāma

The Single King

Aṭṭhacattālīsatimo paricchedo.

The Forty-Eighth Chapter.

Ekūnapaññāsatima pariccheda

The Forty-Ninth Chapter

Rājadvayadīpano

The Illumination of Two Kings

1.

1.

Evaṃ tasmiṃ mate tassa, kātabbaṃ sādhukāriya;

Mahādīpādo senavho, ādāya balavāhanaṃ.

Thus, when he had died, and the proper rites for him were to be performed, the Mahādipāda named Sena, taking his army and vehicles,

2.

2.

Āgamma nagaraṃ rājā, ahosi dharaṇī tale;

Ādikappamhi rājūnaṃ, dassanto cariyaṃ piya.

Having come to the city, he became king upon the earth, showing the beloved conduct of the kings of the primeval age.

3.

3.

Saddho mahādhano sūro, muttacāgī nirālayo;

Yācayogo mahābhogo, sampannabalavāhano.

He was faithful, of great wealth, heroic, freely generous, and unattached; worthy of requests, of great enjoyment, and endowed with an army and transport.

4.

4.

Kittiyā’malabhūtāya, tathā tejo guṇena ca;

Sannipātaṃva so canda-sūriyānaṃ nidassayi.

By his spotless fame and by his quality of majesty, he displayed, as it were, a conjunction of the moon and sun.

5.

5.

Asaṅkiṇṇa guṇākiṇṇo, suviciṇṇa guṇāguṇo;

Nitthiṇṇapāpo nibbiṇṇa-saṃsāro sāradassano.

Pure and filled with virtues, one who had well-discriminated between good and bad qualities; he had overcome evil, was weary of the round of rebirth, and perceived the essential.

6.

6.

Bhariyā tassa yā āsi, saṅghātaṃ so bhisecayi;

Mahesībhāve datvāna, parihāraṃ yathābhataṃ.

He consecrated Saṅghā, who was his wife, to the rank of chief queen, having given her the appropriate honors.

7.

7.

Mahindaṃ nāma sappaññaṃ, kaṇiṭṭhaṃ bhātaraṃ sakaṃ;

Datvā dakkhiṇabhāgaṃ so, oparajje’bhisecayi.

He consecrated his own younger brother, the wise one named Mahinda, as viceroy, having given him the southern region.

8.

8.

Antepure’parajjhitvā, so raññā avadhārite;

Saputtadāro vuṭṭhāya, aññāto malayaṃ agā.

Having committed an offense in the inner palace and being condemned by the king, he departed with his sons and wife and went, unrecognized, to the Malaya region.

9.

9.

Uppajjittha [M 0.0321] tadā putto, rañño saṅghāya deviyā;

Dassento’va panādassa, kumāra rūpamattano.

Then a son was born to the king by Queen Saṅghā, displaying, as it were, his own princely form.

10.

10.

Rājā taṃ jātamattaṃ’va, disvā santhuṭṭhamānuso;

Siddhatthaṃ lumbinījātaṃ, rājā suddhodano viya.

The king, seeing him just as he was born, was, with a delighted heart, like King Suddhodana seeing Siddhattha born in Lumbinī.

11.

11.

Dhaññapuññaguṇūpeto, ṭhapetvā dīpamekakaṃ;

Jambudīpe’pi kasiṇe, rajjayoggoti me suto.

'Endowed with the qualities of fortune and merit, my son is fit for kingship not only over this single island, but even over the whole of Jambudīpa.'

12.

12.

Nāmadāna dineyeva, parihārena sabbaso;

Oparajje bhisiñcitvā, dakkhiṇaṃ desamassa’dā.

On the very day of the name-giving ceremony, with all due honors, having consecrated him as viceroy, he gave him the southern region.

13.

13.

Yuvarājāpi malaye, vasanto’va mahīpatiṃ;

Ārādhetvā upāyena, anuññato sabhātarā.

The Yuvarāja, while dwelling in the Malaya region, having pleased the king by skillful means, was pardoned along with his kinsmen.

14.

14.

Nikāyattaya vā sīhi, saddhiṃ bhikkhūhi āgato;

Disvā rājānamettheva, sandhīṃ’kāsi akuppiyaṃ.

He came together with monks of the three Nikāyas; having seen the king right there, he made an unshakeable agreement.

15.

15.

Yā tassa yuvarājassa, bhariyā tissā nāmikā;

Rājinī sā vijāyittha, dhītaraṃ saṅghanāmikaṃ.

That wife of the crown prince, named Tissā, that queen gave birth to a daughter named Saṅghā.

16.

16.

Kittināmā’parāyā ca, bhariyā sāpi kho pana;

Vijāyi putte cattāro, tathā ekañca dhītaraṃ.

And his other wife, named Kitti, she too indeed gave birth to four sons and also one daughter.

17.

17.

Tadā rājāpi cintetvā, evaṃ sati kaṇiṭṭhako;

Nissaṅko mayi hotīti, sammā mantīhi mantiya.

Then the king, having consulted properly with his ministers, reflected thus: 'If this is so, the youngest will be without suspicion towards me.'

18.

18.

Dhītaraṃ yuvarājassa, surūpiṃ rūpanāmikaṃ;

Kassapassa’tta puttassa, vivāhaṃ kārayi budho.

The wise one arranged the marriage of the crown prince's beautiful daughter, named Rūpa, for his own son, Kassapa.

19.

19.

Dakkhiṇaṃ desamasseva, kaṇiṭṭhassa sadāpayi;

Rājaputtassa pādāpi, paccekaṃ bhogamattano.

He had the southern region given to the youngest; and to the other princes, he also assigned from his own revenues an individual portion for their support.

20.

20.

Rajjamhi sabbaṃ tasseva, paribhogāya dāpayi;

Kevalantu vicāresi, dīpaṃ dīpa hitāvaho.

He had everything in the kingdom given to him for his use; but he, the benefactor of the island, administered only the island itself.

21.

21.

Tesaṃ saṃvāsamanvāya, ubhinnaṃ puññakamminaṃ;

Dhaññapuññaguṇūpetā, vijātā puttadhītaro.

Following the cohabitation of them both, who had performed meritorious deeds, sons and daughters were born, endowed with the virtues of fortune and merit.

22.

22.

Katvā sabbopahārena, dāṭhādhātu mahāmahaṃ;

Āruyha varapāsādaṃ, ratanavhaṃ mahīpati.

The lord of the earth, having held a great festival for the Tooth Relic with all offerings, ascended the excellent palace named Ratana.

23.

23.

Tadā sovaṇṇayassāpi, sambuddhassa purā ṭhitaṃ;

Suññaṃ piṭṭhaṃ sayaṃ disvā, kasmā evanti saṃvadi.

Then, seeing for himself the empty platform that stood before the golden Buddha, he spoke, 'Why is it thus?'

24.

24.

Tato [M 0.0322] amaccā āhaṃsu, nājānāsi mahīpati;

Mahāpitunarindassa, kāle tava narissaraṃ.

Then the ministers said: 'O lord of the earth, do you not know what happened in the time of your great father, the king, that ruler of men?'

25.

25.

Paṇḍurājā idhāgamma, dīpametaṃ vināsiya;

Sabbaṃ sāragataṃ dīpe, samādāya gato iti.

'King Paṇḍu, having come here, devastated this island; having taken all things of value on the island, he departed.'

26.

26.

Taṃ sutvā lajjito rājā, sayaṃ viya parājito;

Tadaheva niyojesi, amacce balasaṅgahe.

Having heard that, the king was ashamed, as if he himself were defeated; on that very day he commanded his ministers to gather an army.

27.

27.

Tadā’va kira āgañchi, paṇḍurājakumārako;

Paribhūto sarājena, rajjatthaṃ kata nicchayo.

On that very day, it is said, a Paṇḍu prince arrived, who had been scorned by his king and was resolved to gain the kingdom.

28.

28.

Rājā disvā’ti santuṭṭho, kattabbaṃ tassa kāriya;

Mahātittha mupāgamma, paṭṭanaṃ sematraso.

The king, seeing him, was greatly pleased and made the necessary arrangements for him; going to Mahātittha, he had the port prepared.

29.

29.

Mahantaṃ balakāyañca, tassopakaraṇāni ca;

Anunaṃ paṭiyādetvā, devasenaṃva sajjitaṃ.

Having prepared a great army and its equipment in full, it was arrayed like an army of the gods.

30.

30.

Paṇḍurājakumārena, saddhiṃ senāpati sakaṃ;

Gantvā taṃ paṇḍurājānaṃ, hantvānikamito purā.

His own commander, together with the Paṇḍu prince, went and killed that Paṇḍu king, and then departed from the city.

31.

31.

Ratanaṃ sabbamādāya, datvā rajjaṃ imassa ca;

Na cireneva ehītī, uyyojesi mahāyaso.

The one of great fame sent him forth with these instructions: 'Take all the treasures, give the kingdom to this prince, and return without delay.'

32.

32.

Sopi evaṃ karomīti, paṭissutvā mahīpatiṃ;

Vinditvā balamādāya, nāmamāruyha taṃ khaṇe.

Having promised the king, 'I will do so,' he took the army provided and at that moment boarded a ship.

33.

33.

Paratīraṃ tato gantvā, saṃvuḷaha balavāhano;

Vināsayanto paccantaṃ, vāresi madhuraṃ puraṃ.

Then, having gone to the further shore with his massed forces and transport, he destroyed the border regions and besieged the city of Madhura.

34.

34.

Dvārāni pidahitvāna, pacchindittha gatāgataṃ;

Tato aggiṃ khipāpesi, gopuraṭṭāla koṭṭhake.

Having blocked the gates, they cut off all coming and going; then he had fire thrown upon the gate-towers, watchtowers, and bastions.

35.

35.

Evaṃ sīhaḷasenāya, paviṭṭhāya sakaṃ puraṃ;

Sabbaṃ vilumpamānāya, senaṅgaṃ ghātayantiyā.

Thus, with the Sinhalese army having entered their city, plundering everything and slaughtering their troops,

36.

36.

Paṇḍurājā nisammetaṃ, samādāya sakaṃ balaṃ;

Vegasā taṃ samāgamma, yuddhaṃ kātuṃ samārabhi.

King Paṇḍu, having learned of this, gathered his own forces; approaching swiftly, he began to give battle.

37.

37.

Asampuṇṇa balattā so, viddho sallena bhūpati;

Hatthikkhandhagatoyeva, vihāya puramattano.

The king, his forces being incomplete, was struck by an arrow and, while still on the back of his elephant, abandoned his own city.

38.

38.

Palāyitvā gataṭhāne, jīvitaṃ nijamessaji;

Bhariyāva’ssa tenāsi, sampattā jīvitakkhayaṃ.

Having fled, in the place where he went he gave up his own life; his wife also, on his account, reached the end of her life.

39.

39.

Tato [M 0.0323] sīhaḷasenāsā, paviṭṭhā nibbhayā puraṃ;

Tattha sabbaṃ vilumpittha, devā’sirapuraṃ yathā.

Then that Sinhalese army, fearless, entered the city; there they plundered everything, just as the gods plunder the city of the Asuras.

40.

40.

Senāpati tato rāja-gehe bhattaṃ samekkhiya;

Dīpānitamimamhā ca, tatraṭṭhañca mahārahaṃ.

The commander then examined the goods in the royal palace: those of great value that were already there, and those that had been brought from this island.

41.

41.

Sāraṃ sabbaṃsamādāya, dese ca nagare ṭhitaṃ;

Katvā issariyaṃ tattha, vasevattiya attano.

Taking all the valuables situated in the country and in the city, and establishing his authority there, he brought the land under his own control.

42.

42.

Paṇḍurāja kumāraṃ tu, tattha rajje’bhi siñciya;

Kāretvā parihārañca, desaṃ tassa samappiya.

Then, having anointed the Paṇḍu prince as king in that kingdom and having arranged for its administration, he entrusted the country to him.

43.

43.

Yathāruciṃ gahetvāna, hatthiasse nare’pi ca;

Tattha tattha yathā kāmaṃ, vasanto akuto bhayo.

Taking elephants, horses, and men as he pleased, he dwelt here and there as he wished, free from any fear.

44.

44.

Samudda taṭamāgamma, ṭhatvā tattha yathāsukhaṃ;

Kīḷanto viya nāvaṃ so, samāruyha visārado.

Having come to the seashore and standing there at ease, that skilled one boarded a ship as if in sport.

45.

45.

Mahātittha mupāgamma, vanditvā dharaṇī patiṃ;

Taṃ sāsanaṃ nivedetvā, sāraṃ dassesi āhaṭaṃ.

Having arrived at the great landing place and paid homage to the lord of the earth, he announced that message and showed the valuable tribute he had brought.

46.

46.

Rājā sādhūti vatvāna, kāretvā tassa saṅgahaṃ;

Saddhiṃ senāya āgantvā, pakaṭṭhāya sakaṃ puraṃ.

The king, saying, 'Excellent!' and having arranged hospitality for him, came with his army to his own renowned city.

47.

47.

Jayapānaṃ pivitvāna, katvā vijayamaṅgalaṃ;

Mahādhāgaṃ pavattetvā, yācakānaṃ yathā ruciṃ.

Having drunk the drink of victory and performed the victory festival, he distributed great gifts to the supplicants according to their desire.

48.

48.

Sabbaṃ pākatikaṃ kāsi, sāraṃ dīpe nirālayo;

Sovaṇṇa paṭimāyo ca, yathāṭhāne ṭhapāpayi.

He, being without attachment, restored everything on the island to its natural state; and he had the golden images placed in their proper positions.

49.

49.

Suññaṃ ratanapāsāde, piṭṭhaṃ pūresi satthuno;

Kāsi rakkhapidhānena, nibbhayaṃ dharaṇītalaṃ.

He filled the empty Jeweled Palace with the Teacher's relics; by means of a protective arrangement, he made the surface of the earth fearless.

50.

50.

Tato paṭṭhāya dīpaṃso, arīnaṃ duppadhaṃsiyaṃ;

Katvā vaḍḍhesi bhogehi, uttarādikuruṃ piya.

From then on, having made the island difficult for enemies to assail, he developed it with riches, making it like the beloved Uttarakuru.

51.

51.

Khinnā pubbassa rājassa, kāle dīpamhi pāṇino;

Nibbutā taṃ samāgamma, ghammā viya valāhakā.

The living beings on the island, who were distressed in the time of the former king, found peace upon meeting him, as if cooled by a rain-cloud from the heat.

52.

52.

Tassa vīsatime vasse, vihāre abhayuttare;

Nikkhamitvā gatā hesuṃ, paṃsukūlika bhikkhavo.

In the twentieth year of his reign, the Pamsukulika monks, having departed from the Abhayuttara monastery, went away.

53.

53.

Yuvarājā mahindo so, dhumarājassa satthuno;

Kārāpayi gharaṃ rammaṃ, dassaneyyaṃ manoramaṃ.

That Prince Mahinda, of the master Dhumaraja, had a delightful house built, fair to see and pleasing to the mind.

54.

54.

Bodhigehaṃ [M 0.0324] karonto taṃ, disvā vaḍḍhakīno tadā;

Vaṃsena sākhaṃ āhacca, bhijjantaṃ varabodhiyā.

While that Bodhi-shrine was being constructed, the carpenters saw a branch of the excellent Bodhi tree breaking, it having been struck with a bamboo.

55.

55.

Kintu kātabbametthāti, yuvarājaṃ nivedayuṃ;

So taṃ taṃ mupasaṃkamma, mahāpūjāya pūjiya.

'But what is to be done about this?' thus they informed the prince. He, having approached that tree, honored it with a great offering.

56.

56.

Sace satthā, hitatthāya, sambhūto sabbapāṇinaṃ;

Laddhuṃ puññassa’nagghassa, gharassa karaṇeti’dha.

If the Teacher has arisen for the welfare of all beings, may the making of this house here be for the gaining of priceless merit.

57.

57.

Sākhā gacchaṃ tu uddhaṃva, kātuṃ sakkā yathāgharaṃ;

58.

59.

60.

62.

113.

116.

5.

5.

Taṃ sutvā kupito rājā, balaṃ pesesi attano;

Yujjhitvā taṃ parājesi, mahindo so mahābhaṭo.

Hearing that, the king grew angry and sent forth his own army; that great warrior Mahinda fought and defeated it.

6.

6.

Tato rājā nivattetuṃ, pitaraṃ tassa pesayi;

Kassapaṃ yuvarājaṃ taṃ, so gantvā puttasantikaṃ.

Then the king sent his father, that crown prince Kassapa, to turn him back; he, having gone to the presence of his son,

7.

7.

Nānādhammakathopetaṃ, vatvā yuttimanekadhā;

Saṅghāmato nivattetvā, puttaṃ so punarāgami.

Having spoken appropriately and in many ways with various Dhamma discourses, and having turned his son back from battle, he returned.

8.

8.

Ādipādo tu so pacchā, ghātetvā maṇḍalādhipe;

Kuddhejanapade disvā, agamāsi purantikaṃ.

But that Ādipāda, later, having had the regional rulers killed and seeing the populace angered, went near to the city.

9.

9.

Bhikkhusaṅgho tamānetvā, dassesi vasudhādhipaṃ;

Datvā so dhītaraṃ tassā, pesesi puna rohaṇaṃ.

The Saṅgha of monks brought him and presented him to the lord of the earth. He gave his daughter to him and sent him back to Rohaṇa.

10.

10.

Nīharitvāna dussīle, nikāyattayavāsīsu;

Gāhāpesi nave bhikkhū, āvāse tattha tattha so.

Having expelled the immoral ones dwelling in the three Nikāyas, he had new monks installed in residences here and there.

11.

11.

Dvayābhisekajātena, ādipādena sununā;

Mahāvihāre bodhimhi, paṃsuṃ vaḍḍhesi pūjayaṃ.

Together with his son, the Ādipāda born of a double consecration, he paid homage by adding soil to the mound of the Bodhi tree in the Great Monastery.

12.

12.

Akāsi [M 0.0331] ca nikāyesu, tīsu bimbe silāmaye;

Sovaṇṇaye raṃsijāle, chattaṃ cūḷāmaṇiṃ tathā.

And in the three Nikāyas he made stone images, as well as golden nets of rays, a parasol, and a crest-jewel.

13.

13.

Abhayagirivihāramhi, pāsādaṃ sakanāmakaṃ;

Katvā tattha nivāsetvā, bhikkhu gāmamadāpayi.

In the Abhayagiri Monastery, having built a palatial residence named after himself and having settled monks there, he had a village bestowed upon it.

14.

14.

Mahiyaṅgaṇavihārasmiṃ, gāmaṃ so cetiyassa’dā;

Savatthaṃ paṭimābhattaṃ, sabbabhikkhūna dāpayi.

In the Mahiyangana Monastery, he gave a village to the shrine. He had food provided for the image and for all the monks.

15.

15.

Thale jale ca sattānaṃ, adāsi abhayaṃ tadā;

Cārittapubbarājūnaṃ, paripālesi sabbadā.

He then gave safety to beings on land and in water; he always maintained the traditions of former kings.

16.

16.

Tassa senāpati seno, ilaṅgorājavaṃsajo;

Theriyānaṃ akā’vāsaṃ; Thūpārāmassa pacchato.

His general, Sena, of the lineage of King Ilaṅga, made a dwelling for the elder nuns behind the Thūpārāma.

17.

17.

Dhammārucikabhikkhūnaṃ, dhammārāmamakārayi;

Tathā sāgalikānañca, kassapasenanāmakaṃ.

He had the Dhammārāma built for the Dhammārucika monks; likewise for the Sāgalika monks, he had one built named Kassapasena.

18.

18.

Hadayuṇhābhidhānaṃ so, katvā cetiyapabbate;

Pariveṇaṃ adādhamma-rucikānañca bhikkhūnaṃ.

Having built a monastic dwelling named Hadayuṇhā on Cetiyapabbata, he gave it to the Dhammārucika monks.

19.

19.

Ārāmikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ārāmesu tahiṃ tahiṃ;

Ekamekaṃ kuṭiṃ katvā, dāpesi ca camūpati.

For the monastery-attendant monks, here and there in the monasteries, the army chief had individual huts built and given.

20.

20.

Rattamālagirismiṃ so, katvā rammaṃ taraṃ subhaṃ;

Kuciṃ adā sāsanassa, sāmikānaṃ tapassinaṃ.
