On Rattamālagiri, having made an excellent, delightful, and beautiful dwelling, he gave it to the ascetics, the masters of the Dispensation.

21.

21.

Mahāvihāre kāretvā, paviveṇaṃ varaṃ adā;

Paṃsukūlikabhikkhūnaṃ, samuddagirināmakaṃ.

Having had an excellent monastic dwelling named Samuddagiri built in the Great Monastery, he gave it to the Paṃsukūlika monks.

22.

22.

Vāsaṃ araññe kāretvā, attano vaṃsanāmakaṃ;

Mahāvihāre bhikkhūnaṃ, vane nivāsataṃ adā.

Having had a dwelling built in the forest, named after his own lineage, he gave it to the monks of the Great Monastery who were dwelling in the forest.

23.

23.

Vihāresū ca jiṇṇesu, navakammamakārayi;

Dāpesi aggalaṃ sabba-bhikkhūnaṃ jiṇṇacīvare.

He had renovations done on the dilapidated monasteries; he had bolts given to all the monks, and new robes for their worn-out ones.

24.

24.

Tissārāmaṃ karitvāna, bhikkhūnīnamupassayaṃ;

Maricavaṭṭimahābodhi, parihāre nivesayi.

Having constructed the Tissārāma as a residence for the nuns, he established the Maricavaṭṭi Mahābodhi in its precinct.

25.

25.

Anurādhapure ceva, pulatthinagarepi ca;

Upasaggaroganāsāya, vejjasālāpi kārayi.

In Anurādhapura and also in Pulatthinagara, he had hospitals built for the destruction of affliction and disease.

26.

26.

Attanā katavāsanaṃ, bhogagāme ca dāpayi;

Tathārāmikagāme ca, paṭimābharaṇañca so.

He himself had robes made and given in the revenue villages; likewise, in the monastery villages, he also provided ornaments for the statues.

27.

27.

Bhesajjagehaṃ [M 0.0332] kāresi, nagare tattha tattha so;

Paṃsukūlikabhikkhūnaṃ, bhattaṃ vatthañca dāpayi.

He had medical houses built here and there in the city; he had food and clothing given to the rag-robed monks.

28.

28.

Khandhīkate amocesi, tiracchānagate bahū;

Kapaṇānañca dāpesi, mahādānaṃ camūpati.

He released many who were put in stocks, as well as many animals; the commander of the army had great alms given to the poor.

29.

29.

Vicittaṃ byañjanaṃ bhattaṃ, yāguṃ vividhakhajjakaṃ;

Katvā sūkararūpañca, guḷaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dāpayi.

Having prepared rice with various curries, gruel, and assorted delicacies, and also jaggery in the shape of pigs, he had it given to the monks.

30.

30.

Evāmādīni puññāni, katvā senāya nāyako;

Seno kittindupādehi, sabbā obhāsayī disā.

Having performed such meritorious deeds, Sena, the leader of the army, illuminated all directions with the radiance of his fame.

31.

31.

Tasseva ñātako katvā, nāyako rakkhasavhayo;

Savārakamhi gāmamhi, vihāraṃ sumanoharaṃ.

His relative, the leader named Rakkhasa, built a delightful monastery in the village of Savāraka.

32.

32.

Mahāvihāravāsīnaṃ, sārānaṃ paṭipattiyā;

Bhikkhūnaṃ so adā sādhu, ṭhapetvā vattamuttamaṃ.

To the monks dwelling in the Great Monastery, for the sake of their essential practice, he gladly gave, having established the highest code of conduct.

33.

33.

Seno nāma mahālekho, mahālekhakapabbataṃ;

Mahāvihāre kāresi, bhikkhūnaṃ vāsamuttamaṃ.

Sena, the great scribe, had the Mahālekhakapabbata, a supreme dwelling for the monks, built in the Great Monastery.

34.

34.

Coḷarājābhidhāno, ca, amacco tassa rājino;

Pariveṇaṃ akārammaṃ, naṭṭhaṃ taṃ suppatiṭṭhitaṃ.

The minister of that king, named Coḷarāja, also rebuilt a delightful, well-founded residence that had been ruined.

35.

35.

Rājā tīsu nikāyesu, rūpakammamanoramaṃ;

Maṇḍapāni vicittāni, vejayanto pamāni ca.

The king had delightful crafted forms made in the three communities, and splendid pavilions comparable to the Vejayanta palace.

36.

36.

Kāretvā dhātupūjāyo, katvā janamanoharā;

Yathā kammaṃ gato ṭhatvā, vassāni dasasatta ca.

Having caused relic-worships to be performed and having done deeds pleasing to the people, after reigning for seventeen years, he passed away according to his karma.

37.

37.

Dvayābhisekasañjāto, yuvarājātha kassapo;

Āsi laddhābhiseko so, laṃkārajjekamāgate.

Then the crown prince Kassapa, born of a double consecration, having received the consecration, came to the sole sovereignty of Laṅkā.

38.

38.

Saddho āgatamaggova, sābhiñño viya paññavā;

Vattā so maramantiva, cāgavā dhanado viya.

Faithful, like one who has attained the path; wise, as if possessing higher knowledge; eloquent, like one who defeats Māra; liberal, like a giver of wealth.

39.

39.

Bahussuto dhammakathī, sabbasippavisārado;

Yuttāyuttavicārāya, nipuṇo nayakovido.

Learned, a speaker of Dhamma, skilled in all crafts, discerning in judging what is proper and improper, expert in policy.

40.

40.

Acalo indalīlo’va, ṭhito sugatasāsane;

Parappavādivātehi, sabbehi’pi akampiyo.

Unwavering like Indra's pillar, steadfast in the Buddha's dispensation, unshaken by all the winds of others' doctrines.

41.

41.

Māyāsāṭheyyamānādi, pāpānañca agocaro;

Guṇānaṃ ākaro sabba-ratanānaṃ vasāgaro.

Beyond the range of deceit, hypocrisy, pride, and other evils; a mine of virtues, an ocean of all jewels.

42.

42.

Bhūmicando [M 0.0333] narindo so, vaṃse jātassa attano;

Dappuḷassādīpādassa, yuvarājapadaṃ adā.

That king, a moon on earth, gave the position of crown prince to the Ādipāda Dappuḷa, who was born of his own lineage.

43.

43.

Rajjaṃ dasahi dhammehi, catusaṅgahavatthūhi;

Karonto paripālesi, lokaṃ nettaṃva attano.

Governing the kingdom with the ten royal virtues and the four bases of sympathy, he protected the world as if it were his own eye.

44.

44.

So dhetvā sāsanaṃ sabbaṃ, dhammakammena satthuno;

Gahetvā navake bhikkhū, akāsā’vāsapūraṇaṃ.

Having upheld the entire Dispensation through the Dhamma-work of the Master, he took newly ordained monks and filled the empty dwellings.

45.

45.

Duṭṭhagāmaṇirājena, kataṃ maricavaṭṭikaṃ;

Naṭṭhaṃ vihāraṃ kāretvā, nānāāvāsa bhūsitaṃ.

He had the ruined Maricavaṭṭika monastery, which was built by King Duṭṭhagāmaṇi, rebuilt and adorned with various dwellings.

46.

46.

Theravaṃsajabhikkhūnaṃ, adā katvā mahāmahaṃ;

Tesaṃ pañcasatānañca, bhogagāme ca dāpayi.

Having held a great festival, he gave to the monks of the Theravāda lineage; and to five hundred of them, he also had revenue villages given.

47.

47.

Tattha so tusite ramme, devasaṅghapurakkhataṃ;

Metteyyaṃ lokanāthaṃ taṃ, desentaṃ dhammamuttamaṃ.

There, in delightful Tusita, honored by the assembly of devas, he saw Metteyya, the Lord of the world, teaching the supreme Dhamma.

48.

48.

Dassento viya lokassa, vihāre sabbasajjite;

Nisinno maṇḍape ramme, nānāratanabhūsite.

As if showing this to the world, he sat in a lovely pavilion decorated with various jewels, within the fully adorned monastery.

49.

49.

Nagarehi ca sabbehi, bhikkhūhi parivārito;

Buddhalilāya laṃkindo, abhidhamma mabhāsayi.

Surrounded by all the monks of the city, the king of Laṅkā, with the deportment of a Buddha, expounded the Abhidhamma.

50.

50.

Soṇṇapaṭṭe likhāpetvā-bhidhammapiṭakaṃ tadā;

Dhammasaṅgaṇikaṃ potthaṃ, nānāratana bhūsitaṃ.

Then, having had the Abhidhamma Piṭaka inscribed on golden plates, he had the book of the Dhammasaṅgaṇī adorned with various jewels.

51.

51.

Katvā nagaramajjhamhi, kāretvā hemamuttamaṃ;

Taṃ tattha ṭhapayitvāna, parihāramadāpayi.

Having had a superb golden casket made and a building erected in the center of the city, he placed the book there and provided for its maintenance.

52.

52.

Sakkasenāpatiṭṭhānaṃ, datvā puttassa attano;

Parihāre niyojesi, tattha taṃ dhammapotthake.

Giving the position of Sakka's general to his own son, he appointed him to the care of that Dhamma book.

53.

53.

Anusaṃvaccharaṃ rājā, puraṃ devapurī viya;

Vibhūsitāya senāya, sajjetvā parivārito.

Year after year, the king, having adorned the city to be like a city of devas, was surrounded by a splendid army.

54.

54.

Devarājāva sobhanto, sabbābharaṇabhūsito;

Hatthikhaṇḍe nisīditvā, caranto puravīthiyaṃ.

Shining like the king of devas, adorned with all ornaments, seated on an elephant's back, proceeding through the city streets.

55.

55.

Mahatā parihārena, netvā taṃ dhammasaṅgahaṃ;

Attanā kāritaṃ rammaṃ, vihāraṃ sabbasajjitaṃ.

With a great retinue, having brought that collection of the Dhamma to the lovely, fully equipped monastery he had caused to be built.

56.

56.

Tattha dhātugate ramme, nānāratanabhūsite;

Maṇḍape dhātupiṭhasmiṃ, patiṭṭhāpiya pūjayi.

There, in the delightful relic chamber adorned with various jewels, he enshrined it in the pavilion on the relic dais and paid homage.

57.

57.

Ganthākarapariveṇaṃ[M 0.0334], mahāmeghavane akā;

Nagare vajjasālā ca, tesaṃ gāme ca dāpayi.

He built the Ganthākara Pariveṇa in the Mahāmeghavana and the Vajjasālā in the city, and he also caused villages to be given to them.

58.

58.

Bhaṇḍikapariveṇañca, silāmeghañca pabbataṃ;

Katvā’bhayagirismiṃ so, tesaṃ gāmamadāpayi.

Having built the Bhaṇḍika Pariveṇa and the Silāmeghapabbata at Abhayagiri, he caused a village to be given to them.

59.

59.

Jotivanavihārasmiṃ, rājā laṅkāya nāyako;

Bhattaggassa adā gāmaṃ, tathā’bhayagirimhi ca.

At the Jotivana monastery, the king, the leader of Laṅkā, gave a village for the refectory, and likewise at Abhayagiri.

60.

60.

Dakkhiṇagirināmassa, vihārassa ca dāpayi;

Gāmaṃ kataññubhāvena, rājā paramadhammiko.

To the monastery named Dakkhiṇagiri he also caused a village to be given; the king, supremely righteous, acted out of gratitude.

61.

61.

Sakkasenāpati rammaṃ, pariveṇaṃ sumāpiya;

Adāsi sahagāmehi, theriyānaṃ sanāmikaṃ.

The general Sakkasenāpati, having caused a delightful residence to be well built, gave it to the elder nuns, together with villages, naming it after himself.

62.

62.

Bhariyā vajirā tassa, tesaṃyeva adāpayi;

Pariveṇaṃ karitvāna, sagāmaṃ sakanāmakaṃ.

His wife Vajirā, having had a residence built, caused it to be given to those same nuns, together with a village, naming it after herself.

63.

63.

Upassayaṃ karitvāna, sā eva padalañchane;

Bhikkhūnīnaṃ adā thera-vaṃse sabbattha pūjite.

Having made a dwelling, she herself gave it to the bhikkhunīs at the footprint shrine, which is honored everywhere in the lineage of the elders.

64.

64.

Sakkasenāpati mātā, devā’raññaka bhikkhūnaṃ;

Theravaṃsappadīpānaṃ, akā’vāsaṃ sanāmakaṃ.

The mother of the general Sakkasenāpati, Devā, made a dwelling named after herself for the forest-dwelling monks, who were lamps of the lineage of the elders.

65.

65.

Sā eva paṭibimbassa, satthu maricavaṭṭiyaṃ;

Cūḷāmaṇiṃ pādajalaṃ, akā chattañca cīvaraṃ.

She herself also made for the image of the Teacher at Maricavaṭṭi a crest-jewel, a foot-ornament, an umbrella, and a robe.

66.

66.

Rājā rājālayeyeva, rājavaṃsaṃ sanāmakaṃ;

Akāsi pāḷikaṃ nāma, pāsādaṃ sumano haraṃ.

The king, in the royal palace itself, built a delightful and captivating mansion named Pāḷika, also named for the royal lineage.

67.

67.

Pūjesi rājinī nāma, rājino bhariyā’parā;

Paṭṭakañcukapūjāya, hemamālika cetiyaṃ.

Another wife of the king, named Rājinī, worshipped the Hemamālika Cetiya with an offering of a silken bodice.

68.

68.

Tassā puttosi siddhattho, nāma issariye ṭhito;

Suto malayarājāti, rūpena makaraddhajo.

Her son was Siddhattha by name, established in sovereignty; he was known as the king of Malaya, his beauty like that of Makaraddhaja.

69.

69.

Rājā tasmiṃ mate katvā, sālaṃ bhikkhunamuttamaṃ;

Dānavaṭṭaṃ paṭṭhapetvā, tassa pattimadā tadā.

When he died, the king, having built an excellent hall for the monks and having established a regular alms-giving, then transferred the merit to him.

70.

70.

Evaṃ dhammena kārente, rajjaṃ laṅkādīpe tadā;

Coḷarājena yujjhitvā, paṇḍurājā parājito.

While he was thus ruling the kingdom in the island of Laṅkā righteously, the Paṇḍu king, having fought with the Coḷa king, was defeated.

71.

71.

Paṇṇākārāni nekāni, balaṃ sandhāya pesayi;

Rājālaṃkissaro saddhiṃ, mantetvā sacivehi so.

He (the Paṇḍu king) sent many kinds of tribute, seeking military aid. That king, the lord of Laṅkā, having consulted with his ministers,

72.

72.

Sannayha [M 0.0335] balakāyaṃ so, sakkasenāpatiṃ sakaṃ;

Balassa nāyakaṃ katvā, mahāyitthamupāgami.

Having assembled his army and having made his own Sakkasenāpati the leader of the force, he set out for the great battle.

73.

73.

Vijayaṃ pubbarājūnaṃ, vatvā velātaṭe ṭhito;

Ussāhaṃ janayitvāna, nāvaṃ āropayī balaṃ.

Standing on the seashore, he spoke of the victories of former kings, and having aroused enthusiasm, he embarked the army on the ships.

74.

74.

Balakāyaṃ samādāya, sakkasenāpatiṃ tadā;

Sukhena sāgaraṃ tiṇṇo, paṇḍudesamupāgami.

The Sakkasenāpati, taking the army, then crossed the ocean with ease and reached the Paṇḍu country.

75.

75.

Disvā balañca tañceva, paṇḍurājā sumānaso;

Ekacchattaṃ karissāmi, jambudīpanti abravi.

Seeing that very army, the Paṇḍu king, delighted, said, "I will make Jambudīpa to be under one umbrella."

76.

76.

Baladvayaṃ gahetvāna, rājā so coḷavaṃsajaṃ;

Jetuṃ asakkuṇitvāna yuddhamujjhiya nikkhami.

That king, having taken both forces, being unable to conquer the descendant of the Coḷa lineage, abandoned the battle and departed.

77.

77.

Yujjhissāmīti gantāna, sakkasenāpatī puna;

Nisinno upasaggena, mato pāpena paṇḍuto.

The wise Sakkasenāpati, having gone again, thinking, 'I will fight,' died from a painful affliction while he was seated.

78.

78.

Laṃkissaro balassāpi, tena rogena nānasaṃ;

Sutvā dayālubhāvena, senaṃ āṇāpayī tato.

The lord of Laṅkā, having heard of the destruction of the army by that disease, out of compassion, then gave orders to the army.

79.

79.

Sakka senāpatiṭṭhānaṃ, tassa puttassa’dā tadā;

Vaḍḍhesi tena taṃ puttaṃ, katvā senāya nāyakaṃ.

He then gave the position of Sakkasenāpati to his son. By that, he promoted that son, making him leader of the army.

80.

80.

Nikāyattayavāsīhi, parittaṃ nagare tadā;

Kāretvā rogadubbuṭṭhi-bhayaṃ nāsesi jantunaṃ.

Having caused the protective verses to be recited in the city at that time by the residents of the three Nikāyas, he dispelled the fear of disease and drought for the people.

81.

81.

Sāsanassa ca lokassa, santiṃ katvā anekadhā;

Rājā so dasame vasse, sukhena tidivaṃ gato.

Having established peace for the Dispensation and the world in many ways, that king, in the tenth year, went to heaven with ease.

82.

82.

Laṃkārajjepi ṭhatvā kathitatipiṭako sabbavijjāpadīpo,

Vattāvādī kavī so satidhītivisado desako bhāvako ca;

Paññāsaddhādayā vā parahitanirato lokavedīvadaññū;

Rājindo kassapo’yaṃ viya vimalaguṇo hotulokopi sabbo.

Established in the kingdom of Laṅkā, he had expounded the Tipiṭaka and was a lamp of all knowledge. He was a speaker of the doctrine, a poet, clear in mindfulness and wisdom, a teacher and a cultivator. Endowed with wisdom, faith, and compassion, intent on the welfare of others, a knower of the world, and generous. May the entire world become one of pure virtue, like this King Kassapa.

Sujanappasādasaṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Great Chronicle, composed for the serene joy and spiritual urgency of the virtuous.

Dvirājako nāma

The Two Kings

Paññāsatimo paricchedo.

The Fiftieth Chapter.

Ekapaññāsatima pariccheda

The Fifty-First Chapter

Pañcarājako nāma

The Five Kings

1.

1.

Yuvarājā [M 0.0336] tadā hutvā, rājā dappuḷanāmako;

Ṭhapesi oparajjamhi, ādipadaṃ sanāmakaṃ.

Then, having been the crown prince, the king named Dappula established in the viceroyalty the ādipāda of his own name.

2.

2.

Maricavaṭṭivihārassa, gāmaṃ datvā tato pure;

Cārittaṃ pubbarājūnaṃ, rakkhitvāna mahiṃ imaṃ.

Having given a village to the Maricavaṭṭi Vihāra, and having previously protected this earth, preserving the tradition of the former kings,

3.

3.

Abhutvā dīghakālañhi, pubbakammena attano;

Rājā so sattame māse, paviṭṭho paccuno mukhaṃ.

Not having been king for a long time, due to his own former kamma, that king, in the seventh month, entered the mouth of death.

4.

4.

Uparājā ahurājā, dappuḷo tadanantaraṃ;

Udayassādipādassa, yuvarājapadaṃ adā.

Thereafter, Dappula, who was the viceroy, became king; he gave the position of crown prince to the ādipāda Udaya.

5.

5.

Tadā coḷabhayā paṇḍu-rājaṃ janapadaṃ sakaṃ;

Cajitvā nāvamāruyha, mahātitthamupāgami.

Then, from fear of the Coḷas, the Paṇḍu king, having abandoned his own country, boarded a ship and came to Mahātittha.

6.

6.

Āṇāpetvāna taṃ rājā, disvā santuṭṭhamānaso;

Mahābhogaṃ adā tassa, nivāsesi purā bahi.

The king, having had him brought, and seeing him content in mind, gave him great wealth and had him reside outside the city.

7.

7.

Coḷarājena yujjhitvā, gahetvā paṭṭanadvayaṃ;

Paṇḍurājassa dammīti, sannaddhe laṅkarājini.

When the king of Laṅkā was prepared, thinking, “Having fought with the Coḷa king and captured two port-towns, I shall give them to the Paṇḍu king,”

8.

8.

Kenā’pi karaṇīyena, khattiyā dīpavāsino;

Akaṃsu viggahaṃ ghoraṃ, pāpakammena paṇḍuno.

For some reason, the khattiyas dwelling on the island engaged in a terrible conflict, due to the evil kamma of the Paṇḍu king.

9.

9.

Paṇḍurāje’ttha vāsena, kammaṃ natthīti cintiya;

Ṭhapetvā makuṭādīni, gato keraḷasantikaṃ.

Thinking, “There is no purpose in residing here,” the Paṇḍu king left behind his crown and other regalia and went to the vicinity of Kerala.

10.

10.

Viggahe niṭṭhite rājā, mahāmeghavane tadā;

Mahābodhigharassā’dā, gāmaṃ nagarasantike.

When the conflict was over, the king then gave a village near the city to the House of the Great Bodhi-tree in the Mahāmeghavana.

11.

11.

Āvāsaṃ rakkhako nāma, tassa senāpatī akā;

Thūpārāmasamīpamhi, iḷaṅgo rājanāmakaṃ.

His general, named Rakkha Iḷaṅga, built a residence near the Thūpārāma, which was named after the king.

12.

12.

Kataṃ taṃ pubbarājehi, rājā so paripāliya;

Patto dvādasamaṃ vassaṃ, yathākammamupāgami.

That king, having upheld the work of former kings, upon reaching his twelfth year, passed away according to his kamma.

13.

13.

Udayo [M 0.0337] yuvarājā’si, laṃkāvāsīnamissaro;

Senanāmādipādaṃ so, oparajje’bhisecayi.

The crown prince Udaya became the lord of the inhabitants of Laṅkā. He consecrated the ādipāda named Sena in the viceroyalty.

14.

14.

Rañño bhītā tadāmaccā, pavisiṃsu tapovanaṃ;

Rājoparājā gantvāna, tesaṃ sīsāni chedayuṃ.

Then the ministers, fearing the king, entered the ascetic grove. The king and the viceroy went and cut off their heads.

15.

15.

Tena kammena nibbinnā, yatayo tannivāsino;

Hitvā janapadaṃ rañño, tadāgacchiṃsu rohaṇaṃ.

Disgusted by that deed, the ascetics dwelling there abandoned the king’s realm and then went to Rohaṇa.

16.

16.

Tadā jānapadā ceva, nāgarā ca balāni ca;

Kupitā caṇḍuvātena, sāgaro viya kampito.

Then the country-folk, the townspeople, and the armies, being angered, were shaken like the ocean by a fierce wind.

17.

17.

Ratanapāsādamāruyha, vihāre abhayuttare;

Santāsetvāna rājānaṃ, dassetvāna vibhīsikaṃ.

Ascending the Ratanapāsāda in the Abhayuttara Vihāra, they terrified the king, showing him fearful sights.

18.

18.

Upatthambhakamaccānaṃ, viggahassa tapovane;

Tadā sīsāni chinditvā, kavātena nipātayuṃ.

Then, having cut off the heads of the ministers who supported the conflict in the ascetic grove, they threw them down at the gate.

19.

19.

Taṃ sutvā yuvarājā ca, ādipādo ca taṃ sakhā;

Ullaṅghitvāna pākāraṃ, sīghaṃ gacchiṃsu rohaṇaṃ.

Hearing that, the crown prince and the ādipāda, his friend, leaping over the wall, quickly went to Rohaṇa.

20.

20.

Balakāyonubandhitvā, yāva kaṇhanadītaṭā;

Alābhena ca nāvānaṃ, tiṇṇattā tesamāgami.

A body of troops pursued them as far as the bank of the Kaṇha River; but because the princes had crossed over and the troops could not obtain boats, they returned.

21.

21.

Rājaputtāgatā tattha, vane abhayabhedino;

Yatīnaṃ purato tesaṃ, nipajjitvā urena te.

Those princes, having come there to the grove that dispels fear, lay down on their chests before those ascetics.

22.

22.

Allavatthā’llakesā ca, paridevittha’nekadhā;

Kandītvā rodanaṃ katvā, khamāpesuṃ tapassino.

With wet clothes and wet hair, they lamented in many ways. Having cried out and wept, they begged forgiveness from the ascetics.

23.

23.

Khantimettānubhāvena, tesaṃ sāsanasāminaṃ;

Puññodayo ahu tesaṃ, ubhinnaṃ dīpasāminaṃ.

Through the power of the patience and loving-kindness of those lords of the Dispensation, there arose merit for them, the two lords of the island.

24.

24.

Yuvarājabalañceva, nikāyattayavāsino;

Gamiṃsu tesamānetuṃ, santibhūte mahābale.

The crown prince's forces and the dwellers of the three fraternities went to bring them back, the peaceful and greatly powerful ones.

25.

25.

Rājaputtā ubho byattā, paṇḍitā paṃsukūlino;

Yācitvā tesamādāya, agamaṃsu sakaṃ puraṃ.

The two princes, both clever and wise, having begged the rag-robe-wearing ascetics and taking them along, returned to their own city.

26.

26.

Bhikkhūnaṃ purato maggaṃ, rājāgantā khamāpayi;

Ādāya te vanaṃ tesaṃ, netvā rājagharaṃ gato.

The king, having come before the monks on the path, asked for their forgiveness. Taking them from their forest, he led them to the royal palace.

27.

27.

Tato paṭṭhāya cāritthaṃ, pāletvā pubbarājunaṃ;

Rājā so tatiye vasse, yathākammamupāgami.

From that time onward, having protected the conduct of former kings, that king, in the third year, met his end according to his kamma.

28.

28.

Laṃkābhisekaṃ [M 0.0338] patvāna, seno so matimā tato;

Udayaṃ ādipādaṃ taṃ, yuvarājaṃ akā sakhaṃ.

Having attained the consecration of Laṅkā, that wise Sena then made his friend, Udaya the ādipāda, the crown prince.

29.

29.

Kahāpaṇasahassaṃ so, duggatānaṃ uposathe;

Hotu’posathiko datvā, yāvajīvaṃ narādhipo.

The lord of men, having given a thousand kahāpaṇas to the poor on the Uposatha day, observed the Uposatha for as long as he lived.

30.

30.

Paṭimā bhattavatthāni, bhikkhūnaṃ dharaṇī pati;

Adā daṇḍissaraṃ dānaṃ, yācakānañca sippīnaṃ.

The lord of the earth gave food and robes for the images and to the monks, and the Daṇḍissara donation to beggars and craftsmen.

31.

31.

Ṭhāne katthaci sippīnaṃ, pāsādesu manohare;

Kāretvā bhogagāme ca, adāpesi mahāmati.

The great wise one, in some places, caused delightful palaces to be built for craftsmen, and also caused prosperous villages to be given to them.

32.

32.

Kahāpaṇasahassaṃ vā, datvā pañcasatāni vā;

Laṅkāyaṃ jiṇṇakāvāse, navakammamakārayī.

Having given a thousand or five hundred kahāpaṇas, he caused renovation work to be done in the old monasteries in Laṅkā.

33.

33.

Cattālīsasahassāni, abhayuttaracetiye;

Silāpattharaṇatthāya, dāpesi ca mahīpati.

The lord of the earth also caused forty thousand to be given at the Abhayuttara Cetiya for the laying of a stone pavement.

34.

34.

Mahāvāpīsu laṃkāyaṃ, jiṇṇaniddhamane akā;

Navakammañca mariyādaṃ, thiyaṃ pāsāṇapaṃsunā.

In the great tanks of Laṅkā, he carried out the removal of old and decayed parts, and established new works and a firm embankment with stone and earth.

35.

35.

Akā rājaghare rammaṃ, mālāgehaṃ mahārahaṃ;

Ṭhapitaṃ punarājūhi, dānaṃ sammāpavattayi.

He made a delightful and highly valuable garland house in the royal palace. He properly maintained the donation that had been established by former kings.

36.

36.

Kataṃ malayarājena, amaccena’gga bodhinā;

Pariveṇaṃ nāgasālaṃ, disvā gāma madā tadā.

Having seen the Nāgasāla pariveṇa, which was made by the Malayarāja and the chief minister Aggabodhi, he then gave a village.

37.

37.

Katvā catuvihāresu, rūpakammāni sādhukaṃ;

Maṇḍapāni ca rammāni, dhātupūjaṃ akā sadā.

Having had fine works of art and delightful pavilions made in the four monasteries, he always made offerings to the relics.

38.

38.

Evamādīni puññāni, anekāni anekadhā;

Katvā so navame vasse, yathākammamupāgami.

Having performed such numerous and diverse meritorious deeds, he, in the ninth year, met his end according to his kamma.

39.

39.

Laṃkābhisekaṃ patvāna, yuvarājodayo tato;

Senanāmādipādaṃ so, oparajje’bhi secayi.

Having attained the consecration of Laṅkā, the crown prince Udaya then consecrated the ādipāda named Sena to the office of sub-king.

40.

40.

Niddālu majjapo āsi, rājā pāpena jantunaṃ;

Coḷo pamattataṃ tassa, sutvā santuṭṭhamānaso.

The king was slothful and a drunkard, and evil towards beings. The Cola king, hearing of his negligence, was satisfied in mind.

41.

41.

Paṇḍudesātisekaṃ so, pattukā mettha pesayi;

Makuṭādīnamatthāya, ṭhapitānaṃva paṇḍunā.

Desiring to obtain the regalia of the Pāṇḍu country, he sent a messenger here for the crown and other items that had been deposited by the Pāṇḍu king.

42.

42.

Tāni nādāsi so rājā, tena coḷo mahabbalo;

Balaṃ sannayha pesesi, balakkārena gaṇhituṃ.

That king did not give them; for that reason, the mighty Cola king, having assembled his army, sent it forth to seize them by force.

43.

43.

Tadā [M 0.0339] senāpati ettha, paccante kupite gato;

Āṇāpetvāna taṃ rājā, yujjhanatthāya pesayi.

Then, as the border was in turmoil, the general went there. The king, having commanded him, sent him to wage war.

44.

44.

Hato senāpati tattha, yujjhi na raṇe mato;

Kakūṭādīni ādāya, rājā so rohaṇaṃ agā.

The general was slain there; the king fought but did not die in the battle. Taking the royal insignia and other valuables, that king went to Rohaṇa.

45.

45.

Gantvā coḷabalaṃ tattha, alabhitvā pavesanaṃ;

Nivattitvā sakaṃ raṭṭhaṃ, agamāsi idhatā bhayā.

The Cola army, having gone there but failing to gain entry, turned back and went to its own country, departing from here in fear.

46.

46.

Tato senāpatiṭṭhāne, viduraggaṃ tu nāyakaṃ;

Ṭhapesi rājā laṃkindo, tejavantaṃ mahāmatiṃ.

Then the king of Laṅkā appointed the leader Viduragga, a mighty and greatly wise man, to the position of general.

47.

47.

Paccantaṃ coḷarājassa, ghātetvā so camūpati;

Āṇāpesi ito nītaṃ, dassetvāna vibhīsitaṃ.

That general, having slain the frontier commander of the Cola king, had him brought here and displayed as a terrifying spectacle.

48.

48.

Tato dāpesi so sabba-parikkhāraṃ mahārahaṃ;

Paṃsukūlikabhikkhūnaṃ, sabbesaṃ dīpavāsinaṃ.

Then he caused all the valuable requisites to be given to all the Pāṃsukūlika monks dwelling on the island.

49.

49.

Mahāvihāre laṃkindo, paṭibimbassa satthuno;

Jalantaṃ maṇiraṃsīhi, akā cūḷāmaṇiṃ tadā.

Then, in the Great Monastery, the king of Laṅkā made a crest-jewel for the image of the Teacher, radiant with the rays of gems.

50.

50.

Orodhā vidurā tassa, pādajālena pūjayi;

Maṇīhi pajjalantehi, paṭimaṃ taṃ silāmayaṃ.

His wise ladies of the harem honored that stone image with a foot-net that blazed with jewels.

51.

51.

Jhāpitaṃ coḷarājassa, balena maṇināmakaṃ;

Pāsādaṃ kātumāraddho, cuto vassamhi aṭṭhame.

He began to build the palace named Maṇi, which had been burned down by the Cola king's army, but he passed away in the eighth year.

52.

52.

Pañcete vasudhādhipā vasumahiṃ ekātapattaṅkitaṃ;

Bhutvā niggahasaṅgahehi sakalaṃ lokaṃ vase vattiya;

Yā tā maccuvasaṃ saputtavaṇitā sāmaccamittānugā;

Iccevaṃ satataṃ sarantu sujanā hātuṃ pamādaṃ madaṃ.

These five lords of the earth, having enjoyed the world marked by a single parasol, and having brought the entire populace under their sway through restraint and patronage, nevertheless went, together with their sons, wives, ministers, friends, and followers, under the power of death. Thus, let good people ever remember this, in order to abandon negligence and conceit.

Sujanappasādasaṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Mahāvaṃsa, composed for the faith and spiritual urgency of the virtuous.

Pañcarājako nāma

Named 'The Five Kings'.

Ekapaññāsatimo paricchedo.

The Fifty-first Chapter.

Dvipaññāsatima pariccheda

The Fifty-second Chapter.

Tirājakonāma

Named 'The Three Kings'.

1.

1.

Tato [M 0.0340] laṅkābhisekaṃ so, patvā seno kamāgataṃ;

Mahindassādipādassa, yuvarājapadaṃ adā.

Then, having attained consecration in Laṅkā, that Sena gave the position of heir apparent to Mahinda, the foremost prince, who had come in due succession.

2.

2.

Pañño mahākavī byatto, majjhatto mittasattusu;

Yutto dayāya mettāya, rājā so sabbadā ahu.

That king was always wise, a great poet, skilled, impartial to friends and foes, and endowed with compassion and loving-kindness.

3.

3.

Kālaṃ devo’natikkamma, sammā dhārābhivassati;

Raṭṭhe tasmiṃ vasantā’suṃ, sukhitā nibbhayā sadā.

The god, not transgressing the proper time, rained down rightly. Those dwelling in that realm were always happy and free from fear.

4.

4.

Suttantaṃ lohapāsāde, nisinno vaṇṇayī tadā;

Nikāyattayavāsīhi, rājā so parivārito.

Then, seated in the Lohapāsāda, that king, surrounded by the dwellers of the three Nikāyas, expounded the Suttanta.

5.

5.

Dāṭhadhātukaraṇḍaṃ so, nānāratanabhūsitaṃ;

Akā catuvihāresu, dhātupūjā ca’nekadhā.

He made a reliquary for the Tooth Relic, adorned with various jewels, and performed relic worship in many ways in the four monasteries.

6.

6.

Pariveṇaṃ sitthagāmaṃ, kāretvā vutthamattanā;

Lokaṃ puttaṃva pāletvā, tivassena divaṅgato.

Having caused a monastery to be built in Sitthagāma, he himself dwelt there. Protecting the world like his own son, he passed away after three years.

7.

7.

Yuvarājā mahindo so, rājāsi tadanantaraṃ;

Mahāpuñño mahātejo, mahāseno mahāyaso.

Thereafter, that heir apparent Mahinda became king, one of great merit, great might, with a great army, and of great fame.

8.

8.

Ekacchattaṃ akā laṅkaṃ, ghātetvā corupaddavaṃ;

Akaṃsu tamupaṭṭhānaṃ, niccamaṇḍalanāyakaṃ.

He made Laṅkā a single dominion, having destroyed the menace of robbers. The local chieftains constantly attended upon him.

9.

9.

Vijjamānepi laṅkāyaṃ, khattiyānaṃ narādhipo;

Kāliṅgacakkavattissa, vaṃse jātaṃ kumārikaṃ.

Though there were Khattiyas in Laṅkā, the lord of men sent for a princess born in the lineage of the universal monarch of Kāliṅga.

10.

10.

Āṇāpetvāna taṃ agga-mahesiṃ attano akā;

Tassā puttā duve jātā, dhītā ekā manoramā.

Having sent for her, he made her his chief queen. To her were born two sons and one delightful daughter.

11.

11.

Ādipāde akā putte, dhītaraṃ coparājiniṃ;

Iti sīhaḷavaṃsañca, paṭṭhapesi sabhūpati.

He made his sons Ādipādas and his daughter an Uparājinī. Thus, that ruler established the Sinhala dynasty.

12.

12.

Balakāyaṃ imaṃ desaṃ, maddanatthāya vallabho;

Pesesi nāgadīpaṃ so, sutvā taṃ bhūpati idha.

The Vallabha king sent an army to Nāgadīpa to subdue this land. Hearing of this, the king here also dispatched forces.

13.

13.

Balaṃ [M 0.0341] datvāna senavha-rājasenāpatiṃ tadā;

Vallabhassa balene’sa, yujjhituṃ tattha pesayi.

Then, having given an army to the royal general named Sena, he sent him there to wage war with the forces of the Vallabha.

14.

14.

Gantvā senāpatī tattha, balene’tassa rājino;

Yujjhitvā taṃ vināsetvā, gaṇhi so yuddhamaṇḍale.

Having gone there, the general, with the army of this king, fought, destroyed the enemy, and seized the battlefield.

15.

15.

Asakkento imaṃ jetuṃ, rājā naṃ vallabhādayo;

Rājāno mittasambandhaṃ, laṃkindena akaṃsu te.

Unable to conquer this king, the Vallabha and other rulers made a friendly alliance with the Lord of Laṅkā.

16.

16.

Icchevaṃ rājino tejo, jambudīpamavatthari;

Pattharitvāna laṃkāyaṃ, ullaṅghitvāna sāgaraṃ.

Thus, the king's glory, having spread in Laṅkā and crossed the ocean, pervaded Jambudīpa.

17.

17.

Saddhammaṃ kathāyantānaṃ, katvā sammā na muttamaṃ;

Dhammaṃ sutvāna so rājā, pasanno buddhasāsane.

Having paid the highest honor to those who expound the True Dhamma, that king, upon hearing the Dhamma, became devoted to the Buddha's Dispensation.

18.

18.

Rājā so sannipātetvā, paṃsukūlikabhikkhavo;

Yācitvā attano gehaṃ, āṇāpetvāna sādhukaṃ.

That king, having gathered the Pāṃsukūlika bhikkhus and invited them to his own house, then gave careful instructions.

19.

19.

Āsanaṃ paññapetvāna, nisīdāpiya bhojanaṃ;

Dāpesi vipulaṃ suddhaṃ, sadā ekadine viya.

Having prepared seats and had them seated, he always provided abundant and pure food, as if for a single great occasion.

20.

20.

Anekabyañjanaṃ rājā-raññakānaṃ tapassinaṃ;

Pesesi bhojanaṃ suddhaṃ, mahagghaṃ vipulaṃ sadā.

The king always sent pure, costly, and abundant food with many delicacies to the forest-dwelling ascetics.

21.

21.

Vejjeva pesayitvāna, vilānānaṃ tapassinaṃ;

Santikaṃ so dayāvāso, tikicchāpesi niccaso.

That abode of compassion, having sent physicians to the sick ascetics, constantly had them treated.

22.

22.

Guḷāni ghanapākāni, lasuṇānaṃ rasāni ca;

Tambulamukhavāsañca, pacchabhatte adā sadā.

He always gave after the meal: jaggery, thick syrups, juices of garlic, and betel for perfuming the mouth.

23.

23.

Pattesu pūrayitvāna, lasuṇaṃ maricampi ca;

Pipphalisaṅgīverāni, guḷāni tiphalāni ca.

Having filled bowls with garlic, pepper, long pepper, ginger, jaggery, and the three myrobalans,

24.

24.

Ghataṃ telaṃ madhuñcāya, pāpurattharaṇāni ca;

Paṃsukūlikabhikkhūnaṃ, paccekaṃ sabbadā adā.

ghee, oil, and honey, as well as cloaks and rugs—these he always gave individually to the Pāṃsukūlika bhikkhus.

25.

25.

Cīvarādīni sabbāni, parikkhārāni bhūpati;

Kārāpetvāna dāpesi, bhikkhūnaṃ paṃsukulinaṃ.

The ruler, having had all requisites beginning with robes made, gave them to the Pāṃsukūlika bhikkhus.

26.

26.

Rājā mahāvihārasmiṃ, ekekassa hi bhikkhuno;

Paccekaṃ navavatthāni, cīvaratthāya dāpayi.

The king had new cloths given separately to each and every bhikkhu in the Mahāvihāra for the purpose of making robes.

27.

27.

Nikāyattayavāsīnaṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ lābhavāsinaṃ;

Tulābhāramadā dvīsu, vāresu samahīpati.

On two occasions, that great king gave a Tulābhāra gift to the bhikkhus dwelling in the three Nikāyas, who were accustomed to receiving offerings.

28.

28.

Rājā [M 0.0342] so nāgatebhogaṃ,

Rājāno saṅghabhogato;

Na gaṇhantūni pāsāṇe,

Likhāpetvā nidhāpayi.

That king had the following inscribed on stone and established: 'Let kings not take for themselves wealth set aside for the future from the property of the Saṅgha.'

29.

29.

Kathāpetvāna buddhassa, saraṇāni guṇenava;

Anāthehi ca tesañca, bhattavatthāni dāpayi.

Having caused the refuges and virtues of the Buddha to be taught, he provided food and clothing for the destitute and for them.

30.

30.

Dānasālaṃ karitvāna, hatthisālakabhūmiyaṃ;

Yācakānaṃ adā dānaṃ, tesañca sayanāsanaṃ.

Having built an alms-hall on the grounds of the elephant stables, he gave alms to supplicants and provided them with beds and seats.

31.

31.

Vejjasālāsu sabbāsu, bhesajjaṃ mañcakañca so;

Corānaṃ bandhanāgāre, niccaṃ bhattāni dāpayi.

In all dispensaries, he provided medicine and beds; and in the prisons, he regularly had food given to the criminals.

32.

32.

Vānarānaṃ varahānaṃ, migānaṃ sunakhāna ca;

Bhattaṃ pūvañca dāpesi, dayāvāso yathicchakaṃ.

He, an abode of compassion, provided food and cakes for monkeys, boars, deer, and dogs, according to their desire.

33.

33.

Rājā catuvihāresu, katvā so vīhirāsayo;

Yathicchitena gaṇhantu, anāthā iti dāpayi.

The king, having built rice granaries in the four monasteries, had them given out with the proclamation: 'Let the destitute take as they wish.'

34.

34.

Nānāpūjāhi pūjetvā, katvā maṅgalamuttamaṃ;

Kathāpesi ca bhikkhūhi, byattehi vinayaṃ tadā.

Having worshipped with various offerings and having performed the supreme auspicious ceremony, he then had the Vinaya recited by skilled monks.

35.

35.

Therena dhammamittena-sitthagāmakavāsinā;

Pūjayitvāna kāresi, abhidhammassa vaṇṇanaṃ.

Having paid homage, he caused a commentary on the Abhidhamma to be composed by the Elder Dhammamitta, a resident of the village of Sitthagāma.

36.

36.

Dāṭhānāgā’bhidhānena, therenā’raññavāsinā;

Laṃkālaṃkārabhūtena, abhidhammaṃ kathāpayi.

He had the Abhidhamma taught by the elder named Dāṭhānāga, a forest-dweller who was an ornament to Laṅkā.

37.

37.

Paṭṭakañcukapūjāhi, hemamālikacetiyaṃ;

Naccagītehi gandhehi, pupphehi vividhehi ca.

With offerings of silk cloth and tunics to the Hemamālika Cetiya; with dance, song, perfumes, and various flowers;

38.

38.

Dīpamālāhi dhūpehi, pūjayitvāna’nekadhā;

Tassa vatthāni bhājetvā, bhikkhūnaṃ dāpayī sayaṃ.

with garlands of lamps and with incense, having worshipped in many ways, he distributed those cloths and himself had them given to the monks.

39.

39.

Sadā so attano rajje, uyyānesu tahiṃtahiṃ;

Āṇāpetvāna pupphāni, pūjesi ratanattayaṃ.

Always in his own kingdom, in parks here and there, he commanded flowers to be brought and worshipped the Triple Gem.

40.

40.

Pāsādaṃ candanaṃ nāma, kātuṃ maricavaṭṭiyaṃ;

Akārambhañca bhikkhūnaṃ bhogagāme ca dāpayi.

He undertook to build a palace named Candana in Maricavaṭṭi, and had the Akārambha given to the monks in the village of Bhogagāma.

41.

41.

Kesadhātuṃ nidhāpetvā, karaṇḍaṃ ratanehi so;

Kārayitvāna pūjesi, ṭhapetvā tattha bhūpati.

That lord of the land had a jeweled casket made, and having enshrined the Hair Relic, placed it therein and worshipped it.

42.

42.

Soṇṇarajatapaṭṭehi[M 0.0343], thūpārāmamhi cetiyaṃ;

Chādāpetvā yathārajjaṃ, pūjaṃ kāresi bhūpati.

The lord of the land had the cetiya in the Thūpārāma covered with plates of gold and silver, and performed worship befitting his royal state.

43.

43.

Tasmiṃ dhātughare rājā, soṇṇadvāramakārayi;

Pajjalantaṃ sineruṃva, raṃsīhi sūriyassa so.

In that relic-chamber, the king had a golden door made, blazing like Mount Sineru with the rays of the sun.

44.

44.

Jhāpitaṃ coḷarājassa, balena padalañchane;

Catunnaṃ cetiyānaṃ so, ramanīyaṃ gharaṃ akā.

At Padalañchana, at the place burnt by the army of the Coḷa king, he built a delightful shrine-house for the four cetiyas.

45.

45.

Jhātaṃ nagaramajjhamhi, dāṭhādhātugharaṃ akā;

Dhammasaṅgaṇīgehañca, mahāpāḷiñca bhūpati.

In the middle of the city, at a place that had been burnt, the lord of the land built the house for the Tooth Relic, the Dhammasaṅgaṇī hall, and the Mahāpāli alms-hall.

46.

46.

Tambūlamaṇḍapaṃ katvā, tattha suṅkaṃ mahīpati;

Bhikkhūnaṃ theravaṃse so, bhesajjatthāya dāpayi.

Having built a betel pavilion, the king had the tax from that place given to the monks of the Theravāda lineage for the purpose of medicine.

47.

47.

Upassayaṃ karitvāna, mahāmaṅgalanāmakaṃ;

Theravaṃsamhi jātānaṃ, bhikkhunīnaṃ adāpayi.

Having built a residence named Mahāmaṅgala, he had it given to the nuns of the Theravāda lineage.

48.

48.

Mātulodayarājena, āraddhaṃ sādhunā tadā;

Niṭṭhāpesi mahīpālo, pāsādaṃ maṇināmakaṃ.

The great ruler completed the palace named Maṇi, which had then been diligently begun by King Mātulodaya.

49.

49.

Pariveṇāni cattāri, tasmiṃ jetavane tadā;

Kārāpayiṃsu cattāro, amaccā tassa rājino.

At that time, in the Jetavana monastery, four ministers of that king had four monastic residences built.

50.

50.

Rañño kittisamādevī, kittināmā manoramā;

Pariveṇaṃ akārāmaṃ, thūpārāmassa pacchato.

The king's delightful queen, Kittī by name, built a monastic residence behind the Thūpārāma.

51.

51.

Sā tasmiṃ pariveṇe ca, akā kappāsagāmake;

Cīvaracetiye ceva, tisso pokkharaṇī suci.

In that monastic residence, she also established a small cotton-producing village, a Cīvara-cetiya, and three pure ponds.

52.

52.

Dvādasaratanāyāmaṃ, dhajaṃ soṇṇamayañca sā;

Pūjesi puññasambhāraṃ, hemamālika cetiye.

She made an offering at the Hemamālika Cetiya of a golden banner twelve cubits in length, an accumulation of merit.

53.

53.

Gihīnaṃ vajjasālañca, putto tassā pureakā;

Guṇavāsakkasenānī, bhikkhūnañca purābahi.

Her son, the general Guṇavāsakka, built a hall for laypeople in the city, and a residence for monks outside the city.

54.

54.

Rājā catuvihāresu, dibbapāsādasannibhe;

Maṇḍape kārayitvāna, dhātupūjā anekadhā.

The king, having had pavilions resembling divine palaces built in the four great monasteries, performed various kinds of worship for the relics.

55.

55.

Vassamekamatikkamma, kārāpetvā mahīpati;

Cārittaṃ pubbarājūnaṃ, paripālesi sādhukaṃ.

Having passed one year, the great ruler had these works completed, and he diligently maintained the traditions of former kings.

56.

56.

Evamādīni puññāni, uḷārāni anekadhā;

Katvā soḷasame vasse, rājā so tidivaṃ gato.

Having thus performed these and other great and manifold meritorious deeds, in the sixteenth year that king went to heaven.

57.

57.

Jāto [M 0.0344] paṭicca taṃ rājaṃ, senā dvādasavassiko;

Kāliṅgadeviyā putto, pattarajjo tadā ahu.

Following that king, Sena, the son of Queen Kāliṅga, being twelve years of age, then attained the kingship.

58.

58.

Udayassa kaniṭṭhassa, yuvarājapadaṃ adā;

Pitu senāpati seno, tassa senāpati ahu.

He gave the position of crown prince to his younger brother, Udaya. Sena, who had been his father's general, became his general.

59.

59.

Paccantaṃ balamādāya, gate senāpatimhi so;

Mātarā saha vattantaṃ, kaṇiṭṭhaṃ tassa bhātaraṃ.

When that general had departed, taking a border force, he dealt with his younger brother, who was living with their mother.

60.

60.

Mārāpetvā mahāmallaṃ, akā senāpatiṃ tadā;

Amaccaṃ udayaṃ nāma, sakaṃ vacanakārakaṃ.

Having caused the great warrior to be killed, he then made the minister named Udaya, who was obedient to his word, the general.

61.

61.

Taṃ sutvā kupito hutvā, seno senāpati tadā;

Balamādāya āgañchi, gaṇhissāmīti sattavo.

Hearing that, Sena the general then became angry; taking his army, he came, thinking, 'I will seize the enemy.'

62.

62.

Sutvāna taṃ mahīpālo, katavantaṃ vācamattano;

Rakkhāmi taṃ amaccanti, gato nikkhamma rohaṇaṃ.

Hearing that, the lord of the earth, thinking, 'I will protect that minister who carried out my command,' departed and went to Rohaṇa.

63.

63.

Tassa māyā nivattitvā, yuvarājañca rājiniṃ;

Ādāya kupitā tena āṇāpesi camūpatiṃ.

His stratagem having failed, she, angered by him, took the crown prince and the queen and commanded the commander of the army.

64.

64.

Tāya so saṅgahītova, damiḷe sannipātiya;

Datvā janapadaṃ tesaṃ, puṭatthinagare vasī.

Having been won over by her, he assembled the Damiḷas, and having given the country to them, he dwelt in the city of Puḷatthinagara.

65.

65.

Yujjhituṃ tena so rājā, balaṃ pesesi rohaṇā;

Senāpati vināsesi, sabbaṃ taṃ rājino balaṃ.

To fight with him, that king sent an army from Rohaṇa; the general destroyed all of that king's forces.

66.

66.

Damiḷā te janapadaṃ, pīḷetvā rakkhasā viya;

Vilumpitvāna gaṇhanti, narānaṃ santakaṃ tadā.

Those Damiḷas, oppressing the country like ogres, then plundered and seized the possessions of the people.

67.

67.

Khittā manussā gantvāna, rohaṇaṃ rājasantikaṃ;

Nivedesuṃ pavattiṃ taṃ, mantetvā sacīvehi so.

The distressed people went to the king's presence in Rohaṇa; they reported that event, and he consulted with his ministers.

68.

68.

Rakkhituṃ sāsanaṃ raṭṭhaṃ, tampahāya camūpatiṃ;

Sandhiṃ katvāna senena, puḷatthinagaraṃ agā.

To protect the Dispensation and the kingdom, abandoning that army chief and having made peace with Sena, he went to the city of Puḷatthinagara.

69.

69.

Mahesiṃ attajaṃ katvā, pāletuṃ vaṃsamattano;

Puttaṃ uppādayitvāna, kassapaṃ nāma uttamaṃ.

To preserve his own lineage, he made his daughter the chief queen and begot an excellent son named Kassapa.

70.

70.

Vasante tattha laṃkinde, ahitā vallabhā janā;

Alabhantā suraṃ pātu-māriyā tassa santike.

While the lord of Laṅkā was dwelling there, people, both hostile and friendly, unable to obtain liquor to drink, approached him.

71.

71.

Majjapāne guṇaṃ vatvā, pāyesuṃ taṃ mahīpatiṃ;

Pivitvā majjapānaṃ so, mattabyāḷo ahu tadā.

Praising the qualities of liquor, they made that lord of the earth drink; having drunk the liquor, he then became like an intoxicated wild beast.

72.

72.

Āhārānaṃ [M 0.0345] khayaṃ patvā, cajitvā dullabhaṃ padaṃ;

Mato so dasame vasse, taruṇoyeva bhūpati.

Reaching the end of his sustenance, relinquishing the state so hard to attain, the king died in his tenth year, while still a youth.

73.

73.

Ito viditvā khalupāpamitta-

Vidheyyabhāvaṃ parihāni hetuṃ;

Sukhattitoyeva ida vā huraṃ vā;

Jahantu te ghoravisaṃ’va bālaṃ.

Knowing from this that being under the sway of wicked friends is a cause of decline, those who desire happiness, whether in this world or the next, should shun a fool as they would a deadly poison.

Sujanappasādasaṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃseti rājako nāma

In the Mahāvaṃsa, composed for the serene faith and spiritual emotion of good people, this is the chapter named 'The Prince'.

Dvipaññāsatimo paricchedo.

The Fifty-second Chapter.

Tivaññāsatima paccheda

The Fifty-third Chapter.

Laṃkāviloponāma

The Plundering of Laṅkā.

1.

1.

Mahindo taṃ kaṇiṭṭho so, rājaputto tadaccaye;

Ussāpiya setacchatta-manurādhapure vare.

After his death, his younger brother, the prince Mahinda, raised the white parasol in the excellent city of Anurādhapura.

2.

2.

Sena senānīnā’nīta desantarajanā kule;

Tattha vāsamakappesi, kicchena dasavacchare.

For ten years he dwelt there with difficulty among the families of people from foreign lands who had been brought by the general Sena.

3.

3.

Apetanīti maggassa, mudubhūtassa sabbaso;

Uppādabhāgaṃ nādaṃsu, tassa jānapadā tadā.

Since his path of policy was abandoned and he had become completely soft, the country-folk then did not give him his share of the revenue.

4.

4.

Accantaṃ khīṇacitto so, vassamhi dasame vibhū;

Vuttidānena nāsakkhi, saṅgahetuṃ sakaṃ balaṃ.

Utterly disheartened, in the tenth year, the lord was not able to hold his forces together by providing sustenance.

5.

5.

Aladdha vuttino sabbe, keraḷā sahitā tato;

Na vuttidānaṃ no yāva, hoti mātāva bhuñjatu.

Then all the Keraḷas, united and having received no livelihood, said: 'Until livelihood is given to us, let our mother eat!'

6.

6.

Iti rājagharadvāre, sāhasekarasā bhusaṃ;

Cāpahatā nisīdiṃsu, sannaddhachurikāyudhā.

Thus, at the gate of the royal palace, exceedingly delighting in violence, they sat down, with bows in hand and armed with daggers.

7.

7.

Hatthasāraṃ samādāya, te vivañciya bhūpati;

Ummaggato viniggamma, turito rohaṇaṃ agā.

The king, deceiving them, took his best elephant, and escaping through a secret passage, swiftly went to Rohaṇa.

8.

8.

Sīdupabbatagāmamhi[M 0.0346], khandhavāraṃ nibandhiya;

Bhātu jāyamma hesitte, ṭhapetvā so tahiṃ vasī.

In the village of Sīdupabbata, having established a camp, he made his brother's wife the chief queen and dwelt there.

9.

9.

Na cirasseva tassāya, matā yasamahīpati;

Mahesitte nivesesi, sakabhātussa dhītaraṃ.

Not long after she had died, the glorious king installed his own brother's daughter in the rank of chief queen.

10.

10.

Deviyā tāya sañjāte, sute kassapanāmake;

Ajjhāvuttaṃ vihāyā’tha, khandhāvāraṃ mahīmati.

When a son named Kassapa was born to that queen, the wise king then left his residence and went to the encampment.

11.

11.

Kārayitvāna nagaraṃ, kappagallakagāmake;

Adhipaccaṃ pavattento, rohaṇe suciraṃ vasī.

Having caused a city to be built in the village of Kappagallaka, he lived in Rohaṇa for a very long time, wielding sovereignty.

12.

12.

Tato sesesu ṭhānesu, keraḷā sīhaḷā tadā;

Kaṇṇāṭā ca yathākāma-mādhipaccaṃ pavattayuṃ.

Thereafter, in the remaining regions, the Keraḷas, the Sīhaḷas, and the Kaṇṇāṭas exercised sovereignty as they pleased.

13.

13.

Athassa vāṇijo eko, paratīraṃ idhāgato;

Gantvā pavattiṃ laṃkāya, coḷarañño nivedayi.

Then a certain merchant who had come here from the other shore, went and reported the affairs of Laṅkā to the Coḷa king.

14.

14.

Sotaṃ suṇitvā pesesi, laṃkāgahaṇamānaso;

Balaṃ mahantaṃ balavā, taṃ khippaṃ laṃkamotari.

Hearing that news, the powerful one, with a mind to seize Laṅkā, sent a great army; it quickly descended upon Laṅkā.

15.

15.

Paṭṭhāyo tiṇṇaṭhānamhā, viheṭhentaṃ bahū jane;

Anukkamena taṃ coḷa-balaṃ rohaṇamajjhagā.

Setting out from three places and harassing many people, that Coḷa army gradually reached the midst of Rohaṇa.

16.

16.

Chattiṃse rājino vasse, mahesiṃ ratanāni ca;

Makuṭañca kamāyātaṃ, sabbamābharaṇaṃ tathā.

In the thirty-sixth year of the king, the chief queen, the jewels, the crown that had come down by succession, and likewise all the regalia.

17.

17.

Amūlikañcavajira-valayaṃ devadattiyaṃ;

Acchejjacchurikaṃ chinna-paṭṭikā dhātukañca te.

The priceless diamond bracelet, the sword given by a deva, the unbreakable dagger, the severed sash, and those relics.

18.

18.

Paviṭṭhaṃ vanaduggamhi, bhayātañca mahīpatiṃ;

Jīvaggāhamagaṇhiṃsu, sandhilesampadassiya.

They seized alive the terrified king, who had entered the impenetrable forest, by revealing a secret passage.

19.

19.

Mahīpālaṃ dhanaṃ tañca, sabbaṃ hatthagataṃ tato;

Pesayiṃsu lahuṃ coḷa-mahīpālassa santikaṃ.

The king, that wealth, and all that had fallen into their hands, they then swiftly sent to the presence of the Coḷa king.

20.

20.

Nikāyattitaye dhātu-gabbhe laṃkātale khile;

Mahārahe suvaṇṇādi-paṭibimbe ca’nappake.

In the relic-chambers of the three Nikāyas throughout the land of Laṅkā, and the many priceless images of gold and other materials.

21.

21.

Bhinditvā sahasā sabbe, vihāre ca tahiṃ tahiṃ;

Yatho johārino yakkhā, laṅkāyaṃ sāramaggahuṃ.

Having suddenly broken into all the vihāras here and there, they seized the wealth of Laṅkā, like yakkhas stealing its vital essence.

22.

22.

Te coḷā rājaraṭṭhaṃ taṃ, pulatthipuranissitā;

Rakkhapāsāṇakaṇḍavha, ṭhānāvadhimabhuñjisuṃ.

Those Coḷas, based in Pulatthipura, ruled that royal kingdom up to the boundaries of the places called Rakkha, Pāsāṇa, and Kaṇḍa.

23.

23.

Taṃ [M 0.0347] kumārakamādāya, kassapaṃ raṭṭhavāsino;

Vaḍḍhenti coḷabhayato, gopayantā susādarā.

The inhabitants of the country took that prince, Kassapa, and, protecting him from fear of the Coḷas, raised him with great care.

24.

24.

Coḷarājā kumāraṃ taṃ, sutvā dvādasavassikaṃ;

Gahaṇatthāya pesesi, mahāmacce mahābale.

The Coḷa king, hearing that the prince was twelve years of age, sent great ministers of mighty strength to capture him.

25.

25.

Ūnaṃ pañcasahassena, yodhalakkhaṃ samādiya;

Sabbaṃ te rohaṇaṃ desaṃ, saṅkhobhesu mito tato.

Having taken ninety-five thousand warriors, they threw the entire country of Rohaṇa into confusion here and there.

26.

26.

Kittināmo’tha sacivo, makkhakudrūsavāsiko;

Muddhanāmo tathāmacco, māragallakavāsiko.

Then there was a minister named Kitti, a resident of Makkhakudrūsa, and likewise a minister named Buddha, a resident of Māragallaka.

27.

27.

Ubhopi te mahāvīrā, yuddhopāyavicakkhaṇā;

Coḷasenaṃ vināsetu-maccantakatanicchayā.

Both those great heroes, skilled in the stratagems of war, made a firm resolve to utterly destroy the Coḷa army.

28.

28.

Paluṭṭhagirināmamhi, ṭhāne dugge nivesiya;

Katvā chamāsaṃ saṅgāmaṃ, haniṃsu damiḷe bahūṃ.

Having established themselves in a stronghold on the mountain named Paluṭṭha, and having waged war for six months, they slew many Tamils.

29.

29.

Hatāvasiṭṭhā coḷātā, raṇe tasmiṃ bhayadditā;

Palāyitvā yathāpubbaṃ, pulattipuramāvasuṃ.

The remaining Coḷas, afflicted by fear in that battle, fled and, as before, took up residence in Pulatthipura.

30.

30.

Kumāro jayito disvā, ubho te sacive tadā;

Haṭṭhatuṭṭho “varaṃ tātā, gaṇhathā”ti sa cabravī.

The victorious prince, seeing both those ministers, then, joyful and delighted, said: 'My good sirs, accept a boon!'

31.

31.

Buddho paveṇigāmaṃ so, varaṃ yācittha kittiko;

Saṅghikaṃ gahitaṃ bhāgaṃ, vissajjetuṃ varaṃ vari.

That Buddha asked for his ancestral village as a boon; Kitti chose the boon to have the portion seized from the Saṅgha released.

32.

32.

Rājaputtavarāladdha-varā’maccavarā tadā;

Niddarā sādarā vīrā, pāde vandiṃsu tassa te.

Then those excellent ministers, who had received boons from the excellent prince, being fearless, respectful, and heroic, paid homage at his feet.

33.

33.

Rājā dvādasavassāni, vasitvā coḷamaṇḍale;

Aṭṭhatālīsavassamhi, mahindo so divaṃgato.

That king, Mahinda, having dwelt in the Coḷa country for twelve years, passed away in the forty-eighth year of his reign.

34.

34.

Pamāda dosānagatena evaṃ,

Laddhā’pi bhogānanathirā bhavanti;

Iccappamaṃdaṃ hitamāsasāno,

Niccaṃ suviññūsusamā careyya.

Thus, through the fault of heedlessness, even possessions that have been gained become unstable. Therefore, the wise person, desiring heedfulness as his welfare, should ever conduct himself well.

Sujanappasādasaṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Mahāvaṃsa, composed for the faith and spiritual urgency of the virtuous.

Laṃkāvilopo nāma

The Plundering of Laṅkā.

Tipaññāsatimo paricchedo.

The Fifty-third Chapter.

Catupaññāsatima pariccheda

The Fifty-fourth Chapter.

Cha rājakonāma

The Six Kings.

1.

1.

Katvā [M 0.0348] vikkamma bāhū’ti, nāma bhūpālasūnuto;

Tassāṇāya pavattiṃsu, sādaraṃ sīhaḷā khilā.

A king's son, named Vikkamabāhu for having shown prowess with his arms, arose; all the Sīhaḷas respectfully submitted to his command.

2.

2.

So rājā damiḷe hantuṃ, dhanaṃ sañciya’nekādhā;

Saṅgahaṃ sevakānañca, kurumāno yathocitaṃ.

That king, in order to slay the Tamils, amassed wealth in many ways and bestowed favours upon his servants as was fitting.

3.

3.

Alaṅkārakirīṭāni, chattasīhāsanāni ca;

Kārayitvā’bhisekatthaṃ, sacivehā’bhiyācito.

Having had ornaments, crowns, parasols, and thrones made for the purpose of consecration, he was entreated by the ministers.

4.

4.

Na yāva rājaraṭṭhassa, gahaṇaṃ hoti tāva me;

Chattussāpanakammena, kiṃ tenā’ti vivāriya.

He refused, saying: 'So long as the royal kingdom has not been taken, what use to me is this act of raising the parasol?'

5.

5.

Sataṃ narasahassānaṃ, saṅkaletvā mahabbalo;

Saṅgāmārabbha kālamhi, vātarogābhipīḷito.

Having assembled a hundred thousand men, the mighty one, at the time of commencing battle, was afflicted by a wind-disease.

6.

6.

Yujjhituṃ samayo neti, dvādase vacchare lahuṃ;

Upecca devanagaraṃ, gañchidevasahabyataṃ.

The time to fight did not come for him. Swiftly, in the twelfth year, having approached the city of the gods, he went to the fellowship of the gods.

7.

7.

Kittināmo ca sacivo, senāpaccamadhiṭṭhito;

Rajjatthiko dinānaṭṭha, nijāṇaṃ sampavattayi.

And a minister named Kitti, appointed as commander of the army and desiring the kingdom, set his own command in motion day and night.

8.

8.

Ghātetvā taṃ mahālāna-kittināmo mahabbalo;

Patvā’bhisekaṃ bhuñjanto, desaṃ taṃ rohaṇavhayaṃ.

The mighty Mahālāna-Kitti, having slain him, attained consecration and governed that land called Rohaṇa.

9.

9.

Saṃvaccharamhi tatiye, coḷayuddhe parājito;

Sahatthena sakaṃ sīsaṃ, chinditvā sahasā mari.

In the third year, defeated in the Cola war, he severed his own head with his own hand and died instantly.

10.

10.

Tadāpite kirīṭādi-dhanasāraṃ samādiya;

Pesesuṃ damiḷā coḷa-mahīpālassa santikaṃ.

Then the Tamils, having collected the crowns and other valuable treasures, sent them to the presence of the Cola king.

11.

11.

Bhayā saraṭṭhaṃ hitvā’tha, duṭṭhadese vasaṃ tadā;

Eko vikkamapaṇḍūti, vissuto patthivattajo.

Then a certain king's son, renowned as Vikkamapaṇḍu, having abandoned his own country out of fear, was dwelling in a hostile land.

12.

12.

Viññātalaṅkāvuttanto, desamāgamma rohaṇaṃ;

Kāḷatitthe vasaṃ vassa-mekaṃ rajjamakārayi.

Having learned of the affairs in Laṅkā, he came to the Rohaṇa country. Dwelling at Kāḷatittha, he ruled the kingdom for one year.

13.

13.

Rāmanvayasamubbhūto[M 0.0349], tadāyujjha purāgato;

Jagatī pālanāmena, vissuto bhūbhujattajo.

Then a king's son renowned by the name Jagatīpāla, born in the lineage of Rāma and having come from the city of Ayojjhā, was in that place.

14.

14.

Raṇe vikkamapaṇḍutaṃ, ghātāpetvā mahabbalo;

Tato cattāri vassāni, rajjaṃ kāresi rohaṇe.

The mighty one, having caused Vikkamapaṇḍu to be slain in battle, then ruled in Rohaṇa for four years.

15.

15.

Tampi coḷāraṇe hantvā, mahesiṃ dhītarā saha;

Vittasārañca sākalaṃ, coḷaraṭṭhamapesayuṃ.

Having slain him also in a battle with the Colas, they sent his queen, together with her daughter and all the valuable treasure, to the Cola country.

16.

16.

Rājā parakkamo nāma, paṇḍurājasuto tato;

Akā vassadvayaṃ coḷā, ghātesuṃ tampi yujjhiya.

Then a king named Parakkama, son of the Paṇḍu king, ruled for two years. The Colas fought and slew him also.

17.

17.

Ime bhusaṃ lobhabalābhibhūtā,

Gatā asesā vivasā vināsaṃ;

Iccevamaññāya sadā sapañño,

Taṇhakkhayeyeva ratiṃ kareyya.

These men, greatly overcome by the power of greed, went completely and helplessly to ruin. Thus, always understanding this, the wise one should delight only in the destruction of craving.

Sujanappasādasaṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Mahāvaṃsa, composed for the purpose of serene joy and spiritual urgency of the virtuous.

Cha rājako nāma

The Six Kings

Catupaññāsatimo paricchedo.

The Fifty-fourth Chapter.

Pañcapaññāsatima pariccheda

The Fifty-fifth Chapter

Rohaṇārāti vijayonāma

The Victory over the Enemies of Rohaṇa

1.

1.

Lokanāmo camūnātho, makkhakudrūsavāsiko;

Saccapaṭiñño dhītimā, coḷadappavighātano.

An army commander named Loka, a resident of Makkhakudrūsa, was true to his pledge, resolute, and a destroyer of the Colas' arrogance.

2.

2.

Abhibhūya jane patvā, rajjaṃ rohaṇamaṇḍale;

Vasī kājaragāmamhi, cārittavidhikovido.

Having subdued the people and attained sovereignty in the Rohaṇa region, he, skilled in the rules of conduct, dwelt in Kājaragāma.

3.

3.

Ahu tadā kittināmo, rājaputto mahabbalo;

Tassa vaṃsādisampattī, nupubbena pavuccate.

At that time there was a prince of great power named Kitti. His lineage and other accomplishments are now recounted in due order.

4.

4.

Suto kassapabhūpassa, māṇanāmena vissuto;

Ādipādo ahu dhīro, sadācāravibhūsito.

The son of King Kassapa, renowned by the name Māna, was an Ādipāda, wise and always adorned with good conduct.

5.

5.

Tassā’tha [M 0.0350] jeṭṭhako bhātā, māṇavammo mahāmati;

Gokaṇṇakasamīpaṭṭha-nadītīre nisīdiya.

Then her eldest brother, the wise Māṇavamma, sat down on the bank of a river situated near Gokaṇṇaka.

6.

6.

Katamantupacāro so, yathāvidhimasesato;

Akkhamālaṃ gahetvāna, mantaṃ jappitumārabhi.

He, having performed the ritual procedure for the mantra completely and according to rule, took up his rosary and began to recite the mantra.

7.

7.

Kumāro kira bhattagge, pāturāsi savāhano;

Sikhaṇḍi mukhatuṇḍena, balipaṭṭaṃ vikhaṇḍiya.

The god Kumāra, it is said, appeared at the mealtime with his mount; the peacock, with its beak, shattered the offering plate.

8.

8.

Sacchiddake nāḷikera-kapāle viccunodake;

Lūkhe jalamapassanto, japantassa mukhaṃgato.

Not seeing water in the dry, perforated coconut shell, which contained but little water, it went to the mouth of the one who was reciting.

9.

9.

Tato bhāviniṃ siddhi, mapekkhaṃ nayanaṃ sakaṃ;

Tassopanesi, nibbhijja, sopi taṃ sahasāpici.

Then she, expecting the future success, pierced her own eye and offered it to him; and he too drank from it quickly.

10.

10.

Kumāro tassa santuṭṭho, kumārassābhipatthitaṃ;

Varaṃ padāya nabhasā, rājamāno gato tato.

The god Kumāra, pleased with him, granted the prince's desired boon and then, shining, departed through the sky.

11.

11.

Bhinnekanayanaṃ disvā, sacivātaṃ paro disuṃ;

Varalābhaṃ pakāsetvā, samassāsesi so jane.

Seeing the one with a pierced eye, the ministers pointed to the other; having announced the excellent gain, he consoled the people.

12.

12.

Tato so sacivātassa, santuṭṭhārādhayiṃsu taṃ;

Anurādhapuraṃ patvā, bhiseko kāriyo iti.

Then those ministers, pleased, entreated him; having arrived at Anurādhapura, they said, 'The consecration should be performed.'

13.

13.

Attho ko mamarajjena, vikalaṅgassa sampati;

Tapokammaṃ karissāmi, pabbajjamupagammahaṃ.

'What use is kingship to me, now that I am deformed? I will undertake ascetic practice, having gone forth into homelessness.'

14.

14.

Kaṇiṭṭho māṇanāmo ca, laṅkārajjaṃ kamāgataṃ;

Pāletu iti so rajjaṃ, sampattaṃ sampaṭikkhipi.

'Let the youngest, named Māṇa, rule the kingdom of Laṅkā that has come in due course.' Thus he rejected the kingdom that had come to him.

15.

15.

Viññātacittasañcārā, sacivā tassa sabbathā;

Vattumetaṃ kaṇiṭṭhassa, pesesuṃ purise tadā.

Knowing the movements of his mind, his ministers then sent men in every way to say this to the youngest.

16.

16.

Sutvā taṃ sīghamāgamma, passitvā sakabhātaraṃ;

Patitvā pādamūlamhi, bahuṃ kandiya rodiya.

Hearing that, he came quickly, and seeing his own brother, he fell at his feet, weeping and lamenting greatly.

17.

17.

Jeṭṭhena bhātarā saddhi-manurādhapuraṃ gato;

Makuṭaṃ tattha dhāresi, jeṭṭhacittānuvattako.

Together with his elder brother, he went to Anurādhapura. There he wore the crown, acting in accordance with his elder brother's mind.

18.

18.

Tato’bhayagiriṃ gantvā, pabbajjaṃ sakabhātuno;

Yata yo tattha yācittha, bahumānapurassaraṃ.

Then, having gone to Abhayagiri, he requested with great respect the going-forth for his own brother from the ascetics there.

19.

19.

Tato te yatayo tassa, pabbajjamupasampadaṃ;

Akaṃsu vikalaṅgassa, sikkhāpadanirādarā.

Then those ascetics, disregarding the training rules, performed the going-forth and full admission for him, the deformed one.

20.

20.

Pariveṇamuttaroḷa-muḷāraṃ [M 0.0351] tassa kāriya;

Katvā taṃ pariveṇassa, sāmikaṃ dharaṇī pati.

Having had a splendid dwelling named Uttaroḷa built for him, the lord of the earth made him the master of that dwelling.

21.

21.

Bhikkhūnaṃ chasataṃ tattha, vidhāya tadadhīnakaṃ;

Parihāre adā tassa, pessavagge ca pañca so.

Having placed six hundred monks there under his authority, he granted him immunities and five groups of attendants.

22.

22.

Samappesi ca so nānā-sippakammavicakkhaṇe;

Jane cākā tadāyatte, so dāṭhādhāturakkhiye.

And he appointed people skilled in various crafts and arts, and also made those who were to protect the Tooth Relic dependent on him.

23.

23.

Tassevādakarā’hesuṃ, bhikkhū’bhayagirimhi te;

Rājā ca lokaṃ pālesi, sammā tassānusiṭṭhiyā.

Those monks at Abhayagiri were indeed his supporters; and the king ruled the world righteously, according to his instruction.

24.

24.

Janā tabbaṃsajā keci, taṃ rajjanirapekkhakā;

Nivasiṃsu yathākāmaṃ, mahāsāmi padaṃsitā.

Some people born of that lineage, being indifferent to that kingship, lived as they pleased, relying on the position of the great lord.

25.

25.

Etassa māṇavammassa, rañño dhammanayaññuno;

Aggabodhikumārādi-puttanattukkamāgate.

Of this King Māṇavamma, who knew the way of the Dhamma, and of the lineage that came in succession through sons and grandsons, beginning with Aggabodhi Kumāra.

26.

26.

Vaṃse visuddhe jātassa, bhūpālanvayamuddhani;

Samāsoḷasakaṅkāyaṃ, sammā rajjānusāsino.

Of him who was born in a pure lineage, at the head of a royal dynasty, rightly governing the kingdom for sixteen years.

27.

27.

Mahīpassa mahindassa, duve mākuladhītaro;

Devalā lokikā cāti, nāmato vissutā subhā.

King Mahinda had two beautiful and renowned daughters of the Mākula clan, named Devalā and Lokikā.

28.

28.

Etāsu dvīsu dhītāsu, lokikā mātulattajaṃ;

Paṭicca rājatanayaṃ, subhaṃ kassapanāmakaṃ.

Of these two daughters, Lokikā married her maternal uncle's son, the handsome prince named Kassapa.

29.

29.

Sā moggallāna lokavhe, putte dve labhi sobhane;

Tesu jeṭṭhasuto loka-sāsanādhārakovido.

She bore two splendid sons, named Moggallāna and Loka; among them, the elder son was skilled as a supporter of the world and the Dispensation.

30.

30.

Mahāsāmīti paññāto, saṅghupāsanapālayo;

Nekasāraguṇāvāso, vāsaṃ kappesi rohaṇe.

He was known as Mahāsāmī, a supporter and protector of the Saṅgha; an abode of many excellent qualities, he resided in Rohaṇa.

31.

31.

Dāṭhopatissa rājassa, nattā sugatasāsane;

Pabbajjūpagato saddho, dhutavā sīlasaṃvuto.

The grandson of King Dāṭhopatissa, faithful to the Dispensation of the Sugata, having gone forth, he practiced the ascetic observances and was restrained in virtue.

32.

32.

Pahitatto vicittoso, pantasenāsane vasī;

Guṇaṃ sabbattha vaṇṇesuṃ, tasmiṃ devā pasīdiya.

With a resolute mind and discerning, he dwelt in secluded lodgings; the gods, pleased with him, praised his virtues everywhere.

33.

33.

Guṇaṃ suṇitvā laṃkindo, tadā sabbattha patthaṭaṃ;

Upasaṅkamma taṃ natvā, kātumattānusāsanaṃ.

Hearing of his virtue, which was then spread everywhere, the King of Laṅkā approached him, paid homage, and sought to receive instruction for himself.

34.

34.

Ārādhayamanicchantaṃ, yācitvāna punappunaṃ;

Ānīya vāsayitvā taṃ, pāsāde sādhukārite.

He entreated him, though he was unwilling, and having begged again and again, brought him and had him reside in a well-built palace.

35.

35.

Yatissarassa [M 0.0352] vasato, kattha rājāguṇappiyo;

Tassānusiṭṭhimaggaṭṭho, lokaṃ dhammena pālayi.

While the chief of ascetics was residing there, the king, who was fond of virtues, standing on the path of his instruction, ruled the world according to the Dhamma.

36.

36.

Uddissārādhanaṃ sammā, laṃkindena kataṃ tadā;

Selantarābhinikkhamma, yatindo so dayānugo.

In response to the entreaty properly made then by the King of Laṅkā, that compassionate chief of ascetics emerged from Selantara.

37.

37.

Yato bhikkhū samūhetvā, vāsaṃ kappesi yattha so;

Selantarasamūho’ti, vikkhyātiṃ so tato gato.

Since he gathered monks and established a residence where he dwelt, that place thenceforth became renowned as the 'Selantara Assembly'.

38.

38.

Tato paṭṭhāya vāsetvā, rattiyaṃ devapalliyaṃ;

Devatānumataṃ bhikkhuṃ, mūlaṭhāne ṭhapenti hi.

From then on, having caused the monk approved by the deities to reside at night in the divine enclosure, they indeed placed him at the root-place.

39.

39.

Mūlattamāvasantānaṃ, yatīnamanusāsanā;

Laṃkissarā pavattanti, pālentā lokasāsanaṃ.

By the instruction of the ascetics dwelling at the root-place, the lords of Laṅkā proceeded, protecting the world and the Dispensation.

40.

40.

Tassa dāṭhopatissassa, vaṃsajaṃ rājaputtakaṃ;

Bodhiṃ paṭicca tabbaṃsā, buddhanāmā kumārikā.

The princess named Buddhā, from that same lineage, having married the prince named Bodhi, born of the lineage of that Dāṭhopatissa...

41.

41.

Alattha lokitaṃ nāma, dhītaraṃ varalakkhaṇaṃ;

Kālena sā padinnā’si, moggallānassa dhīmato.

She obtained a daughter named Lokitā, of excellent marks; in time she was given to the wise Moggallāna.

42.

42.

Sā taṃ paṭicca kittiñca, mittaṃ nāma kumārikaṃ;

Mahindaṃ rakkhitaṃ cāpi, latittha caturo pajā.

By him, she bore four children: Kitti, the maiden named Mittā, and also Mahinda and Rakkhita.

43.

43.

Ahu jeṭṭhasuto dhīro, vīro terasavassiko;

Katahattho visesena, dhanusippamhi so tato.

The elder son was wise, a hero, thirteen years old, and then especially skilled in the art of archery.

44.

44.

Kathaṃ laṅkaṃ gahessāmi, dūretvā’rāti kaṇṭakaṃ;

Iti cintāparogāme, mūlasālavhaye vasī.

“How shall I seize Laṅkā, having removed the enemy thorn?” Thus pondering, he dwelt in the village named Mūlasāla.

45.

45.

Eko mahābalo vīro, buddharājoti vissuto;

Vilomavattī hutvāna, lokasenānino tadā.

A certain mighty hero, famed as Buddharāja, then acted in opposition to the commander Loka.

46.

46.

Palāto cuṇṇasālavhaṃ, khippaṃ janapadaṃ tahiṃ;

Kittādike jane neke, vase vattiya sabbathā.

Having fled swiftly to the country named Cuṇṇasāla, he there brought many people, such as Kitta, completely under his sway.

47.

47.

Saddhiṃ bandhūhi saṅgāma-sūrehi bahukehi so;

Malayācalapādesu, vasī duppasaho tadā.

With many kinsmen, heroes in battle, he, being hard to subdue, then dwelt at the foot of Malayācala.

48.

48.

Tassa’ntikamupāgamma, saṃvaccharikanāyako;

Saṅgho nāma kumārassa, sarūpaṃ sādhuvaṃ bravi.

Approaching him, the yearly leader named Saṅgha spoke well of the prince’s true nature.

49.

49.

Mahāsāmissa tanayo, jeṭṭho kitti sanāmako;

Dhaññalakkhaṇasampanno, sampannamativikkamo.

The eldest son of Mahāsāmi, named Kitti, was endowed with auspicious marks, and accomplished in intellect and valor.

50.

50.

Jambudīpepi [M 0.0353] taṃ rajjaṃ, kattumekātapattakaṃ;

Samatthoti vicintepi, laṅkādīpamhi kā kathā.

Even if one considers him capable of establishing sole sovereignty in Jambudīpa, what need is there to speak of the isle of Laṅkā?

51.

51.

Tassa so vacanaṃ sutvā, sevitabbo kumārako;

Iti nicchiya pesesi, kumārassa’ntikaṃ jane.

Hearing his words, he decided, “This prince should be served,” and sent people to the prince.

52.

52.

Suṇitvā so vaco tesaṃ, nivattanabhayā vibhū;

Ajānahaṃ pitunnaṃ so, vīro dhanusahāyako.

Hearing their words, the mighty hero, the wielder of the bow, fearing retreat, declared: 'I do not know my fathers.'

53.

53.

Gehā nikkhamma passanto, sunimittāninekadhā;

Agālahuṃ sarīvagga-piṭṭhigāmaṃ mahāmati.

Leaving home, beholding many auspicious signs, the great-minded one swiftly went to the village of Sarīvagga-piṭṭhi.

54.

54.

Tahiṃ so nivasaṃ vīro, pesayitvā sasevake;

Vipakkhādhiṭṭhitaṃ jesi, bodhivālavhagāmakaṃ.

Dwelling there, the hero, having sent forth his own attendants, conquered the opponent-held village named Bodhivāla.

55.

55.

Tato’bhimānī senānī, senaṃ so tattha pesayi;

Sā parikkhipataṃ gāmaṃ, saṅgāmāya samārabhī.

Then the arrogant general dispatched his army there; that army surrounded the village and began the battle.

56.

56.

Kumāro tehi yujjhanto, subhaṭo paṭuvikkamo;

Disāsu vikirīsabbe, tulaṃ caṇḍova māḷuto.

The prince, a fine warrior swift in valor, fighting with them, scattered them all in every direction, like a fierce wind scatters cotton.

57.

57.

Cuṇṇasālaṃ janapadaṃ, gantvā ṭhānavidū tadā;

Tahiṃ vasaṃ vasekāsi, sabbaṃ malayamaṇḍalaṃ.

Then, having gone to the Cuṇṇasāla country, knowing the suitable place, he dwelt there and brought the entire Malaya region under his control.

58.

58.

Tadāpi senaṃ senindo, pesetvā asakiṃ sakaṃ;

Abhibhūtimasakkonto, kātuṃ dummanataṃ gato.

Even then the army chief, repeatedly sending forth his own army, being unable to achieve victory, became dejected.

59.

59.

Makkhakudrusavāsissa, sacipassātha kittino;

Suto mahabbalo deva-malloti vidito tadā.

Then the mighty son of Kitti, an inhabitant of Makkhakudrusa and seer of Saci, was known as Devamalla.

60.

60.

Sahito bandhumittehi, bahū rohaṇavāsino;

Samādāyā’bhigantvāna, kumāraṃ passi sādaro.

Accompanied by kinsmen and friends, and taking with him many inhabitants of Rohaṇa, he approached the prince and saw him with respect.

61.

61.

Bandhiya churikaṃ cheko, so pannarasavassiko;

Ādipādapadaṃ tattha, sampāpuṇi mahāyaso.

Having bound his dagger, he, the skilled one of great fame, being fifteen years old, there attained the foremost rank.

62.

62.

Tato hiraññamalaya, mupāgamma mahabbalo;

Tahiṃ remuṇaselamhi, khandhāvāraṃ nibandhayi.

Then, having approached Hiraññamalaya, the mighty one established his camp there at Remuṇa Rock.

63.

63.

Tatthāpi senaṃ pesetvā, saṅgāmento camūpati;

Aladdhavijayo chandaṃ, punayuddhe jahitato.

There too, the army commander sent forth his army and engaged in battle; failing to gain victory, he then abandoned his desire for further battle.

64.

64.

Lokanāmo camūnātho, lokaṃ hitvā sakaṃ tadā;

Ahu vassamhi chaṭṭheso, paralokaparāyano.

The army leader named Loka, having then abandoned his own world, in the sixth year passed away, destined for another world.

65.

65.

Tadā [M 0.0354] kassapanāmeko, kesadhātukanāyako;

Jane’bhibhūyavattesi, nījāṇaṃ rohaṇe tadā.

Then one named Kassapa, a guardian of the hair-relic, having overcome the people, established his own rule in Rohaṇa.

66.

66.

Sutvā taṃ coḷasāmanto, puḷatthinagarā tadā;

Nikkhamma yuddhasanaddho, gantvā kājaragāmakaṃ.

Hearing that, the Coḷa chieftain from Puḷatthinagara then set out, equipped for battle, and went to Kājaragāmaka.

67.

67.

Kesādhātu tato yuddhe, bhinditvā damiḷaṃ balaṃ;

Rakkhapāsāṇasīmāyaṃ, ṭhapetvā rakkhiye jane.

Then Kesadhātu, having shattered the Damiḷa forces in battle, placed guards at the boundary of Rakkhapāsāṇa.

68.

68.

Paṭiladdhajayuddāmo, mahāsenā purakkhato;

Punarāgamma pāvekkhi, vīro kājaragāmakaṃ.

The hero, emboldened by the victory he had gained, preceded by a great army, returned and entered Kājaragāmaka.

69.

69.

Tadādipādo sutvāna, sabbaṃ sutthīradhātuko;

Kesadhātuṃ nighātetuṃ, balaṃ sannayhi vegasā.

Then the Ādipāda, of most resolute character, hearing all this, swiftly marshaled his forces to destroy Kesadhātu.

70.

70.

Pavattiṃ taṃ suṇitvā so, sābhimāno bhusaṃtato;

Samattaṃ balamādāya, sippatthalakamāgamā.

Upon hearing that account, he, proud and greatly agitated, gathered his entire force and came to Sippatthalaka.

71.

71.

Pañcayojanaraṭṭhādi-vāsikesu bahūjane;

Samādāya samāsanne, rājaputte sudujjaye.

Having assembled many people dwelling in the five-yojana district and other regions, he approached the prince who was very difficult to conquer.

72.

72.

Virattatañca so ñatvā, bahunnaṃ raṭṭhavāsinaṃ;

Dukkaraṃ ettha yuddhanti, gato so khadiraṅgaṇiṃ.

And he, knowing the disaffection of many inhabitants of the kingdom, thinking, “Battle here is difficult,” went to Khadiraṅgaṇi.

73.

73.

Mahāsenāya bhūpāla suto soḷasavassīko;

Khippaṃ vāpekkhi so vīta-daro kājaragāmakaṃ.

That fearless king's son, sixteen years of age, with a great army, quickly advanced upon the village of Kājaraga.

74.

74.

Chammāsamanubhotvāna, rohaṇaṃ ruṭṭhamānaso;

Kesadhātukanāthopi, saṅgāmatthāya tatthagā.

Having enjoyed Rohaṇa for six months, with an enraged mind, even the lord of the Hair Relic went there for the sake of battle.

75.

75.

Rājaputtassa senā’tha, vattenti samaraṃ kharaṃ;

Kesadhātukanāthassa, sīsaṃ gaṇhi mahabbalā.

Then the prince’s army waged a fierce battle; the mighty ones seized the head of the lord of the Hair Relic.

76.

76.

Āgamma sattarasavayaṃ kumāro;

Sabbattha patthaṭamahāyasakittitejo;

Sumādineka vidhiyogavisesadakkho;

Khīṇārikaṇṭakamakā’khilarohaṇaṃ taṃ.

The prince, having reached the age of seventeen, whose great fame, glory, and splendor were spread everywhere, skilled in many excellent methods and special disciplines, made that entire Rohaṇa free from the thorns of enemies.

Sujanappasādasaṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Mahāvaṃsa, composed for the serene joy and spiritual urgency of the good.

Rohaṇārātivijayo nāma

Named the Victory over the Enemies of Rohaṇa

Pañcapaññāsatimo paricchedo.

The Fifty-fifth Chapter.

Chapaññāsatima pariccheda

The Fifty-sixth Chapter.

Anurādhapurābhigamano

The Advance upon Anurādhapura

1.

1.

Yuvarājapade [M 0.0355] tassa, ṭhitassā’tha nayaññuno;

Ahū vijayabāhūti, nāmaṃ sabbattha pākaṭaṃ.

Then, while he, the knower of statecraft, was established in the position of heir-apparent, his name, Vijayabāhu, became renowned everywhere.

2.

2.

Mahāññaṇo nijāṇāya, tattha bheriṃ carāviya;

Ṭhapento sacive’neke, patirūpe padantare.

The one of great wisdom, having the drum sounded there by his own command, appointed many suitable ministers to their respective positions.

3.

3.

Coḷānaṃ maddanatthāya, rājaraṭṭhādhivāsinaṃ;

Caturo caturopāye, yo jayaṃ tattha so vasī.

For the purpose of crushing the Coḷas, the inhabitants of the King's Country, he, the master, achieved victory there by the four stratagems.

4.

4.

Coḷarājā suṇitvā taṃ, puḷatthinagare ṭhitaṃ;

Senāpatima pesesi, datvāna balavāhanaṃ.

The Coḷa king, having heard that he was residing in the city of Puḷatthi, sent his general, having provided him with a powerful army.

5.

5.

Senindaṃ kājaraggāma-samīpaṃ samupāgataṃ;

Duppasayhaṃ viditvāna, giriduggamagā tato.

Recognizing that the army commander who had approached the vicinity of Kājaraggāma was difficult to assail, he then went to a mountain stronghold.

6.

6.

Senindo kājaraggāmaṃ, vilumpitvāna vegasā;

Tattha vatthumasakkonto, sadesaṃ puna rāgami.

The army commander, having swiftly plundered Kājaraggāma and being unable to remain there, returned again to his own country.

7.

7.

Tato mahādipādo’pi, āgamma malayā lahuṃ;

Mahatā balakāyena, sippatthalakamāvasi.

Then the Great Ādipāda, coming swiftly from the Malaya region with a large body of troops, took up residence in Sippatthala.

8.

8.

Rājā rāmaññavisaye, rājino santikaṃ jane;

Pesesi bahukesāraṃ, dhanajātañca’nappakaṃ.

The king in the country of Rāmañña sent messengers to the king, along with many valuables and no small amount of wealth.

9.

9.

Vicittavatthakappūra-candanādīhi vatthūhi;

Paripuṇṇā ca nāvāyo, nekātitthe samosaṭā.

And ships, filled full with goods such as various textiles, camphor, and sandalwood, assembled at many ports.

10.

10.

Dhanajā tehi nekehi, karonto bhaṭasaṅgahaṃ;

Tato tambalagāmamhi, nivasittha mahabbalo.

Recruiting soldiers with those many resources, the mighty one then took up residence in the village of Tambala.

11.

11.

Aññamaññaviruddhattā, rājāraṭṭhādhivāsino;

Upaggamma janā sabbe, karaṃ no denti sabbaso.

Because they were hostile to one another, all the inhabitants of the King's Country, when approached, would not give taxes at all.

12.

12.

Vipakkhācoḷarājassa, bhindantā’ṇaṃ maduddhatā;

Āyuttake vihiṃsento, yathākāmaṃ caranti ca.

Hostile to the Coḷa king, arrogant with pride, they broke his command, harassed his officials, and acted as they pleased.

13.

13.

Taṃ [M 0.0356] sutvā coḷabhūpālo, sampakopavasīkato;

Senaṃ mahantiṃ datvāna, pesesi sacivaṃ nijaṃ.

Hearing this, the Coḷa king was overcome by intense anger and, providing a great army, sent his own minister.

14.

14.

Mahātitthe’vahiṇṇo so, tattha tattha bahūjane;

Ghātento savase katvā, rājāraṭṭhādhivāsino.

Having landed at Mahātittha, he brought the inhabitants of the King's Country under his control, killing many people here and there.

15.

15.

Anukkamena gantvāna, kharāṇo rohaṇaṃ tadā;

Ajjhotthari saseno sa, bhinno velovasāgaro.

Gradually advancing, that fierce one then, with his army, overwhelmed Rohaṇa, like the ocean breaking its shore.

16.

16.

Rañño paccatthikā hutvā, ravidevacalavhayā;

Ubho damiḷaseninda-vasaṃ yātā mahabbalā.

Having become enemies of the king, the two mighty ones named Ravi and Devacala went under the control of the Damiḷa general.

17.

17.

Mahāpakkhabalopete, te passiya camūpati;

Rohaṇaṃ sakalaṃ khippaṃ, maññittha sakahatthagaṃ.

Seeing them endowed with a great faction and army, the commander thought that all of Rohaṇa was quickly in his grasp.

18.

18.

Ekādasamhi so vasse, rājā coḷābhibhūtiyā;

Paluṭṭhapabbate duggaṃ, pavidhāya tahiṃ vasī.

In the eleventh year, the king, being overwhelmed by the Coḷas, constructed a fortress on Paluṭṭha mountain and dwelt there.

19.

19.

Coḷasenā tadāselaṃ, samantā samparikkhipi;

Tattho’bhayesaṃ senāna-mahū bhiṃsanakaṃ raṇaṃ.

The Coḷa army then completely surrounded that mountain; thereupon a terrifying battle between the two armies occurred.

20.

20.

Rañño bhaṭā vināsetvā, sabbaṃ taṃ damiḷaṃ balaṃ;

Palāyantaṃ mahācoḷa-sāmantañcānubandhiya.

The king's soldiers, having destroyed all that Damiḷa force, pursued the fleeing great Coḷa chieftain.

21.

21.

Gahetvāna siraṃ tassa, gāmasmiṃ tambaviṭṭhike

Saddhiṃ vāhanayānehi, sārabhūtadhanehi ca.

Having taken his head in the village of Tambaviṭṭhika, along with his mounts, vehicles, and essential wealth,

22.

22.

Tahiṃ taṃ sakalaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ, netvā rañño padassiya;

Puḷatthinagaraṃ gantuṃ, kālo iti samabravuṃ.

Having brought all those goods there and shown them to the king, they declared, 'It is time to go to Puḷatthinagara.'

23.

23.

Mahīpālopi taṃ sutvā, sacivānaṃ vaco tadā;

Mahatā balakāyena, pulatthinagaraṃ gato.

Then the lord of the earth, having heard that word of his ministers, went to Puḷatthinagara with a great army.

24.

24.

Pavattimetaṃ sakalaṃ, sutvā coḷanarissaro;

Tibbakopavasaṃyāto, bhūpālagahaṇatthiko.

Having heard all this news, the Coḷa king, overcome by fierce anger, became desirous of capturing the king.

25.

25.

Sāmaṃ khippaṃ samāgamma, vīro sāgarapaṭṭanaṃ;

Bhiyyopi mahatiṃ senaṃ, laṃkādīpamapesayī.

The hero himself, having quickly come to the seaport, sent an even greater army to the island of Laṅkā.

26.

26.
