Taṃ vijāniya bhūmindo, senindaṃ pesayī sakaṃ;

Balaṃ mahantaṃ datvāna, coḷasenāya yujjhituṃ.

Knowing this, the lord of the land dispatched his own commander-in-chief, giving him a great force to fight the Coḷa army.

27.

27.

Gacchamāno camūnātho, so’nurādhapurantike;

Saddhiṃ damiḷasenāya, vattesi tumulaṃ raṇaṃ.

While on the march, that commander of the army waged a tumultuous battle against the Damiḷa army near Anurādhapura.

28.

28.

Patiṃsu [M 0.0357] tasmiṃ saṅgāme, bhūpālassa narā bahū;

Bhiyyopi damiḷāyattā, jātā taṃ raṭṭhavāsino.

Many of the king's men fell in that battle, and furthermore, the inhabitants of that country became subject to the Damiḷas.

29.

29.

Vihāya dharaṇīpālo, pulatthinagaraṃ tadā;

Villikābāṇakaṃ raṭṭhaṃ, sampāpuṇiya vegasā.

Then the protector of the earth, having abandoned Puḷatthinagara, swiftly reached the country of Villikābāṇaka.

30.

30.

Nihaccāmaccayugalaṃ, taṃ raṭṭhādhiṭṭhitaṃ tadā;

Tahiṃ vāsamakappesi, sabhaṭe sannipātayaṃ.

Having slain the pair of ministers who were established in that country, he then made his residence there, gathering his soldiers.

31.

31.

Attānamanubandhantaṃ, sutvā coḷacamūpatiṃ;

Gantvā vātagiriṃ nāma, samayaññū siluccayaṃ.

Hearing that the Coḷa army commander was pursuing him, he, knowing the opportune time, went to a rocky mountain named Vātagiri.

32.

32.

Upaccakāya selassa, tattha duggaṃ nivesiya;

Raṇaṃ karonto temāsaṃ, damiḷe paṭibāhayi.

Having established a stronghold there at the foot of the rock, he fought for three months, repelling the Damiḷas.

33.

33.

Kesadhātukanāthassa, māritassa purāraṇe;

Bhātā kaṇiṭṭho sampatta, mahāpakkhabalo tadā.

The younger brother of Kesadhātukanātha, who had been killed in a previous battle, then arrived with a great supporting force.

34.

34.

Māraṇaṃ sakabhātussa, saranto ruṭṭhamānaso;

Sakalaṃ parivattesi, guttahālakamaṇḍalaṃ.

Remembering the death of his own brother, with a wrathful mind, he laid waste to the entire Guttahālaka district.

35.

35.

Atho laṃkissaro tattha, khippaṃ gantvā mahabbalo;

Ṭhāne maccutthale nāma, khandhāvāraṃ nibandhiya.

Then the powerful lord of Laṅkā, having quickly gone there, established an encampment at a place named Maccutthala.

36.

36.

Khadiraṅgaṇiduggamhā, palāpetvāna taṃ raṇe;

Ṭhānā kubulagallā ca, yujjhanto taṃ palāpayi.

Having made him flee in battle from the stronghold of Khadiraṅgaṇi, and fighting at the place of Kubulagalla, he routed him.

37.

37.

Vihāya puttadārādi-sabbaṃ nekadhanaṃ balaṃ;

Palāyamāno so raṭṭhaṃ, coḷāyatta magālahuṃ.

Leaving behind his children, wife, and all his various wealth and forces, he, while fleeing, quickly went to the country subject to the Coḷas.

38.

38.

Tadā narissaro tata, tassa sabbaṃ samādiya;

Gantvā tambalagāmamhi, navaṃ duggaṃ nivesiya.

Then the lord of men, having taken all of his possessions, went to the village of Tambala and established a new stronghold.

39.

39.

Anukkamena gantvāna, mahānāgahulavhaye;

Purevasī susajjento, balaṃ coḷehi yujjhituṃ.

Proceeding gradually, he dwelt in the city called Mahānāgahula, thoroughly preparing his army to fight with the Coḷas.

40.

40.

Tato rājā samavhāya, sacīve dve mahabbale;

Pesesi dikkhiṇaṃ passaṃ, vasaṃ netuṃ tahiṃ jane.

Then the king, having summoned two mighty ministers, sent them to the southern region to bring the people there under his control.

41.

41.

Sampesesi mahāmacca-yugalaṃ kakkhalaṃ vibhū;

Coḷadappavināsāya, tato velā mahāpathe.

The powerful king dispatched a pair of fierce great ministers to destroy the arrogance of the Coḷas; then, at the right time, on the great road.

42.

42.

Pesitā dakkhiṇaṃ passaṃ, amaccā’me mahabbalā;

Muhunnaruggamaduggaṃ, badaḷatthalameva ca.

These mighty ministers were sent to the southern region, to the stronghold of Muhunnaruggama and also to Badaḷatthala,

43.

43.

Vāpīnagaraduggañca[M 0.0358], buddhagāmakameva ca;

Tilagullaṃ mahāgallaṃ, maṇḍagallakameva ca.

and the stronghold of Vāpīnagara, and Buddhagāmaka, Tilagulla, Mahāgalla, and also Maṇḍagallaka.

44.

44.

Anurādhapurañcāti, gahetvāna kamena te;

Vattentā savase raṭṭhaṃ, mahātitthamupāgatā.

and Anurādhapura—having seized these in succession, they brought the country under their control and arrived at Mahātittha.

45.

45.

Pesitā sacivādvetu, tato velā mahāpathe;

Vilumpantā chagāmādi-khandhāvāre tahiṃ tahiṃ.

But the two ministers sent forth then on the great road went about plundering village encampments here and there.

46.

46.

Pulatthinagarāsannaṃ, kamenā’gamma pesayuṃ;

Dūte rājantikakhippa-māgantuṃ vaṭṭatītiha.

Having gradually come near to Puḷatthinagara, they sent messengers to the king, saying, 'It is right that you come quickly.'

47.

47.

Disāsā dvīsu yānehi, sacivehi pavattitaṃ;

Vikkamāti sayaṃ sutvā, kālaññū so mahīpahi.

That king, knowing the opportune time, having heard of the valorous campaign set in motion by the ministers in two directions,

48.

48.

Sīghaṃ sannayha senaṅgaṃ, samaggaṃ vidikovido;

Ummūlanāyacoḷānaṃ, purātamhā’bhinikkhami.

He, being skilled in strategy, quickly assembled his entire army and marched out from that city to uproot the Coḷas.

49.

49.

Gacchaṃ gaṅgāya mahiya-ṅgaṇathūpantike vibhū;

Senānivesaṃ kāretvā kañcikālaṃ tahiṃ vasī.

The powerful king, proceeding to the vicinity of the Gaṅgā near the Mahiyangana Thūpa, had a military camp established and dwelt there for some time.

50.

50.

Kamenāgamma ṭhānaññū, puḷatthinagarantike;

Bandhāpesi mahāvīro, khandhāvāraṃ thiraṃ varaṃ.

Having come gradually, the great hero, knowing the suitable place near Pulatthinagara, had a strong and excellent encampment built.

51.

51.

Tattha tattha ṭhitā sūrā, coḷā ye kakkhalā’khilā;

Pulatthinagare yuddhaṃ, kātuṃ sannipatiṃsu te.

The fierce and harsh Coḷa heroes, all of them, who were stationed here and there, gathered in Pulatthinagara to do battle.

52.

52.

Nikkhamma nagarā gantvā, coḷā bahi mahāraṇaṃ;

Katvā parājitā bhītā, pavissa nagaraṃ sakaṃ.

Emerging from the city, the Coḷas went out to a great battle, but, defeated and frightened, they entered their own city.

53.

53.

Guttā sesapuradvārā, gopuraṭṭālanissitā;

Mahāhavaṃ bahussāhā, pavattesuṃ bhayāvahaṃ.

Guarding the remaining city gates, stationed on the gate-towers and watchtowers, with great energy they waged a fearsome battle.

54.

54.

Diyaḍḍhamāsaṃ yujjhanti, nagaraṃ tamuparundhiya;

Sādhetuṃ nevasā’sakkhi, bhūpālassa mahācamū.

For a month and a half they fought, besieging that city, but the king's great army was not able to conquer it.

55.

55.

Mahārañño mahāvīrā, mahāsūrā mahabbalā;

Mahābhaṭā mahāmānā, ravidevacalādayo.

The great heroes of the great king—greatly courageous, greatly powerful, great warriors of great renown—were Ravideva, Acala, and others.

56.

56.

Ullaṅghitvāna pākāraṃ, pavissa sahasā puraṃ;

Khaṇena damiḷe sabbe, mūlaghaccamaghātayuṃ.

Scaling the ramparts, they swiftly burst into the city and, in an instant, annihilated all the Damiḷas, cutting them down to the root.

57.

57.

Evaṃ laddhajayo rājā, tadā vijayabāhuso;

Carāpesi nijāṇāya, bheriṃ bhūrimatipure.

Thus having gained the victory, King Vijayabāhu then, by his own command, caused the proclamation drum to be sounded in the city of Bhūrimati.

58.

58.

Taṃ [M 0.0359] sutvā sakasenāya, vināsaṃ coḷabhūpati;

Sīhaḷā balavantoti, bhiyyo senaṃ na pāhiṇi.

Hearing of the destruction of his army, the Coḷa king, thinking, 'The Sīhaḷas are powerful,' did not send an army again.

59.

59.

Vīro asesanihatuddhaṭa coḷaseṭṭho;

Viññū susādhuṭṭhapitākhilarājaraṭṭho;

Iṭṭhannurādhapuraseṭṭhamatīva haṭṭho;

Vassamhi pañcadasame gami rājaseṭṭho.

The hero, who had utterly slain the arrogant Coḷa chiefs; the wise one, who had well established the entire kingdom; exceedingly delighted, he set his heart on the excellent Anurādhapura; in the fifteenth year, that noble king went there.

Sujanappasādasaṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Great Chronicle, composed for the serene joy and spiritual urgency of the virtuous.

Anurādhapurābhigamano nāma

The Arrival at Anurādhapura

Chappaññāsatimo paricchedo

The Fifty-sixth Chapter

Sattapaññāsatima pariccheda

The Fifty-seventh Chapter

Saṃgahakaraṇonāma

The Consolidation of the Kingdom

1.

1.

Laṅkārakkhāya sacive, balino yodhasammate;

Paṭipāṭiṃ samuddissa, samantā sanniyojayi.

For the protection of Laṅkā, he appointed powerful ministers, who were esteemed as warriors, assigning them their posts in due order and deploying them on all sides.

2.

2.

Abhisekamaṅgalatthāya, pāsādādimanekataṃ;

Kiccaṃ sampādanīyanti, sacivaṃ sanniyojiya.

For the sake of the consecration ceremony, he instructed a minister that various duties, beginning with the palace, were to be accomplished.

3.

3.

Vandanīye’bhivandanto, padesenekaketahiṃ;

Netvā māsattayaṃ gañchi, pulatthinagaraṃ puna.

Paying homage to those worthy of homage in various places, and leading his forces for three months, he went again to the city of Pulatthi.

4.

4.

Vissuto ādimalaya-nāmena balanāyako;

Ujupaccatthiko hutvā, mahīpālassa sabbaso.

A leader of forces, renowned by the name Ādimalaya, became a direct adversary to the king in every way.

5.

5.

Gaṅgā matthayu’pāgañchi, balaṃ sabbaṃ samādiya;

Andūti vissutaṃ manda-pañño gāmaṃ purantike.

Having gathered all his forces, that slow-witted man approached the village renowned as Andūti, near the city on the bank of the Gaṅgā.

6.

6.

Laṃkissaro tahiṃ gantvā, uddharitvā tamuddhataṃ;

Pulatthinagaraṃ gañchi, vase vattiya taṃ balaṃ.

The Lord of Laṅkā went there, and having overthrown that arrogant one, he went to the city of Pulatthi, bringing that force under his control.

7.

7.

Yuvarājapadaṃyeva, sito santo likhāpayi;

So sattarasavassāni, sappañño narasattamo.

That wise best of men, being serene, had the position of crown prince itself established by decree; for seventeen years he reigned.

8.

8.

Tato’nurādhanagara-mabhigamma [M 0.0360] yathāvidhiṃ;

Anubhotvā vidhānaññū, abhisekamahussavaṃ.

Then, having gone to the city of Anurādhapura according to custom, he who knew the rites experienced the great festival of consecration.

9.

9.

Aṭṭhito pāpadhammesu, suṭṭhito seṭṭhakammani;

So aṭṭhārasamaṃ vassaṃ, likhāpayi susaṇṭhito.

Not standing in evil ways, well-established in the noblest actions, he, being well-composed, caused inscriptions to be made in the eighteenth year.

10.

10.

Tato āgamma nivasi, pulatthinagare vare;

So sirīsaṅghabodhī’ti, nāmadheyyena vissuto.

Then, having come there, he dwelt in the excellent city of Pulatthi. He was renowned by the name Sirīsaṅghabodhi.

11.

11.

Anujaṃ so vīrabāhu-moparajje nivesiya;

Datvāna dakkhiṇaṃ desaṃ, taṃ saṅgaṇhi yathāvidhiṃ.

He installed his younger brother Vīrabāhu in the office of sub-king; having given him the southern region, he won him over according to custom.

12.

12.

Kaṇiṭṭhassātha bhātussa, jayabāhussa bhūbhujo;

Ādipādapadaṃ datvā, raṭṭhaṃ cā’dāsi rohaṇaṃ.

Then to his youngest brother, Jayabāhu, the king gave the position of Ādipāda and also granted him the country of Rohaṇa.

13.

13.

Ṭhānantarāni sabbesa-mamaccānaṃ yathārahaṃ;

Datvā rajje yathāñāyaṃ, karaṃ yojesi gaṇhituṃ.

Having given positions to all the ministers according to their merit, he arranged for the collection of taxes in the kingdom in a just manner.

14.

14.

Cirassaṃ parihīnaṃ so, dayāvāso mahīpati;

Pavattesi yathādhammaṃ, ṭhitadhammo vinicchayaṃ.

That king, an abode of compassion and firm in the Dhamma, set in motion the administration of justice in accordance with the Dhamma, which had been neglected for a long time.

15.

15.

Evaṃ samuddhaṭāneka, ripukaṇṭakasañcaye;

Niccaṃ rajjaṃ pasāsente, laṅkaṃsammānarissare.

Thus, with the multitude of enemy-thorns uprooted, the lord of men was constantly ruling the kingdom of Laṅkā in a righteous manner.

16.

16.

Chattaggāhakanātho ca, dhammagehakanāyako;

Tatheva seṭṭhinātho ca, iccete bhātaro tayo.

Chattaggāhakanātha, the chief umbrella-bearer; Dhammagehakanāyaka, the leader of the Dhamma-house; and likewise Seṭṭhinātha, the merchant chief—these three were brothers.

17.

17.

Rañño virodhitaṃ yātā, phalātā jampudīpakaṃ;

Laṅkaṃ vīsatime vasse, ekenūne samotaruṃ.

Having incurred the king's displeasure, they fled to Jambudīpa. In the nineteenth year, they landed in Laṅkā.

18.

18.

Te sabbe rohaṇaṃ raṭṭhaṃ, sabbaṃ malayamaṇḍalaṃ;

Sabbaṃ dakkhiṇapassañca, sahasā parivattayuṃ.

They swiftly brought under their control the entire kingdom of Rohaṇa, the entire Malaya region, and the entire southern side.

19.

19.

Nipuṇo rohaṇaṃ gantvā, tathā malayamaṇḍalaṃ;

Nighātento bahū tattha, tattha paccatthike jane.

The skillful one, going to Rohaṇa and likewise to the Malaya region, struck down many hostile people there.

20.

20.

Sammāvupasametvā taṃ, ṭhapetvā sacive tahiṃ;

Dakkhiṇo dakkhiṇaṃ desaṃ, sayaṃ gantvā mahabbalo.

Having completely pacified that region and stationed his ministers there, the mighty Dakkhiṇa himself went to the southern country.

21.

21.

Pesetvā samaṇībhātu-vaṃsajaṃ sacivaṃ tadā;

Gāhetvā samareghore, vīro te sakaverino.

Then, sending a minister from the lineage of the nun's brother, the hero captured his own enemies in fierce battle.

22.

22.

Samāropiyasūlamhi, laṅkaṃ vigatakaṇṭakaṃ;

Kāretvāna nirātaṅkaṃ, pulatthipuramāgami.

Having impaled them on stakes, he made Laṅkā free of thorns and secure, and then came to Pulatthipura.

23.

23.

Vasantī [M 0.0361] coḷavisaye, jagatipālarājinī;

Coḷahatthā pamuñcitvā, saddhiṃ dhītu kumāriyā.

The queen of Jagatipāla, dwelling in the Coḷa territory, having freed herself from the grasp of the Coḷas, together with her daughter, the princess,

24.

24.

Līlāvatyābhidhānāya, nāvāmāruyha vegasā;

Laṃkādīpamhi otiṇṇā, passi laṃkissaraṃ tadā.

who was named Līlāvatī, swiftly boarded a ship, disembarked on the island of Laṅkā, and then beheld the lord of Laṅkā.

25.

25.

Sutvā vaṃsakkamaṃ tassā, so ñatvā suddhavaṃsataṃ;

Līlāvatiṃ mahisitte, abhisiñci narissaro.

Hearing of her lineage and recognizing its purity, the lord of men consecrated Līlāvatī as chief queen.

26.

26.

Sā taṃ paṭicca rājānaṃ, mahesī dhītaraṃ labhi;

Nāmaṃ yasodharāti’ssā, akāsi dharaṇī pati.

That chief queen bore a daughter to the king. The lord of the earth named her Yasodharā.

27.

27.

Merukandararaṭṭhena, saddhiṃ rājā sadhītaraṃ;

Vīravammassa pādāsi, sā labhi dhītaro duve.

The king gave his daughter, together with the kingdom of Merukandara, to Vīravamma; she bore two daughters.

28.

28.

Samānanāmikā jeṭṭhā, sā mātā mahiyā ahu;

Sugalā nāmikā āsi, tāsu dvīsu kaṇiṭṭhikā.

The elder, who had the same name as her mother, became the mother of the great one; Sugalā was the name of the younger of the two.

29.

29.

Kāliṅgadharaṇīpāla-vaṃsajaṃ cārudassanaṃ;

Tilokasundaraṃ nāma, sukumāraṃ kumārikaṃ.

A tender young maiden, charming to behold, named Tilokasundarī, born of the lineage of the earth-protector of Kāliṅga,

30.

30.

Kāliṅgaraṭṭhato rājā, āṇāpetvā ciraṭṭhitiṃ;

Nijavaṃsassa icchanto, mahesitte’bhi secayi.

the king, desiring the long continuance of his own lineage, had her brought from the Kāliṅga kingdom and consecrated her as chief queen.

31.

31.

Subhaddā ca sumittā ca, lokanāthavhayāpi ca;

Subhaddā, Sumittā, Lokanāthā, Ratanāvalī, and Rūpavatī—these were the five daughters.

32.

32.

Puttaṃ vikkamabāhuñca, sā labhī dhaññalakkhaṇaṃ;

She bore a son, Vikkamabāhu, endowed with auspicious marks. Having attained an increase in progeny, she captivated the king's mind.

33.

33.

Itthāgāresu sesesu, vītā samakulaṅganā;

Gabbho jātumahīpālaṃ, taṃ paṭicca na saṇṭhahi.

Among the other women in the harem, even those of equal lineage, no womb was ever established on account of that king.

34.

34.

Athekadivasaṃ rājā, amaccagaṇamajjhago;

Pilokiyaṭhibhā sabbā, dhītaro paṭipāṭiyā.

Then one day the king, amidst his assembly of ministers, observed all his daughters in order.

35.

35.

Dhītu navamavasesānaṃ, ṭhapetvā ratanāvaliṃ;

Setting aside Ratanāvalī, he sought among the nine remaining daughters for the sign indicating the birth of a son endowed with auspicious marks.

36.

36.

Lakkhaṇaṃ lakkhaṇaññū so, apassaṃ pemacegavā;

37.

37.

Tejoguṇehi [M 0.0362] cāgehi, dhiyā sūrattanena ca;

A son who, by his majesty, generosity, wisdom, and heroism, would surpass all kings, past and future.

38.

38.

Niccaṃ laṅkaṃ nirāsaṅka-mekacchattakameva ca;

Of one capable of always making Laṅkā secure and under a single parasol, a protector of the true teaching.

39.

39.

Sobhanānekavattassa, imissā kucchihessati;

'This one's womb will be the birthplace of a son possessing many excellent qualities,' thus he gently spoke.

40.

40.

Yāvantassāpikhocoḷa-mahīpālassa nekaso;

Kulābhimānī rājā so, adatvāna kaṇīyasiṃ.

Though requested many times by the Coḷa king, that king, proud of his lineage, did not give him his younger sister.

41.

41.

Āṇāpetvā paṇḍurājaṃ, visuddhatvayasambhavaṃ;

Anujaṃ rājiniṃ vassa, mittavhayamadāsiso.

Having sent for the Paṇḍu king, who was of pure lineage on both sides, he gave to him his younger sister, the queen named Mittā.

42.

42.

Sāmāṇabharaṇaṃ kitti, sirī meghābhidhānakaṃ;

She bore three sons: Māṇābharaṇa, Kitti Sirimegha, and Sirivallabha.

43.

43.

Subhadda vīrabāhussa, sumittaṃ jayabāhuno;

The lord of the earth gave Subhaddā to Vīrabāhu and Sumittā to Jayabāhu with great ceremony.

44.

44.

Adāsi māṇābharaṇe, dhītaraṃ ratanāvaliṃ;

45.

45.

Rūpatyabhidhānāya, dhītuyo paratāyahi;

Sarīrivallabhasādā, sugalavha kumārikaṃ.

He gave his daughter named Rūpavatī to Sirivallabha, and the maiden named Sugalā to Māṇābharaṇa.

46.

46.

Madhukaṇṇavabhīmarāja, balakkāra sanāmake;

Mahesī bandhaverāja-putte sīhapurāgate.

Madhukaṇṇava, Bhīmarāja, and he named Balakkāra; the chief queen Bandhumatī, and the princes who had come to Sīhapura.

47.

47.

Passitvāna pahīpālo, tadā sañjātapītiko;

Tesaṃ pādāsi paccekaṃ, vuttiṃ so anurūpakaṃ.

Having seen them, the king, in whom joy had then arisen, gave to each of them a suitable livelihood.

48.

48.

Te sabbe laddhasakkāra sammānādharaṇīpatiṃ;

All of them, having received honor and respect, constantly pleasing the lord of the earth, lived as they wished.

49.

49.

Etesaṃ rājaputtānaṃ, sundarivhaṃ kaṇiṭṭhakaṃ;

Of these royal children, he who desired the continuance of his own lineage gave the youngest, named Sundarī, to Vikkamabāhu.

50.

50.

51.

Vidhāya evaṃ sajane janindo;

Nissesato bhogasamappito;

Dayāparo ñātijanātamatthaṃ;

Having thus provided for his own people, the lord of men, with his wealth completely dedicated, being compassionate and for the welfare of his kinsfolk and subjects, acted in accordance with the path of wise policy.

Sujanappasādasaṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Mahāvaṃsa, composed for the serene joy and spiritual urgency of the virtuous,

Saṃgahakaraṇo nāma

Named 'The Act of Support'.

Sattapaññāsatimo paricchedo

The Fifty-seventh Chapter.

Aṭṭhapaññāsatima pariccheda

The Fifty-eighth Chapter

Lokasāsana saṃgahakaraṇo

Supporting the World and the Dispensation

1.

1.

Vicinitvā kulīne so, jane sabbe samādiya;

Sakārakkhāya yojesi, yathācāraṃ mahīpati.

Having investigated and gathered all the people of good family, the king, in accordance with custom, employed them for their own protection.

2.

2.

Uccaṃ pulatthinagare, pākāraṃ kārayī thiraṃ;

Nekagopurasaṃyuttaṃ, yudhākammasurañjitaṃ.

In the city of Pulatthi, he had a high, strong wall built, endowed with many gate-towers and well-adorned for the work of battle.

3.

3.

Samantāyatavitthiṇṇa-gambhīraparikhāyutaṃ;

Uccapatthaṇḍilopetaṃ, duppadhaṃsamarātihi.

It was endowed with a deep, wide, and long moat all around, furnished with high level-ground on top, and difficult for enemies to assault.

4.

4.

Upasampadakammassa, gaṇapūrakabhikkhūnaṃ;

His mind set on the stability of the Dispensation, because there were not enough monks to complete the quorum for the act of higher ordination,

5.

5.

Anuruddhanarindassa, sahāyassātha santikaṃ;

Rāmaññavisayaṃ dūte, pesetvā sahapābhate.

6.

Tato āṇāpayitvāna, piṭakattayapārage;

Then, having requested from there monks esteemed as elders, who had mastered the Three Piṭakas and were abodes of virtues such as morality,

7.

Te uḷārāhi pūjāhi, pūjayitvā narissaro;

Pabbajjā upasampatti, kārayitvā anekaso.

8.

8.

Piṭakattayañca bahuso, kathāpetvā savaṇṇanaṃ;

Laṅkāyo’sakkamānaṃ so, jotayī jinasāsanaṃ.

And having caused the Three Piṭakas with their commentaries to be recited extensively, he illuminated the Dispensation of the Victor, which was flourishing in Laṅkā.

9.

9.

Putatthinagarassanto[M 0.0364], padesasmiṃ tahiṃ tahiṃ;

Within the city of Pulatthi, in various places here and there, having had many very delightful monasteries built,

10.

10.

Bhikkhavo tattha vāsetvā, nikāyattayavāsino;

Paccayehi uḷārehi, santappesi catūhipi.

Having settled there monks dwelling in the three Nikāyas, he satisfied them with the four magnificent requisites.

11.

11.

Phalikatthambhakacāru-pākāraparikhāyutaṃ;

Endowed with beautiful walls, a moat, and crystal pillars, it was adorned with excellent five-storied mansions.

12.

12.

Samasantā vāsapantīhi, subhāhi suvirājitaṃ;

Resplendent on all sides with beautiful rows of dwellings, it had excellent, radiant gateways, and was uncrowded and spacious.

13.

Vihāraṃ kārayitvāna, vatthuttayaparāyano;

Having had the monastery built, he, being devoted to the Triple Gem, gave it to the community of monks dwelling in the three Nikāyas.

14.

14.

Saṅghassa pākavaṭṭatthaṃ, raṭṭhaṃ datvā’ḷisārakaṃ;

For the provision of the Sangha's sustenance, he gave the entire district of Aḷisāraka, together with its inhabitants and officials.

15.

15.

Nekasatānibhikkhūnaṃ, vāsayitvāna tattha so;

Having settled many hundreds of monks there, he constantly provided the four magnificent requisites.

16.

16.

Dāṭṭhādhātugharaṃcāru, kārayitvā mahārahaṃ;

Having had a beautiful and costly house for the Tooth Relic built, he regularly had a great festival held for the Tooth Relic.

17.

Gaṇasaṅgaṇikā’peto, potthakaṃ dhammasaṅgaṇiṃ;

18.

18.

Naccādigandhamālādi-nekapūjampavattiya;

19.

Jambudīpāgate cāga, sūro so bhuvirisūrayo;

Tappesi dhanadānena, dāniyeneka so vibhū.

20.

20.

Saddhammakathikānaṃ so, pūjā katvāna nekaso;

Desāpesica saddhammaṃ, sadādhammaguṇe rato.

Having honored the preachers of the True Dhamma on many occasions, he had the True Dhamma taught, ever delighting in the virtues of the Dhamma.

21.

Tikkhattuṃ so tulābhāra-dānaṃ dinesu dāpayi;

Uposathaṃ vopavasi, suvisuddhamuposathe.

22.

23.

24.

Sent by the ruler of the Kaṇṇāṭa country and by the Cola king, envoys arrived here, bringing a great tribute.

25.

25.

Addasaṃsu mahīpālaṃ, tato so tuṭṭhamānaso;

Tesaṃ ubhinnaṃ dūtānaṃ, kattabbaṃ sādhukāriya.

They saw the monarch; thereupon he, with a gladdened heart, performed a fitting service for both those envoys.

26.

26.

Tesu ādo’va kaṇṇāṭa-dūtehi saha pesiya;

Dūte sakīye kaṇṇāṭa-nikaṭaṃ sārapābhate.

First, among them, he sent his own envoys, along with the Kaṇṇāṭa envoys, to the vicinity of Kaṇṇāṭa with a valuable gift.

27.

When the Sinhala envoys reached his territory, the Cola king's men suddenly disfigured their ears and noses.

28.

Sampattavippakārāke, idhāgantvāna rājino;

Having met with this injury, they came here to the king and then recounted all that had been done to them by the Cola king.

29.

29.

Uddipitābhimāno so, sakalāmaccamajjhago;

His pride inflamed, he, amidst all his ministers, summoned the Tamil envoys and sent this message to the Cola king:

30.

30.

Senaṃ vinā’va ekasmiṃ, dīpe majjhe mahaṇṇave;

Bāhābalaparikkhāvā, hotuno dvandayuddhato.

"Without an army, on an island in the midst of the great ocean, let there be for us a test of the strength of our arms, or a duel.

31.

31.

Balaṃ sannayha sakalaṃ, rajje tuyhaṃ mamā’tha vā;

Tavā’bhimata dosamhi, saṅgāmo vā karīyataṃ.

Or, having assembled all forces, either in your kingdom or in mine, let battle be waged at a place of your choosing."

32.

32.

Mayā vuttakkameneva, vattabbo vo janādhipo;

Iti vatvāna te dūte, itthalaṅkāra maṇḍite.

"Your lord of men should be informed in the very manner I have spoken." Having said this, he had the envoys adorned with women's ornaments,

33.

33.

Vissajjiya lahuṃcoḷa-mahīpālassa santikaṃ;

Tato senaṅgamādāya, anurādha puraṃ gami.

and swiftly dispatched them to the Cola king. Then, taking his army, he went to Anurādhapura.

34.

34.

Mattikāvāṭatitthe ca, mahātitthe ca pesayī;

Coḷaraṭṭhaṃ’va gantvāna, yujjhituṃ dve camūpati.

35.

35.

Sajjantesu camūpesu, nāvāpātheyyakāni ca;

36.

36.

Tadā tiṃsatime vasse, veḷakkārasanāmakā;

Balakāyā tahiṃgantu-manicchantā virodhino.

then, in the thirtieth year, the troops named Veḷakkāras, not wishing to go there, became hostile.

37.

37.

Māretvāna ubho senā-nāthe mattagajāviya;

38.

38.

Puttehi [M 0.0366] tīhi sahitaṃ, rājino ca kaṇīyasiṃ;

39.

39.

Rājā nikkhamma khippaṃ so, gantvā dakkhiṇapassakaṃ;

Sele vātagirivhasmiṃ, sāraṃ bhaṇḍaṃ ṭhapāpiya.

That king, departing quickly, went to the southern region; on the rock called Vātagiri, he had his valuable goods stored.

40.

40.

Vīrabāhuparājena, sīhavikkamasālinā;

Mahatā ca baloghena, samantā parivārito.

Surrounded on all sides by the sub-king Vīrabāhu, who possessed the prowess of a lion, and by a great mass of forces,

41.

41.

Pulatthipuramāgamma, vattento dāruṇaṃ raṇaṃ;

Palāpesi khaṇeneva, balakāye samāgate.

he came to Pulatthipura and, waging a fierce battle, in an instant routed the assembled forces.

42.

42.

Māritāna camūpāna-maṭṭhisaṅghāṭadhiṭṭhitaṃ;

Parikkhipitvā citakaṃ, veribhūte balādhipe.

Having surrounded the pyre, which was built upon a heap of the bones of the slain commanders, he had the leaders of the forces, who had become his enemies,

43.

43.

Bandhayitvāna khāṇumhi, pacchā bāhaṃ subandhanaṃ;

Parito vipphurantīhi, aggijālāhi jhāpayi.

bound to stakes, with their arms tightly fastened behind them, and caused them to be burned with flames that blazed all around.

44.

44.

Ghātetvā tattha mānītaṃ, gāmāni dharaṇīpati;

Having slain the proud ones there, the lord of the earth made the land of Lanka entirely free from troubles in every way.

45.

45.

Yujjhituṃ saha coḷena, rājā attakatāvadhiṃ;

Anatikkamma so pañca-cattālīsamhi vacchare.

46.

46.

Sannaddhaṃ balamādāya, gantvā sāgarapaṭṭanaṃ;

Tassābhigamanaṃ passaṃ, kañcikālaṃ tahiṃ vasaṃ.

took his armored army and went to the seaport. Awaiting his arrival, he dwelt there for some time.

47.

47.

Anāgatattā coḷassa, tassa dūte vissajjiya;

Punāgantvā vasīrājā, pulatthinagare ciraṃ.

48.

48.

Mahāheḷi sareharu, mahādattikanāmikā;

Kaṭunnarūpaṇḍavāpī, kallagallika nāmikā.

The great Mahāheḷi tank, the one named Mahādattika, the Kaṭunnarūpaṇḍa tank, and the one named Kallagallika.

49.

49.

Eraṇḍegallavāpī ca, dīghavatthukavāpikā;

Maṇḍavāṭakavāpī, ca, kittaggabodhipabbatā.

The Eraṇḍegalla tank, the Dīghavatthuka tank, the Maṇḍavāṭaka tank, and the Kittaggabodhipabbata tank.

50.

50.

Valāhassa mahādāru, gallakumbhīlasobbhakā;

Pattapāsāṇavāpī ca, vāpī ca kāṇanāmikā.

Valāhassa-mahādāru, Gallakumbhīla-sobbhaka, Pattapāsāṇa-vāpī, and the reservoir named Kāṇa.

51.

51.

Etā caññā ca so chinna-mariyādā vāpiyo bahū;

Bandhāpesi sadādīna-satte baddha hitāsayo.

These and many other reservoirs whose banks were broken, he had constructed, ever aspiring for the welfare of afflicted beings.

52.

52.

Bhūmindo [M 0.0367] kandarā-gaṅgā-nadīsu ca tahiṃ tahiṃ;

Subhikkhaṃ kārayī raṭṭhaṃ, bandhetvā’varaṇāni so.

The lord of the land made the country prosperous with abundant food by building dams here and there on mountain streams, great rivers, and other rivers.

53.

53.

Vihārā’bhayacāritta-bhediniṃ mahisaṃsaka;

Parihāre sabbasocchijja-gāhayitvā galamhi taṃ.

He completely eradicated the troubles that violated the safety and good conduct of the monasteries, seizing them by the throat.

54.

54.

Purambhā bahi kāretvā, mahāsaṅghaṃ khamāpiya;

Pakāsesi ca lokassa, saṅghagāravamattano.

Having expelled them from the city, and having asked for the forgiveness of the great Saṅgha, he proclaimed to the world his own reverence for the Saṅgha.

56.

56.

Mahāgāme nikāyānaṃ, titaye coḷanāsite;

Dhātugabbhe ca bandhesi, thūpārāmadvaye’pi ca.

In Mahāgāma, for the three Nikāyas that had been destroyed by the Coḷas, he built relic chambers, and did likewise at the two Thūpārāmas.

57.

57.

Mātuyā’ḷāhaṇaṭhāne, tatheva pitunopi ca;

Akā pañca mahāvāse, tathā budalaviṭṭhiyaṃ.

He built five great monasteries: at his mother’s cremation site, likewise at his father’s, and also at Budalaviṭṭhi.

58.

58.

Paṇḍavāpī ca pāṭhīno, rakkhacetiyapabbato;

Tatheva maṇḍalagiri-madhutthalavihārako.

Also at Paṇḍavāpī, Pāṭhīna, Rakkhacetiyapabbata, and likewise the monasteries of Maṇḍalagiri and Madhutthala.

59.

59.

Uruvelavhayo deva-nagare ca vihārako;

Mahiyaṅgaṇavihāro ca, sītalaggāmaleṇakaṃ.

The monastery called Uruvela in Devanagara, the Mahiyangana Monastery, and the Sītalaggāma Cave.

60.

60.

Jambukolavihāro ca, tatheva girikaṇḍako;

Kurundiyavihāro ca, jambukolakaleṇakaṃ.

Jambukola Monastery, and likewise Girikaṇḍaka, Kurundiya Monastery, and the Jambukola Cave.

61.

61.

Bhallātakavihāro ca, tatheva paragāmako;

Kāsagallavhayo canda-girivhaya vihārako.

Bhallātaka Monastery, likewise Paragāmaka, and the monasteries called Kāsagalla and Candagiri.

62.

62.

Velagāmavihāro ca, mahāsenavhagāmako;

Vihāro cā’nurādhamhi, pure bodhigharaṃ tathā.

Velagāma Monastery, the village called Mahāsena, a monastery in the city of Anurādhapura, and likewise the Bodhi-tree shrine.

63.

63.

Iccevamādayoneke, vihāre ca bahū vibhū;

Paṭisaṅkharijiṇṇe so, gāme cā’dā visuṃ visuṃ.

Thus the ruler restored these and many other decayed monasteries, and gave villages to each one separately.

64.

64.

Samantakūṭa selatthaṃ, munindapadalañjanaṃ;

Paṇamatthāya gacchantā, manussā duggamañjase.

To Samantakūṭa, the rocky peak marked with the footprint of the Lord of Sages, people go to pay homage, though the path is difficult to travel.

65.

65.

Sabbe mā kilamantū’ti, dānavaṭṭāya dāpayi;

Sālikkhettādisampannaṃ, gilīmalayanāmakaṃ.

Thinking, 'Let no one become weary,' he established a perpetual endowment of alms, providing the place named Gilīmalaya, which was complete with rice fields and so forth.

66.

66.

Kadalīgāmamagge ca, hūvaraḷañjase tathā;

Gāme datvāna paccekaṃ, sālāyo cāpi kārayi.

On the road to Kadalīgāma and likewise on the path to Hūvaraḷa, he had rest houses built, giving villages for the support of each one.

67.

67.

Anāgate taṃ bhūpālā, mā gaṇhantū’ti lekhiya;

Akkharāni silāthambhe, patiṭṭhāpesi bhūmipo.

'Let future kings not seize them'—thus thinking, the lord of the land had these words inscribed on stone pillars and had them set up.

68.

68.

Gāmaṃ [M 0.0368] antaraviṭṭhiñca, tathā saṅghāṭagāmakaṃ;

Sirimaṇḍagalārāmañca, adāso lābhavāsinaṃ.

He gave the village of Antaraviṭṭhi, and likewise Saṅghāṭagāmaka and Sirimaṇḍagalārāma, to the monks who were dependent on offerings.

69.

69.

Vanajīvakabhikkhūna-madā so catupaccaye;

Bandhūnampi ca so tesaṃ, bhogagāme padāpayi.

To the forest-dwelling monks he gave the four requisites; and to their relatives also, he had revenue-villages granted.

70.

70.

Pāvāraggikapallāni, vividhe osadhepi ca;

Sīte utumhi bahuso, bhikkhusaṅghassa dāpayi.

During the cold season, he frequently had outer cloaks, blankets, and various medicines given to the community of monks.

71.

71.

Adā sabbaparikkhāre, parikkhāre tathāttha so;

Nekavāresu sakkaccaṃ, bhikkhusaṅghassa buddhimā.

The wise one, on many occasions, respectfully gave to the community of monks all the requisites, and likewise other requisites for their welfare.

72.

72.

Saṅghassa pākavaṭṭatthaṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ lābhavāsinaṃ;

Veyyāvaccakarānañca, pūjetuṃ cetiyādikaṃ.

For the provision of food for the Saṅgha, for the monks dependent on offerings, for those who perform services, and for the worship of cetiyas and so forth.

73.

73.

Padinnā pubbarājūhi, ye gāmā rohaṇe bahū;

Tepi sabbe anūne so, yathāpubbaṃ ṭhapesi ca.

And the many villages in Rohaṇa that had been given by former kings, he established them all, undiminished, as they were before.

74.

74.

Adāsi piṭhasappīna-musabhe balino bahi;

Bhattaṃ cā’dāsi so kāka soṇādīnaṃ dayāparo.

He gave strong bulls to the cripples; and, being compassionate, he also gave food to crows, dogs, and other animals.

75.

75.

Adāsinekatā veyya-kārakānaṃ mahākavī;

Saddhiṃ paveṇigāmehi, vittajātamanappakaṃ.

The great poet gave abundant wealth, together with their hereditary villages, to those who performed services.

76.

76.

Rājāmaccādiputtānaṃ, siloke racite suṇaṃ;

Yathānurūpaṃ pādāsi, dhanaṃ tesaṃ kavissaro.

Hearing the verses composed by the sons of kings, ministers, and others, the lord of poets bestowed fitting wealth upon them.

77.

77.

Andhānaṃ paṅgulānañca, gāme cā’dā visuṃ visuṃ;

Nānādevakulānañca, dinnaṃ pubbaṃ na hāpayi.

To the blind and the crippled he gave villages, to each separately; and he did not diminish what had been previously given to the various shrines of the gods.

78.

78.

Patti vo so kulitthīna-manāthānaṃ yathārahaṃ;

Vidhavānamadāgāme, bhattaacchādanāni ca.

To helpless women of good family he gave what was fitting; and to widows in the villages he gave food and clothing.

79.

79.

Rājā sīhaḷakā veyya-karaṇe so mahāpati;

Aggo sīhaḷakāveyya-kārakānamahosi ca.

That king was a great master in the administration of Sīhaḷa, and he was the foremost among the administrators of Sīhaḷa.

80.

80.

Subhe baddhādaro baddha guṇavhaya vihārake;

Bandhesi uparājā so, cetiyaṃ coḷanāsitaṃ.

The viceroy Subha, with great reverence, rebuilt the cetiya in the Guṇavhaya monastery, which had been destroyed by the Coḷas.

81.

81.

Muttacāgī tato tassa, vihārapavarassa so;

Datvā gāmavare niccaṃ, pūjāyo sampavattayi.

Then he, being of liberal generosity, having given choice villages, continually instituted acts of worship for that excellent monastery.

82.

82.

Sova tassa vihārassa, upacāravanantike;

Bandhāpesi mahāvāpiṃ, thīrībhūtamahodakaṃ.

He also had a great tank built near the woods within the precincts of that monastery, a tank with great and stable waters.

83.

83.

Kappūramūlāyatane[M 0.0369], rañño dhītā yasodharā;

Akāresi thiraṃ rammaṃ, mahantaṃ paṭimāgharaṃ.

In the Kappūramūla residence, the king's daughter, Yasodharā, had a firm, delightful, and great image-house built.

84.

84.

Selantarasamūhasmiṃ, rājino rājino sakā;

Kāresi cārupāsādaṃ, pasādāvahamuggataṃ.

In the Selantara complex, the king's own sister had a beautiful, lofty, and delightful palace built.

85.

85.

Tadā neke ca sacivā, tasso rodhajanāpi ca;

Samāciniṃsu puññāni, anekāni anekaso.

Then many ministers, and also the ladies of his harem, accumulated many merits in diverse ways.

86.

86.

Evaṃ samanusāsante, laṃkaṃ laṃkā narissare;

Uparājā vasaṃnīto, vinīto gheramaccunā.

Thus, while the lord of men was ruling Laṅkā, the viceroy was brought into submission, subdued by death in his own house.

87.

87.

Tassa kattabbakiccāni, sakalāni samāpiya;

Jayabāhussoparajjaṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ matiyā adā.

Having completed all the funeral rites for him, he gave the viceroyalty to Jayabāhu with the consent of the bhikkhus.

88.

88.

Athādipādapadaviṃ, datvā vikkamabāhuno;

Gajabāhū’ti vidite, tassa jāte sute tato.

Then, having given the rank of Ādipāda to Vikkamabāhu, a son known as Gajabāhu was born to him.

89.

89.

Mahāmaccehi mantetvā, rājāputtahitatthiko;

Rohaṇaṃ kasiṇaṃ datvā, tahiṃ vāsāya pesayi.

Having consulted with the great ministers, the king, desiring the welfare of the prince, gave him the whole of Rohaṇa and sent him there to dwell.

90.

90.

Tato so tattha gantvāna, mahānāgahulaṃ puraṃ;

Rājadhāniṃ karitvāna, tattha vāsamakappayī.

Then he, having gone there to the city of Mahānāgahula, made it the royal capital and there established his dwelling.

91.

91.

Evaṃ paññāsavassāni’ha vijayabhujo vattayitvāna sammā,

Āṇācakkaṃ janindo pyapagatakhalanaṃ esa pañcādhikāni;

Vaḍḍhetvā sāsanaṃ taṃ khaladamiḷabhayo paddutañcāpilokaṃ,

Saggaṃ lokaṃ sapuññappabhavamuruphalaṃ passituṃ cā’ru roha.

Thus, having righteously wielded his victorious arm for fifty years, this lord of men also turned the wheel of command, free from disturbance, for five more. Having advanced the Dispensation and delivered the afflicted world from the fear of the wicked Damiḷas, he beautifully ascended to the heavenly world to behold the great fruit born of his merit.

Sujanappasāda saṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Mahāvaṃsa, composed for the faith and spiritual urgency of the virtuous,

Lokasāsanasaṃgahakaraṇo nāma

named 'The Support of the World and the Dispensation'.

Aṭṭhapaññāsatimo paricchedo

The Fifty-eighth Chapter.

Ekūnasaṭṭhima pariccheda

The Fifty-ninth Chapter.

Caturājacariya niddeso

An Exposition on the Conduct of the Four Kings.

1.

1.

Tadārañño [M 0.0370] nujāmittā, tassa puttā tayo’pi ca;

Mahāmaccā cayatayo, tathā yatanavāsino.

Then the king's younger brothers and friends, and also his three sons, the great ministers and the generals, as well as the inhabitants of the residence.

2.

2.

Tabbete ādipādassa, rohaṇe vasato sato;

Anārocāpayitvāna, bhūpālamatasāsanaṃ.

All of them, without informing the Ādipāda who was dwelling in Rohaṇa of the news of the king's death,

3.

3.

Sambhūyamantayitvāna, samānacchandataṃ gatā;

Adaṃsu yuvarājassa, laṅkārajjābhisecanaṃ.

Having consulted together and reached a unanimous decision, they gave the royal consecration of Laṅkā to the Yuvarāja.

4.

4.

Oparajje nivesesuṃ, mānabharaṇanāmakaṃ;

Kumāraṃ pubbacāritta-maggaṃ laṅghittha te’khilā.

They established the prince named Māṇābharaṇa in the viceroyalty; thus all of them transgressed the path of ancient custom.

5.

5.

Tayo’tha bhātaro sabbe, te māṇabharaṇādayo;

Jayabāhumahīpāla-sahitā sahasā tadā.

Then all three of those brothers, Māṇābharaṇa and the others, together with King Jayabāhu, suddenly...

6.

6.

Muttāmaṇippabhūtikaṃ, ratanaṃ sārasammataṃ;

Sabbaṃ hatthagataṃ katvā, vāhanañca gajādikaṃ.

Having taken into their hands all the valuable treasures, such as pearls and gems, and the vehicles, such as elephants,

7.

7.

Sakalaṃ balamādāya, pulatthinagarā tadā;

Khippaṃ taṃ vikkamabhujaṃ, gaṇhisāmā’ti nikkhamuṃ.

Taking their entire army, they then set out from the city of Pulatthinagara, thinking, 'We shall quickly seize that Vikkamabāhu.'

8.

8.

Sutvā pavattiṃ sakalaṃ, imaṃ vikkamabāhuso;

Tā tassantimasakkāraṃ, vidhātuṃ handano labhiṃ.

That Vikkamabāhu, having heard all this news, lamented: 'Alas, I was not able to perform his final rites!'

9.

9.

Idāni khippaṃ gantvāna, pulatthinagaraṃ tahiṃ,

Tā tassāḷāhanaṭṭhāna dassane neva so ahaṃ.

Now, if I go quickly to the city of Pulatthinagara, I shall not even see his cremation ground.

10.

10.

Sokabhāraṃ vinodessaṃ, mama ceto gataṃ iti;

Katadaḷha vavatthāno, viniggamma tato purā.

Thinking, 'I will dispel this burden of sorrow that has entered my heart,' he made a firm resolution and went forth from that city.

11.

11.

Pulatthipuramāgacchaṃ, ādipādo’ti sāsaso;

Sattaṭṭhasatasaṅkhena, balena parivārito.

The Ādipāda came towards Pulatthipura, surrounded by a force numbering seven or eight hundred.

12.

12.

Antarālapatheyeva, guttahālakamaṇḍale;

Gāme pana samukkavhe, disvā senaṅgamāgataṃ.

On the way, in the district of Guttahālaka, in a village named Samukka, having seen the approaching army,

13.

13.

Mahantaṃ [M 0.0371] yuddhasannaddhaṃ, ekavīro bhayātiko;

Yujjhitvā te palāpesi, khaṇeneva disodisaṃ.

That lone hero, who had overcome fear, fought against the great army arrayed for battle and in a single moment put them to flight in all directions.

14.

14.

Tayo te bhātaro tattha, sampattāva jayā tato;

Abhimānuddhatā khippaṃ, annayha balavāhanaṃ.

Those three brothers, having met with defeat there, though arrogant with pride, quickly assembled another army.

15.

15.

Ādipādakajambūti, vissutamhi padesake;

Saṅgāmesuṃ parājesi, bhiyyo yujjhittha so tayo.

In the renowned place called Ādipādaka Jambū, he defeated them in battles, and he fought those three again.

16.

16.

Tatiyaṃ kaṭagāmasmiṃ, kāḷavāpyaṃ catutthakaṃ;

Pañcamaṃ uddhaṭadvāre, chaṭṭhaṃso paṅkavelake.

The third at Kaṭagāma, the fourth at Kāḷavāpi, the fifth at Uddhaṭadvāra, and the sixth he fought at Paṅkavelaka.

17.

17.

Tehi yuddhaṃ karitvāna, gahītavijayo sadā;

Pulatthipuramāgañci, sahāmacca parijjano.

Having fought battles with them and always being victorious, he came to the city of Pulatthi with his ministers and retinue.

18.

18.

Sacintitakkameneva, passitvāḷāhanaṃ pitu;

Vidūritamahāseko, laddhassāso purevasaṃ.

Just as he had thought, having seen his father's cremation ground, his great flood of sorrow was dispelled, and having gained comfort, he dwelt as before.

19.

19.

Dukkhe sahāya bhūtāna-mattano so yathārahaṃ;

Amaccānamadā sabba-bhoge ṭhānantare hi so.

As was fitting, to his ministers who had been his companions in suffering, he indeed gave all possessions and high positions.

20.

20.

Bhaṭānañcāpi sabbesaṃ, sahāyātānamattano;

Anurūpamadā vuttiṃ, saraṃ dukkhasahāyataṃ.

And also to all the soldiers and those who had come as his companions, he gave a suitable livelihood, remembering their companionship in suffering.

21.

21.

Māṇābharaṇabhūpopi, saddhiṃ sesehi bhātūhi;

Karitvā rohaṇaṃ passaṃ, rohaṇañca sahatthagaṃ.

King Māṇābharaṇa also, together with his remaining brothers, having made the Rohaṇa region his own, and having Rohaṇa in his hand,...

22.

22.

Tato kittisirīmeghe, sadvādasasahassakaṃ;

Raṭṭhaṃ datvāna vasituṃ, tahiṃyeva samādisi.

Then, having given a country with twelve thousand [villages] to Kittisirimegha, he ordered him to dwell right there.

23.

23.

Āṇatto bhātarākitti-sirīmegho janādhipo;

Gantvā vasi puretattha, mahānāgahulavhaye.

King Kittisirimegha, commanded by his brother, went and resided in the city there, called Mahānāgahula.

24.

24.

Sirīvallabhanāmassa, kumārassāpi cādisi;

Desamaṭṭhasahassavhaṃ, datvāna vasituṃ tahiṃ.

He also commanded the prince named Sirīvallabha to dwell there, having given him the region known as 'Eight Thousand'.

25.

25.

Tatheva sopi gantvāna, uddhanadvāranāmakaṃ;

Gāmaṃ katvā rājadāniṃ, vasanto anusāsitaṃ.

Likewise, he also went and, having made the village named Uddhanadvāra his capital, dwelt there, ruling.

26.

26.

Sayañca sahasenāya, gantvā dakkhiṇapassakaṃ;

Vīrabāhūti paññāto, puṅkhagāmaṃ samāvasi.

And he himself, known as Vīrabāhu, having gone with his army to the southern region, dwelt in Puṅkhagāma.

27.

27.

Mātā ca tiṇṇaṃ bhātūnaṃ, jayabāhu ca bhūmipo;

Nivasiṃsu tadā kitti-sirimeghassa santike.

The mother of the three brothers and King Jayabāhu dwelt at that time near Kittisirimegha.

28.

28.

Tato [M 0.0372] saṃvacchare’tīte, te māṇabharaṇādayo;

Tenattani kataṃ yuddhe, sabbaṃ vikkamabāhunā.

Then, after a year had passed, those led by Māṇābharaṇa recalled all that had been done to them in battle by Vikkamabāhu.

29.

29.

Durārohaṃ mahantaṃ taṃ, parājayatarābhavaṃ;

Anussarantabahuso, abhimānasamunnatā.

Recalling often that great and hard-to-surmount defeat, they, lofty with pride,

30.

30.

Muddhābhisittarājūna-mekākīrājaraṭṭhakaṃ;

Vināyamabhisekena, kathaṃ nāmānubhossati.

“How indeed will this lone one, without consecration, enjoy the kingdom of crowned kings?”

31.

31.

Iti issā parattañca, yātā saṅgayhasāvake;

Bhiyyo sambhūyasaṅgāma-karaṇatthāya nikkhamuṃ.

Thus, overcome by envy, and having gathered their followers, they marched out again for the purpose of making war together.

32.

32.

Sutvā tamatthaṃ dūtehi, so vikkamabhujopi ca;

Agā tesaṃva visayaṃ, mahāsenāpurakkhato.

Hearing that matter from the messengers, that Vikkamabāhu also, with a great army at the forefront, went to their territory.

33.

33.

Dese dakkhiṇake bodhi-senapabbatagāmake;

Yujjhitvā te parājesi, tayo vikkamabāhuso.

In the southern region, at the village of Bodhisenapabbata, Vikkamabāhu fought and defeated the three of them.

34.

34.

Ripavo dāni me sabbe, ummūlessāmahaṃ iti;

Palāyante nubandhittha, padānupadikaṃ’va te.

Thinking, “Now I shall uproot all my enemies,” he pursued them as they fled, as if tracking them step by step.

35.

35.

Te ca duggaṃ palāyiṃsu, pañcayojanaraṭṭhake;

Khippaṃ pāvekkhi kalyāṇiṃ, so’pi te gahaṇatthiko.

And they fled to a stronghold in the Pañcayojanaraṭṭha; he also, desirous of capturing them, swiftly entered Kalyāṇī.

36.

36.

Vīro ariyadesiyo, vīradevoti pākaṭo;

Paḷandīpissaro eko, bhūsaṃ sahasiko tadā.

A hero from the Āryan land, known as Vīradeva, the sole lord of Paḷandīpa, was at that time exceedingly daring.

37.

37.

Saddhiṃ sūrehi yodhehi, mahātitthamhi otari;

Kātuṃ hatthagahaṃ sakkā, laṃkādīpanti cintiya.

With his brave warriors, he landed at Mahātittha, thinking, “It is possible to seize the island of Laṅkā by force.”

38.

38.

So vikkamabhujo sutvā, pavattiṃ bhūbhujo tadā;

Yāvatā nātra laṃkāyaṃ, laddhogāho bhavissati.

Then that Vikkamabāhu, having heard the news of the king, thought:

39.

39.

Tāva ummūlanīyoti, kalyāṇimhā viniggato;

Mahātitthamhi mannāra-nāmakaṃ gāmakaṃ gato.

“Before he can gain a foothold, he must be uprooted.” Thus, having departed from Kalyāṇī, he went to the village named Mannāra at Mahātittha.

40.

40.

Katvāna vīradevo’pi, saṅgāmaṃ tena rājinā;

Anīkaṅgādayo rāja-putte dve bhātaropi ca.

Vīradeva also, having made battle with that king, along with the two princes, who were brothers, led by Anīkaṅga,

41.

41.

Senādhināyakañceva, kittināmappakāsitaṃ;

Ghātetvā sahasā vīra-sammate ca bahūjane.

and having swiftly slain the general known by the name Kitti, and many people esteemed as heroes,

42.

42.

Gāhetvā jīvaggāhaṃso, rakkhakañca camūpatiṃ;

Sabalaṃ taṃ parājetvā, anubandhi padāpadaṃ.

and having captured the guard and the army commander alive, and having defeated him with his forces, he pursued him step by step.

43.

43.

Palāyamāno [M 0.0373] so bhīto, āgantvāna nijaṃ puraṃ;

Hatthasāraṃ samādāya, koṭṭhasāraṃ gato lahuṃ.

Fleeing in fear, he came to his own city, and having taken his most valuable possessions, he went quickly to the treasury.

44.

44.

Pacchato pacchato vīra-devo tamanubandhiya;

Āgantvāna purevāsaṃ, katipāhaṃ vidhāyaso.

Pursuing him close behind, he came to his former dwelling and stayed for some days.

45.

45.

Gaṇhituṃ vikkamabhujaṃ, tattheva turitaṃ agā;

Pesayitvā sakaṃ sopi, mahantaṃ sakalaṃ balaṃ.

Having sent forth his own entire great army, he also swiftly went to that very place to seize the mighty-armed one.

46.

46.

Yujjhāpetvāna ghātetvā, gāme antaraviṭṭhike;

Mahākaddamaduggamhi, vīradevaṃ mahabbalo.

The one of great strength, having caused them to fight, slew Vīradeva in the Mahākaddama fortress in the village of Antaraviṭṭhika.

47.

47.

Abhisekaṃ vināyeva, pulatthi nagare vasaṃ;

Without any consecration, residing in the city of Pulatthi, the glorious one administered the affairs of the Rājaraṭṭha.

48.

48.

Apanīyaraṇe chandaṃ, bhātaropi tayo tato;

Āvasiṃsu yathāpubbaṃ, gantvā raṭṭhaṃ sakaṃ sakaṃ.

Then his three brothers also, having abandoned their desire for battle, went to their own respective lands and dwelt there as before.

49.

49.

Caturopi mahīpālā, yatamānā ciraṃ tahiṃ;

Ekacchattaṅkitaṃ kātuṃ, neva sakkhiṃsu sabbaso.

The four kings also, striving there for a long time, were altogether unable to bring the land under a single umbrella.

50.

50.

Anisammakāribhāvena, kulīne parihāpayuṃ;

Ṭhapesuñca mahantatte, hīne sābhimate jane.

Through their thoughtless actions, they ruined the noble families and established base and self-willed people in high positions.

51.

51.

Vaḍḍhitaṃnekadhā sammā, raññā vijayabāhunā;

Sāsanañca tathālokaṃ, hāpayiṃsu subuddhino.

These men of great wisdom caused both the Teaching and the world to decline, which had been rightly fostered in many ways by King Vijayabāhu.

52.

52.

Kulīnānaṃ manussāna-mabhāvepi ca tādise;

Dose vittaṃ tadāyattaṃ, pasayhāvahariṃsu ca.

And even in the absence of such noble men, they forcibly seized the wealth under their control by imposing fines for faults.

53.

53.

Pīḷetuṃ sakalaṃ loka-muddharantādhikaṃ baliṃ;

Ucchūva ucchuyantete, khīṇako sādhanesino.

Seeking wealth with their treasuries depleted, they oppressed the whole world by extracting excessive tribute, and were themselves pressed just like sugarcane.

54.

54.

Uddharitvāna buddhādi-santake bhogagāmake;

So vikkamabhujo rājā, sevakesu samappayī.

Having seized the revenue villages belonging to the Buddha and others, that king, Vikkamabhuja, handed them over to his servants.

55.

55.

Pulatthinagare neka-vihāre dhātumaṇḍite;

Sova desantarīyānaṃ, bhaṭānaṃ vasituṃ adā.

In the city of Pulatthi, he gave many monasteries adorned with relics to foreign soldiers to dwell in.

56.

56.

Saddhehi pattadhātussa, dāṭhādhātuvarassa ca;

Pūjanatthāya dinnāni, maṇimuttādikāni ca.

And gems, pearls, and other such things had been given by the faithful for the veneration of the Bowl Relic and the excellent Tooth Relic.

57.

57.

Candanāgarukappuraṃ, suvaṇṇādimayā bahū;

Paṭimāyo ca acchijja, yathākāmaṃ vayaṃ nayī.

He also seized sandalwood, aloeswood, and camphor, and many images made of gold and other materials, and spent them according to his desire.

58.

58.

Sāsanassa [M 0.0374] ca lokassa, kriyamānamupaddavaṃ;

Passantā bahuso tasmiṃ, tadā nibbannamānasā.

Seeing the manifold troubles being inflicted upon the Teaching and the world, their minds were then disheartened.

59.

59.

Aṭṭhamūlavihāresu, yatayo garusammatā;

Paṃsukūlikabhikkhū ca, koṭṭhāsadvayanissitā.

The highly esteemed monastics of the eight principal monasteries, and the Pāṃsukūlika bhikkhus who belonged to the two fraternities,

60.

60.

Evaṃ titthiyatulyānaṃ, sāsanopaddavaṃ bahuṃ;

Karontānaṃ sakā sambhā-payātaṃ pavaraṃ iti.

While those rulers were thus acting like heretics and causing much harm to the Teaching, the monks departed, deeming this the best course.

61.

61.

Dāṭhādhātuvaraṃ patta-dhātumādāya rohaṇaṃ;

Gantvā vāsamakappesuṃ, phāsuṭhāne tahiṃ tahiṃ.

Taking the excellent Tooth Relic and the Bowl Relic, they went to Rohaṇa and made their dwellings here and there in comfortable places.

62.

62.

Tatheva phāsuṭhānesu, vippakiṇṇā tahiṃ tahiṃ;

Te kulīnā nilīnā’va, hutvā vāsamakappayuṃ.

Similarly, scattered here and there in comfortable places, those noble ones made their dwellings as if concealed.

63.

63.

Pakkhadvayamahīpāla-gayhāsīmā suṭhāpitā;

Sāmantā aññamaññehi, karonto bahuso raṇaṃ.

The kings of the two factions had their boundaries well established, while the neighboring chieftains frequently made war with one another.

64.

64.

Susamiddhesu nekesu, gāmesu nigamesu ca;

Aggiṃ dentā taḷāke ca, chindantā jalapūrite.

Setting fire to many prosperous villages and market towns, and breaching the tanks that were full of water,

65.

65.

Nāsentā sabbathā sabba-mātikāvaraṇāni ca;

Chindantā nāḷikerādi, so pakāre ca bhūruhe.

Completely destroying all the water channels and weirs, and cutting down coconut palms and other such trees,

66.

66.

Yathā porāṇakaggāma-ṭhānantipi na ñāyate;

Vināsesuṃ tathā raṭṭhaṃ, aññamaññavirodhino.

Those who were hostile to one another so destroyed the kingdom that even the site of a former principal village could not be recognized.

67.

67.

Te ca bhūmi patīgāma-vilopaṃ patthamosanaṃ;

Kārentā nijacārehi, ācaruṃ lokupaddavaṃ.

And those lords of the land, causing the destruction of villages and the plundering of the harvest through their own agents, brought disaster upon the world.

68.

68.

Kulīnānaṃ manussānaṃ, dāsakammakarāpi ca;

Sasāmino’ti vattantā, nissaṅkā vītabhītikā.

Even the slaves and workers of noble men, declaring themselves to be their own masters, were without hesitation and free from fear.

69.

69.

Hutvā yudhīyā rājūnaṃ, abbhantarapavattino;

Balavantatarā jātā, laddhaṭhānantarā tadā.

Having become soldiers for the kings and acting as insiders, they became more powerful, having then obtained positions of rank.

70.

70.

Janā samantakūṭādi-nekadugganivāsino;

Adentā bhūmipālānaṃ, pubbapaṭṭhapitaṃ karaṃ.

The people dwelling in many inaccessible places such as Samantakūṭa, not giving the rulers the tax that was previously established,

71.

71.

Rājāṇamagaṇentā te, gatā dāmarikattanaṃ;

Sakaṃ sakaṃ’va visaya-māvasiṃsu samuddhatā.

Disregarding the royal command, they became rebels and, being haughty, each dwelt in his own territory.

72.

72.

Anatthe nicitā nāma, parivattanti sabbatā;

Iti vattabba taṃyeva, yātaṃ laṅkātalaṃ tadā.

It should be said that the land of Laṅkā at that time had indeed become 'heaped with disaster,' changing on all sides.

73.

73.

Evaṃ [M 0.0375] gāmakabhojakā viya bhusaṃtejo vihīnā sadā;

Accantaṃ byasanāti sattahadayā rājābhimānujjhitā.

Thus, like mere village headmen, they were always greatly lacking in majesty, their hearts deeply afflicted by calamity, and they were bereft of royal pride.

74.

74.

Niccaṃ attaparatthasiddhividhurāsaṅgā vihīnāsayā;

Sabbe te vihariṃsu bhūmipatayo cārittamaggātigā.

Always failing to accomplish their own or others' welfare, lacking in resolve and free from scruples, all those kings lived, having transgressed the path of proper conduct.

Sujanappasādasaṃvegatthāya kate mahāvaṃse

In the Great Chronicle, composed for the serene joy and spiritual urgency of the virtuous,

Caturājacariyaniddeso nāma

Named the Exposition of the Conduct of the Four Kings,

Ekūnasaṭṭhimo paricchedo.

The Fifty-ninth Chapter.

Saṭṭhima pariccheda

The Sixtieth Chapter.

Kumārodayo

The Arising of the Prince.

1.

1.

Rohaṇe nivasitthā’va, jayabāhumahīpati;

Mittāvhā rājinī ceva, tadā kālamakaṃsu te.

King Jayabāhu and Queen Mittā, who dwelt in Rohaṇa, passed away at that time.

2.

2.

Sirīvallabhajāyā’tha, janesi sugalā duve;

Māṇabharaṇakaṃ puttaṃ, puttiṃ līlāvatimpi ca.

Then Sugalā, the wife of Sirīvallabha, gave birth to two children: a son, Māṇābharaṇa, and a daughter, Līlāvatī.

3.

3.

Māṇābharaṇabhūpāla-devī’pi ratanāvalī;

Mittaṃ pabhāvatiñcāpi, alabhī dhītaro duve.

Queen Ratanāvalī, the consort of King Māṇābharaṇa, also obtained two daughters, Mittā and Pabhāvatī.

4.

4.

Passantassa ubho tāyo, dhītaro vīrabāhuno;

Tadā mahādipādassa, evaṃ āsi vitakkitaṃ.

As the Mahādipāda was looking at those two daughters of Vīrabāhu, this thought occurred to him:

5.

5.

Lokābhisammate sabba-bhūpālanvayamuddhani;

Visuddhe somavaṃsamhi, abhijātā mayaṃ pana.

“We are indeed nobly born in the pure Lunar Dynasty, which is revered by the world and stands at the head of all royal lineages.

6.

6.

Pihanīyatarākārā, sabbasattisamunnatā;

Nānāvijjāsu nipuṇā, hatthiassādisukkhamā.

Most desirable in appearance, exalted in all power, skilled in various arts, and well-trained in matters of elephants, horses, and so forth.

7.

7.

Tathā pekākinā ve’te, tayo vikkamabāhunā;

Parājayaṃ paribhavaṃ, pāpitā bahuso raṇe.

Even so, these three were brought to defeat and disgrace many times in battle by Vikkamabāhu alone.

8.

8.

Sūnuno susamatthassa, visodhetu mimaṃ malaṃ;

Na dissate pātubhāvo, aho no appapuññatā.

Alas, how lacking in merit we are, for no manifestation is seen of a son capable of cleansing this stain!

9.

9.

Janavādakiliṭṭhena[M 0.0376], rājattenāpi kiṃ mama;

Idāni visayāsaṅgaṃ, hitvā kalyāṇakammasu.

What use is kingship to me, defiled by public criticism? Now, having abandoned attachment to sense-objects, I must engage in wholesome deeds.

10.

10.

Appamattassa satataṃ, netabbā vāsarā’iti;

Niyyātetvā amaccānaṃ, sabbaṃ rajjavicāraṇaṃ.

Thinking, ‘My days must always be spent heedfully,’ he entrusted all administration of the kingdom to his ministers.

11.

11.

Tahiṃ satta’ṭṭhamāsañhi, vasaṃ rattiyamekadā;

Devarājaghareseyyaṃ, kappesi sīlasaṃyato.

Dwelling there for seven or eight months, restrained by virtue, one night he lay down to sleep in the house of the Devarāja.

12.

12.

Tato paccūsakālamhi, devaputtaṃ mahiddhikaṃ;

Vicittavatthābharaṇaṃ, gandhamālāvibhūsitaṃ.

Then, at dawn, he saw a mighty divine being, adorned with varied garments and ornaments, and embellished with fragrant garlands.

13.

13.

Uḷāratararūpena, dehobhāsena attano;

Obhāsentaṃ asesā’sā, sūriyañca na bhuggataṃ.

With a most excellent form and with the splendor of his own body, he illuminated all directions, like the not-yet-risen sun.

14.

14.

Vadantaṃ supine evaṃ, adakkhi daraṇīpati;

Pasīdassu mahābhāga, pitobhava mahipati.

The lord of the earth beheld him speaking thus in a dream: ‘Be pleased, O great one! Be a father, O king!’

15.

15.

Dhaññalakkhaṇasampanno, icchitatthassasādhako;

Vinīto lokakuhara-byāpitejo parakkamo.

‘Endowed with auspicious marks, a fulfiller of desired aims, disciplined, his might and valor pervading the cavity of the world.

16.

16.

Āṇabalayasokitti-bhāsuro sagguṇākaro;

Lokasāsanasaṃvuddhi-karo puttavaro tava.

Glorious with command, power, fame, and renown, a mine of good qualities, a promoter of the welfare of the world and the Teaching—such will be your excellent son.

17.

17.

Labbhīssate mahārāja, na cirasseva sampati;

18.

18.

Pabujjhitvāna sañjāta-pītivegotha rattiyā;

Vibhātāya tatopoṅkha-gāmaṃ gañchinaruttamo.

Awakening, with a surge of joy having arisen, then at dawn the best of men went from there to the village of Poṅkha.

19.

19.

Yathā diṭṭhappakārantaṃ, kathesi supinaṃ subhaṃ;

That king recounted the auspicious dream, just as he had seen it, to his ministers, headed by the chief queen.

20.

20.

Saddhiṃ mahesiyā tattha, patthento puttamuttamaṃ;

Cintonto dānasīlādiṃ, subhaṃ nānappakārakaṃ.

There, together with his chief queen, longing for an excellent son, he contemplated various kinds of auspicious deeds such as generosity and virtue.

21.

21.

Athekadivasaṃkāle, paccūse supine pana;

Sabbalakkhaṇasampannaṃ, sabbasetaṃ manoharaṃ.

Then one day at dawn, in a dream, he saw a being endowed with all marks, completely white and captivating:

22.

22.

Dantīpotavaraṃ dantaṃ, kaṇṇe gaṇiyapemato;

Pavisantamivattānaṃ, seyyāgabbhaṃ mahesiyā.

a superb young elephant, tamed, being grasped affectionately by the ear, as if entering the queen's bedchamber.

23.

23.

Sampassiya pabujjhitvā, uṭṭhāya sayanāvarā;

Sañjātapītipāmojja-vegapīṇitamānaso.

Having seen this, he awoke and rose from his excellent bed, his mind suffused with a surge of rapture and delight.

24.

24.

Tāyaṃ [M 0.0377] velāyamedāsu-seyyāgabbhaṃ mahesiyā;

Pavissasupinaṃ tassā, yathādiṭṭhaṃ pakāsayī.

At that very moment, the chief queen entered his bedchamber and related her dream just as she had seen it.

25.

25.

Ahampi tādisaṃ hatthi-potakaṃ sayanaṃ mama;

Padakkhiṇaṃ karitvāna, ṭhitaṃ soṇḍe samādiya.
